the destination does not reset at the same time (due to different reset or non resettable
register), this causes metastability at destination. By default, X injection happens for one
clock cycle of the source clock and can be controlled by substituting argument ‘N’ with the
required value.

-sdc=random_delay:uniform
This option enables random delay injection support for all the destination flop during SDC
validation. This ensures that random delays are inserted based on the path multiplier limit,
preventing masking of timing issues.
With uniform random delays, VCS-SDC can check a violation when the source changes
within the specified violation window and capture occurs on the destination side. It adjusts
the number of cycles for inserting x or bool values based on the maximum multiplier value
associated with the destination flop and remaining violation window.
%simv -sdc=random_delay:uniform <vcs options>
Consider the following compile time option:
% vcs -sdc=verify_false_path:N
Here, by default the value of N is 10.
In the following example, the FP constraint has "10" cycles of path multiplier limit and the
tool provides an equal weightage for 1,2,39 cycles (1->10-1) on the destination flip-flop.
Consider the following RTL:
//FP source flop
dff S2 (in, clk2, rst, ff3);
//FP destination flop
dff D2 (ff3, clk2, rst, ff4);

module dff (input [7:0] d, input clk, input rst, output reg [7:0] q);

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst)
if(!rst) q <= 0;
else q <= d;
Figure 5 False Path from S2 to D2
In the false path from S2 to D2, X- insertion occurs between 0 to 9 cycles randomly. At
runtime, during early capture event for a destination, the tool injects X for a specified
number of clock cycles (N). Let the remaining violation window for destination be W. This
number N is decided randomly between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W). Here, M is the
maximum multiplier value associated with the destination. The probability of selection of a
number between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W) is equal.

In this example, 9 is the minimum number of cores and the simulation terminates if there
are less than 9 cores.
-fgp=num_cores:<value>
Use this option to specify the number of cores. The number of cores, specified as
<value>, are picked that includes one master core and <value>-1 child cores.
It is recommended to use the -fgp=num_cores:<value> option with the
-fgp=single_socket_mode option.
% simv -fgp=single_socket_mode -fgp=num_cores:<value>
% simv -fgp=single_socket_mode -fgp=num_cores:10
In this example, 10 number of cores are picked that includes one master core and nine
child cores.

-fgp=num_fsdb_threads:<value>
Use this option to indicate VCS that dumping is involved. This option is mandatory when
FSDB dumping is enabled. VCS allocates as many cores as specified by <value> for
dumping.
When <value>=0, FSDB dumping runs on the master core (core that runs all the non-
parallel portion of the design) and VCS generates a warning message. The remaining
cores of the socket are used for FGP.
When <value> is greater than 0 , additional cores are allocated for dumping.
When the num_fsdb_threads:<value> option is not specified, VCS generates the
following error:
Error-[FGP_NO_FSDB_DUMPING_THREADS] No cores specified for FSDB dumping
Exclusive cores for FSDB dumping must be specified in non-mutex
synchronization mode.
Specify exclusive cores for FSDB dumping using the following command:
%simv -fgp=num_threads:<value> -fgp=num_fsdb_threads:M
%simv -fgp=num_threads:8 -fgp=num_fsdb_threads:5
-fgp=num_threads:<value>
The num_threads runtime option specifies the number of cores. <value>+1 cores are
picked that includes one master core and <value> child cores.
%simv -fgp=num_threads:<value>
simv collects a list of free cores. A core is determined to be loaded or free based on the
load threshold.
If the number of free cores is less than the requested number of threads (<value>+1),
then VCS generates an error. Otherwise, VCS uses <value>+1 cores out of the list (first
use the cores on one socket) and bind threads to them. If enough free cores are not
available, VCS generates an error message.

When you use the following runtime command:
% simv -fgp=num_threads:8
9 cores are selected from the 10 available node1 CPUs.
-fgp=schedpli
This option improves FGP runtime performance when the design has large number of PLI
call-backs at runtime.
% simv -fgp=num_threads:<value> -fgp=schedpli
% simv -fgp=num_threads:5 -fgp=schedpli
-fgp=single_socket_mode
Use this option to use all the available cores on the given socket. If you enable dumping,
some cores are shared with the FSDB dumping threads.
When simulation starts, VCS detects the number of cores that are available on the current
socket. All cores are treated as available irrespective of the current CPU load. When the
simulation threads are created, VCS distributes these threads to the available cores. If the
simulation threads do not use all the assigned cores, the simulation continues, but VCS
generates a warning message.
It is recommended to use the -fgp=num_cores:<value> option with the
-fgp=single_socket_mode option.
% simv -fgp=single_socket_mode -fgp=num_cores:<value>
% simv -fgp=single_socket_mode -fgp=num_cores:9

-fgp=sync:<scheme_value>
Use this option to specify thread synchronization scheme. The default synchronization
scheme used for optimal performance is -fgp=sync:busywait, which is best
for optimizing simulation performance. You can also select any of the following
synchronization schemes to override the default scheme:
• mutex - Specify this scheme to use pthread_mutex based synchronization.
• serial - Specify this scheme to run the threads serially. This is used to debug any
potential thread race issue.
%simv -fgp=sync:<scheme_value>
%simv -fgp=sync:busywait
-fgp=use_least_locked_socket
This option enforces the selection of the socket with the least number of cores that are
locked by other processes.
% simv -fgp=single_socket_mode -fgp=num_cores:<value>
-fgp=use_least_locked_socket
% simv -fgp=single_socket_mode -fgp=num_cores:8
-fgp=use_least_locked_socket

+define+UVM_VCS_RECORD
VCS allows you to record the UVM phases and enables the phase debugging capabilities.
With this phase recording, you can see the start time and the end time for each
component in each phase and the connectivity information for ports in end_of_elab. This
feature is available with UVM-1.1 libraries in VCS.
To turn on UVM phase recording, use +UVM_PHASE_RECORD at runtime and pass the
-debug_access option during compilation. The phase recordings are stored in the
simulation VPD file.
You can enable UVM phase recording in your UVM-1.1 by running the VCS 3-step flow:
1. Define +UVM_VCS_RECORD at first step while compiling UVM library:
% vlogan -ntb_opts uvm +define+UVM_VCS_RECORD
% vlogan -ntb_opts uvm [compile_options] \

Chapter 22: Methodology (UVM/VVM/OVM) Options
2. Pass the -debug_access option at the compilation command line, as shown:
% vcs -sverilog -ntb_opts -debug_access [compile_options]
3. Enable phase recording during simulation by adding +UVM_PHASE_RECORD
% simv +UVM_TESTNAME= \+UVM_PHASE_RECORD [simv_options]
You can then use Verdi to debug the UVM phases in UVM Phase View. This is supported
for Interactive Debug.

problems related to the launch of Verdi in the copied or relocated

-debug_access
Enables the required debug capabilities in a simulation. You can optimize simulation
performance by enabling only the required debug capabilities.
Table Supported Options of -debug_access describes the supported options of
-debug_access.
The -debug_access option without any additional option_name enables VPD and FSDB
dumping capability. This option allows you to enter the UCLI prompt and use only the run,
quit, and dump commands.
Table 3 Supported Options of -debug_access
Option Name Description
r This option enables the read capability for the entire design. This enables PLI
access to get value, and enables the UCLI get command. This is the minimum
debug option to invoke the Verdi interactive mode.
w This option applies write (deposit) capability to the registers and variables for the
entire design.
wn This option applies write (deposit) capability to the nets for the entire design.
fn This option applies force capability to the nets for the entire design. This option is
equivalent to -debug_access+r+fn.
fwn This option applies write (deposit) and force capability to all nets in the design. This
option is equivalent to -debug_access+r+wn+fn.
f This option enables the following:
• Read capability on registers, variables, and nets
• Write (deposit) capability on registers and variables
• Force capability on registers, variables, and nets
This option is equivalent to -debug_access+r+w+fn+f.
drivers
drivers This option enables driver debugging capability. This option is equivalent to
-debug_access+r+drivers.
line
line This option enables line debugging. It allows you to use the commands
for step/next and line breakpoints. This option is equivalent to
-debug_access+r+line.
cbk
cbk This option enables dumping of SystemVerilog string type signals and PLI-based
callbacks on nets, registers, and variables. This option is equivalent to
-debug_access+r+cbk.

Table 3 Supported Options of -debug_access (Continued)
Option Name Description
cbkd
cbkd This option enables both dumping and PLI-based callbacks on dynamic nets,
registers, and variables defined in classes. Class object debugging is also enabled.
This option is equivalent to -debug_access+r+line+cbkd.
thread
thread This option enables the debugging of the SystemVerilog threads. This option is
equivalent to -debug_access+r+thread.
class
class This option enables debugging of the SystemVerilog classes and class
objects, but the capability is also applied to the remaining portion of the
design as specified by the -debug_region option. This option is equivalent
to:-debug_access+r+w+thread+line+cbk+cbkd.
pp
pp This option enables write capability on registers and variables, callbacks for the
entire design, driver capability, and assertion debug capability. This option is
equivalent to:-debug_access+w+cbk+drivers.
dmptf
dmptf This option enables dumping of ports and internal nodes/memories of
tasks/functions.
all This option enables all the above options. This option is equivalent
to:-debug_access+r+w+wn+f+fn+fwn+drivers+line+cbk+cbkd+
thread+class+pp+dmptf.
-memcbk
-memcbk The -debug_access-memcbk option disables callbacks for memories and
multidimensional arrays (MDAs). By default, -debug_access enables callbacks for
memories and MDAs.
reverse
reverse This option enables the reverse debugging feature.
designer
designer This option enables the following debug capabilities:
• Read and write for both variables and nets
• PLI and value change callbacks and line callback
• FSDB/VPD dumping capability
• Debugging or dumping of cell ports
• Class and thread debugging (no SystemVerilog Testbench debugging) • Driver
debugging
This option is equivalent to: -debug_access+line+r+w+wn+cbk
-debug_region+cellports.
You can use the -debug_access+designer option for debugging design and
simulation mismatches.
This option does not support the following:
• Driver debugging

simctrl This option does not support the following:

verbose

-kdb
Generates Verdi Knowledge Database (KDB). In case of VCS three-step flow, add the
-kdb option in all the vlogan/vhdlan/vcs command lines.
When you specify the -kdboption, Verdi creates the KDB and dumps the design into the
libraries specified in the synopsys_sim.setup file.
// Compile the design using VCS and generate both VCS database and Verdi
KDB //
// -kdb in VCS two-step flow
%> vcs -kdb <compile_options> <source files>
// -kdb in VCS three-step flow
% vlogan -kdb <vlogan_options> <source files>
% vhdlan -kdb <vhdlan_options> <source files>
% vcs -kdb <top_name>

-kdb=only
Generates only the Verdi KDB that is required for both post-process and interactive
simulation debug with Verdi.
In the VCS two-step flow, this option does not generate the VCS compile data/executable
and does not disturb the existing VCS compile data/executables.
Following is the use model in the VCS two-step flow:
% vcs -kdb=only <compile_options> <source files>
In the VCS three-step flow, vlogan/vhdlan does not support the -kdb=only option, it is
recommended to use the -kdb option instead.
Following is the use model in the VCS three-step flow:
% vlogan -kdb <vlogan_options> <source files>
% vhdlan -kdb <vhdlan_options> <source files>
% vcs -kdb=only <top_name> <compile_options>
-diag env
Enables you to dump all environment variables that are set before starting the compilation
and the simulation process. The list of environment variables that are set in the terminal is
stored in the log file, which can be used to debug the environment related issues when the
verification setup is complex and multiple and when nested scripts are used.
VCS dumps all the environment variables in the vcs_env_diag_<pid>.log log file that is
generated in the simv.daidir directory.
% vcs -diag env

This option is useful to encounter problems related to the launch of Verdi in the copied or

-sdc=verify_false_path:<N>
This option evaluates set_false_path commands present in SDC similar to
set_multicycle_path command.
If no value is specified, a multicycle path delay of 10 destination clock cycles is computed
by default. You can override the default delay by substituting argument 'N' with the
required value.
%vcs -sdc=verify_false_path:<N> <vcs options>
-sdc=verify_false_path:2 <vcs options>
-sdc=verify_clock_group:<N>
When you use this option, the paths between clocks grouped as asynchronous in SDC
(using set_clock_groups -asynchronous commands) are modeled similarly to multicycle
paths but with a Boolean value inserted (instead of X).
If no value is specified, a multi-cycle path delay of two destination clock cycles is
computed by default. You can override the default delay by substituting argument 'N' with
the required value.
% vcs -sdc=verify_clock_group:<N> <vcs options>
% vcs -sdc=verify_clock_group:2 <vcs options>
-sdc=verify_reset
This option exposes reset domain crossing bugs via X injection at all resettable flops. If
the destination does not reset at the same time (due to different reset or non resettable
register), this causes metastability at destination. By default, X injection happens for one
clock cycle of the source clock and can be controlled by substituting argument ‘N’ with the
required value.

The -sdc=verify_reset option adds the following options, as it is not
recommended to run verify_reset together with the FP/MCP/CG verification:
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:off
• -sdc=verify_false_path:off
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:off
The following warning message is reported:
Warning-[SDC-RESET-NYS] SDC verification with verify reset is
not yet supported
'SDC' command is getting ignored in presence of
-sdc=verify_reset
Limitations
With verify_reset, usage of verify_max_delay and dynamic_multi_clock compile-
time switches, like MCP/FP/CG is not recommended.
% vcs -sdc=verify_reset <vcs options>

-sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle
A multicycle path is specified when the path between sequential elements needs multiple
clock cycles, which would otherwise need a single cycle. Therefore, by default, the tool
expects the setup multiplier to be a number greater than 1. If a setup multiplier of 1 is
specified, by default, MCP analysis is not performed, and instead the following warning is
reported:
Warning-[MCP-SINGLE-CYCLE] MCP of single cycle
MCP command(test.sdc:3) has cycle multiplier of 1 and will be ignored
during analysis. Use -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle to turn on
MCP verification of single cycles.
To avoid this warning, -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle compile time
switch can be used.
%vcs -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle <vcs options>
-sdc=abort_no_sdc_path

-sdc=no_x
This option does not inject X or Boolean values in the MCP path. It only prints the violation
message of the MCP constraint in the simulation log. The simulation remains untouched
(without any X or delay insertion) and is similar to a plain VCS run. The verify_reset
checking (if turned on) remains active even with -sdc=no_x, that is, reset related X-
injection can still be observed.
%simv -sdc=no_x <vcs options>
-sdc=off
This option turns off all the SDC and verify_reset -related runtime checks. Therefore,
neither MCP constraint violations are printed nor X-injection happens.
%simv -sdc=off <vcs options>
-sdc=diag:path
This option gives a more detailed report of the active and violating paths. Details of the
SDC command considered, relevant line number in SDC file, hierarchical path of the
signal is mentioned. Snippet of output from this sub option is as follows:
set_multicycle_path (book_example.sdc:8) is ACTIVE & VIOLATING PATH
top.d.q1 => top.d.q4 is ACTIVE & VIOLATING
MCP path summary: considered 1, active 1, inactive 0, violating 1
%simv -sdc=diag:path <vcs options>
-sdc=random_delay
In this mode, delay between source and destination is randomly selected between 0 to
N(N= MCP delay specified in set_multicycle_path command) cycles. Correct value is

always available after N cycles. In case of an early capture, destination samples random
value if this runtime switch is specified.
%simv -sdc=random_delay <vcs options>
-sdc=sanity:sanitystarttime:<time>
This option defines the time after which the detection of clock sanity violations checks
kicks in, at runtime.
%simv -sdc=sanity:sanitystarttime:<time> <vcs options>
./simv -sdc=sanity:sanitystarttime:105ns <vcs options>
Here,the clock sanity checks start after 105 ns, and takes into consideration of stabilization
from 105 ns on wards. Any violations before this time are not considered, also no clock
stabilization logic kicks in before this time. All analysis takes place post 105ns.
-sdc=starttime:<time>
This option defines the time after which both EARLY CAPTURE violations and clock sanity
checks are tracked and reported.
%simv -sdc=starttime:<time> <vcs options>
./simv -sdc=starttime:274us <vcs options>
A violation initiated before this time is not detected. If both options are specified, then clock
sanity checks starts at sanity:sanitystarttime. Alternatively, early Capture Violation checks
can also be turned off and on via Verilog toggles or UCLI command.

-sdc=sanity:clock:margin:<percent>
This option defines the percentage margin beyond which the violations for period and
duty-cycle is thrown.
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:margin: <vcs options>
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:margin:20 <vcs options>
For example, if clock period is 100 in sdc and 115 in observed with a margin of 20,that is,
-sdc=sanity:clock:margin:20 there wont be a period violation.
sdc=sanity:clock:delaymargin:<time>
This option ignores and throws no error if there is a misalignment of time between master
versus generated clocks
%simv sdc=sanity:clock:delaymargin:<time> <vcs options>
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:delaymargin:1000fs <vcs options>
if the misalignment is >= 1000fs then only the clock timing alignment violation is reported.
-sdc=max_destination_violation:<N>
When you specify <N>in this option, the number of violations reported per destination stops
when the specified number of violations is reached (N)
%simv -sdc=max_destination_violation:<N> <vcs options>

-sdc=finish_max_violation:<N>
When you specify <N> in this option, simulation terminates after the specified number of
violations (global count) is reached. The default of N is 1000.
%simv -sdc=finish_max_violation:<N> <vcs options>
%simv -sdc=finish_max_violation:7 <vcs options>
-sdc=violation_prefix:<prefix>
This option adds <prefix> at the start of violation.
%simv -sdc=violation_prefix:<prefix> <vcs options>
%simv -sdc=violation_prefix:MCP_check <vcs options>
-sdc=noprint_violation
This option stops violation message printing
%simv -sdc=noprint_violation <vcs options>

-sdc=clockglitch:<N>
This option denotes percentage of clock period which is used for clock shifting delay. By
default, 10% delay is applied.
%simv -sdc=clockglitch:<N> <vcs options>
For -simv=clockglitch:10 <vcs options> , delay of 10% of the period is applied.
-sdc=sanity:clock:noexit
Although the SDC analysis terminates for paths with identified Clock period violation, with
this option SDC checks continues for other clocks with no clock period violation
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:noexit <vcs options>
At the point of encountering a clock period violation, all SDC checks are disabled.
Adding the following options overrides this behavior and continues the SDC checks. use
-sdc=sanity:clock:noexit to continue checks for other clocks.
-sdc=verify_reset:off
This option stops all the reset verification checks. All other runtime SDC checks proceed
as normal.
%simv -sdc=verify_reset:off <vcs options>
-sdc=dynamicfrequency
Without this option, all delay calculations are computed in the compile time and are
supposed to be the same even if the clocks related to these calculations are running
with a different clock period than what is specified in the SDC files. Any change in clock

period beyond the specified clock-margin would terminate the analysis for that clock. For
additional messages, this switch can be augmented with "diag" and "hi" options and can
be used as either -sdc=dynamicfrequency:diag or -sdc=dynamicfrequency:diag:hi.
Since clock periods are learnt dynamically, when this feature is enabled the clock-margin
grace argument (-sdc=sanity:clock:margin:n) is ignored.
%simv -sdc=dynamicfrequency <vcs options>
Sample messages relating to observed clock period change when dynamicfrequency
option is used during runtime:
SDC-WARN @ time 133 s : Clock period violation (due to change in
clock period) has been identified. All further SDC analysis related
to this clock: sys_clk except sanity:clock will be stopped.

SDC-LOG @ time 133 s : Clock period updated for clock:
testbench.mult.clk(sys_clk) (File:dynfreq_fs.sdc, Line:1) from 20 s
to 22 s

SDC-WARN @ time 155 s : Clock period within limits (due to clock
period stabilization). SDC analysis related to clock: sys_clk
started.
-sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:<N>
This option enables the reporting of Early Capture violations on the destination for the
same transition in input on successive N or S -1 clock cycles, whichever is smaller.
Here is N any number higher than 1, and S is the setup multiplier specified in the
set_multicycle_path command.
By default, the reporting count is limited to 1 for a given input transition that
causes a change in the destination within the violation window. This reporting
count can be increased using by setting N to any number higher than 1 in
-sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:<N>.
%simv -sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:<N> <vcs options>
set_multicycle_path -setup 5 -from ff1* -to ff2*

Here, by default, only single violation is reported for a given change in ff1 that causes ff2
to change within 5 cycles. However, if -sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:10 is used, then
Early Capture violations would be reported on consecutive cycles for 4 cycles for a given
change in ff1.
sanity:clock:noflop
Ensures that a sanity clock check is not performed by default, if this clock is not associated
with any flip-flops . You must mark this argument as true to conduct sanity clock checks
on clocks that have not experienced any flip-flops. The default of this clock is FALSE.
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:noflop <vcs options>
sanity:clock:higherfreq
Reports clock sanity errors only when the runtime detected clock frequency is higher
than the compile time SDC defined clock frequency. If the frequency is higher, the margin
calculations are done after this check. The default of this clock is OFF .
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:higherfreq <vcs options>
sanity:clock:period:nosdcoff
Ensures that after a few errors the SDC checks are disabled by default. Do not stop the
SDC checks just because period errors occur. The default of this clock is OFF.
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:period:nosdcoff <vcs options>
sanity:clock:off
Ensures that sanity clock check is not required. Dynamic and regular clock sanity is
disabled in RT.

%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:off <vcs options>
sanity:clock:stabilizecount
Whenever a clocks period changes in simulation the number of cycles of the clock period
is used to stabilize the new clock, during this time no SDC analysis is performed. The new
period is accepted only after this duration if the period is stable.
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:stabilizecount <vcs options>
dynamicfrequency:verbose
Enables the printing of period updates as well as delay value recalculation prints.
%simv -sdc=dynamicfrequency:verbose <vcs options>
-sdc=coverage:cmt
This option enables the comments from Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) commands
to be included in the exclusion file together with the coverage report for all SDC levels.
This allows you to quickly and effectively locate commands in the exclusion file.
%simv -sdc=coverage:cmt <vcs options>
Figure 2 SDC Command with Comments

evels.
This allows you to quickly and effectively locate commands in the exclusion file.
%simv -sdc=coverage:cmt <vcs options>
Figure 2 SDC Command with Comments

Figure 3 Exclusion File Generated with Comments
Figure 4 Coverage Report with Comments
-sdc=noprint_violation:<tag>
During simulation time, this option suppresses EARLY CAPTURE violation messages for
particular SDC kinds. Specify the SDC command type as an argument to this option.
-sdc=noprint_violation:mcp: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_multicycle_path commands.
-sdc=noprint_violation:fp: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_false_path commands.
-sdc=noprint_violation:cg: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_clock_group commands.
-sdc=noprint_violation:max_del: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for
set_max_delay commands.

-sdc=noprint_violation: This stops all EARLY CAPTURE violation printing.
-sdc=sanity:clock:higherfreq
hen this option is enabled, CLOCK PERIOD mismatch violations at runtime are triggered
only if the actual clock period is less than the value defined in the SDC. That is, the clock
is running at a higher frequency than specified.
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:higherfreq <vcs options>
-sdc=random_delay:uniform
This option enables random delay injection support for all the destination flop during SDC
validation. This ensures that random delays are inserted based on the path multiplier limit,
preventing masking of timing issues.
With uniform random delays, VCS-SDC can check a violation when the source changes
within the specified violation window and capture occurs on the destination side. It adjusts
the number of cycles for inserting x or bool values based on the maximum multiplier value
associated with the destination flop and remaining violation window.
%simv -sdc=random_delay:uniform <vcs options>
Consider the following compile time option:
% vcs -sdc=verify_false_path:N
Here, by default the value of N is 10.
In the following example, the FP constraint has "10" cycles of path multiplier limit and the
tool provides an equal weightage for 1,2,39 cycles (1->10-1) on the destination flip-flop.
Consider the following RTL:
//FP source flop
dff S2 (in, clk2, rst, ff3);
//FP destination flop
dff D2 (ff3, clk2, rst, ff4);

//FP destination flop
dff D2 (ff3, clk2, rst, ff4);

//FP destination flop
dff D2 (ff3, clk2, rst, ff4);

/FP destination flop
dff D2 (ff3, clk2, rst, ff4);
module dff (input [7:0] d, input clk, input rst, output reg [7:0] q);

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst)
if(!rst) q <= 0;
else q <= d;
Figure 5 False Path from S2 to D2
In the false path from S2 to D2, X- insertion occurs between 0 to 9 cycles randomly. At
runtime, during early capture event for a destination, the tool injects X for a specified
number of clock cycles (N). Let the remaining violation window for destination be W. This
number N is decided randomly between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W). Here, M is the
maximum multiplier value associated with the destination. The probability of selection of a
number between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W) is equal.

UNR Options
-unr=config.txt This switch invokes UNR flow which uses VC Formal Coverage
Analyzer under the hood to find unreachable coverage targets in
the design.
-unr=config.txt
This switch invokes UNR flow which uses VC Formal Coverage Analyzer under the hood
to find unreachable coverage targets in the design and saves them in an exclusion file
which can then be read with simulation coverage database to generate the final coverage
score. The configuration file sent with this switch helps to setup the Formal unreachability
analysis by providing the necessary options.
The following is the usage:
% vcs -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm -unr=config.txt <other_options>
% vcs -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm -unr=config.txt
For more details, refer to the Verification Continuum Guide to VCS Unreachability
Analysis.

Licensing Options
-licwait timeout Enables VCS to retry for a license until timeout expires, where
timeout is the time in minutes.
-licqueue /
+vcs+lic+wait
Tells VCS to try for the license till it finds the license.
VCS_LICENSE_WAIT You must set the VCS_LICENSE_WAIT variable to 1 and use the
-licqueue option, which enables the license queuing.
-licwait timeout
Enables license queuing, where timeout is the time in minutes that VCS waits for a
license before finally exiting.
% vcs -licwait timeout
% vcs -licwait 10 <other compile options>
Here, VCS waits for the license for 10 minutes.

Chapter 26: Licensing Options
-licqueue /+vcs+lic+wait
Tells VCS to try for the license till it finds the license. If there are multiple jobs asking for a
license, then any one of those jobs get the license (similar to the older or the deprecated
option +vcs+lic+wait).
% vcs -licqueue <other compile options> or % vcs +vcs+lic+wait
VCS_LICENSE_WAIT
You must set the VCS_LICENSE_WAIT variable to 1 and use the -licqueue option, which
enables the license queuing. Thus, the first job to enter the queue gets the license when
the license is available. This option must be used along with the -licqueue option.
% vcs VCS_LICENSE_WAIT
-licwait timeout Enables license queuing, where timeout is the time in minutes that
VCS waits for a license before finally exiting.
-licqueue /
+vcs+lic+wait
Tells VCS to wait for a network license if none is available.
VCS_LICENSE_WAIT You must set the VCS_LICENSE_WAIT variable to 1 and use the
-licqueue option, which enables the license queuing.
-licwait timeout
Enables license queuing, where timeout is the time in minutes that VCS waits for a
license before finally exiting.

Chapter 26: Licensing Options
% simv -licwait timeout
-licqueue / +vcs+lic+wait
Tells VCS to try for the license till it finds the license. If there are multiple jobs asking for a
license, then any one of those jobs get the license (similar to the older or the deprecated
option +vcs+lic+wait).
% simv -licqueue or % simv +vcs+lic+wait
VCS_LICENSE_WAIT
You must set the VCS_LICENSE_WAIT variable to 1 and use the -licqueue option, which
enables the license queuing. Thus, the first job to enter the queue gets the license when
the license is available. This option must be used along with the -licqueue option.
setenv VCS_LICENSE_WAIT 1
simv -licqueue <simv options>

RACE Options
-race Enables dynamic race detection (read-write races, write-write
races) for the entire design.
-racecd Enables race detection for the part of your design that is enclosed
between the ‘race and ‘endrace compiler directives.
+race=all Enables the static race detection tool.
-hsopt=racedetect Enables detection of clock-data races during simulation.
-race

% vcs test.v -race

Preface
This document describes all the Error, Warning, and Note messages that are associated
with the VCS tool. The preface discusses the following:
• Customer Support

Customer Support
Customer support is available through SolvNetPlus.
Accessing SolvNetPlus
The SolvNetPlus site includes a knowledge base of technical articles and answers to
frequently asked questions about Synopsys tools. The SolvNetPlus site also gives you
access to a wide range of Synopsys online services including software downloads,
documentation, and technical support.
To access the SolvNetPlus site, go to the following address:
https://solvnetplus.synopsys.com
If prompted, enter your user name and password. If you do not have a Synopsys user
name and password, follow the instructions to sign up for an account.
If you need help using the SolvNetPlus site, click REGISTRATION HELP in the top-right
menu bar.
Contacting Customer Support
To contact Customer Support, go to https://solvnetplus.synopsys.com.
Synopsys Statement on Inclusivity and Diversity
Synopsys is committed to creating an inclusive environment where every employee,
customer, and partner feels welcomed. We are reviewing and removing exclusionary
language from our products and supporting customer-facing collateral. Our effort also
includes internal initiatives to remove biased language from our engineering and working
environment, including terms that are embedded in our software and IPs. At the same
time, we are working to ensure that our web content and software applications are usable
to people of varying abilities. You may still find examples of non-inclusive language in our

software or documentation as our IPs implement industry-standard specifications that are
currently under review to remove exclusionary language.

This warning occurs when the $sdf_annotate system task successfully resolves the
specified XMR (cross-module reference) and aligns its path to the digital RTVS view.

Redundant use_spice command

command for this cell in the default configuration.

Read and write debug capabilities enabled in RTVS flow
VCS automatically enables the read and write debug capabilities since they are required in
RTVS flow.
You can avoid this warning by enabling these capabilities with the -debug_access+r+w
+wn option or another appropriate method.

from the VCS command line.
MSV-RTVS-XMR-TID
Cannot replicate RTVS xmr in digital instance hierarchy
The XMR '%s' points to an object within the hierarchy of the RTVS Spice instance '%s'.
However, the object cannot be located in the corresponding digital RTVS hierarchy due to
the absence of target node '%s' in module '%s'. When the RTVS XMR rewrite is enabled
and an XMR points to an object in the RTVS Spice hierarchy, it is required that the object
exist in the corresponding digital RTVS instance hierarchy.
To address this issue, rectify the XMR problem or disable the RTVS XMR rewrite feature.
You can disable RTVS XMR rewrite by removing '-adopt rtvs_xmr' from the VCS command
line or by adding the V2K attribute 'SNPS_NO_RTVS_XMR_REWRITE' to the relevant
statement or its enclosing scope.

UXMRBB
Unresolved hierarchical reference due to black box
The hierarchical reference '%s' cannot be resolved because token '%s' refer to non-port or
non-parameter item of black box.
VCF_NONEED_COMPILE
Recompilation checking success
There is no need to recompile the design.
If you want to recompile the design, set app variable enable_incremental_compile to
false.
VCM-ARCMV
Multiple variants are not supported

FSM arc coverage has been enabled with -cm_fsmopt arc, but the module '%s' has
multiple shape variants in the design. Currently
VCM-ARCNI
Could not monitor arcs
VCS found at least one state assignment for FSM '%s' in module '%s' that could not be
monitored for arc coverage. Some constructs such as ternary expressions and state
assignments in procedural loops and in functions are not supported for arc coverage.
This FSM is only monitored for states and transitions.
VCM-ARCSM
Could not monitor arc in submodule
The FSM '%s' has at least one state assignment in a submodule of module '%s'. FSMs
with state assignments in submodules are not supported for arc coverage.
This FSM is only monitored for states and transitions.
VCM-MAOL
Multiple arcs on the same line

VCS detected multiple possible 'from' states for the arc assignment on line %s for the FSM
\"%s\".
VCS_PARAL
Parallel code-gen is enabled
VCS is running with parallel code generation(-j).
XP_FAUTO
Xprop is presumably to be with fauto
The default lifetime (static) of function %s is converted to automatic at analysis phase.
ZEMI-DPI-STREAMING
Import DPI inferred as streaming DPI
Import DPI %s in module %s which was initially non-streaming, has been inferred as
streaming DPI due to the use of UTF option zemi3 -enforce_streaming true.

CNST-AAEU
Constraint assoc array exists() error
The associative array exists() method in constraints with keys longer than 64 bits is
Ensure that the key length is equal or less than 64 bits.

Constraint array index cyclic unsolvable error

The solver does not solve for the array '%s' indexed by the random variable '%s'.
The solving of the random index is dependent on the random array itself.
CNST-AID
Array in distribution
The variable '%s' is an array and arrays are not yet supported as a distribution item.
CNST-AIVE
Constraint array index value error
The rand_mode() is called with an index that contains X/Z of an array '%s'.
Avoid using ambiguous/unknown/no value as an array index.
CNST-AMME
Constraint array member missing error

The array member %s does not exist.
Check whether the array index is valid.
CNST-AOE
Constraint array oversize error
The array %s.size() has value %s. Enough memory could not be allocated for it.
Consider modifying the a .size() constraint on the array %s.
CNST-AZSE
Constraint array zero size error
The array %s has the size 0. The array aggregate function %s() is not defined when the
array has size zero.
Ensure that the array %s is not empty when the aggregate function %s() is called.

URG-FMM-CTDNP
Compile Time Data Not Provided
No compile-time data was found in any specified VDB directory, but compile-time data is
required for '%s'.
Ensure that at least one database contains compile time data.
URG-GCGNS
The %s grading option is not supported with path coverage.
You can use a different grading algorithm by omitting the '%s' suboption from the -grade
flag. Alternatively, you can use the %s option on just the supported metrics by using the
-metric <line+tgl+fsm+cond+branch> flag. For example, if your database has line,
cond, and path coverage, you can grade the line and condition the data by using only the
-metric line+cond flag.
URG-GIMX

The indexlimit grading option can only be used when index grading is selected first.
URG-GIRT
The rarethreshold grading option can only be used when score grading is selected first.
URG-GLF
Test load failed
You specified the '-grade' option to URG, but grading failed: %s.
The test may have been corrupted. Try regenerating it. If the problem still persists, contact
URG-GRCOL-LCA

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
The 'columns' grading feature in URG is a Limited Customer Availability (LCA) feature and
is not enabled by default.
You can enable use of the 'columns' flag by adding the '-lca' option on the URG command
line.
URG-GRSCI
Incompatible options
The -grade %s grading algorithm cannot be used with the scores grading suboption. The
scores suboption is supported only with index, greedy, and cost-based grading.
URG-GRTM
Conflicting limits
You specified a rare threshold of %s and an index limit of %s, but the index limit must be
greater than the rare threshold. Otherwise, every object is counted as rare.
Use an index limit greater than the rare threshold. If you do not specify an index limit, URG
automatically uses an index limit greater than the specified rare threshold.
URG-GRUR
Combination not supported

You specifed both the rarecounts and %s flags to urg -grade, but these options cannot be
used together.
URG-GSID-LCA
URG HVP '-group show_in_design' is a Limited Customer Availability (LCA) feature and is
not enabled by default.
Enable LCA by adding the '-lca' option to the URG command line.
URG-HCF-LCA
The HVP compressed feature in URG is a Limited Customer Availability (LCA) feature and
is not enabled by default.
You can enable use of the feature by adding the '-lca' option on the URG command line.

URG-HVP-CFO
Conflict options
The '%s' option is not supported with %s.
Use only one of them. Refer to the URG user guide for more information.
URG-IDF
Obsolete coverage database format
The coverage database found in '%s' is in the olddb format. This format is deprecated and
Regenerate the database in the newdb format.
URG-IOER
File I/O Error
Cannot %s the data file %s (Reason: %s).

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Check for the write permission on the file or check the disk quota.
URG-LCA-FEATURE
URG option '%s' is a Limited Customer Availability (LCA) feature and is not enabled by
default.
Enable LCA by adding the '-lca' option to the URG command line.
URG-LTFF
Load test failed
A fatal error occurred while loading the test '%s', and URG has to exit.
URG-MIDR
Input database required
The merging mapped modules coverage requires the input database.

Specify both the base database and input database with the '-map' or '-mapfile' option.
URG-MINC
Incompatible algorithm
URG's -grade %s algorithm cannot be used on a merged test, but the test '%s' is the result
of merging with 'urg -dbname'.
URG-MO
Missing options
The '%s' option works with %s.
%s. Refer to the URG user guide for more information.
URG-MVOT
Multiple VDBs or Tests

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
The '-modtreefile' option is supported only on a compiled VDB with a single test in it, or on
a merged VDB.
To report the coverage of multiple tests using the '-modtreefile' option, you need to merge
their VDBs.
URG-NF
Executable not found
The %s executable was not found in %s.
Check that your installation process was successful and that the install area has not been
URG-NO-COST
Tests do not have requested cost
Cost-based grading based on %s was selected, but none of the tests to be graded had %s
measured for them.
URG-NOC
Cannot combine VDBs

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
The VDB directories %s and %s cannot be combined with the -combine flag %s.
URG-NOCN
Wrong number of VDB specified
The -combine switch requires exactly two VDB directories to work, but you specified %s.
URG-NTFD
No test found for the base design
URG could not find any test associated with the base design directory '%s'. So the input
coverage data cannot be mapped.
Add test directories after the base design directory and try again.

Not yet implemented for NEWDB

text:

Either remove the option from URG command line or switch to the old coverage database
URG-PAR-ARG
URG Arguments for Parallel Mode
Argument '%s' is only used in URG parallel mode.
Add '-parallel' argument or run 'urg -parallel -help' for information.
URG-PAR-CFO
Conflict options
The options %s will cause conflict.
Use one of them or set correct value for these options.
URG-PAR-CMDLL
Command line too long

The command line specified is too long for urg -parallel mode (%s characters).
URG-PAR-ENV
Submit command failed
Failed to run the submit command '%s'. The %s environment is not configured properly.
Check your %s settings.
URG-PAR-ENVVCS
Environment variable required
The VCS_HOME or VERA_HOME environment variable is not set.
Set the environment variable then try again.
URG-PAR-FC
Farm System Check Error

URG parallel does a quick check of the designated farm system before starting. In this
case the check had still not finished after ten seconds.
If you believe nothing is wrong, you can use the '-nocheck' option to skip this check.
URG-PAR-FOE
Open file failed
The file '%s' could not be opened: %s.
URG-PAR-ICO
Incompatible options
Only one of the -lsf, -grid or <mfile> options can be specified for a single urg -parallel run.
Use only one of the above options and try again.
URG-PAR-ICP
Incompatible options

The option '%s' cannot be used together with '-parallel'.
Run 'urg -parallel -help' to see the complete list of options that are supported in parallel
mode.
URG-PAR-INT
No merged database
URG could not find the final merged database at %s.
This could be due to errors reported previously during the merge.
URG-PAR-INV
Invalid options
The option '%s' could only be specified with the '-lsf' or '-grid' option.
Run 'urg -parallel -help' for information.

URG-PAR-IOP
Invalid options
The option '%s' could only be specified with the '%s' option.
Run 'urg -parallel -help' for information.
URG-PAR-LSF
Unsupported combination of switches
The '%s' switch can only be used when the '%s' switch is given.
It is not supported in other modes.
URG-PAR-MSA
Missing argument
The '%s' switch requires a %ssubargument.

%s
URG-PAR-NAM
No available machine
None of the machines listed in the machine list file '%s' could be used.
Check that the machine names are given correctly and that you have permission to rsh to
them.
URG-PAR-PNV
Incorrect numeric argument
The '%s' option requires a non-negative numeric argument to specify the number of
seconds to wait between checking the LSF grid (or 0 to disable it) but you specified '%s'.
Use a valid value.
URG-PAR-RF
Parallel URG failed in the final step

While URG was able to merge the specified VDBs, an error occurred during the final step
while generating the %s.
A file named %s/urg_parallel_error.log has been generated that contains more
information about the failure.
URG-PAR-SCF
Command failure
URG encountered an error %s. The command '%s' %s
Contact vcs_support@synopsys.com for help understanding the error.
URG-PAR-SKF
Sub-job missing from LSF farm
The final merge job submitted to the LSF farm for urg -parallel never completed, and no
more jobs are running on the LSF farm.
URG-PAR-SUB
Sub job failure

An error has occurred in a sub-job started by the URG parallel merging feature.
Refer to the later mentioned log.
URG-PAR-VERSION
URG version not found
Cannot find URG version by running 'urg -id'.
Check your URG setup and try again.
URG-PAR-WR
Missing argument
Argument '%s' should be specified for the option '%s'.
Run 'urg -parallel -help' for information.

URG-PATH-LCA
The path coverage in URG is a Limited Customer Availability (LCA) feature and is not
enabled by default.
You can enable the path coverage by adding the -lca option on the URG command line.
You can disable it by explicitly listing all metrics except path coverage as an argument to
the -metric option.
URG-PERM
Cannot execute
The %s executable was found at %s but it is not executable.
Check the permissions.
URG-PFBF
Project File Bad Format

Unable to process project file: %s
URG-PFLE
Project File Load Error
Unable to load project file: %s
URG-PGR-LCA
The Plan-Grading feature in URG is a Limited Customer Availability (LCA) feature and is
not enabled by default.
You can enable use of the feature by adding the '-lca' option on the URG command line.
URG-RCE
Reset Coverage error
Option '-dbname' is mandatory with '-reset_coverage' option.

Provide the option '-dbname' followed by a database name to exercise '-reset_coverage'.
URG-TNVE
No entry
None of the -tests files contain any entry.
Ensure that the -tests files contain valid test entries separated by newline.
URG-UNVM
Test load failed
Grading cannot proceed: %s
This can happen if you try to grade tests.
URG-USM
UnSupported metric

The metric '%s' is not supported with the option %s.
Supported metrics are: %s. Run urg -help for information.
URG-UVP
Unsupported VDB Provided
The VDB provided cannot be used with -show_summary.
Create a merged vdb with -dbname and provide it with -show_summary.
URG-WAG
Invalid argument for option
The first item '%s' given to the -warn option is not recognized as a valid usage.
To suppress the list of warning IDs, use -warn no<ID>,,no<ID>. To suppress all
warnings, use -warn none. To suppress all warnings with a few exceptions, use -warn
none,<ID>,,<ID>.
URG-WAII
Invalid message ID

The %s ID '%s' given to the %s option is invalid.
Ensure that you are using the correct %s ID.
URG-WAMI
Missing message ID
The %s ID is missing after the keyword 'no'.
Add the %s ID you want to %s after the keyword 'no'.
URG-WANO
Missing keyword 'no'
The item '%s' you are trying to suppress does not begin with the keyword 'no'.
Add the keyword 'no' before the %s ID you want to suppress.

URG-WIU
Invalid option usage
The '%s' option does not allow the usage of suppressing a list of %s IDs and suppressing
all %ss (with a list of exceptions) at the same time.

One-hot state too large
State \"%s\" was specified for FSM \"%s\" in module \"%s\" (file %s, line %s) in the

brackets []. But its value is greater than that can be contained in a 64-bit signal, and
therefore cannot be a one-hot FSM state. Values this large cannot be one-hot states. This
FSM will not be monitored.

%s, %s.

State name \"%s\" specified for FSM \"%s\" in module \"%s\" (file %s, line %s) in the

This FSM will not be monitored.
VCM-FSMLTA
Illegal sub-option for -cm_fsm_limit

The -cm_fsm_limit allows you to specify a +-separated list of these suboptions to control
FSM extraction.
VCM-FSMPVRG
Parameter value used for FSM changed
The parameter \"%s\" was used to define a value range in the code for FSM \"%s\" in
an 'inside' expression, but that value is different in different instances of the module (%s
%s in instance %s vs. %s%s in others). Ranges are enabled for SystemVerilog by the
-cm_fsmopt rangestates option. This allows VCS to extract FSMs based on these
ranges, but if parameters are used for the endpoints of ranges and those parameter
values are overridden, incorrect or incomplete results may occur.
VCM-INCOPT
Incompatible Options
The %s and %s options cannot be used together as they are mutually exclusive.
VCM-IRIS-CIERR
IRIS Internal Error

An error has occurred because IRIS optimization was detected in the coverage flow, but
the -Xkeyopt=iris+coverage option was not explicitly specified at compile time. To
enable this optimization feature, use the -Xkeyopt=iris+coverage compile-time option.

The value of a module or an instance in the \'%s\' call is illegal.
See your design to find out valid instance names. It is recommended to use the module
identifier (or name) of a module or the hierarchical name of a module instance enclosed in
quotation marks as a valid value for this argument. If the \'%s\' task does not exist in the
source file, then contact vcs_support@synopsys.com.
MON-RTOPTIGN-LINE
Runtime option ignored.
The '-cm_line %s' option was given on the command line, but has no effect. Line coverage
suboptions controlled by -cm_line can be specified at compile time only.
If the option was already specified in compile time, there is no need to specify it again at
runtime.

MSVR-CFG-UNKNOWN-W
Unknown value in config
Unknown value '%s' was found at %s in the config file '%s'.
Skipping this tag now. Provide a valid value.
NENVF
Variable Undefined
Undefined environment variable '${%s}' \nin file '%s' \nat line '%s'.
Set the environment variable and re-run.
NO-VHDL-COV-WITH-VHDL-RUNTIME-GENERICS
No vhdl coverage with runtime generics
VHDL generic assignments at runtime can change the number of coverable objects of a
VHDL component instantiation. For example, a change in the width of a signal can change
the number of bits for toggle coverage, can change the number of conditions for condition

coverage, and so on. This might lead to different number of VHDL compile time and
runtime coverable objects and wrong results. VCS currently does not support coverage for
this use-model and skips the monitoring of VHDL coverage.
To monitor VHDL coverage, avoid the generic assignments at runtime and do the generic
assignments at elaboration time.
OLTL
Object list is too long
Object list is too long, linker may have trouble taking it.
Try adding the -Marchive option for vcs or scs.
PC-INVLINE
Invalid line in partition file.
The warning occurs as an empty line is detected.
It is recommended to ensure that there are no empty lines in the partition file.

Coverage Option Ignored

VCM-PCPI
Path Coverage performance impact
The switch \"-cm path\" can impact performance when enabled on entire design. Enable
path coverage for only selected modules or hierarchies using the -cm_hier <hier_config>.

VCM-REDOPWIDTH
Reduction operator operand too wide.

Using the redops condition coverage mode, the number of columns for the truth table
would be %s. To make the coverage report readable, VCS will monitor each bit of the
expression separately. The limit for the width of the operand for reduction operator is 1024.
There is no way to change this upper limit.
VCM-TRIMVEC
Too many vectors in condition coverage
Using the full/allops condition coverage mode, the number of vectors for the above
expression would be %s. To avoid significant simulation slowdown, VCS has an upper limit
of %s vectors per condition. Therefore, only the first %s vectors(in the truth table order)
will be monitored and reported for this condition. There is no way to change this upper
limit.

AST-MAXC
Number of hits on assertion exceeds limit

One or more assertions has a hit count that exceeds the maximum value supported in
reports. The affected assertions are shown in the report with a \"*\" character next to the
counts.
CCT_NRBIN_CHG
Non-random sample bin changed
The sampled bin of the non random coverpoint '%s' in covergroup '%s', which is part of
cross, has changed from '%s' to '%s'. This might lead to reduced effectiveness for cross
coverage hole targeting.
Check if the change in the bin of the non random coverpoint '%s' is intentional.
CG-MAXC
Number of hits on covergroup bin exceeds limit
One or more covergroup has a bin hit count that exceeds the maximum value supported in
reports. The affected covergroup bins are shown in the report with a \"*\" character next to
the counts.
CM-FSMPST
Parameter states with equal values merged

The FSM \"%s\" in module \"%s\" has two parameter states, \"%s\" and \"%s\", that have
the same value (%s) in instance \"%s\".
These two states are combined into a single state, reducing the number of states in the
FSM. The name \"%s\" is used for this value in coverage reporting. Any transitions to or
from state \"%s\" are reported as transitions for \"%s\" instead.

UCAPI-DIAG
UCAPI Diagnostic message
UCAPI Diagnostic Message for optimization : %s

UCAPI-HEX-BINNAME-OLDVDB
Hexadecimal bin names on old vdb requested
Generating hexadecimal bin names for user-defined array bins is not supported in older
VDBs.
UCAPI-INSMIS
Instance mismatch in input vdb
Instance '%s' in the input vdb '%s' is defined by module '%s', but it is defined by a different
module '%s' in the base vdb.
The instance in the input vdb is renamed to '%s' in the merged results.
UCAPI-MMSTU
Merge mode set to union
Default merging is not supported on union merged databases.
Continuing the merging in flex union mode.
UCAPI-NDI
No design information

The coverage databases loaded does not contain any design information, so the %s
relation from %s handle cannot be used.
UCAPI-NTCO
No Tests Covered Object
Specifying -trimtestrecords in the URG command line instructs URG to discard test
records for tests that are not included in any object's test correlation list.
UCAPI-OTRF
Only One Test Record Found
When there is only one test record in a VDB, the -trimtestrecords flag has no effect.
UCAPI-RCGLTCH
A Probable Coverage Glitch
Unreachable objects might have been covered due to a possible race condition in the
design. Compiling the design with -cm_glitch 0 might help to resolve it.

UCAPI-SLFT
Skipped Loading Failed Test
The coverage data from the '%s' test is not used, as its status is '%s' and the
-skip_failed_test option is used.
The test result status is set with the cm_post command or the $cm_post system call.
UCAPI-STTO
Show Tests Turned ON
-trimtestrecords is automatically turned on -show tests.
UCAPI-TRM-DIAG
Design Mismatch Reporting Enabled
The \"-diag tglmerge\" option is available along with the \"-flex_merge tgl\"
option to report mismatch between base and input designs.
UCAPI-TRM-DIAGREPEX
Mismatch Report Capacity Exceeded

Mismatch report exceeded its capacity. Therefore, Some portion of the report is truncated.
UCAPI-UMGUNS
Union merge of simulation vdb
You are attempting to union-merge data from '%s', which is a simulation-only vdb directory.
Union merge for code coverage is only supported for compiled or merged vdbs.
Coverage data from this vdb is merged with the default merge rule. Design data from '%s'
is used here.
UCAPI-UNINST
New module instance seen in input vdb
Instance name '%s' in the input vdb '%s' is not found in base design. Since union merging
is enabled it gets added to the merged result.
If you do not want to add regions from the input vdb, do not use the union merge option
on the URG command line.
UCAPI-UNIONADV
Exclusion of union member signal

Exclusion entry %s in exclusion file %s at line number %s is marked compile-time
excluded due to the usage of -cm_tgl union_adv option.
This signal cannot be excluded. if the -cm_tgl union_excl option has been used. The
tool automatically excludes corresponding bits of the top level union. You must review.
UCAPI-UNOBJ
New object seen in input vdb
%s, %s instance '%s' in the input vdb '%s' there is a '%s' at this location that does not exist
in the base vdb
Because union merge is specified, the objects are included in the merged vdb and the
generated report.
UCAPI-UNOBJGN
New generate iteration seen in input vdb
%s, %s instance '%s' in the input vdb '%s' there is a '%s' for a for-generate loop iteration
'%s' that does not exist in the base vdb. Because, union merge is specified, the objects
in this additional generate loop iteration is included in the merged vdb and the report is
generated.

The directory '%s' passed to the URG command line was generated from a 64-bit
simulation kernel, so URG automatically runs in 64-bit mode.

No Echo bias file has been generated as all holes have been targeted. The holes with

Signal \"%s\" is compared to a zero value in the code, which normally would disqualify it
from being a one-hot FSM, but since the -cm_fsmopt allowZeroChecks flag was given
on the VCS command line, VCS still considers it.
If you don't want one-hot FSMs that are compared to zero to be extracted as one-hot
FSMs, don't use this option.
VCM-FSMZCMP
Signal \"%s\" was rejected as an FSM because it looks like a one-hot FSM but VCS found
a comparison to zero as if zero were a legal state.
If this comparison to zero is an error check or you otherwise want to allow \"%s\" to be a
one-hot FSM, you can use the -cm_fsmopt allowZeroChecks flag on the VCS command
line.
VCM-FSMZEQC
FSM not one hot

Signal \"%s\" is not considered as a one-hot FSM because VCS found a comparison to
zero as if zero were a legal state.
VCM-FSMZVAL
Ignoring state for one-hot FSM
The state \"%s\" with value 0 is assigned to the fan-in of signal \"%s\", which might be a
one-hot FSM.
VCM-NAVP
Unable to monitor arc coverage in instance
VCS was unable to retrieve arc coverage information in the module instance %s. Arc
coverage for this instance is reported as 0%.
Not all modes are supported for arc coverage. See the VCS Coverage User Guide for
more information.
VCM-NCLMTR
Constant analysis limit reached
The sub hierarchy rooted at instance %s has been iterated over %s times for noconst
analysis, which is the limit you specified with the -cm_noconst_limit option. No further

noconst analysis is done for this sub hierarchy even though it's possible additional
unreachable coverage targets could be identified.
You can change the value passed to -cm_noconst_limit to raise or lower this limit.
Raising the limit increases compile time.
VCM-NCSTPF
Constant analysis performance
During processing for the %s flag, VCS has detected %s.
This could cause significant compile-time overhead.
VCM-NOCLMT
Constant analysis limit set
The -cm_noconst_limit flag was used to set the limit to %s.%s
Setting this limit potentially reduces the time spent analyzing the design for unreachable
coverage objects, which may improve compile time, but could result in fewer unreachables
being identified. The lower the limit value, the more restricted the unreachables analysis
will be.

Skipping Encrypted Hierarchies

Some modules are encrypted (partially or fully) and therefore, VCS does not monitor all
the instance hierarchies of the design for coverage%s
%s%s

Cannot analyze signal for constants
Coverage constant analysis cannot analyze the signal \"%s\" because it is an output port
of child instance %s but is being assigned.
VCM-NODRIP
Cannot analyze signal for constants
Coverage constant analysis cannot analyze the signal \"%s\" because it is an input port
but is being assigned.

Design hierarchy will not be reported

You have specified the -cm_instr nohierarchy flag. As a result, only the modules and
instances specified in the cm_hier file are shown in reports, and no design hierarchy is
reported.

Unsupported config file entry

The option will be ignored. This option will be deprecated in subsequent releases.

There are SPICE modules, such as %s, in the design. Therefore, code coverage may not
work correctly for such designs.

The -cm_tgl_unpacked_limit 10000 switch improves performance by removing nodes

Bounds of expression cannot be extracted
VCS can attempt to identify part-select FSMs for coverage when the bounds are locally
static or simple expressions using globally static values, such as generics and generate
variables. But the bounds for the expression \"%s\" or the bounds of the signal \"%s\" are
too complex for FSM identification to be done reliably.
This expression and similar slice/index expressions with complex indexes are not
considered for FSM extraction.

$dumpports is not supported in precompiled hierarchy flow.

$dumpvars is not supported in precompiled hierarchy flow.
Contact vcs_support@synopsys.com for further assistance.
EMPTY_TABF
Empty PLI Learn tab file.
The PLI learn tab file '%s' is empty or contains only comments.

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Check how this PLI Learn tab file is created.
EVCD-PROTECTED-PORT
Protected ports.
The design unit '%s' has protected ports for primary IO pins.
The EVCD dumping is not supported for protected ports.
EVCD-REGISTER-CB
Extended Value Change Dump callback registration failed.
Callback registration on '%s' failed. %s.
The EVCD dumping on loads of this signal is incorrect.
EVCD-USDU
Unsupported SystemC design unit.

Design unit '%s' is a SystemC instance. EVCD dumping for SystemC instance is not
EXECTF-NODBG
Not enough debug caps to call TF.
The design is not compiled with enough debug capability to enable calling Verilog tasks
and functions.
Recompile with '-debug', '-debug_all' or '-debug_access+r'.
FGP_UNSUPP_FEATURE
Unsupported feature for -fgp.
'%s' is not supported in -fgp flow. Simulation runs in serial mode.
FRCLST_DTL_OBJ
Dynamic Test Loading forces not printed.

Forces in the Dynamic Test Loading (DTL) object is not printed to the force list file.
FRCLST_NEED_TRDCAP
Missing debug caps for force list.
-force_list=uniqueID, stack needs thread debug capability.
Recompile with -debug_access+thread.
FRCLST_REM_EXISTF
Failed to remove an existing file.
Unable to remove an existing file \"%s\" needed by -force_list output generation ,
cause: \"%s\".
This file is either the user specified output file or an internal file used to create the output
file.
FRCLST_REM_INTF
Failed to remove an internal file.

Unable to remove an internal file \"%s\" during -force_list output file creation, cause:
\"%s\".
This is a problem on subsequent -force_list runs, if the file cannot be removed.
FS-NOT-EFFECTIVE
Fast search not effective
VCS has been called with the option '%s', however, without any debug option. Fast search
can only be effective if a debug option is also passed to VCS.
Call VCS again with a debug option such as -debug_access+all.
FSDB_MAX_FILES
Max FSDB files already open.
You are requesting to open an FSDB file but the maximum number (32) of opened FSDB
files has already been reached.
FSDBON_REG
Unrecognized '+vcs+fsdbon' option.

Option '%s' is not a valid '+vcs+fsdbon' option.
The option is ignored.
FSDBON_REG0
Unrecognized '+vcs+fsdbon' syntax.
The syntax is +vcs+fsdbon+level, path.
The option is ignored.
FSDBON_REG_NOTUSE
Illegal '+vcs+fsdbon' usage.
The option '%s' cannot be used when option '-debug_region+%s' is specified. The
option is ignored.
HDLXMR-INVALID-PATH
$hdl_xmr hierarchy path invalid

The path %s is invalid and cannot be resolved.
Correct the path otherwise the $hdl_xmr connection fails at runtime.
HXDOGN
Hdl_xmr: vpiOrigin could not be found
Destination signal '%s' could not be found in the design. Therefore the connection with its
source signal is not established.
Use VCS option -debug=2 to find destination signal. Refer to VCS User Guide for detailed
HXDOGN-NL
Hdl_xmr: vpiOrigin could not be found
%s Destination signal '%s' could not be found in the design. Therefore the connection with
its source signal is not established.

Use VCS option -debug=2 to find destination signal. Refer to VCS User Guide for detailed
information. (Use -debug_access+all compile option if you would like to get the line
number of hdl_xmr call)
HXDS-AV
Hdl_xmr: Destination signal is automatic variable
Automatic variable '%s' is used as a destination signal in hdl_xmr. A hdl_xmr connection
to an automatic variable is not supported. Therefore the connection between the two
signals is not established.
Use a valid destination signal in Verilog/VHDL.
HXDS-WR
Hdl_xmr: Destination signal wreal
Wreal node '%s' is used as destination signal in hdl_xmr. hdl_xmr destination to a
wreal node is not supported. Therefore the connection between the two signals is not
established.
Use a valid destination signal in Verilog/VHDL. Wreal node can only be used as source
signal or can be forced with hdl_xmr_force.

HXDTI
Hdl_xmr_force: Force type invalid.
The force type '%s' used on the signal '%s' (VHDL variable) is invalid.
Only deposit is valid for VHDL variable, so deposit is applied instead.
HXDTI-NL
Hdl_xmr_force: Force type invalid
%s The force type '%s' used on the signal '%s' (VHDL variable) is invalid.
Only deposit is valid for VHDL variable, so deposit is applied instead. (use '-
debug_access+all' compile option if you would like to get the line number of 'hdl_xmr'
call.)
HXISS-NODBG
Hdl_Xmr: No debugcaps on signal for GENIP

The signal '%s' is declared in '%s' IP that is not compiled with debug. Recompile that IP
with at least read/write capability.
HXISS-NODBG-NL
Hdl_Xmr: No debugcaps on signal for GENIP
The signal '%s' is declared in '%s' IP that is not compiled with debug. Recompile that IP
with at least read/write capability.
HXMCV
Hdl_xmr: Missing callback capability.
Source signal '%s' (VHDL variable) does not have callback capabilities therefore, the
connection with its destination signal is not established.
Recompile the design with '-debug_all' or '-debug_acc+all'.
HXMCV-NL
Hdl_xmr: Missing callback capability

%s Source signal '%s'(VHDL variable) does not have callback capabilities. Therefore the
connection with its destination signal is not established.
Recompile the design with -debug_all or -debug_acc+all. Refer to VCS User Guide for
details. (Use '-debug_access+all' compile option if you would like to get the line number of
hdl_xmr call.)

Recompile the partition with appropriate capability. Refer to VCS User Guide for detailed

ICOS
Illegal combination of switch
Both sv_package_opt switch and dump_unused_packages switch are provided. Switch
sv_package_opt overrides dump_unused_packages.%s
ICSQA-W
Incompatible queue assignment
Incompatible queue in assignment pattern. %s
ILLEGAL_VLOG_MEM_FORMAT
Error in reading mem file.

The Verilog format mem file '%s' do not match Vlog LRM.
Check the file format, it should have illegal characters other than digits and @.
INTFDV
VCD dumping of interface or program or package.
Selective VCD dumping of %s '%s' is not supported. Selective VCD dumping for
interfaces, packages and programs is not supported.
Use full VCD dumping '$dumpvars(0)', or use VPD or FSDB dumping, recompile with '-
debug_access'.
IRTVIR_DUMP_DPR
Deprecated -irtvir_dump option
The -irtvir_dump option is deprecated.
LOG-BAD-LEVELS
Invalid value for class levels

The class levels argument #%s \"%s\" should be greater than or equal to -1. A value of -1
is assumed.
Use one of the values below: 0 for stack only, no local or class variables -1 for stack, local
variables, and all class and extended (super) class variables N>0 for stack, local variables,
class variables, and N-1 levels of extended (super) class variables.
LOG-VALUE-OVRFLW
Record size is too large
The combined values of the objects being dumped with this $vcdplusmsglog call is too
large to be recorded with one call. The variable \"%s\" is not dumped.
Break this call into multiple calls or remove variables with large values.
MEM_WORD_TOO_LONG
Error when reading mem file.
Data '%s' is too long for word.
Check the file format.

MSGLOG-LARGE_STR
Msglog string too large.
Msglog string length (%s) is too large to store in VPD file.
Only the first %s characters are stored in the VPD file.
MSGLOG-NODBG
$vcdplusmsglog task call without debug.
The design was not compiled with any of the -debug_pp/-debug/-debug_all/-
debug_access options. The $vcdplusmsglog calls require one of these debug options to
work correctly. All $vcdplusmsglog calls in this design are ignored.
MSV-AEF-NCE
Bad argument to analog event function.
The '%s' argument of the analog event function '%s' has been passed with a non-constant
expression '%s'.

MSV-ATBAD
Bad ams_tunnel statement.
There is an ams_tunnel statement at line %s in the config file '%s'.
It refers to signals '%s' and '%s' within a module named '%s'.
MSV-ATMODNF
Module in ams_tunnel statement not found.
There is an ams_tunnel statement at line %s in config file '%s'. This statement refers to
'%s' as a module. However, no module named '%s' is found in the design. Because of this
problem this ams_tunnel statement is ignored.
MSV-ATSIGNF
Signal in ams_tunnel statement not found.
There is an ams_tunnel statement at line %s in config file '%s'.
This statement refers to '%s' as a signal within the module '%s'.

MSV-CM-NPC
Connect module has noportcoerce.
Connect module '%s' has '%s' digital port '%s'. To enable the driver-receiver segregation
on this port, it needs to be coerced to inout.
Ignore the noportcoerce directive on this connect module.
MSV-IAT-BADEXPR
Invalid analog tunnel assignment.
Analog tunnel cannot be established due to the expression '%s' in the %s of the tunnel
assignment statement.
MSV-IVZD
Wreal init_val_0 is default.
The argument 'init_val_0' for '-wreal' compile time switch is made default from VCS
2014.03 onward.

Remove the switch '-wreal init_val_0'.
MSV-OBSPICEOPT
Obsolete option used.
Ignoring obsolete option \"-hsopt=spiceopt\".
MSV_PART_CMDS
Missing partition command.
No partition command is found in the HSIM-VCS AD config file '%s' that is provided with
the -ad_hsim=<AD config file> compile time switch.
HSIM-VCS VPI flow requires digital_cell or analog_cell or spice_cell as partition
command in the AD config file.

Invalid DB Pin Attribute.

DB pin attribute '%s' for pin '%s' of cell '%s' in DB file '%s' is invalid.
You can provide attribute '%s' only for a '%s' cell. Provide correct DB for compilation.

VCS and Specman versions incompatible.
This VCS simulator version is not supported with the your Specman version. If you use

Attribute ret_mode not yet implemented in partcomp flow
Attribute 'ret_mode' specified in the 'set_design_attribute' command is not
implemented in the partition comp flow.
Either use single compile flow or remove 'set_design_attribute' from UPF.
UPF_RPPDM
RTL PG Port Direction Mismatch
Direction '%s' of RTL PG port '%s' specified in UPF does not match with the direction '%s'
specified in the design.
Ensure direction of RTL PG ports are same in design and UPF.
UPF_RSLV_DONT_MATCH
Inconsistent -resolve value specified

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Inconsistent -resolve value '%s' specified for UPF Supply Net '%s' that has resolve value
'%s' specified in earlier declaration at line '%s' of file '%s'.
Specify only one resolution type for a supply net.
UPF_RTLPG_DNP
Different RTL PG Net and Port Connected
RTL PG Supply Net '%s' is connected to RTL PG Supply Port '%s' in same scope. RTL PG
supply net can only be connected to same name RTL PG supply port in same scope.
Specify only same name RTL PG supply port in 'connect_supply_net' for the same
scope.
UPF_RTLPG_MPC
Multiple ports connected to RTL PG Net
RTL PG Supply Net '%s' is connected to multiple ports in same scope. RTL PG supply net
can only be connected to an RTL PG supply port in same scope.

Specify only one RTL PG supply port in 'connect_supply_net' for the same scope.
UPF_RTLPG_NRP
Non RTL PG Port in same scope
RTL PG Supply Net '%s' is connected to a non RTL PG Supply Port '%s' in same scope.
RTL PG supply net can only be connected to an RTL PG supply port in same scope.
Specify only RTL PG supply port in 'connect_supply_net' for same scope.
UPF_RTLPG_USP
Unconnected RTL PG Port
RTL PG Supply Port '%s' does not have a RTL PG Supply Net connected to in its scope.
Remove 'create_supply_port' command for this port.
UPF_RUOUSN
'-reuse' used on undefined Supply Net

In the 'create_supply_net' command, '-reuse' is specified, but Supply net '%s' is not
defined in either UPF or the design.
Ensure that the supply net is already defined when using '-reuse'.
UPF_SAC_CTRL_EXPR_NON_USER_OBJECT
Control expression contains unsupported object
The option -control_expr contains internal UPF object: %s.
UPF_SAC_CTRL_EXPR_NON_VERILOG_OBJECT
Control expression contains unsupported object type.
A non-Verilog object %s referred in the -control_expr option of command
'sim_assertion_control'. Only Verilog signals are supported in control_expr.
UPF_SDA_CNS
Command not supported

Command '%s' is not supported inside scope '%s' with attribute %s '%s'.
Set the attribute value for scope '%s' to '%s' using command '%s'.

Conflicting ret_mode values
%s '%s' has ret_mode specified as both RET_ACCURATE and RET_PESSIMISTIC.
Remove conflicting ret_mode definitions from UPF file to avoid this error.
UPF_SDA_INVALID_VAL
Invalid change of attribute value
Attribute value cannot be changed for '%s', as this scope already has supply set states.
Attribute enable_state_propagation_in_add_power_state can only be applied to
scope before specification of supply set states.
UPF_SDA_WM
Attribute without -models

Attribute '%s' specified without mandatory option '-models' in 'set_design_attributes'
Specify valid command and recompile.

Syntax error in UPF
There is a Tcl syntax or semantic error in UPF. %s.
Fix according to normal Tcl/UPF syntax.

Supply Net used as both power/ground
Supply Net '%s' is used as %s and a connected Supply Net '%s' has been used as '%s'.

A supply net can either be a power or ground. Some of the possible ways to mark
a net as power ground are by using the commands 'set_domain_supply_net/
create_supply_net/set_related_supply_net'.

Specify a valid supply port and recompile.
