Excluding Uncoverable Bins From Reports
When running a TB with ICO, you may encounter some uncovered bins due to user-
specified constraints such as state variable or inlined constraints. To generate meaningful
reports, bins that are not covered due to user-specified constraints can be considered for
exclusion.
You can use the -elfile option in the crg command line to exclude selected uncoverable
bins based on the user-specified constraints in the input bias mode.
The following steps describe the use model:
1. Use the runtime options +ntb_solver_bias_mode=265 and
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<path_to_record> during simv using the
following command:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<path_to_record>
+ntb_solver_bias_mode=265
2. Generate the report using the following command:
% crg -dir <dir> -report <report_dir0> -format text
3. Keep the lines with UNCOVERED bins from the report_dir0/bininst_status.csv file
and save it in a file (for example, excl0.txt).
4. Generate the exclusion report using the following command:
% crg -dir <dir> -report <report_dir1> -format text -elfile
<excl0.txt>

or,
% crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -merge <mdir> -report <report_dir1>
-format text -elfile <excl0.txt>
The report_dir1 contains the excluded UNCOVERED bins, which are specified in the file
excl0.txt with potentially improved coverage and diversity scores.
-elfile <elFile>
Exclude all the bins specified in the file. For example, you can use the text report file
bininst_status.csv to keep the lines that you want to exclude.
-merge <mdir>
If one or more database directories are specified, this option creates a merged database
in the output directory merge_dir after optional operations such as -purge, -reset_tag,
-purge_untag, and -zip.
Example to exclude all uncovered bins
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode=1 +ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record0
% crg -dir record0 -report crgReport0 -format text
% grep -v UNCOVERED ./crgReport0/bininst_status.csv > excl0.txt// to
exclude all UNCOVERED bins from the report.
% crg -dir record0 -report crgReport1 -format html -elfile excl0.txt
Exclusion Report
In the HTML report, a separate column for exclusion and category “Excluded” is included,
as shown in Figure 41. The red rectangle shows the additional column corresponding to

Support for Exclusion File Migration
Exclusion support allows you to exclude some bins for coverage calculation as they
cannot be hit due to some blocking conditions that are not due to over constraints. This
support is enhanced to perform the following:
• Migrate exclusion files across regressions, even across incremental TB changes.
Therefore, you can use the exclusion file across CDBs generated for different
regression for the same compiled TB code.
• Add comment for each bin in an additional field (column) optionally. This support for
comment/annotation helps you to track the reason for applying exclusion.
• Generate exclusion report with excluded bins only, including the corresponding
comments. This report can used as an input to elfile on the same or different CDB
(from same or modified TB).
These enhancements are supported under the -report <rpt> , -elfile <elFile> , and
-work <wrk> crg options.
% crg -dir record .. -report <rptDir> -elfile <elFile> -work <wrk>
-dir <dir>: [Input]

Specifies the CDB database generated from simv.
-report <rptDir>: [Output]
Generates report in rptDir. If the -elfile is provided, the binstatus_excluded.csv
(with excluded bins) file is generated independent of the format option. Modified
bininstatus_status.csv is generated with text report option.
-elfile <elFile>: [Input]
Excludes all the bins specified in the file. Allows you to add a new column for comment
optionally. You can use the bininst_status.csv file and can keep the lines you want to
exclude.
-work <wrk>
If you specify only the -elfile option, then the binstatus_excluded.csv file is
generated in <wrk>. If -work is not specified, then the default work directory is used.
Usage Example:
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record1

% crg -dir record1 -format both -report rpt1

% grep ILLEGAL rpt/bininst_status.csv > excluded.lst

% vim excluded.lst // add annotation

+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record2

% crg -dir record2 -elfile excluded.lst -report rpt2 //generate
rpt2/bininst_excluded.csv + other reports

% crg -dir record2 -elfile excluded.lst -work wrk2 //generate
wrk2/bininst_excluded.csv
Exclusion File Format
The following topics describe the file format:
Exclusion File Input Format
Input format is the same as bininst_status.csv. Any line starting with ‘#’ or is not
formatted correctly is ignored.

You can add comment in the last field or column, but there are two restrictions:
• Comment must be in only one line.
• Length of each line including the comment is restricted to 4095 characters. It is
truncated if it exceeds the limit. The following message is issued if it exceeds the limit:
Warning-[CRG-XF-LC] Exclusion File Long Comment
Specified Exclusion file 'excluded1.lst' has entries with long comment
line
(>= 4096).
The long comments are truncated to fit the length.
Exclusion File Output Format: bininst_excluded.csv
The format of the bininst_excluded.csv file is same as the bininst_status.csv
file. This file only reports the excluded bins per line. The comments can be included but
truncated if exceeds the limit as mentioned above. The category of each bin is shown as
EXCLUDED. This file can also be used as an argument to the -elfile option.
The following note is issued when the exclusion report is generated in a work directory:
Note-[CRG-OUT-XF] Exclusion Report Generated
Exclusion report is generated in 'WORK/bininst_excluded.csv'
successfully.
Purging Variables From CDB
The -purge option in Intelligent Coverage Optimization (ICO) allows you to remove
specific variables from a coverage database (cdb) after changes to your testbench. Use
this feature to create a new, clean cdb that reflects only the current variables, which you
can then load in later simulation runs or use for merging. This helps ensure your coverage
data stays accurate and relevant after design modifications.
You may want to sanitize a cdb that is generated before modification of TB and want to
purge some variables affected by the change to obtain a new cdb. This can be loaded in
later simv runs or used for merging. ICO supports purging of variables using the -purge
option as follows:
-purge <pFile>
All the variables in the file are purged. Use varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt
and keep the lines you want to purge.
% crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -merge <mdir> -report crgReport -purge
<pFile> -format text

% crg -dir record0 -report crgReport3 -format text -purge ./crgReport0/
varinst_scope.txt -merge purgedCdb
The -purge option does not modify the input records. The purged record is saved if the
-merge option is provided.
Format: varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt
The varinst_scope.txt file contains a line denoting a variable var for the randomization
object identified by randomize site file:line and class name, as follows:
file:line:class:var
Example: test.sv:10:foo:x
The varclass_scope.txt file contains a line denoting a variable var for the
randomization object identified by class name, as follows:
*:*:class:var
Example: *:*:foo:x
The varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt file can be used as scope file
(+ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=scope.txt in simv run) or as pFile in crg -purge
<pFile>. For more information, refer to “Scoping Random Variables and Constraint Blocks
for Biasing”.
RCA Noise Reduction
VCS ICO provides the following crg runtime options to include/exclude variables during
report generation and to reduce RCA noise.-purge_key uvm+rca+sbin
-purge_key uvm+rca+sbin
Purges variables depending on the keys uvm, rca, and sbin. The ‘+’ sign denotes the
disjunction of the keys.
-purgeX_key uvm+rca+sbin
-purgeX_key uvm+rca+sbin
Purges variables excluding those captured with the key uvm, rca, or sbin. The ‘+’ sign
denotes the disjunction of the keys.
Attributes:
<uvm> - Variables belonging to the UVM library such as seq_kind, select_kind, and so
on.
<rca> - Variables with the RCA information on at least one bin.

<sbin> - Variables with the sbin information (enabled with
+ntb_solver_bias_sbin_file).
If both the options are specified, variables retained after purging are the
intersection of the variables specified by -purgeX_key and those NOT specified
in -purge_key.
Examples
If you intend to purge all variables that belong to the UVM library and retain those that
have either RCA information or have sbin or both, use the following crg command:
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge_key uvm -purgeX_key rca+sbin -report rpt -format
both
The following crg command issues a warning message:
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge_key uvm -purgeX_key none
Warning-[CRG-PKX-I] PurgeX Key Invalid
Specified PurgeX Key 'none' is not valid.
Nothing to exclude. Proceeding without applying the option
'-purgeX_key'.
--
Warning-[CRG-PK-F] Purging with Key Failed
Purge/PurgeX could not be applied.
Proceeding without applying the option '-purge_key/- purgeX_key'.
The following crg command issues a note message:
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge_key uvm -purgeX_key rca+sbin
Note-[CRG-PK] Purging with Key Applied
Purge/PurgeX with Key is applied successfully.
Base Class Merging Based on User-Defined Level
ICO supports base class merging for a given user-defined level, wherein all the coverage
and distribution information of the class instance variables and the bins that are
below the parent class by a given level are merged. This feature is enabled using the
+ntb_solver_bias_class_info=<0|1> simulation option.
Example 24 test.sv
class Config;
rand bit[2:0] cfg;

class Bus extends Config;
rand bit[9:0] addr;
constraint cstr {
soft addr[1:0] == 2'b0;
cfg[2] == 1'b0;
}
class BusA extends Bus;
rand bit[9:0] data;
addr inside { [0:255] } ;
data inside { [0:1023] } ;
}
class BusB extends Bus;
rand bit[7:0] data;
addr inside { [512:1023] };
data inside { [0:255] };
}
BusA busA0 = new, busA1 = new;
BusB busB0 = new, busB1 = new;
Bus bus0 = new, bus1 = new;
repeat(1000) begin
busA0.randomize();
busA1.randomize();
busB0.randomize();
busB1.randomize();
bus0.randomize();
bus1.randomize();
end
end
In the above example, test.sv, the two classes BusA and BusB are derived from Bus,
which in turn is derived from Config. The variables addr, cfg are common for BusA, BusB,
Bus. The variable data has different precision for BusA and BusB.
By default, class instances BusA0 and BusA1 are merged. Similarly, BusB0, BusB1 and
Bus0, Bus1 are also merged.
This feature allows merging of BusA0, BusA1, BusB0, BusB1, Bus0, and Bus1, which are
instances of parent class Bus at level 1 as follows:
File:Line:Class, #randomization, #randVars, #biasedVars
test.sv:36:Bus, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:35:Bus, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:34:BusB, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:32:BusA, 1000, 2, 2

test.sv:33:BusB, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:31:BusA, 1000, 2, 2
Union of coverage information occurs only for variables that are compatible, that is, same
precision and signedness.
The following sections describe the use model of this feature:
You can use the following simulation option to enable base class merging for a given user-
defined level:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_class_info=<0|1> +ntb_solver_bias_mode=<mode> ….
+ntb_solver_class_info=<0|1>
1: Enable information collection of class hierarchy
0: Disable (default)
To enable base class merging, you must enable collection of class hierarchy information
by specifying the +ntb_solver_bias_class_info=1 option.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record
+ntb_solver_bias_class_info=1 +ntb_solver_bias_mode=16649
+ntb_enable_fast_solver=0 +ntb_solver_mode=2 +ntb_solver_bias_diag=2
Crg Option
Following is the crg option:
crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -base_merge <level> -report <rpt>
Specifies the coverage database <dir1>
-base_merge <level>
Specifies the base class merge <level>.
0: No base merging (same as merging of class instances)

L>0: All leaf classes with same base class at level L are merged. This argument only
affects -report.
If simv is run with +ntb_solver_bias_class_info=1 and crg is run on the generated
record, then a file class_info.txt gets generated in the report directory.
If base merge level is too high, and if no parent class exists at that level, no
report is generated.
Format: class_info.txt
Following is the format of class_info.txt file:
class_id class_name parent_id is_rand

-elfile <elFile>: [Input]
Excludes all the bins specified in the file. Allows you to add a new column for comment
optionally. You can use the bininst_status.csv file and can keep the lines you want to
exclude.
-work <wrk>
If you specify only the -elfile option, then the binstatus_excluded.csv file is
generated in <wrk>. If -work is not specified, then the default work directory is used.
Usage Example:
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record1

% crg -dir record1 -format both -report rpt1

% grep ILLEGAL rpt/bininst_status.csv > excluded.lst

% vim excluded.lst // add annotation

% crg -dir record2 -elfile excluded.lst -report rpt2 //generate
rpt2/bininst_excluded.csv + other reports

% crg -dir record2 -elfile excluded.lst -work wrk2 //generate
wrk2/bininst_excluded.csv
Exclusion File Format
The following topics describe the file format:
Exclusion File Input Format
Input format is the same as bininst_status.csv. Any line starting with ‘#’ or is not
formatted correctly is ignored.

You can add comment in the last field or column, but there are two restrictions:
• Comment must be in only one line.
• Length of each line including the comment is restricted to 4095 characters. It is
truncated if it exceeds the limit. The following message is issued if it exceeds the limit:
Warning-[CRG-XF-LC] Exclusion File Long Comment
Specified Exclusion file 'excluded1.lst' has entries with long comment
line
(>= 4096).
The long comments are truncated to fit the length.
Exclusion File Output Format: bininst_excluded.csv
The format of the bininst_excluded.csv file is same as the bininst_status.csv
file. This file only reports the excluded bins per line. The comments can be included but
truncated if exceeds the limit as mentioned above. The category of each bin is shown as
EXCLUDED. This file can also be used as an argument to the -elfile option.
The following note is issued when the exclusion report is generated in a work directory:
Note-[CRG-OUT-XF] Exclusion Report Generated
Exclusion report is generated in 'WORK/bininst_excluded.csv'
successfully.
Purging Variables From CDB
The -purge option in Intelligent Coverage Optimization (ICO) allows you to remove
specific variables from a coverage database (cdb) after changes to your testbench. Use
this feature to create a new, clean cdb that reflects only the current variables, which you
can then load in later simulation runs or use for merging. This helps ensure your coverage
data stays accurate and relevant after design modifications.
You may want to sanitize a cdb that is generated before modification of TB and want to
purge some variables affected by the change to obtain a new cdb. This can be loaded in
later simv runs or used for merging. ICO supports purging of variables using the -purge
option as follows:
-purge <pFile>
All the variables in the file are purged. Use varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt
and keep the lines you want to purge.
% crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -merge <mdir> -report crgReport -purge
<pFile> -format text

% crg -dir record0 -report crgReport3 -format text -purge ./crgReport0/
varinst_scope.txt -merge purgedCdb
The -purge option does not modify the input records. The purged record is saved if the
-merge option is provided.
Format: varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt
The varinst_scope.txt file contains a line denoting a variable var for the randomization
object identified by randomize site file:line and class name, as follows:
file:line:class:var
Example: test.sv:10:foo:x
The varclass_scope.txt file contains a line denoting a variable var for the
randomization object identified by class name, as follows:
*:*:class:var
Example: *:*:foo:x
The varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt file can be used as scope file
(+ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=scope.txt in simv run) or as pFile in crg -purge
<pFile>. For more information, refer to “Scoping Random Variables and Constraint Blocks
for Biasing”.
RCA Noise Reduction
VCS ICO provides the following crg runtime options to include/exclude variables during
report generation and to reduce RCA noise.-purge_key uvm+rca+sbin
-purge_key uvm+rca+sbin
Purges variables depending on the keys uvm, rca, and sbin. The ‘+’ sign denotes the
disjunction of the keys.
-purgeX_key uvm+rca+sbin
-purgeX_key uvm+rca+sbin
Purges variables excluding those captured with the key uvm, rca, or sbin. The ‘+’ sign
denotes the disjunction of the keys.
Attributes:
<uvm> - Variables belonging to the UVM library such as seq_kind, select_kind, and so
on.
<rca> - Variables with the RCA information on at least one bin.

<sbin> - Variables with the sbin information (enabled with
+ntb_solver_bias_sbin_file).
If both the options are specified, variables retained after purging are the
intersection of the variables specified by -purgeX_key and those NOT specified
in -purge_key.
Examples
If you intend to purge all variables that belong to the UVM library and retain those that
have either RCA information or have sbin or both, use the following crg command:
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge_key uvm -purgeX_key rca+sbin -report rpt -format
both
The following crg command issues a warning message:
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge_key uvm -purgeX_key none
Warning-[CRG-PKX-I] PurgeX Key Invalid
Specified PurgeX Key 'none' is not valid.
Nothing to exclude. Proceeding without applying the option
'-purgeX_key'.
--
Warning-[CRG-PK-F] Purging with Key Failed
Purge/PurgeX could not be applied.
Proceeding without applying the option '-purge_key/- purgeX_key'.
The following crg command issues a note message:
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge_key uvm -purgeX_key rca+sbin
Note-[CRG-PK] Purging with Key Applied
Purge/PurgeX with Key is applied successfully.
Base Class Merging Based on User-Defined Level
ICO supports base class merging for a given user-defined level, wherein all the coverage
and distribution information of the class instance variables and the bins that are
below the parent class by a given level are merged. This feature is enabled using the
+ntb_solver_bias_class_info=<0|1> simulation option.
Example 24 test.sv
class Config;
rand bit[2:0] cfg;

class Bus extends Config;
rand bit[9:0] addr;
constraint cstr {
soft addr[1:0] == 2'b0;
cfg[2] == 1'b0;
}
class BusA extends Bus;
rand bit[9:0] data;
addr inside { [0:255] } ;
data inside { [0:1023] } ;
}
class BusB extends Bus;
rand bit[7:0] data;
addr inside { [512:1023] };
data inside { [0:255] };
}
BusA busA0 = new, busA1 = new;
BusB busB0 = new, busB1 = new;
Bus bus0 = new, bus1 = new;
repeat(1000) begin
busA0.randomize();
busA1.randomize();
busB0.randomize();
busB1.randomize();
bus0.randomize();
bus1.randomize();
end
end
In the above example, test.sv, the two classes BusA and BusB are derived from Bus,

Bus bus0 = new, bus1 = new;
repeat(1000) begin
busA0.randomize();
busA1.randomize();
busB0.randomize();
busB1.randomize();
bus0.randomize();
bus1.randomize();
end
end
In the above example, test.sv, the two classes BusA and BusB are derived from Bus,
which in turn is derived from Config. The variables addr, cfg are common for BusA, BusB,
Bus. The variable data has different precision for BusA and BusB.
By default, class instances BusA0 and BusA1 are merged. Similarly, BusB0, BusB1 and
Bus0, Bus1 are also merged.
This feature allows merging of BusA0, BusA1, BusB0, BusB1, Bus0, and Bus1, which are
instances of parent class Bus at level 1 as follows:
File:Line:Class, #randomization, #randVars, #biasedVars
test.sv:36:Bus, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:35:Bus, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:34:BusB, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:32:BusA, 1000, 2, 2

test.sv:33:BusB, 1000, 2, 2
test.sv:31:BusA, 1000, 2, 2
Union of coverage information occurs only for variables that are compatible, that is, same
precision and signedness.
The following sections describe the use model of this feature:
You can use the following simulation option to enable base class merging for a given user-
defined level:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_class_info=<0|1> +ntb_solver_bias_mode=<mode> ….
+ntb_solver_class_info=<0|1>
1: Enable information collection of class hierarchy
0: Disable (default)
To enable base class merging, you must enable collection of class hierarchy information
by specifying the +ntb_solver_bias_class_info=1 option.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record
+ntb_solver_bias_class_info=1 +ntb_solver_bias_mode=16649
+ntb_enable_fast_solver=0 +ntb_solver_mode=2 +ntb_solver_bias_diag=2
Crg Option
Following is the crg option:
crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -base_merge <level> -report <rpt>
Specifies the coverage database <dir1>
-base_merge <level>
Specifies the base class merge <level>.
0: No base merging (same as merging of class instances)

L>0: All leaf classes with same base class at level L are merged. This argument only
affects -report.
If simv is run with +ntb_solver_bias_class_info=1 and crg is run on the generated
record, then a file class_info.txt gets generated in the report directory.
If base merge level is too high, and if no parent class exists at that level, no
report is generated.

Delta Difference Between Two CDBs
The crg utility also allows you to highlight delta difference between two coverage
databases using the -diff coverage runtime option. This feature helps you to understand
and focus on part of the constraint and variables where the differences are observed or not
observed between two coverage databases, especially when the coverage databases are
generated from changing TB or from two regression runs.
The delta difference can be used to triage failures by taking the difference between the
local load coverage databases (specified with +ntb_solver_bias_load_record) and
local store coverage databases (specified with +input_solver_bias_store_record),
and focus on classes, variables with largest coverage and diversity score delta.
This feature is applicable only for HTML/text reports.
crg -dir <leftCDB> -dir <rightCDB> -report crgDiffReport -diff

-dir <leftCDB>: [Input]
Left (or first) coverage database specified in the command.
-dir <rightCDB>: [Input]
Right (or second) coverage database specified in the command.
-report <crgDiffReport>: [Output]
Generates the delta difference report in the crgDiffReport directory.
-format <text|html>
Specifies the report format (Default: html).
-diff: [option]
Shows the bin category change |leftCDB - rightCDB| in the report corresponding to
leftCDB.
Other options of coverage including -f, -merge, -purge, -elfile, -exclude,
-shared, -zip, -reset_tag, -purge_untag will have no impact.

Enum type names are displayed for the corresponding bins in the coverage reports,
instead of a numeric value. For example, random variable a of enum type state_t is
defined as follows:
typedef enum bit [2:0] {one=0,two,three,four,five} state_t;
rand state_t a;
The crg report shows the enum label for corresponding bin as follows:
Figure 49 Enum Labels in Coverage Reports
Sorting and Searching in Coverage HTML Reports
ICO is enhanced to provide sort and search capabilities in the coverage HTML reports.
This feature allows you to sort table columns, search any field values, and display partially
matching rows. This helps in better navigation of the reports.
Sorting and Searching in the details.html Page
You can sort each column field. Clicking on the column header toggles between ascending
and descending order for that column. For example, Figure 50 shows the O-SCORE
column sorted in descending order.

Figure 50 Sorting and Searching in the details.html Page
You can use the Search filed (rectangular field) to search the page and view the partially
matching results. Figure 51 shows partially matching rows for the matching word ‘mxtn’.
Figure 51 Partially Matching Rows for Matching Word
Sorting and Searching in the Per Class Instance Page
You can sort each column field. Clicking on the column header toggles between ascending
and descending order for that column. For example, Figure 52 shows the VARIABLES
column sorted in descending order.

Figure 52 Sorting Column Fields
You can use the Search filed (rectangular field) to search the page and view partially
matching results. Figure 53 shows partially matching rows for matching word ‘25’.
Figure 53 Viewing Partially Matching Results

You can select the number of variables to display per page. For example, Figure 54 shows
that a maximum of 69 variables can be set per page:
Figure 54 Selecting Number of Variables to Display Per Page
You can select the number of variables to display per page. For example, Figure 55 shows
5 variables per page, spanning over 14 pages.
Figure 55 Selecting the Number of Variables to Display Per Page

Separating Detail Information in Coverage HTML reports
HTML coverage reporting is enhanced to separate the class instances and the class
information in two separate pages along with the capabilities such as sort table columns,
search field values, display partially matching rows, and display specified number of rows
per page. The detail.html is replaced by two additional htmls: inst_detail.html and
class_detail.html.
Viewing Inst_detail.html Report
This report provides the information on per class instance scores with sort and search
capabilities. It also allows you to select the number of rows per page. The coverage and
diversity scores are aggregate of the class instance variables as shown in Figure 56:
Figure 56 Viewing Inst_detail.html Report
When the -diff option is selected, it shows the delta difference on the corresponding
class instances information.

Viewing Class_detail.html Report
This report provides the information on per class scores with sorting and searching
capabilities. It also allows you to select the number of rows per page. The coverage and
diversity scores are aggregate of the class variables as shown in Figure 57.
Figure 57 Viewing Class_detail.html Report
When the -diff option is selected, it shows the delta difference on the corresponding
class information. When the -base_merge option is used, it shows information per base
merged class.
Reporting Part-Select Variables for Coverage and Diversity
Distribution
Use the part-select reporting feature to include coverage and diversity information
for specific bit slices (part-selects) of variables in your coverage reports. This helps
you analyze how different parts of a variable contribute to overall coverage, providing
more detailed insight into your design's verification quality. Enable this feature with the
-part_select option in the crg command to see separate coverage data for each part-
select, which supports more precise verification and debugging.
You can use the -part_select crg option to enable the reporting of the coverage and
diversity information of the part-selects of variables in the crg reports generated from the
CDB.

% crg -dir <dir> -part_select -report <rpt>
-part_select
Includes part-selects of variables in the crg report.
Due to the part-select variables, the total score or diversity information is different between
with and without using the -part_select option.
This option does not change exclusion flow.
This option does not cause any changes to the varinst_scope.txt and
varinst_biased.txt text reports.
Viewing Part-Select Variables in the Coverage Report
Consider the following testcase:
Example 25 test.sv
rand bit signed [10:0] x;
constraint cons {
x[2:0] >= 4;
x[10:3] >= 10;
}
endclass initial begin
end
end
Perform the following commands:
% crg -dir simv.cst/stimuliDB/record -report rpt_bs -part_select

Figure 58 Viewing Part-Select Variables in the Coverage Reports
As shown in Figure 6-4, the part-selects x[10:3] and x[2:0] are shown as separate
variables with their actual precision. The scores are different than the crg report generated
without using the -part_select option.
The text reports contain additional rows corresponding to these part-selects as follows for
bininst_status.csv:
1@32 test.sv 11 cls x[10:3] [2^5:(2^6)-1] 11.11 COVERED -
1@33 test.sv 11 cls x[10:3] [2^6:(2^7)-1] 33.33 COVERED -
1@34 test.sv 11 cls x[10:3] [2^7:(2^8)-1] 44.44 COVERED -
2@0 test.sv 11 cls x[2:0] [0:0] 0.00 UNCOVERED -
2@1 test.sv 11 cls x[2:0] [1:1] 0.00 UNCOVERED -
2@2 test.sv 11 cls x[2:0] [2:2] 0.00 UNCOVERED -
2@3 test.sv 11 cls x[2:0] [3:3] 0.00 UNCOVERED -

• The part-select variables do not have illegal category. However, they can be
excluded.
• RCA is not done on the part-select variables.
• Part-select variables cannot be purged without purging the base variable.

1 cls x[2:0] [3:3] 0.00 UNCOVERED -

• The part-select variables do not have illegal category. However, they can be
excluded.
• RCA is not done on the part-select variables.
• Part-select variables cannot be purged without purging the base variable.
For example, x[2:0] cannot be purged from CDB separately, but when x is
purged then x[2:0] is also purged.
Viewing Coverage and Diversity of Additional Singleton Bins in
the Coverage Reports
ICO displays the coverage and diversity scores of additional singleton bins in the coverage
reports. You must use the +ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=16,17 option to enable this
feature.
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=1 +ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=16,17
Example 26 test.sv

class BusA;
rand bit[10:0] varA;
rand bit signed [10:0] varD;
varA inside { [64:1000] } ;
varD inside { [-500:-300],[-100:40], [80:400] } ;
}
BusA busA0 = new;

repeat(800) begin
busA0.randomize();
end
end
This testcase is used in the following examples to view the coverage reports using
+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=16,17.

Support for ICO Weighted Diversity
Use the weighted diversity feature in Intelligent Coverage Optimization (ICO) to measure
diversity in your stimulus, considering the size of each bin. Execute the -wdiv option with
the crg command to compute weighted Shannon entropy, which gives a more accurate
assessment of diversity, especially when some categories are more important. This

helps you track true diversity improvements across regression runs and make informed
decisions about your coverage quality.
Crg reports provide coverage and diversity information of the generated stimulus. By
default, the diversity scores reported do not consider interval size. The computed diversity
does not account for the size of the bins and therefore does not reflect the true diversity or
its improvement with additional regression runs.
To measure the actual diversity, weighted diversity that considers the interval size is
required. ICO supports the calculation of weighted diversity using the -wdiv crg runtime
option. This feature uses weighted Shannon entropy and helps to assess diversity in
situations where certain categories hold more significance than others.
The following is the usage of the -wdiv crg runtime option:
% crg -dir <dir> -wdiv -report <rpt>
Specifies cdb database <dir1>.
-wdiv (default: off)
Computes weighted diversity.
% crg -dir shared -dir snap1 -report rpt -diff -wdiv
Example 27 test.sv
rand int a;
rand int b;
rand int c;
constraint cons{
a inside {[-100:100]};
b inside {[0:1000]};
c inside {[1000:10000]};
a < b;
}

repeat(10000) begin
end
end

Coverage Performance Feature
This section describes the following coverage performance feature:
• Reducing Disk Footprint of CDB
Reducing Disk Footprint of CDB
The learned information is accumulated in the coverage database (cdb) memory during
runtime (simv runs) and is later saved in the disk before the run is finished. For later simv
runs, the learned information in the cdb is loaded from the disk and an updated cdb with
additional learning is stored back in the disk. For example:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_store=<recordStore>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record=<recordLoad> +ntb_solver_bias_mode=2
By default, the stimuli distribution history is loaded from the record <recordLoad> (if
specified), and the updated history is stored in the record <recordStore>. Each cdb

Coverage Performance Feature
loaded during the run must be saved for reproducing the run during debugging. This can
lead to a requirement of large disk space and possibly management of disk cleaning.
ICO allows you to reduce the size of a cdb with lossless compression technique enabled
at runtime using the simulation option +ntb_solver_bias_zip.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_zip=<level>
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<recordShared> …
The cdb databases are compressed and stored in the disk based on the compression
level.
Compression level: 0 to 9 (default: 0).
0: No compression
1: Fastest compression

title: 2 to 8: Fastest to best compression
text:
9: Best compression
Compression level greater than 0 compresses the local store record (specified
with +ntb_solver_bias_store_record), local load record (specified
with +ntb_solver_bias_load_record), and share record (specified with
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record).
During generation of the merge database using crg, you can use compression to reduce
the size of the merge database.
% crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -zip <level> -merge <mdir> -report <rpt>
-zip <level>
Compression level: 0 to 9 (default: 0).
0: No compression
1: Fastest compression

title: 2 to 8: Fastest to best compression
text:
9: Best compression
Compression level greater than 0 compresses the local store record (specified
with +ntb_solver_bias_store_record), local load record (specified
with +ntb_solver_bias_load_record), and share record (specified with
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record).
During generation of the merge database using crg, you can use compression to reduce
the size of the merge database.
% crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -zip <level> -merge <mdir> -report <rpt>
-zip <level>
Compression level: 0 to 9 (default: 0).
0: No compression
1: Fastest compression

title: 2 to 8: Fastest to best compression
text:
9: Best compression
Based on the zip level, the merge output <mdir> is compressed.

Coverage Usability Feature
To load a cdb compressed with +ntb_solver_bias_zip at runtime or with -zip using the
crg utility, there is no need to specify additional options. ICO automatically decompresses
the coverage database on-the-fly during loading if needed.
Following are the advantages of this feature:
• Reduces the need for large disk space and/or frequent disk cleaning
• Improves the performance by reducing the disk input/output data

Invoking ICO in Single Test Mode
Invoking ICO in Single Test Mode
You can use the following runtime options to enable ICO in single test mode:
+ntb_solver_bias_mode=<0|1|2+>
0: Disables bias mode
1: Enables record mode only
2+: Enables both record and bias modes
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<path>
Allows you to specify path to record the information.
+ntb_solver_bias_diag=<0|1|2|3>
Enables solver bias diagnostics.
The following example is used to explain ICO use model throughout the document:
Example 28 test.sv
class my_rand;
rand integer a,b,c,d,e,f;
int temp;

constraint my_constraint {
a == b * c;
b > c;
d << (a %32) != 0;
a > 0;
b > 0;
c > 0;
d > 0;
e > 0;
f > 0;
}

function void post_randomize;
temp++;
if ( (a+b+c+d+e+f < 50) || (a+b+c+d+e+f > 100))
$display("%0d Randomize call FAILS",temp);
endfunction

program test;
my_rand my_rand1 = new();

initial

begin
$display (" RANDOMIZING CLASS MY_RAND\n");
repeat(100)
my_rand1.randomize() with {a+b+c+d+e+f < 100 && a+b+c+d+e+f > 50;};
end

Enables both record and bias modes. The variable values are biased with varying weights

Reusing Shared CDB Across Changing Models
Reusing Shared CDB Across Changing Models
ICO allows the reuse of the shared coverage database across changing models. As
models change (Model1, Model2, … Model<i>…), you can use the auto purge feature
to enable learning and reusing of the shared coverage database across the changing
models. This feature allows you to track and purge stale information as shown in the
following figure:
Figure 68 Auto Purge
You can use the
-auto_purge
-auto_purge crg option to automatically purge the stale information from
the given CDBs, save it in <shared_cdb_new>, and initialize it for sharing. Following is the
use model:
% crg -dir <cdb> [-dir <cdb1>] -auto_purge -merge <shared_cdb_new>
[-report <rpt>]

• You can use any crg command along with the -auto_purge option.
• The report generated during auto purge contains the following files with no
content as the scope and biased tracker are reset:
varinst_scope.txt, varinst_biased.txt, varclass_scope.txt,
varclass_biased.txt
• The following two files are created and show instances and class variables
respectively, irrespective of whether they are present in the scope or not:
varinst_all.txt, varinst_class.txt
You can use the runtime prognosis feature to select a TB where ICO could be most
effective in improving coverage. The prognosis feature is enabled using the following
runtime option:
+ntb_solver_bias_prognosis=1
For a given TB, this feature allows you to select the best modes for coverage convergence
and helps to minimize the evaluation and deployment time.
Specifically, this feature does the following:
• Collects the TB information regarding
◦ Bias ability of variables and values, that is, how much freedom is provided by
constraints for the random variables to take various random values.
◦ Constraint density, that is, how many constraints per variable. This provides insight
to how constrained the TB is.
◦ Number of randomizations, number of random variables, and number of random
instances per tests.
• Saves the TB information per test seed compactly in each record database per test.
• Runs the crg utility post regression on the records created by the various simulation
runs enabled with prognosis feature and creates a prognosis report (CSV format),
which shows the information per test seed, aggregated per test, and per regression
run.

• Simv Runtime Option
• Shortcut to ICO Prognosis
simv +ntb_solver_bias_prognosis=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<templateTestName>_<Id> -cm_test
<templateTestName><Id> -cm_name <templateTestName><Id>
+UVM_TESTNAME=<templateTestName> +OVM_TESTNAME=<templateTestName>
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<record> +ntb_enable_fast_solver=0
+ ntb_solver_bias_test_type=<uvm|ovm|vmm|cm_test|cm_name>
+ntb_solver_bias_prognosis=<0|1> (default: 0)
Enables the runtime prognosis feature. If prognosis is enabled, then most of the
options starting with +ntb_solver_bias* are ignored. Some options starting
with +ntb_solver_bias_test*(for example, ntb_solver_bias_test_name,
ntb_solver_bias_test_type, and ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter) are an
exception.
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<templateTestName>_<Id>
Tracks the test name in the crg reports. The Id should be a random seed (specified using
+ntb_random_seed) if added in the test name. Preference is given to the test names
specified in the following default order on the command line:
• +ntb_solver_bias_test_name
• +UVM_TESTNAME
• +OVM_TESTNAME
• +vmm_test
• -cm_test
• -cm_name
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=<uvm|ovm|vmm|cm_test|cm_name>
You can specify the test type to override the default order by using
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type to one of the cm_name | cm_test | ovm | uvm| vmm strings.

Shortcut to ICO Prognosis

1: Enables prognosis auto-configuration with default solver orchestration

Specifies the work directory.

You can use the following command to generate prognosis report:
% crg -dir record -f <filelist> -prognosis -report <reportDir>
Example: crg -dir cdb_store_prog3 -report rpt_prog3 -prognosis
-prognosis (default off)
Generates the prognosis.csv file in the <reportDir> directory for the records that are
created during runtime with prognosis feature. All other crg options are ignored. Figure 69
shows the format of the prognosis.csv file.
Figure 69 Format of the prognosis.csv File
The description of each column in the above report is as follows:
• db-name: Name of the record dir of the test
• test-name: Specified at runtime through ntb_solver_bias_test_name/cm_test/
cm_name/UVM_TESTNAME/OVM_TESTNAME
• template-name: Unique test name (test name without random seed)
• #rand-prob: Number of randomizations
• #rand-inst: Number of random instances
• cstr-per-var: Constraint density, that is, number of constraints per variable averaged
over each randomization.

Dumping Failure Signatures
ICO can dump failure signatures during simulation when you run it in bug-finding mode.
A failure signature is a normalized form of an error message in which dynamic content ,
such as simulation time and data values, has been removed. As a result, multiple error
messages that report the same underlying problem collapse to a single signature.
This feature helps you do the following:
• Identify unique failure patterns in bug-finding runs.
• Group repeated error messages that differ only in dynamic content.
• Triage and count unique failures more efficiently.

Dumping Failure Signatures
You enable this feature through existing simv runtime options. ICO writes the failure
signature data to the fail_sig.txt file in the store record directory. No change is
required at compilation.
• Use Model
• Failure Signature
• Example
• Counting Unique Failure Signatures
ICO dumps failure signatures when you run simulation with either of the following settings:
• +ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=bugs
• +ntb_solver_bias_fail_predict=<nonzero_value>
The following is the overall use model:
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=<bug|bug2|bug3|bugs|bal|cov|nob|rca>
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record>
+ntb_solver_bias_replay=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_fail_regex=<regex>
-l <simv.log>
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=<bug|bug2|bug3|bugs|bal|cov|nob|rca>
Selects the ICO biasing strategy for the run. Use the bugs value to enable the bug-finding
strategy that triggers failure signature dumping.
Enables failure prediction. Specify a non-zero value to trigger failure signature dumping
independently of the strategy mode.
ICO dumps failure signatures only when
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=bugs is set or
+ntb_solver_bias_fail_predict is set to a non-zero value. When ICO
detects failures under one of these supported modes, it writes failure signature
information to fail_sig.txt in the store record directory.

Dumping Failure Signatures
Failure Signature
When failure signature dumping is enabled, ICO writes the signature data to the following
file in the store record directory:
<store_record>/fail_sig.txt
For example, if the store record directory is wdir/test_1.store_record, ICO writes the
signature data to:
wdir/test_1.store_record/fail_sig.txt
For each failure observed in a run, ICO writes two lines to fail_sig.txt:
M: <err_message>
S: <err_signature>
Where:
• M: records the actual error message observed during simulation.
• S: records the corresponding normalized failure signature.
ICO derives the failure signature from the original error message by stripping out dynamic
content. Dynamic content includes values that change from one run or one occurrence to
another, such as simulation time, line offsets, and data values. As a result, multiple error
messages that share the same underlying failure pattern map to a single signature. This
lets you group and count unique failure patterns rather than individual error occurrences.
The following example shows the contents of fail_sig.txt for a run in which four error
messages were observed. The messages differ in simulation time and in the reported
illegal state value, but they all share the same underlying failure pattern and therefore map

Counting Unique Failure Signatures
To count the number of unique failure signatures recorded for a run, filter the lines that
begin with S:, sort them, and count the unique entries. For example:
% cat wdir/test_1.store_record/fail_sig.txt | grep "^S:" | sort -u | wc
-l
In this example, although the run produced four error messages, all four map to the same
signature, so the count of unique failure signatures is 1.

Figure 71 Viewing Improved Diversity Scores
Configuring Shared CDB for Congested Network
Performance of ICO, measured in terms of diversification of stimulus, also diminishes
when huge test run data cannot be merged online as the subsequent test runs of the
regression cannot exploit the new information learned. Also, congestion is more severe
when the regression size is big.
To address this issue, ICO supports a mechanism to configure the shared cdb at the time
of its initialization using the -shared init_sfs crg runtime option. This feature helps you
to mitigate online merging failures and improves the performance of ICO.

Optimizing Load Record Directory Size
You can use the following command to configure shared coverage database to address
merging failures due to congestion:
% crg -dir <shared_record> -shared <init|init_sfs>
Specifies cdb database <dir1>.
-shared init
Initializes shared record <dir> for normal file server (nfs).
-shared init_sfs
Initializes shared record <dir> for slow file server (sfs).
Examples:
% crg -dir sh1 -shared init_sfs
The sh1 directory is initialized for shared recording and configured for slow file server.
% crg -dir sh2 -shared init
The sh2 directory is initialized for shared recording.

Making Load Record Optimal by Default
Making Load Record Optimal by Default
In a distributed shared record setting, for each simv run enabled with ICO, a backup load
record directory is created which is the snapshot of the shared record. This backup load
record can be used to replay the simv run.
The +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=1 option can be used at runtime to
reduce the backup load size, however the usage of the optimized backup load requires a
change in the script file during replay, that is, point the load record to the optimized backup
load.
The +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=2 runtime option allows you to
overwrite the backup load record with the optimized backup load record in the shared
mode without the need to change the script during replay. This feature allows you to make
the load record optimal by default avoiding the need to change the load record setting for
replay.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_auto_config=2
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt=<load_record_opt>
where,
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=<0|1|2>
1: Enables creating optimized load record.
2: Enables 1 and enables overwriting the load record with the optimized load record in the
shared mode.
• The +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=2 option only impacts
the shared mode with replay=0. It does not have any impact on non-shared
mode or replay=1|2.
• No change in the behavior of
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=1. The backward
compatibility is preserved.

+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=1.

Reporting Recommendation to Purge the Shared CDB or Use
New DB
The shared cdb can be reused across regressions and across changing models. To use
across models, it is generally recommended to purge the stale variables from the cdb. Too
many stale variables can increase the resident memory size of the cdb during the run. ICO
provides a measure that can be used to decide when to purge the shared cdb or when to
use a new DB.
You can use the -stat crg runtime option to report fraction of the resident memory that is
relevant (that is, in the scope). You can use that information to decide whether to purge or
use a new DB based on if the fraction is above a threshold or not respectively.

Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
Illegal bins can be due to soft constraints, static parameters, state dependent values,
variables that are switched off for randomization, or variables that are unreachable due to
combination of hard constraints of one or more random variables.
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Categorizing Illegal Bins
• Grouping Illegal Bins
Categorizing Illegal Bins
Managing huge number of illegal bins can be difficult. It can also lead to oversight and
user may miss a real over-constraint. The categorization of illegal bins can help you
to prioritize and help manage large number of illegal bins for potential over-constraint
analysis. Without categorization, it is not easy to know the reason without individually
clicking the hyperlink and looking into the blocking constraints.
ICO supports categorization of illegal bins by tagging each illegal bin with attributes SOFT,
UNR, ROFF, and PARA, and prioritizing them. This feature can be enabled by using the
-illegal_attrruntime option in the post-simulation crg utility. Also, you must run the
simulation with RCA enabled, preferably with +ntb_solver_bias_rca=3.
You can use the post runtime option -illegal_attr to annotate CRG HTML and text
report with illegal bin attributes.
% crg -dir <record> -report crgReport -illegal_attr -format both

Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
RCA Visualization
There is no change in the format of the HTML report when -illegal_attr is enabled.
However, each illegal bin with a hyper-link will have one of the following attributes:
ILLEGAL::SOFT - If the value is blocked by at least one soft constraint.
ILLEGAL::UNR - If the value is unreachable due to the combination of hard constraints of
one or more random variables.
ILLEGAL::ROFF - If the value is blocked by hard constraints with at least one random
variable whose rand mode is off.
ILLEGAL::PARA - If the value is blocked by hard constraints due to the presence of
parameter or state values, with no rand-mode-off variables.
These four attributes are shown in the sorted order (using up/down arrow) from top to
bottom in the order of priority, as shown in the following figure:
Figure 72 Categorization of Illegal Bins

Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
Grouping Illegal Bins
Managing huge number of illegal bins with same RCA reason can be difficult. Grouping
of illegal bins with identical reasons can help you to avoid the manual effort of inspecting
each bin with same reason as another bin. It also helps to reduce the disk footprint
significantly by eliminating repeat information.
ICO supports grouping of illegal bins by tagging illegal bins with identical reasons with
G<#>. This feature can be enabled by using the -illegal_group runtime option in the
post-simulation crg utility. This feature can also be combined with attributes enabled by
adding the -illegal_attr runtime option.
The -illegal_group runtime option annotates CRG HTML and text report with illegal bin
group tags.
% crg -dir <record> -report crgReport -illegal_attr -illegal_group
-format both
RCA Visualization
There is no change in the format of the HTML report when -illegal_group is enabled.
When used without the -illegal_attr option, illegal bins are grouped based on common
reasons without any attributes as shown in the following figure:
Figure 73 Grouping of Illegal Bins
The RCA file is generated per group as shown in the following figure. This saves the disk
footprint.

Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge
File
By default, all random variables with constraints are recorded, and biased if bias mode
is selected. The simv runtime option +ntb_solver_bias_scope_file provides a list of
variables for recording and biasing and ignores the rest. However, it is not possible to
exclude variables from recording/biasing. The workaround is to remove variables from the
full list of variables, which is not very user friendly.
Similar issue exists when purging a list of variables from the cdb database. The crg option
-purge <file> allows you to purge variables listed in the file, but you cannot exclude
variables from purging.
ICO supports the following exclusions to make the usage easier:
• Exclusion of variables from recording/biasing in the scope file using the
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file runtime option. For more information, see Excluding
Variables from Recording and Biasing.
• Exclusion of variables from purging in the crg purge file using the -purgeX crg option.
For more information, see Excluding Variables from Purging.
Excluding Variables from Recording and Biasing
The following is the syntax to exclude variables from recording and biasing:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile>
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file=<scopeXFile>

Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge File
+ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile>
Restricts recording and biasing of variables to those specified in the scopeFile.
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file=<scopeXFile>
Excludes variables specified in the scopeXFile from recording and biasing.
If both options are provided, then the recording and biasing variables are the
intersection of the variables specified by scopeFile and those NOT specified in
scopeXFile.
Excluding Variables from Purging
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge <scopeXFile> -purgeX <scopeFile>
-purge <scopeXFile>
Purge variables specified in the scopeXFile.
-purgeX <scopeFile>
Purge variables excluding those specified in the scopeFile.
If both options are provided, then the variables retained after purging are the
intersection of the variables specified by scopeFile and those NOT specified in
scopeXFile.

Reusing Shared CDB Across Changing Models
ICO allows the reuse of the shared coverage database across changing models. As
models change (Model1, Model2, … Model<i>…), you can use the auto purge feature
to enable learning and reusing of the shared coverage database across the changing
models. This feature allows you to track and purge stale information as shown in the
following figure:
Figure 68 Auto Purge
You can use the
-auto_purge
-auto_purge crg option to automatically purge the stale information from
the given CDBs, save it in <shared_cdb_new>, and initialize it for sharing. Following is the
use model:
% crg -dir <cdb> [-dir <cdb1>] -auto_purge -merge <shared_cdb_new>
[-report <rpt>]

• You can use any crg command along with the -auto_purge option.
• The report generated during auto purge contains the following files with no
content as the scope and biased tracker are reset:
varinst_scope.txt, varinst_biased.txt, varclass_scope.txt,
varclass_biased.txt
• The following two files are created and show instances and class variables
respectively, irrespective of whether they are present in the scope or not:
varinst_all.txt, varinst_class.txt
You can use the runtime prognosis feature to select a TB where ICO could be most
effective in improving coverage. The prognosis feature is enabled using the following
runtime option:
+ntb_solver_bias_prognosis=1
For a given TB, this feature allows you to select the best modes for coverage convergence
and helps to minimize the evaluation and deployment time.
Specifically, this feature does the following:
• Collects the TB information regarding
◦ Bias ability of variables and values, that is, how much freedom is provided by
constraints for the random variables to take various random values.
◦ Constraint density, that is, how many constraints per variable. This provides insight
to how constrained the TB is.
◦ Number of randomizations, number of random variables, and number of random
instances per tests.
• Saves the TB information per test seed compactly in each record database per test.
• Runs the crg utility post regression on the records created by the various simulation
runs enabled with prognosis feature and creates a prognosis report (CSV format),
which shows the information per test seed, aggregated per test, and per regression
run.

Dumping Failure Signatures
ICO can dump failure signatures during simulation when you run it in bug-finding mode.
A failure signature is a normalized form of an error message in which dynamic content ,
such as simulation time and data values, has been removed. As a result, multiple error
messages that report the same underlying problem collapse to a single signature.
This feature helps you do the following:
• Identify unique failure patterns in bug-finding runs.
• Group repeated error messages that differ only in dynamic content.
• Triage and count unique failures more efficiently.

Dumping Failure Signatures
You enable this feature through existing simv runtime options. ICO writes the failure
signature data to the fail_sig.txt file in the store record directory. No change is
required at compilation.
• Use Model
• Failure Signature
• Example
• Counting Unique Failure Signatures
ICO dumps failure signatures when you run simulation with either of the following settings:
• +ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=bugs
• +ntb_solver_bias_fail_predict=<nonzero_value>
The following is the overall use model:
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=<bug|bug2|bug3|bugs|bal|cov|nob|rca>
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record>
+ntb_solver_bias_replay=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_fail_regex=<regex>
-l <simv.log>
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=<bug|bug2|bug3|bugs|bal|cov|nob|rca>
Selects the ICO biasing strategy for the run. Use the bugs value to enable the bug-finding
strategy that triggers failure signature dumping.
Enables failure prediction. Specify a non-zero value to trigger failure signature dumping
independently of the strategy mode.
ICO dumps failure signatures only when
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=bugs is set or
+ntb_solver_bias_fail_predict is set to a non-zero value. When ICO
detects failures under one of these supported modes, it writes failure signature
information to fail_sig.txt in the store record directory.

Dumping Failure Signatures
Failure Signature
When failure signature dumping is enabled, ICO writes the signature data to the following
file in the store record directory:
<store_record>/fail_sig.txt
For example, if the store record directory is wdir/test_1.store_record, ICO writes the
signature data to:
wdir/test_1.store_record/fail_sig.txt
For each failure observed in a run, ICO writes two lines to fail_sig.txt:
M: <err_message>
S: <err_signature>
Where:
• M: records the actual error message observed during simulation.
• S: records the corresponding normalized failure signature.
ICO derives the failure signature from the original error message by stripping out dynamic
content. Dynamic content includes values that change from one run or one occurrence to
another, such as simulation time, line offsets, and data values. As a result, multiple error
messages that share the same underlying failure pattern map to a single signature. This
lets you group and count unique failure patterns rather than individual error occurrences.
The following example shows the contents of fail_sig.txt for a run in which four error
messages were observed. The messages differ in simulation time and in the reported
illegal state value, but they all share the same underlying failure pattern and therefore map
to the same signature:
% cat wdir/test_1.store_record/fail_sig.txt
M: UVM_ERROR ./Source/CovBias/CovBias399.models/top.sv(79) @ 19: reporter
[[BAD] STATE] Illegal state: 05
S:
uvm_error./source/covbias/covbias.models/top.sv()@:reporter[[bad]state]i
llegalstate:
M: UVM_ERROR ./Source/CovBias/CovBias399.models/top.sv(79) @ 37: reporter
[[BAD] STATE] Illegal state: 25
S:
uvm_error./source/covbias/covbias.models/top.sv()@:reporter[[bad]state]i
llegalstate:
M: UVM_ERROR ./Source/CovBias/CovBias399.models/top.sv(79) @ 67: reporter
[[BAD] STATE] Illegal state: 25

Improved Debugging of ICO Exposed Failures

uvm_error./source/covbias/covbias.models/top.sv()@:reporter[[bad]state]i
llegalstate:
M: UVM_ERROR ./Source/CovBias/CovBias399.models/top.sv(79) @ 123:
reporter [[BAD] STATE] Illegal state: 05

Counting Unique Failure Signatures
To count the number of unique failure signatures recorded for a run, filter the lines that
begin with S:, sort them, and count the unique entries. For example:
% cat wdir/test_1.store_record/fail_sig.txt | grep "^S:" | sort -u | wc
-l
In this example, although the run produced four error messages, all four map to the same
signature, so the count of unique failure signatures is 1.
Improved Debugging of ICO Exposed Failures
ICO enables reporting of the following information for the delta values of variables during
simulation in a log file:
• Generation time (vcs time)
• Randomize serial
• Location
• File/Line of random class
• Stimulus variable name
• Stimulus variable values
This feature allows the tracing of variables that might have caused divergences in the
simulation. You can use this feature during replay to improve debugging.
You can use the following runtime options to enable this feature:
• +ntb_solver_bias_debug_info=<level>

Replaying Incomplete Tests Using the Original Load CDB and With Shared CDB Update
Replaying Incomplete Tests Using the Original Load CDB and
With Shared CDB Update
In a regression, if some tests are terminated by the grid manager (for example, due to
timeouts), you can relaunch the same test using the +ntb_solver_bias_replay=1 option,
but it does not update the shared CDB.
However, if you like to relaunch the test and update the shared CDB, you can use the
+ntb_solver_bias_replay=2 runtime option as shown below:
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=./shared +ntb_solver_bias_replay=2
+ntb_solver_bias_replay=2
Load from given load_record and not from shared record (like option value 1), but
updates the shared record (if provided) at the end of the run.
When this option is specified, ICO displays a note that there is replay with shared record
update.
VCS Intelligent Coverage Optimization is enabled with AutoBiasIntra
+ DistMerge + Replay feature(s).

Incremental Recording and Merging
ICO supports incremental (non-accumulating) recording of each run in the cdb using the
+ntb_solver_bias_incr_mode simulation option. Incremental recording allows you to
bias the contribution of some tests differently than others during merging, which can also
improve the overall diversity.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_incr_mode=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<recordShared> …
+ntb_solver_bias_incr_mode=<0|1|2> (default: 0)
0: No incremental recording 1: Enables incremental recording 2: Enables incremental
recording and biased merging

Configuring Shared CDB for Congested Network
You can use the following command to generate runtime report:
% crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -incr -merge <mdir> -report <rpt>
-incr
Specifies to use incremental information for merging, report generation, and get the
difference between two coverage databases.
% crg -dir inc_store -incr -merge mergedCdb -report crgReport -diff
Figure 71 shows improved diversity scores with no change in the coverage score when the
+ntb_solver_bias_incr_mode=2 option is used at runtime.
Figure 71 Viewing Improved Diversity Scores
Configuring Shared CDB for Congested Network
Performance of ICO, measured in terms of diversification of stimulus, also diminishes
when huge test run data cannot be merged online as the subsequent test runs of the
regression cannot exploit the new information learned. Also, congestion is more severe
when the regression size is big.
To address this issue, ICO supports a mechanism to configure the shared cdb at the time
of its initialization using the -shared init_sfs crg runtime option. This feature helps you
to mitigate online merging failures and improves the performance of ICO.

Optimizing Load Record Directory Size
You can use the following command to configure shared coverage database to address
merging failures due to congestion:
% crg -dir <shared_record> -shared <init|init_sfs>
Specifies cdb database <dir1>.
-shared init
Initializes shared record <dir> for normal file server (nfs).
-shared init_sfs
Initializes shared record <dir> for slow file server (sfs).
Examples:
% crg -dir sh1 -shared init_sfs
The sh1 directory is initialized for shared recording and configured for slow file server.
% crg -dir sh2 -shared init
The sh2 directory is initialized for shared recording.
Optimizing Load Record Directory Size
The load record (load_cdb) file allows you to replay the failing tests at any given point
of time. Large file sizes of the load_cdb files require excessive memory to save them for
later use.
To create and store the optimized load record, you can use the following runtime options:
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt=<load_record_opt>
simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_clean=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt=<load_record_opt>

Optimizing Load Record Directory Size
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=<0|1>
Creates optimized load record load_record_opt file when set to 1. Default is 0.
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt=<load_record_opt>
Specifies the location of the optimized load record. For default location information, see
Location of load_record_opt.

Making Load Record Optimal by Default
Making Load Record Optimal by Default
In a distributed shared record setting, for each simv run enabled with ICO, a backup load
record directory is created which is the snapshot of the shared record. This backup load
record can be used to replay the simv run.
The +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=1 option can be used at runtime to
reduce the backup load size, however the usage of the optimized backup load requires a
change in the script file during replay, that is, point the load record to the optimized backup
load.
The +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=2 runtime option allows you to
overwrite the backup load record with the optimized backup load record in the shared
mode without the need to change the script during replay. This feature allows you to make
the load record optimal by default avoiding the need to change the load record setting for
replay.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_auto_config=2
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt=<load_record_opt>
where,
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=<0|1|2>
1: Enables creating optimized load record.
2: Enables 1 and enables overwriting the load record with the optimized load record in the
shared mode.
• The +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=2 option only impacts

+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=shared +ntb_solver_bias_test_name=test
+ntb_random_seed=100 +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=2

In contrast,
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=2 +ntb_solver_bias_wdir=wdir
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=shared +ntb_solver_bias_test_name=test
+ntb_random_seed=100 +ntb_solver_bias_load_record_opt_enable=1
This creates an optimized load_record under wdir/test_100.load_record_opt and also
creates wdir/test_100.load_record.
For replaying, you must add the replay option as follows (no change in behavior):
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=2 +ntb_solver_bias_wdir=wdir
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name=test +ntb_random_seed=100
+ntb_solver_bias_replay=1
Reporting Recommendation to Purge the Shared CDB or Use
New DB
The shared cdb can be reused across regressions and across changing models. To use
across models, it is generally recommended to purge the stale variables from the cdb. Too
many stale variables can increase the resident memory size of the cdb during the run. ICO
provides a measure that can be used to decide when to purge the shared cdb or when to
use a new DB.
You can use the -stat crg runtime option to report fraction of the resident memory that is
relevant (that is, in the scope). You can use that information to decide whether to purge or
use a new DB based on if the fraction is above a threshold or not respectively.

Reporting Recommendation to Purge the Shared CDB or Use New DB
% crg -dir <cdb_record> -stat -purge_untag <scope|reset> -purge <inFile>
-work <wdir> -purgeX <exFile>
Specifies cdb database <dir1>.
-stat
Prints cdb statistics in <work_dir>/stat.txt.
-purge_untag <scope|biased>
Purges variables that are not tagged as scope or biased.
-purge <inFile>
Purges variables in <inFile>.
-purgeX <exFile>
Purges variables excluding those in <exFile>.
• Options specified in syntax (other than -stat) are unaffected, but affect
-stat.
• Other options (not specified in syntax) are unaffected, and do not affect
-stat.

mywork/snap_kG0z9V.log)

Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
Snapshot of record is taken at mywork/snap_37mVYj (details logged in
mywork/snap_37mVYj.log)
Stat Report generated in ./WORK/stat.txt

% cat WORK/stat.txt
Number of Total Variables = 15956
Number of Scope Variables = 15956 (100.00%)
Number of Biased Variables = 4855 (30.43%)
Total Variable Memory Footprint = 2.00Mb
Scope Variable Memory Footprint = 2.00Mb (100.00%)
Biased Variable Memory Footprint = 0.88Mb (44.01%)
Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
Illegal bins can be due to soft constraints, static parameters, state dependent values,
variables that are switched off for randomization, or variables that are unreachable due to
combination of hard constraints of one or more random variables.
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Categorizing Illegal Bins
• Grouping Illegal Bins
Categorizing Illegal Bins
Managing huge number of illegal bins can be difficult. It can also lead to oversight and
user may miss a real over-constraint. The categorization of illegal bins can help you
to prioritize and help manage large number of illegal bins for potential over-constraint
analysis. Without categorization, it is not easy to know the reason without individually
clicking the hyperlink and looking into the blocking constraints.
ICO supports categorization of illegal bins by tagging each illegal bin with attributes SOFT,
UNR, ROFF, and PARA, and prioritizing them. This feature can be enabled by using the
-illegal_attrruntime option in the post-simulation crg utility. Also, you must run the
simulation with RCA enabled, preferably with +ntb_solver_bias_rca=3.
You can use the post runtime option -illegal_attr to annotate CRG HTML and text
report with illegal bin attributes.
% crg -dir <record> -report crgReport -illegal_attr -format both

Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
RCA Visualization
There is no change in the format of the HTML report when -illegal_attr is enabled.
However, each illegal bin with a hyper-link will have one of the following attributes:
ILLEGAL::SOFT - If the value is blocked by at least one soft constraint.
ILLEGAL::UNR - If the value is unreachable due to the combination of hard constraints of
one or more random variables.
ILLEGAL::ROFF - If the value is blocked by hard constraints with at least one random
variable whose rand mode is off.
ILLEGAL::PARA - If the value is blocked by hard constraints due to the presence of
parameter or state values, with no rand-mode-off variables.
These four attributes are shown in the sorted order (using up/down arrow) from top to
bottom in the order of priority, as shown in the following figure:
Figure 72 Categorization of Illegal Bins

Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
Grouping Illegal Bins
Managing huge number of illegal bins with same RCA reason can be difficult. Grouping
of illegal bins with identical reasons can help you to avoid the manual effort of inspecting
each bin with same reason as another bin. It also helps to reduce the disk footprint
significantly by eliminating repeat information.
ICO supports grouping of illegal bins by tagging illegal bins with identical reasons with
G<#>. This feature can be enabled by using the -illegal_group runtime option in the
post-simulation crg utility. This feature can also be combined with attributes enabled by
adding the -illegal_attr runtime option.
The -illegal_group runtime option annotates CRG HTML and text report with illegal bin
group tags.
% crg -dir <record> -report crgReport -illegal_attr -illegal_group
-format both
RCA Visualization
There is no change in the format of the HTML report when -illegal_group is enabled.
When used without the -illegal_attr option, illegal bins are grouped based on common
reasons without any attributes as shown in the following figure:
Figure 73 Grouping of Illegal Bins
The RCA file is generated per group as shown in the following figure. This saves the disk
footprint.

Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins
Figure 74 RCA File
However, when both options -illegal_group and -illegal_attr are specified, group
tags are shown along with attributes SOFT, UNR, ROFF, and PARA, as shown in the following
figures. The number of groups is not impacted by the -illegal_attr option.
Figure 75 Group Tags Displayed Along With Attributes

Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge File
Figure 76 RCA File With Group Tags Displayed Along With Attributes

Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge
File
By default, all random variables with constraints are recorded, and biased if bias mode
is selected. The simv runtime option +ntb_solver_bias_scope_file provides a list of
variables for recording and biasing and ignores the rest. However, it is not possible to
exclude variables from recording/biasing. The workaround is to remove variables from the
full list of variables, which is not very user friendly.
Similar issue exists when purging a list of variables from the cdb database. The crg option
-purge <file> allows you to purge variables listed in the file, but you cannot exclude
variables from purging.
ICO supports the following exclusions to make the usage easier:
• Exclusion of variables from recording/biasing in the scope file using the
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file runtime option. For more information, see Excluding
Variables from Recording and Biasing.
• Exclusion of variables from purging in the crg purge file using the -purgeX crg option.
For more information, see Excluding Variables from Purging.
Excluding Variables from Recording and Biasing
The following is the syntax to exclude variables from recording and biasing:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile>
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file=<scopeXFile>

Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge File
+ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile>
Restricts recording and biasing of variables to those specified in the scopeFile.
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file=<scopeXFile>

Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge File
+ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile>
Restricts recording and biasing of variables to those specified in the scopeFile.
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file=<scopeXFile>
Excludes variables specified in the scopeXFile from recording and biasing.
If both options are provided, then the recording and biasing variables are the
intersection of the variables specified by scopeFile and those NOT specified in
scopeXFile.
Excluding Variables from Purging
% crg -dir <cdb> -purge <scopeXFile> -purgeX <scopeFile>
-purge <scopeXFile>
Purge variables specified in the scopeXFile.
-purgeX <scopeFile>
Purge variables excluding those specified in the scopeFile.
If both options are provided, then the variables retained after purging are the
intersection of the variables specified by scopeFile and those NOT specified in
scopeXFile.

Improving Usability With Mnemonic Strategy Options
ICO improves the usability of the strategy options with mnemonics such as bug, cov, rca,
and so on. This feature helps to easily remember the options and avoids setting of the
combinations of runtime options for various strategies.
The following is the syntax:
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=<bug|bug2|bug3|cov|bal|nob|rca>
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record>
+ntb_solver_bias_replay=<0|1>

Improving Usability With Mnemonic Strategy Options

with Aggressive Bug Focus.

strategy mode option, that is

strategy mode option, that is

+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=rca

Also, ICO creates the vcs_ico.config file under the +ntb_solver_bias_store_record
directory with all the runtime options and their values.
• Each strategy is exclusive. If there are multiple strategies, only the first
strategy is selected.
• The strategy keyword matching the prefix of a specified
strategy (assuming it is a longer string) is inferred. For example,
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=covg|coverage is inferred as cov
strategy.

• If the specified strategy does not have a prefix match to any keywords, it is
ignored. There is no default strategy.
• The strategy keywords are case insensitive. For example, CoVg refers to the
cov strategy.

Integrity Check of CDB
The CDB can get corrupted due to many reasons such as file system issues, distributed
merging, and program bug.
ICO allows you to check if the CDB is corrupted or not and reports when if it is corrupted. It
prints the checksum of the CDB in the report. This feature is enabled using the -check_db
crg option.
% crg -dir <dir1> -dir <dir2> -check_db -merge out -work <wdir>
Specifies cdb database <dir1>.
-merge out
Output cdb.
-check_db
Checks each input cdb and output cdb (if specified). Prints check db output in <wdir>/
check_db.txt.

Reporting Warning Messages When CDB is Empty or Not Created
Reporting Warning Messages When CDB is Empty or Not Created
When the testbench does not have any randomization call, or if the constraint random
variable to be recorded does not exist, then the store record is not generated. Similarly,
when the scope file excludes all constraint random variables, or rand mode is off for all the
constraint rand variables, the store record is created but is empty. In these scenarios, ICO
issues a warning message that provides information on why the CDB/prognosis report is
not generated.
The following scenarios describe this feature in detail:
• Scenario-1: No Valid Constraint Random Variable in the Testbench
• Scenario-2: Valid Constraint Random Variable is Not in Scope
• Scenario-3: No Valid Constraint Random Variable Enabled for Randomization
Scenario-1: No Valid Constraint Random Variable in the
Testbench
Example 31 test.v
//no constraint rand variable
rand bit signed [10:0] x;
end
Command-line:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=1 or
+ntb_solver_bias_prognosis_config=1
Warning Message:
Warning-[CNST-SBSRN] Solver bias store record not created
No constraint random variable to record.
Please make sure to randomize and add constraints on random variables.
The CNST-ICO note message is not printed at the start. The [CNST-SBSRN]
warning message is printed at the end of the simulation.

Reporting Warning Messages When CDB is Empty or Not Created
Scenario-2: Valid Constraint Random Variable is Not in Scope
Example 32 test.v
class cls1;
rand bit signed [10:0] x;
constraint cons { x >= 4;}
cls1 obj1 = new;
obj1.randomize;
end
Example 33 scope.txt (exclusion file)
*:*:*:x
Command-line:
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file=./scope.txt
Warning Message:
…
$finish at simulation time 0

Warning-[CNST-SBSRE] Solver bias store record empty
No constraint random variable in scope.
Please 'check scope option and file format'.
The scope does not impact prognosis, hence this scenario does not occur for
prognosis.
Scenario-3: No Valid Constraint Random Variable Enabled for
Randomization
Example 34 test.v
//disabled constraint rand variable
class cls1;

Generating and Using CDB Across Different Platforms
ICO allows cdb to be generated and used across different platforms. That is, cdb
generated by a 32-bit binary can be used by a 64-bit binary, and vice-versa. Consider the
following:
• L is the VCS binary
• PROG_CDB<A>_<V> is the prognosis cdb generated by any version V <= L in platform A
• PROG_RPT<B> is the prognosis crg report generated by the VCS binary L in platform B
Therefore, if PROG_CDB<A>_<V> is specified and PROG_RPT<B> is generated, then for
all A, B that belongs to the 32-bit, 64-bit, aarch64 binaries and V <= L , the generated
PROG_RPT<B> reports are identical.

Generating and Using CDB Across Different Platforms
Similarly, consider the following:
• AUTO_CDB<A>_<V> is the autobias cdb generated by any version V <= L of ICO binary
in platform A
