Name Mapping Between SPICE View and Digital View for XMR in RTVS
Name Mapping Between SPICE View and Digital View for XMR in
RTVS
An RTVS instance has both SPICE and digital views. When you write language XMR (in
RTL/HDL files), then the tokens in the XMR may not match with the instance or net names
in the RTVS SPICE view (assuming that the tokens written in XMR are as per the RTVS
digital view). Therefore, XMR token name and the corresponding node/port/instance name
in the SPICE view can be different. Discrepancies in naming conventions, case sensitivity,
and bus formats can lead to errors or manual intervention.
VCS supports handling of name mapping between the SPICE and digital views of an
RTVS instance. This enhancement only supports X-prefix, case sensitivity, port map, and
bus format consideration for the XMR token resolution between the SPICE and digital
views in RTVS flow. This feature automates the name-mapping process, reducing errors
and improving efficiency.
To enable this feature, use the-adopt rtvs_xmr compile option.
The following scenarios are considered for name mapping:
• X-prefix: In certain SPICE netlists, instance names start with the character x.
However, the equivalent names in the digital view do not have this x prefix, leading to a
discrepancy between the SPICE and digital view instance names.
For example: An XMR, in HDL, in the digital view is represented as top.dut.i1.n1.
However, the same XMR in the SPICE view is represented as top.dut.xi1.n1.
• Case sensitivity: SPICE names are either case-sensitive or insensitive, while Verilog
is consistently case-sensitive. This difference in case sensitivity leads to discrepancies
in instance or node names between these views.
For example: An XMR, in HDL, for the digital view is top.dut.I1.N1. However, the
equivalent XMR for the SPICE view is top.dut.i1.n1.
• Port map: The mapping of ports between SPICE and digital views is accomplished
using the port_map command in the mixed-signal control file. The tool takes into
account this port map information when determining the token name in the SPICE view.
• Bus format: The bus_format command in the mixed-signal control file allows the
user to treat a set of nets in a SPICE sub-circuit as a vector or array object. The tool
considers this bus_format option when resolving XMR token for the SPICE view.

Name Mapping Between SPICE View and Digital View for XMR in RTVS
Understanding the Name Mapping Process
The steps in the name mapping process are as follows:
1. The XMRs in RTL/HDL files are written as per the digital view of the RTVS instance.
2. Besides, VCS tool queries the analog engine to check if an XMR token exists in the
SPICE view. The analog engine returns the actual name of the node or instance
(corresponding to this token) as it appears in the SPICE view.
3. The VCS tool uses the actual token names provided by the analog engine to resolve
the XMR for the SPICE view. This ensures that the XMRs are correctly mapped and
functional for the RTVS SPICE view as well.
The following are the XMR resolution examples for RTVS.
Original scenario
assign sig_val = top.dut.I1.IN1; // dut being RTVS instance and inside
the SPICE view

Automatic Handling of Verilog Force on Mixed-Signal Nets
The force statement in SystemVerilog is a continuous procedural assignment on a net.
When you apply a force statement to a net, it overrides all other drivers to that net.
In simulation, a force statement is used in conjunction with a release statement. The
release statement ends the driver override that was applied on the net through the force
statement.
The behavior of Verilog force/release on a mixed-signal net is now enhanced such that the
Verilog force becomes the only driver for the Spice net. That is, in case of a Verilog force,
the force value is sent to the analog side, and the analog engine considers it as the only
contribution to the respective Spice net. This force value is maintained on the Spice net
until a Verilog release happens on that mixed-signal net.
With this enhancement, a force command is applied the same way as in Verilog, by fully
overriding other analog drivers. When a force is applied to a digital segment of a mixed-
signal net, this information is passed to the analog side to ‘force’ an analog segment of the
net. This tracing also works in the backward (a -> d) direction.
To enable this feature, you must use the -adopt msv_force_release compile option.
The following examples describe this feature in detail:
• Verilog Force on a Spice Net
• Verilog Force on a Digital Net Connected to Spice
• Verilog Force on a Digital Net Connected to Spice Through Select
To understand process to determine the forced voltage, see the Specifying a Voltage
Reference for Interface Elements section of the VCS® PrimeSim™ AMS User Guide.

Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
VCS MSV supports SystemVerilog-Spice flow having a leaf-level Verilog-AMS
(VAMS) module to be used as an electrical instrument. You must use the -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams compile option to enable the leaf-level Verilog-AMS support. This
feature only supports VAMS block at the leaf level of the hierarchy in the SV-Spice flow.

Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
Figure 67 Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support
This feature allows leaf-level VAMS source files to be used as electrical instruments. A
leaf-level VAMS does not allow any hierarchy or analog primitives.
The following is the use model of leaf-level Verilog-AMS support in VCS two-step and
three-step flows:
Two-step flow:
% vcs +verilogamsext+.vams test.vams -sverilog test.v -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams -ad=test.init
Three-step flow:
% vlogan -sverilog test.v
% vlogan -ams test.vams
% vcs -ad=test.init -sverilog top -adopt msv_with_leaf_vams
Consider the following files:
test.sv
reg in , out ;
initial in =0 ;

SystemVerilog does not support connecting signals to ports with different types. To
address this, VCS supports automatic insertion of converter module using the -xlrm
enable_converter compile option. This option allows you to connect a signal to a port of
different type. You must provide the converter modules and converter rules using a VCS
opt-config file.
To enhance the precision of type conversion, VCS allows you to override the parameters
of a set of auto-inserted converter instances in the design. This is specifically important
for multi-voltage designs where different blocks operate at different voltage levels, and
VCS may insert the same converter module inside multiple such blocks. To configure the

instances of this converter module based on the voltage levels of the respective blocks,
VCS allows you to override the converter parameter values using the ams_cm commands.
For bidirectional ports, the type-conversion mechanism is supported through the Super-
Net functionality. VCS now allows you to use the ams_cm commands to configure the
parameters of the converters inside a Super-Net. This feature allows you to override the
parameters of the converter instances within a Super-Net using the ams_cm commands.
This enhancement improves the ease-of-use of Super-Net for multi-voltage designs
and efficiently resolves conflicts of net types in SystemVerilog. You must use the -xlrm
enable_converter compile option to enable this feature.
You must also use the +optconfigfile+config.cfg compile option to specify
bidirectional converters using the config file. Following is the syntax of the config.cfg
configuration file:
config.cfg:
enable_bidir_converter;
converter <src> <dst> <sv converter module>;
connect <src>, <srcN> resolveto <MAR>;
scoped parametrization with ams_cm
converter logic v_wire_sum logic_to_v_wire_sum;
converter logic wrealsum logic_to_wrealsum;
converter v_wire_sum logic v_wire_sum_to_logic;
converter wrealsum logic wrealsum_to_logic;

The following topics describe this feature in detail:
• Bidirectional-Island
• Most Accurate Representative Type
• Bidirectional-Island Processing: Super-Net Formation
• Configuring Unidirectional Converters in a Super-Net Using the ams_cm Commands

Bidirectional-Island
Bidirectional-island for an INOUT port is identified by the complete set of net segments
that are directly or indirectly connected to the port signal through port-connections and
aliases.
For example, in the following figure, there are two bidirectional-islands: Bidir-Island
#1 and Bidir-Island #2 . Both bidirectional-islands contain three different types of
interconnected net segments: wire, wrealmin, and wrealmax.
Figure 68 Multi-Voltage Design
Most Accurate Representative Type
Consider a design with a set of net segments interconnected by INOUT ports and aliases.
Let the types of these segments are NT1, NT2, …, NTn and are different from each other.
Out of these n different types, if the NTx type is most accurate, then NTx is considered as
the Most Accurate Representative (MAR) type.
Bidirectional-Island Processing: Super-Net Formation
In a bidirectional-island, all net segments of the same type are aliased to form one single
net for that respective type.
The following figure is an example of super-net formation for a bidirectional-island.

Figure 69 Super-Net Formation for a Bidirectional-Island
The bidirectional-island in Figure 69 contains three different net types: NT1, NT2, and NT3.
• NT1: This net type has two segments. These two segments are aliased to form a single
net of type NT1.
• NT2: This net type has two segments. These two segments are aliased to form a single
net of type NT2.
• NT3: This type has only one segment.
In Figure 69, after aliasing there are three nets in the bidirectional-island (one net for each
type). Also, two net segments, connected through INOUT ports having different types, are
disconnected from each other. This is shown as Disconnection-1, Disconnection-2,
and so on in Figure 69.
After MAR information is available for a bidirectional-island, the Super-Net can be formed
for this island. If NT3 is the MAR in this example, the Super-Net contains the following
unidirectional converters (unidirectional converters from each non-MAR to MAR, and vice
versa):
• Non-MAR to MAR ( NT1_to_NT3 and NT3_to_NT1)
• MAR to Non-MAR ( NT2_to_NT3 and NT3_to_NT2)

This process ensures that the bidirectional-island is organized into distinct nets for each
type with proper handling of disconnections and the formation of a Super-Net based on the
MAR.
Configuring Unidirectional Converters in a Super-Net Using the
ams_cm Commands
You can specify the ams_cm commands at net-level, instance-level, and cell-level.
For each Super-Net, VCS collects the ams_cm commands that are applicable to each
“Disconnection” location (where two nets of different types are originally connected
through an INOUT port) within that Super-Net.
For example, in Figure 69, there are four “Disconnection” locations in the Super-Net.
For each of these “Disconnection” locations, VCS identifies a set of applicable ams_cm
commands. These commands are later merged using the priority order and conflict
resolution rules as follows:
• Inst-node or node-based ams_cm command has the highest priority, followed by inst-
based, cell-node based, and cell-based.
• Non-overlapping ams_cm commands are merged or unified.
• For conflicting ams_cm commands, the command with the higher line number in the opt-
config file takes precedence.
After prioritization and conflict resolution, a single unified (final) ams_cm command is
established for a Super-Net. VCS uses this final ams_cm command to configure the
unidirectional converters within that Super-Net.
In Figure 68, there are two voltage regions: 2.1 voltage region and 3.5 voltage region. As
there are two bidirectional islands in this design, there are two Super-Nets. To configure
these two Super-Nets , the following ams_cm commands can be used:
enable_bidir_converter ;

converter logic wrealmax logic_to_wrealmax ;
converter wrealmax logic wrealmax_to_logic ;

converter wrealmin wrealmax wrealmin_to_wrealmax ;
converter wrealmax wrealmin wrealmax_to_wrealmin ;

connect logic, wrealmin, wrealmax resolveto wrealmax ;

the tb.DUT.MID35 hierarchy

Consider the following opt-config file (config.cfg). This example describes a situation
where ams_cm with inst is specified and how to interpret its usage.
converter logic wrealsum logic_to_wrealsum;
converter v_wire_sum logic v_wire_sum_to_logic;
converter wrealsum logic wrealsum_to_logic;
converter v_wire_sum wrealsum v_wire_sum_to_wrealsum;

enable_bidir_converter;
enable_local_converter;

connect logic, snps_msv_nettype_pkg::v_wire_sum,
snps_msv_nettype_pkg::wrealsum resolveto
snps_msv_nettype_pkg::v_wire_sum;

ams_cm vthi=3.0 inst=top.t1;

Two Super-Nets are inserted inside top.t1 for the connections to the top.t1.r1 and
top.t1.r2 instances. Therefore, the unidirectional converters of both the Super-Nets
get vthi = 3.0 because ams_cm vthi=3.0 inst=top.t1 is specified in the opt-config
file. Since no Super-Net is inserted below the hierarchy top.t1.r1, no unidirectional

converters of any Super-Net gets vthi=4.0 even though ams_cm vthi=4.0 inst=top.r1
is specified.
The following are the limitations of the super-net support for multi-voltage designs feature:
• Converter configuration through Unified Power Format (UPF) supply specification is not
supported.
• Verilog-AMS, Partition Compile, and Parallel Compile flows are not supported.
The type-coercion feature allows a SystemVerilog generic interconnect or a wire-
interconnect to be converted to wreal or SystemVerilog nettype based on its connectivity
in the Real Number Model (RNM) designs. Type-coercion is generally applied across the
entire design. However, you may want to turn off type-coercion in some scopes based on
the design style.
VCS now supports scope-based type-coercion in the RNM designs using the
ams_coercion commands. This feature allows you to confine the effects of type-coercion
to specific parts of the design hierarchy. This improves the performance of type-coercion
and converter insertion by limiting the boundaries where type-coercion is applied.
The following topics describe this feature in detail:
• Rules for Type-Coercion in Scope-Based Contexts
• Scope-Based Type-Coercion Use Cases
• Scope-Based Type-Coercion Reporting
You can use the following syntax in the VCS opt-config file to enable or disable type-
coercion feature for libraries, cells, or instances in the RNM designs:
ams_coercion [ -lib lib | -cell {cell1, cell2, …}] | [ -inst
{full-hier-path-to-instance1, full-hier-path-to-instance2, …}] -mode < ON
| OFF > | [-override];

The ams_coercion command is supported in both single compile and partition compile
flows.
The following table describes the arguments of the ams_coercion command.
Argument Description
-mode <ON | OFF > It is a mandatory argument.
Enables or disables type-coercion in scopes of a design.
The scope information is specified using the -cell or -inst
argument.
[ -lib library-name ] It is an optional argument.
Specifies the name of a logical library. It must be accompanied
with the -cell argument.
If -lib is provided, then only that specific library is searched to
find a cell that is specified through the -cell argument.
If -lib argument is not provided, all the available libraries are
searched to find the cell that is specified through the -cell
argument.
[ -cell { cell1, cell2, …} ] It is an optional argument.
Specifies a valid list of one or more cell names where
type-coercion is turned on or off.
A cell is a Verilog/Verilog-AMS module, SV interface, or a
SPICE sub-circuit. A cell name is specified with or without the
-lib argument.
If a cell name is specified with -lib, then the ams_coercion
command is applied only to the matching cell from that specific
library.
When the cell name is specified without -lib, then the
ams_coercion command is applied to all the matching cells
from all the available libraries.
Use either the -cell or -inst argument in the ams_coercion
The -cell and -inst arguments cannot be used together
in the same command.
[ -inst {
full-hierarchical-path-to-
instance1,
full-hierarchical-path-to-
instance2, … } ]
It is an optional argument.
Specifies a valid list of absolute hierarchical paths to instances.
Such instances can be of type Verilog/Verilog-AMS module
instances , SV interface instances or SPICE sub-circuit
instances.
Use either the -cell or -inst argument in the ams_coercion
The -cell and -inst arguments cannot be used together
in the same command.

Argument Description
[-override] This is an optional argument.
It can be used with both -inst and -cell type commands.
Commands with the -override option override commands
without the -override option in the same hierarchy.
ams_coercion -mode off -cell leaf;
ams_coercion -mode on -inst top.mid1;
In this example, coercion is enabled within top.mid1 hierarchy except for the instances of
cell leaf. Coercion is also disabled for all other instances of the cell leaf.
Rules for Type-Coercion in Scope-Based Contexts
The rules for type-coercion in scope-based contexts are as follows:
• If a SystemVerilog generic-interconnect is found in a scope where type-coercion is
turned OFF, then by default the type of this generic-interconnect is considered as wire.
• The ams_coercion commands are additive in nature.
• The ams_coercion command is applied transitively downward through the design
hierarchy. A command specified at an upper scope is inherited by the hierarchically
lower level scopes.
• The ams_coercion command specified at a lower level of the design hierarchy
overrides the ams_coercion command coming from its upper layer.
• If two ams_coercion commands point to the same scope, then the instance level
ams_coercion command (with -inst argument) has higher priority than the cell level
ams_coercion command (with -cell argument).
The following rules applies to the ams_override command with -override option.
• If multiple ams_coercion commands with the -override option are applied to different
levels in the same hierarchy, lower level -override command is applied and the
higher the level -override command is ignored for that particular hierarchy. A warning
message is issued in such cases.

Scope-Based Type-Coercion Use Cases
The scope-based type-coercion is implemented in the following use cases:
Refer to the following example to understand these uses cases.
Use Case 1: Additive Nature of ams_coercion Commands
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 };
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid2 };
The two commands are equivalent to the following single command:
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1, top.mid2 };
Use Case 2: Transitive Nature of ams_coercion Command
ams_coercion -mode OFF -inst { top.mid1 };
Type-coercion is turned OFF for the instance top.mid1 and the hierarchy below.
Use Case 3: Lower-Level ams_coercion Command Overrides the Command From its
Upper Level
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid;
ams_coercion -mode ON -cell bot;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1.leaf1 };
The first command disables type-coercion for all instances of the mid cell and its sub-
hierarchy, except for the following two scenarios:
• When the second command enables type-coercion for all instances of the bot cell
( top.mid1.bot1 and top.mid2.bot1), thereby overriding the higher level first
command for this particular scope.
• When the third command enables type-coercion specifically for the instance
top.mid1.leaf1, thereby overriding the higher level first command for this particular
scope.
Use Case 4: Instance Level Commands Take Priority Over Cell Level Commands

ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 };
The first command disables type-coercion for all instances of the mid cell and their sub-
hierarchy.
The second command explicitly enables type-coercion for the instance top.mid1,
overriding the cell level command.
Use Case 5: Conflicting ams_coercion Commands
ams_coercion -mode ON -cell mid_mod;
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid_mod;///Error
A conflict arises when contradictory commands are issued for the same cell. In this case,
an error is generated to prevent ambiguity.
Use Case 6: Usage of the -override Option
• Scenario 1: Instance Level -override Command
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell leaf;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 } -override;
The second command overrides the first, enabling type-coercion for the top.mid1
hierarchy, including instances of the leaf cell within it (for example, top.mid1.leaf1).
However, type-coercion remains disabled for other instances of the leaf cell (For
example, top.mid2.leaf1)
• Scenario 2: Cell Level -override Command
ams_coercion -mode off -cell mid -override;
ams_coercion -mode on -inst top.mid1;
The first command overrides the second, disabling type-coercion for the top.mid1
hierarchy and all other instances of the mid cell.
• Scenario 3: Inst vs Cell -override Commands in the Same Scope
ams_coercion -mode off -cell mid -override;
ams_coercion -mode on -inst top.mid1 -override;
Coercion is enabled for the top.mid1 hierarchy due to the instance level command. A
warning indicates that the cell level command is not applied to the top.mid1 hierarchy.
However, the cell level command still applies to the top.mid2 hierarchy.
• Scenario 4: Multiple -override Commands at Different Levels of the Same Hierarchy
ams_coercion -mode off -cell mid -override;
ams_coercion -mode on -inst top.mid1.leaf1 -override

Coercion is enabled for the top.mid1.leaf1 hierarchy because the lower level
command is applied to it. A warning indicates that the higher-level command is not
applied to the top.mid1.leaf1 hierarchy. However, the higher-level command still
applies to the rest of the top.mid1 instance hierarchy and the top.mid2 instance
hierarchy, thereby disabling coercion for those scopes.
Use Case 7: Generic-Interconnect in a Scope Where Type-Coercion is Turned OFF
When type coercion is turned OFF for a scope, the generic-interconnect is resolved as
wire.
In the following example, type coercion is disabled for the instance top.foo1.
Consequently, the type of the SystemVerilog generic-interconnect XMR top.foo1.in2 is
resolved as wire.
Use Case 8: Scope-Based Type-Coercion in Doughnut Design With Interleaved
Layers of Analog and Digital Blocks
In the following example, type-coercion is applied to the Dut cell, which is a digital module.
Type-coercion algorithm has traversed the doughnut design hierarchy and coerced
generic-interconnect n2 and wire-interconnects n4 to wreal. Thereafter, at the analog/
digital boundary an electrical-to-logic (E2R) connectmodule is inserted by VCS.

Use case 9: Scope Based Type-Coercion Applied to a Hierarchy Where Coercion is
Turned ON and OFF in Alternate Layers
In the following example, type-coercion is turned OFF only for the instance top.I1.I2.
Type-coercion algorithm traversed the design hierarchy and has coerced the generic-
interconnects top.I1.b and top.I1.I2.I3.d to wreal. The interconnect top.I1.I2.c is
coerced to wire because type-coercion is turned OFF for top.I1.I2. Thereafter, Real-to-
Logic (R2L) and Logic-to-Real (L2R) converters are instantiated by VCS at wreal/wire and
wire/wreal port boundaries.

Scope-Based Type-Coercion Reporting
You can use the -coerce=diag compile option to generate the type-coercion report file
simv.daidir/rnm_coerced_info.log. This report file provides the following additional
information for scope-based type-coercion:
• List of ams_coercion commands applied in type-coercion.
• List of ams_coercion commands not applied in type-coercion.

Optimizing Verilog-AMS Auto-Inserted ConnectModules (AICMs)
Using Built-in Interface Elements
In mixed-signal designs, connectmodules (also called Interface Elements or IEs) convert
signals between different disciplines—for example, from a digital logic value to an analog
electrical value (voltage/current) and vice versa. These conversions are guided by the
Verilog-AMS (VAMS) Language Reference Manual (LRM) connect-insertion rules.
In the VCS VAMS flow, interfaces between analog and digital blocks are realized by
automatically inserting connectmodules during the elaboration phase. VCS detects
mismatched ports on the same node and inserts the appropriate ConnectModule(CM)
based on connect rules.

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
Connectmodules can be inserted in:
• Merged Mode (default): If a single net of one discipline (for example, analog) connects
to multiple ports of another discipline (for example, digital), VCS inserts only one
instance of the connectmodule. All destination ports share the converted signal from
this single instance.
• Split Mode: Each mismatched port gets its own connectmodule instance. This mode is
less common and generally less efficient.
Consider the following design example:
Figure 71 Design After D2A Connectmodule Auto-Insertion in Merged Mode
In this figure, the D2A connectmodule is auto inserted in Merged mode between digital
net d1 and electrical ports A1.e and A2.e as per the VAMS connect-insertion rules. The
following is the connectmodule insertion report:
# ================LIST OF CONNECT MODULE INSTANCES============
# Instance: top.MID1
# (1) d1__D2A__electrical (ConnectModule: D2A)
# Net: top.MID1.d1 (logical)
# Ports: top.MID1.A1.e (electrical)
# top.MID1.A2.e (electrical)
# Instance: top.MID2
# (1) d2__D2A__electrical (ConnectModule: D2A)
# Net: top.MID2.d2 (logical)
# Ports: top.MID2.A3.e (electrical)
# top.MID2.A4.e (electrical)
# (2) d3__D2A__electrical (ConnectModule: D2A)
# Net: top.MID2.d3 (logical)
# Ports: top.MID2.A5.e (electrical)
# top.MID2.A6.e (electrical)
# ===================================================================

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
VCS supports optimization of the VAMS auto-inserted connectmodule instances using
built-in interface elements. You can use the -adopt aicm_opt_ie compile option as
follows to enable this feature. This feature improves the simulation performance of the
VAMS designs.
% vlogan -full64 -ams test.vams -sverilog
% vcs -full64 top -sverilog -ams \
-ad=test.init \
-adopt aicm_opt_ie \
-ams_discipline logical \
-ams_iereport
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Properties of Synopsys Built-in Interface Elements
• Optimization Criteria
• Analog Island Optimization
Properties of Synopsys Built-in Interface Elements
The following are the properties of the Synopsys built-in interface element:
• Managed by VCS/PrimeSim
• Support only built-in digital data types
• Independent of Verilog-AMS discipline definitions
• Faster execution and smaller memory footprint compared to VAMS connectmodules
• Inserted in Merged mode only to maximize performance
• Conversion functionality is controlled via:
◦ The ie and resistance-map commands in the vcsAD.init file.
◦ Automatic VDD tracing managed by VCS.
• Driver Receiver Segregation (DRS) happens at the digital port of a connectmodule
to segregate connect-driver from connect-receiver. Bi-directional (inout) built-in IEs
support DRS functionality (that is, analog simulator determines the final value of the
mixed-signal net).

Optimization Criteria
The following criteria must be met to optimize VAMS connectmodule instances using built-
in interface elements:
• The analog-digital boundary data type must be supported by the interface element.
• CM insertion mode must be merged, not split.
• CM instance must be auto-inserted (not manual).
• Mutual Exclusion Rules:
◦ A net cannot have both an IE and a CM. A mixed-signal can either have a
connectmodule or interface element, not both.
◦ If any connection on a mixed-signal net fails the criteria, optimization does not occur
for that net.
Analog Island Optimization
An analog island consists of a set of VAMS CM instances that are interconnected through
digital nets. In the following figure, the design consists of discrete digital blocks and
continuous analog blocks connected by "mixed-signal" nets. At this stage, VCS sees a
discipline mismatch (for example, a logic net connected to an electrical terminal).
Figure 72 VAMS Design Before Connectmodule Insertion

Figure 73 VAMS Design After Connectmodule Insertion
VCS treats the entire island as a single electrical node transition rather than multiple
independent nodes. After optimization:
• Supported islands replace all CMs with built-in IEs.
• Unsupported islands (for example, using user-defined nettypes) retain original CMs.
In this design example, there are two analog islands as follows:
Figure 74 Analog Island-1
For Analog Island-1, the boundary data-type ‘wire’ is supported by D2A and A2D built-
in IEs. All CM instances are inserted in Merged mode, and every CM instance within this
island is auto-inserted (AICM). IEs remain on the mixed-signal nets of this analog island
after optimization.

Figure 75 Analog Island-2

Dynamic Reconfiguration at Runtime
As designs grow in size, memory consumption and simulation speed become crucial
factors in design verification. In general, tests and stimulus are targeted and generated for
specific parts of a design. These tests and stimulus exercise a large portion of the design
while the rest of the design becomes inactive during simulation. Dynamic reconfiguration
at runtime provides a flexible mechanism to substitute portions of a design hierarchy with
empty models at runtime. This feature enables different design configurations to be used
for simulations without recompiling the design.
Figure 76 Dynamic Reconfiguration
Substitute
TOP
U1 U2
U4 U5U3
TOP
U1
U3
In Figure 76, instances U2, U4, and U5 are inactive during the simulation. These instances
and their sub-hierarchies are replaced by an empty module at runtime.
The dynamic reconfiguration at runtime feature is described in the following sections:
• Support with VCS Native Low Power
• Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
• Support for Cross-Module References of Multidimensional Arrays
• Restrictions
This section describes the use model for dynamic reconfiguration. It provides the steps
to specify an alternate module that is instantiated in place of the original sub-hierarchy.

This ensures that designs do not reach an unknown state when you replace portions of the
hierarchy at runtime.
1. Compile-time
At compile time, specify the list of modules that has the potential of not being
elaborated at runtime. In addition, for each such module, provide an alternate module,
which gets bound if an instance is not elaborated. This alternate module must be
provided during the design compilation phase. During compilation, these alternate
modules are treated as top-level modules by VCS because they are not explicitly
instantiated in the design.
In this document, the module that can be deleted is referred to as the “original module”.
The alternate module is referred to as the “substitute module”.
To specify the original module and the substitute module, the configuration file
mechanism in VCS is enhanced with the following entry.
replace module {<original module>} with module {<substitute module>};
Configuration files can be specified to VCS with the +optconfigfile
+<config file name> arguments.
2. Runtime
At runtime, specify the actual instance paths that should not be elaborated by VCS
during runtime simulation. The hierarchical path names should be specified in a file.
The path of the file path can be provided to simv using the following option:
-dynaconfig <file name>
Replacing a Module Instance
This runtime configuration file specifies the hierarchical names of the module instances
that needs to be replaced (the substitute modules are already specified at compile-
time).This configuration file is a list of hierarchical names of instances.
top.d1.eql1
top.d1.arbt1.sbarbt1.sem1
Replacing All Instances of a Module
This runtime configuration file specifies the module names that needs to be replaced
(substitute modules are already specified at compile-time). This configuration file is a
list of module names. For example,
eq1

In this test case, the top-level module named top instantiates a module named test
twice with the instance names test_inst and test_inst1. This source file also has a
substitute module named test_sbst as shown in the following code:

The compile-time configuration file lists the modules whose instances you might replace
along with their corresponding substitute modules.
In this test case, the compile-time configuration file is named as config.txt:

This configuration file specifies the possible replacement of an instance of module test
with an instance of module test_sbst.
The compile-time command-line is as follows:
% vcs basic.v +optconfigfile+config.txt

Support with VCS Native Low Power
VCS displays the following information message from dynamic reconfiguration:
DYNAMIC RECONFIG> Replacing test With test_sbst Enabled
You have enabled replacing instances of module test with instances of module
test_sbst at runtime.
So at runtime, you must first write another configuration file specifying, by hierarchical
name, the module instances you want to replace. In this test case, the configuration file is
named as runconfig.txt:
//runconfig.txt

top.test_inst
This configuration file specifies that you want the module instance with the hierarchical
name top.test_inst to be replaced. The other instance of module test, with the
hierarchical name top.test_inst1, is not replaced.

Also, before the simulation, VCS displays the following information message:
DYNAMIC RECONFIG: Instance top.test_inst is replaced with module
(test_sbst)
Support with VCS Native Low Power
During the design compilation phase, you must provide both the original and substitute
alternate module source files along with the configuration file, and specify the UPF file
using the -upf option, as shown below:
% vcs +optconfigfile+ compile_config_file_name \
top_module_of_design.v \

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
original_module.v substitute_module.v \
-upf original_module.upf
With respect to the VCS Native Low Power (NLP), the following simulation behavior
applies:
• Power-down semantics: Power-down corruption would be instrumented for both the
original and substitute modules. Though the power-down corruption instrumentation is
done for substitute modules, you must not see any corruption behavior at runtime.
• Isolation semantics: Isolation would not get instrumented for the substitute modules
except when you specify the isolation as parent or fanout. You must not observe any
isolation on the ports/pins of the substituted modules except when the isolation location
is parent or fanout.
• Retention semantics: No retention would be instrumented for the substitute modules.
You must not observe any registers being retained in the substituted module.
The following restrictions apply if you use dynamic reconfiguration flow with VCS NLP:
• Though the substituted modules are simulated without Low power semantics, still
runtime low power messages related to the power domain are generated.
• If power domain related control signals like switch, isolation control are present in the
original module and got replaced with the substitute module, then all those control
signals gets “Z” value, and related runtime low power messages are generated
accordingly.
Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
You can use dynamic reconfiguration in a mixed signal verification, but only if the analog
(SPICE or Verilog-A) part of the mixed signal design is entirely in the active, stimulated,
and unchanged part of the design.
Consider the hypothetical design in Figure 79 in which the analog part of the design is
entirely in the active, stimulated and unchanged part of the design.
Note that the sub-hierarchies whose top-level SystemVerilog module instances are eql1
and sem1 are not active or stimulated in a series of tests and are purely digital. As long as
you are not replacing the analog part of the design, you can use dynamic reconfiguration
at runtime to replace these sub-hierarchies with empty substitute modules.

In Figure 79 the analog part of the design is a SPICE deck but a mixed signal design with

Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
• Cross-module references (XMRs) from analog side of mixed signal boundary to the
replaced side of the dynamic reconfiguration boundary are not supported.
• Analog tunnel re-analysis cannot happen when a Verilog module is replaced at runtime
using dynamic reconfiguration. All the connectivity analysis happens at compile-time
and therefore runtime changes from dynamic reconfiguration is not reflected in this
analysis.
The use model for using the dynamic reconfiguration at runtime feature in a mixed signal
design is a combination of the use models for dynamic reconfiguration and mixed signal
verification. The following are the steps in the combined use model:
1. Write substitute empty module definitions to replace the top-level modules of the sub-
hierarchies that are inactive for a series of tests.
2. Write a compile-time configuration file for dynamic reconfiguration that specifies:
◦ the original module definitions of the top-level module instances in the inactive sub-
hierarchies
◦ the substitute empty module definitions that replace the originals at runtime
3. Write a setup file for the analog part of the mixed signal design.
4. Compile the digital part of the design, specifying three things:
◦ compiling for dynamic reconfiguration with the compile-time configuration
file specified with the following option: +optconfigfile+compile-
time_config_file_name
◦ compiling for mixed signal simulation and specifying the setup file with the following
option: -ad=setup_file
◦ the source files for the module definitions in the design and the source files for the
empty substitute modules
The vcs command line has the following syntax:
% vcs +optconfigfile+ compile-time_config_file_name \ -ad=setup_file
top_module_of_design.v original_module.v \ substitute_module.v
Example 110 Example vcs Command Line
% vcs +optconfigfile+com_config.txt -ad=my_spsetup prog.sv \
top.sv introctr.sv ptarbt.sv sem.sv eql.sv. sub_eql.sv \
sub_sem.sv.

5. Write a runtime configuration file for dynamic reconfiguration that specifies the
hierarchical names of the top-level module instances in the inactive sub-hierarchies.
6. Start the simulation with a simv command line specifying the runtime configuration file
with the following option and argument: -dynaconfig runtime_config_file_name

The feature has the following limitations:
• MDAs for interface type object across partial elaboration are not supported.
• Only top-down absolute XMRs in substitute modules are allowed to access object in
the fixed part of the design.
• Original module of partial elaboration hierarchy can have reference to the upward XMR
or the module XMR. These XMRs are valid if no replacement happens at simulation
time. If the substitute module has upward XMR, then VCS generates compile-time
error.
• XMRs with target inside partial elaboration hierarchy do not have value if the module is
replaced at simulation time. If original module is used at simulation time, then values of
XMR are updated.
• The substitute module that do not have any instance in fixed part of the design are
instantiated as a dummy top-level instance at simulation time.
• Only XMRs to scalars. vectors, and MDA across the dynamic reconfiguration boundary
are allowed. All other complex types result in compile-time XMR error conditions.
If replacement happens any XMR reading from the replaced hierarchy returns Z (high
impedance). Even if the replacement module instance matches with the XMR path, the
XMR does not get resolved in the new instance.
• The ports of the original and substitute modules must be the same in terms of:
◦ Direction
◦ Size (bit-width and number of dimensions)
◦ Data type
There is no requirement that the corresponding ports have the same name.

In this example, module test has a port named bto which is defined as output
port. Port bto is replaced with port bti of substitute module test_sbst. Port bti is
an input port.

Error-[DYNAPME] Dynamic reconfig port mismatch
Error occurred while trying to resolve the dynamic reconfig port:

Original port type (11 ) != Dummy port type ( 0)
"dyna.sv", 3: bto

SC flow warning is as follows:
%cat run_sc_flow.csh
vcs -sverilog -full64 dyna.sv +optconfigfile+cfg

Warning-[DYNAPTM] Dynamic reconfig Port type mismatch
dyna.sv, 3
Data type of ports 'bto'(module: 'test') and 'bto' (substitute module:
'test_sbst'(dyna.sv, 6)) do not match.
PE original and substitute modules should have consistent port types.
• Strength declarations, registered nets, and ref ports are not allowed on modules
on the dynamic reconfiguration boundary. This boundary has the following module
definitions:
◦ Original modules whose instances might be replaced at runtime
◦ Substitute modules
• In VCS mixed-HDL designs, module definitions on the boundary must be Verilog or
SystemVerilog and have none of the following hierarchically under them:
◦ VHDL code cannot be hierarchically under a replacement module.
◦ SystemC module
◦ An analog part of a mixed-signal design
◦ A DirectC call, but PLI and VPI calls across the boundary are allowed.
• Parameter values are evaluated at for compile-time. Parameter passing across the
boundary is allowed but VCS does not assign the parameter values in the replaced
instances.
• The module definitions for substitute modules must be part of the design’s source
code. VCS does not create empty modules for you.
VCS generates a compile-time error message if a substitute module in the compile-
time configuration file does not have a module definition in their source files, for
example:
Error-[DYNAMMOD] Missing dynamic reconfig module
Config file name: config.txt, at line 1.
Dynamic reconfig module 'test_sbst' does not exist,
existing the Compilation.
Please check the correctness of the module name.
• Nested enabling is not allowed.

Figure 84 Design Showing Invalid Nested Enabling
TOP
P ARENT
CHILD
LEAF1 LEAF2
SUB_PARENT SUB_CHILD SUB_LEAF
The source code for the design in Figure 84 has the following:
◦ Module TOP
◦ Module PARENT and substitute module SUB_PARENT
◦ Module CHILD and substitute module SUB_CHILD
◦ Module LEAF (two instances) and substitute module SUB_LEAF
If you enable runtime reconfiguration for the instance of module PARENT, you
cannot do the same for module instances in its sub-hierarchy, modules CHILD and
LEAF.
If you enable runtime reconfiguration for the instance of module CHILD, you cannot
do the same for instances of module LEAF.
So the following compile-time configuration file is not allowed:
Example 116 Invalid Compile-time Configuration File
Replace module {PARENT} with {SUB_PARENT};
Replace module {LEAF} with {SUB_LEAF};
Replace module {CHILD} with {SUB_CHILD};
• SDF annotations to the replaced hierarchy are ignored.
• Connecting virtual interface object of mixed types (modport and interface) is not
allowed.

VCS NLP Features
This chapter describes the following VCS Native Low Power (VCS NLP) LCA features:
• Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
• Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
• Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies
• Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
• Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
• Support for Atomic Power Domains
• Support for Modeling Isolation Cell Without Enable Pin in Liberty
• Tunneling SPICE Supply Ports Through UPF Supply Network
• Creating Custom VCTs for Real Data Types
• Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the Direction and Type of Its
PG Pins
• Support for the SPA -applies_to Option without -elements
• Support for Type Real Option With the sim_corruption_control Command
• Support for Golden UPF
• Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
• Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
• Excluding Retention Elements From Retention Strategy
• Setting Attributes on UPF Objects
• Support for Low Power Testbench APIs
• Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
• Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
• Simulation Control Commands Support

Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
• Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
• Support for Overriding Design Connection With UPF Connection on a Power Switch
Acknowledgment Signal
• Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
• Heterogeneous Fanout Support
• Controlling NLP Report Dumping
• Support for Logic Port/Net and Connections
• Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
VCS NLP allows you to specify the connections for the set/reset pins in the
set_isolation command.
Figure 85 Latch Isolation Cell With Set/Reset Pins
An isolation cell with -clamp_value specified as latch can sometimes have an
asynchronous set or reset pin on the cell. When that cell is inserted by the UPF using the
set_isolation command, it also requires connection to the set/reset pins of the isolation
cell. The syntax of set_isolation command is extended to enable you to specify the
control signal which connects to the set/reset pins of the isolation cell.
This feature allows you to model latch type isolation cells with asynchronous set/reset
pins.

Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
VCS NLP supports the following set_isolation command options to enable this feature:
set_isolation
[-async_set_reset { net_name <high | low>}]
[-async_clamp_value <0 | 1>]
[other options]
• The -async_set_reset option specifies the control signal (net) which should be
connected to the set/reset pins of the isolation cell along with the sensitivity (high/low)
of the signal.
• The signal specified with the -async_set_reset option acts either as a set or reset
of the isolation cell based on the clamp value set by the -async_clamp_value option
(clamp value is 0 for reset and 1 for set)
• The net_name is the name of the control signal which acts as the set or reset.

text:
reset option acts either as a set or reset
of the isolation cell based on the clamp value set by the -async_clamp_value option
(clamp value is 0 for reset and 1 for set)
• The net_name is the name of the control signal which acts as the set or reset. Its type
is similar to -isolation_signal and can be either port, pin, or net. The sensitivity is
specified using the high or low keyword.
• The -async_clamp_value option specifies whether the -async_set_reset option acts
as a set or reset.
• When -async_clamp_value is 0, net_name acts as a reset of the isolation cell.
• When -async_clamp_value is 1, net_name acts as a set of the isolation cell.
• Specifying -async_clamp_value is optional. The clamp value can also be set using a
port attribute.
• The -async_set_reset and -async_clamp_value options can be specified with
-update. They can occur in any order.
Using Port Attribute
If you do not want the control pin to act as a set or reset while specifying the strategy, you
can use the UPF_async_clamp_value port attribute. In this case, the same control pin
may get connected to some cells which have set and other cells which have reset pin.
set_port_attributes -ports {p1} -attribute {UPF_async_clamp_value 0/1 }
This attribute is applicable when -async_set_reset option is specified. For an isolation
strategy with -async_set_reset option and without a -async_clamp_value option, VCS
NLP uses the specified clamp value in the port attribute.
If there is a conflict between -async_clamp_value and the UPF_async_clamp_value
attribute, a warning message is issued and the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is used
for behavior.

Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
Error and Warning Conditions
The following are the error and warning conditions:
• An error message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and -clamp_value
is not a latch.
• An error message is issued when net_name is specified, but sensitivity <high|low> is
not specified.
• An error message is issued when net_name does not exist in the design.
• A warning message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and there is
no -async_clamp_value specified in the set_isolation command or through the
set_port_attributes command (as specified in the UPF_async_clamp_value port
attribute). The -async_set_reset option is ignored.
• A warning message is issued when -async_clamp_value is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option. The -async_clamp_value option is ignored.
Also, when the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option, the attribute is ignored.
Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
In some flows, at one point in the design process, it is useful to seamlessly swap between
a liberty model and a UPF based model. In this case, a key goal is that the top level UPF
should not be modified.
You can use a top level virtual net to connect ports of liberty models with direction :
internal. However, when the liberty model is represented with UPF, you can use a new
direction internal with the create_supply_port command, which gives the equivalent
of direction : internal in a liberty model.
The set of possible values for the -direction option of the create_supply_port
command is enhanced to include value internal. This feature allows seamless switching
between liberty models and UPF models during the design process.
create_supply_port port_name
[-domain domain_name]
[-direction <in | out | inout | internal>]

Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies
Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies
A PG pin of direction internal (irrespective of pg_type) is considered as a virtual driver
for a supply net. Any other kind of driver is a real driver.
If there are multiple real drivers, you must specify the resolution for the supply net. If
there are only virtual drivers or one real driver along with other virtual drivers, VCS NLP
considers the resolution as parallel.
For example, VCS NLP supports the following usage where VDD_int is a PG pin of a
macro (whose instances are macro_inst1 and macro_inst2) with direction internal.
Supply VDD that is unresolved has two drivers:
create_supply_net VDD
connect_supply_net VDD -ports {macro_inst1/VDD_int macro_inst2/VDD_int}
For the above UPF code, multiple drivers are created on the virtual supply net that is
connected to the internal PG pins.
Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
VCS NLP supports the -literal_supply option of the set_port_attributes command.
This option allows you to define the supply to be used to model a literal constant value
(1'b0/1'b1) associated to a pin/port marked with this option.
set_port_attributes
[-elements elements_list]
[-exclude_elements elements_exclude_list]
[-ports port_list]
[-exclude_ports port_exclude_list]
[-applies_to inputs | outputs]
-literal_supply supply_set_reference
This enhancement allows you to specify (change) the related supply of literal constants
(1'b0 and 1'b1). That is, you can use a different supply for literal value instead of parent
domain’s supply.
set_port_attributes -literal_supply SS_A0 -ports {OUT1 OUT2}
If a literal constant is associated to a pin/port attributed with literal supply, then the literal
constant is assumed to be powered by the supply referenced in the -literal_supply
option, and consequently affects isolation analysis and modeling of corruption semantics
for the literal.

Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
• The -model option cannot be used with -literal_supply
• At least one of -ports or -elements should be specified while using
-literal_supply.
Semantic Checks
The following semantic checks are added:
• The set of ports to be attributed must not be empty. They must be obtained from
processing the explicit references in -ports and -exclude_ports and the implicit
references in -elements and -exclude_elements.
• For each port to be attributed, precedence resolution is done based on the precedence

• For each port to be attributed, precedence resolution is done based on the precedence
rules described in the LRM for the set_port_attributes command, but with the
following exception:
Instead of issuing error when two settings with the same precedence but different value
are set on a given port, the latest setting that is applied is used.
• If a port that is part of a bus is attributed with -literal_supply, all the ports of the bus
are attributed with -literal_supply with the same value, otherwise an error is issued
and the setting is ignored.
Reporting
The -literal_supply option affects the supplies for source/sink analysis and
also adds a SRSN type of gate for simulating correct power semantics. The
spa_literal_supply_association.rpt report is useful for debugging various scenarios
where an issue is seen with the simulation.
Following is the report format
{
{ <hierarchical name of the port> <port/net driven by literal> <supply
set/net> }
{ <hierarchical name of the port> <port/net driven by literal> <supply
set/net> }
}

Example-2: Constant Driving Primary Output Port

Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
Consider the following UPF:
Example 118 test.upf
create_power_domain PDTOP -elements {.}

set_port_attributes -ports {out1} \
-literal_supply SS_A0
Figure 87 Constant Driving Primary Output Port
PDTOP.primary (VDD) SS_AO.power (A0_VDD) VSS
ON ON GND
OFF ON GND
Without this enhancement:
• Literal constant driver is assumed to be powered by the primary ( VDD).
• Simulates the literal as a Tie-cell powered by PDTOP primary power (VDD), driving the
port out1.
With this enhancement:
• Literal constant driver is assumed to be powered by the primary ( SS_AO (AO_VDD) ).
• Simulates the literal as an AO Tie-cell powered by SS_AO, so there is no isolation
requirement on this path.

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
VCS NLP supports the set_retention -use_retention_as_primary option. When this
option is specified, the retention supply powers the output driver of the register. That is, the
primary supply of the output pin of the retention register is the retention supply.
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name
[ -use_retention_as_primary]
set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -use_retention_as_primary
map_retention_cell -domain PD1 -lib_cells {SDFRET*} RET1
This enhancement allows you to model a retention cell with output related to backup
supply. Specifying the -use_retention_as_primary option instructs VCS NLP to use a
retention cell whose output pin is related to the retention supply (rather than the domain
primary).
Figure 88 Library Cell Used When -use_retention_as_primary is Specified

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is not specified, for paths which
originate from the output of the retention, the primary supply of the domain is
considered as the driver_supply.
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is specified, for paths which originate
from the output of the retention, the retention_supply of the retention strategy is
considered as the driver_supply of the path.
• The -use_retention_as_primary option changes the driver supply of ports that are
sinks of the inserted retention register. Such changes could affect the interpretation of
the -source filters of the set_isolation strategies that apply to those ports.
Corruption and Isolation Semantics
Following are the corruption semantics:
• When - use_retention_as_primary option is specified, the output of the retention
registers associated with this strategy are not corrupted when domain is in CORRUPT
state.
• When - use_retention_as_primary option is not specified, the retention registers are
corrupted when the domain is in CORRUPT state.
Following are the isolation semantics:
• Using the - use_retention_as_primary option with retention strategies impacts the
-source filter of the isolation strategies on the domain crossing driven by the retention
register.
Isolation strategies specified on ports that are driven by this retention register must be
evaluated with the source supply as the retention supply rather than domain primary.
Example: Impact on Source-Based Strategies
Consider the following UPF:
Example 119 test.upf
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {Mid}
create_supply_set SS1

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
set_retention RET1 -domain PD_MID -retention_supply SS1 \
-elements {O1}
set_retention RET2 -domain PD_MID -retention_supply SS1 \
-elements {O2} -use_retention_as_primary

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
set_isolation ISO1 -domain PD_MID -source SS1
set_isolation ISO2 -domain PD_MID -source PD_MID.primary

Support for Atomic Power Domains
Figure 89 Impact on Source-Based Strategies
Isolation cells based on strategy ISO2 are inserted on the net driven by the retention
register O1_reg (associated with retention strategy RET1). Since RET1 strategy does not
specify -use_retention_as_primary, register output supply is PD_MID.primary.
Isolation cell based on strategy ISO1 is inserted on the net driven by the retention
register O2_reg (associated with retention strategy RET2). Since RET2 strategy specifies
-use_retention_as_primary, register output supply is SS1.
Following is the limitation of this feature:
• VHDL is not supported for the isolation semantics.
Support for Atomic Power Domains
VCS NLP supports atomic power domains as per 1801-2018 version of the UPF LRM.
As per the LRM, extent of an atomic power domain can be modified, that is, updating
the options -elements {} and -exclude_elements {} of an atomic power domain is
allowed.
You must use the -atomic option of the create_power_domain command to define an
atomic power domain. Following is the syntax for creating an atomic power domain:
create_power_domain <name> -atomic
[-elements element_list]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[…]

Support for Atomic Power Domains
• To define an atomic power domain, you must specify the -atomic option during the first
definition of that power domain. Specifying the -atomic option later with -update is not
allowed, it results in an error and dropping of that constraint.
• For any cell in the extent of atomic power domain to be added to any other power
domain, the cell or its ancestor must be excluded from the atomic power domain.
• In the rest of this section, any mention of the phrase power domain implies non-atomic
power domain.
Supported Usage
The following points describe the supported usage of the -atomic option:
• An empty power domain can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on macro, ETM, or black box can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on leaf cells can be defined as atomic.
• You can update the extent of an atomic power domain, that is, updating -elements {}
and -exclude_elements {} is allowed.
• An element excluded from atomic power domain can be added to either atomic or non-
atomic power domain. There is no restriction that an element excluded from atomic
should be added only to atomic power domains.
• There is no restriction that root cells of atomic power domains should be part of same
voltage area. They can be part of different voltage areas too.
Error Checks
The following error checks are added:
Error Check-1
VCS NLP will not allow any instance in the descendant subtree of an atomic power
domain to be included in the extent of another power domain, unless that instance name
is, or is in the descendant subtree of an instance which is excluded from that atomic
domain. Violating this results in an error message (see Example 2).
Error Check-2
VCS NLP will not allow updating a non-atomic power domain as atomic (see Example 3).
That is, the -atomic option cannot be specified with -update, unless the power domain is
already defined as atomic. Violating this results in an error message.
In addition to the above checks, all existing checks that are performed while creating non-
atomic power domains applies to atomic power domains too.

Support for Atomic Power Domains
This section provides various examples with respect to the atomic power domains.
Example-1
Consider the following UPF code:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {m2 m1/b1} -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -atomic -elements {m1}
Figure 90 Atomic Power Domains
As per the processing rules of power domains, atomic power domains must be created
first, so PD_MID is created first. Root cell of atomic power domain PD_MID is m1. Therefore,
the entire descendant tree of m1 is in the extent of PD_MID.
Now, non-atomic power domains must be created, so VCS NLP tries to create PD_TOP.
However, m1/b1 listed as root cell of PD_TOP is already in the extent of atomic power
domain PD_MID. As per Error Check-1, this is incorrect and results in an error.
Later, you can fix the UPF in the following two ways:
Approach-1:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {m2 m1/b1} -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -atomic -elements {m1}
…
create_power_domain PD_MID -exclude_elements {m1/b1} -update
You can exclude m1/b1 from atomic power domain PD_MID.
Approach-2:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {m2 m1/b1} -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -atomic -elements {m1}
…
create_power_domain PD_TOP -exclude_elements {m1/b1} -update
You can exclude m1/b1 from non-atomic power domain PD_TOP and add it to atomic power
domain PD_MID.

Support for Modeling Isolation Cell Without Enable Pin in Liberty
Example-2
Consider the following UPF code:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid} -atomic
create_power_domain PD_BOT -elements {mid/bot}
Here, root cell of power domain PD_BOT mid/bot is in the extent of atomic power domain
PD_MID. As per Error Check-1, this is incorrect and results in an error.
Later you can fix the UPF by excluding mid/bot from atomic power domain PD_MID.
create_power_domain PD_TOP -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid} -atomic
create_power_domain PD_BOT -elements {mid/bot}
…
create_power_domain PD_MID -exclude_elements {mid/bot} -update
Example-3
Consider the following UPF code:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid1}
create_power_domain PD_BOT -elements {mid1/bot}
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid2} -update -atomic
Here, non-atomic PD_MID is being updated as atomic by the last create_power_domain
command. As per Error Check-2, updating non-atomic power domain as atomic is not
allowed. The last create_power_domain command results in an error and PD_MID
continues to be a non-atomic power domain.

Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the Direction and Type of Its PG
Pins
Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the
Direction and Type of Its PG Pins
VCS NLP is enhanced to perform a strict DB PG pin matching for a cell or module
by considering the direction and type of its PG pins in Liberty and Verilog model, and
appropriately mark the
IsPowerAwareModuleCell
IsPowerAwareModuleCell attribute as true or false in the
mvsim_native_reports/library_mapping.rpt file. It performs the following checks to
mark a cell or module as power aware:
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : in, it should be direction inout or input in
the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : out, it should be direction inout or output
in the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If the direction of a PG pin in Liberty is unknown, VCS NLP checks for its pg_type.
If pg_type is internal power or ground, it cannot match to an input port, but can match
to either of the output, inout, reg, wire, supply0, supply1, and supply_net_type.
If pg_type is primary power or ground, it can match to any port (input, output, or
inout), reg, wire, supply0, supply1, or supply_net_type.
To enable this feature, use the
-power=strict_db_match
-power=strict_db_match compile-time option.
Simulation behavior depends on whether the Verilog model is power aware or non-power
aware. This feature allows you to correct the Verilog model or make any other required
changes to get accurate simulation behavior of a DB cell or model.

reg [2:0] myBus_1,myBus_2;

Support for Type Real Option With the sim_corruption_control
Command
VCS NLP supports type real option in the sim_corruption_control command. Following
is the syntax:
sim_corruption_control -type real
This feature allows you to disable corruption of real items and is applicable to complete
design hierarchy covered by the UPF. This feature does not have any effect other than
disabling corruption of real. For example, if the real variable values used in the behavior
models are corrupted, this feature allows you to disable corruption of these real items only.

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
Support for Golden UPF
Following are the limitations of this feature:
• This feature is supported only for SystemVerilog real variable type only. Wreal or any
other nettype nodes involving ‘real’ are not supported.
• This feature is supported only for pure Verilog designs. VHDL is not supported.
• The corruption is restricted to the ‘simstate’ based corruption only. Therefore, this
feature does not affect the corruption due to isolation power, SRSN/SPA power, or any
port-based corruption.
Support for Golden UPF
In the UPF flow, each stage of the flow uses a single UPF file that is modified during
synthesis and physical implementation in the following ways:
The original UPF file, written with the RTL description, is modified by the Design Compiler,
resulting in the UPF' (UPF prime) file. The UPF' file reflects the changes that occurred
during synthesis such as insertion of always-on buffers, isolation and retention cells, and
PG connections to the cells.
The UPF' file is modified by the IC Compiler, resulting in the UPF'' (UPF double prime) file.
The UPF'' file reflects the changes that occurred during physical implementation, such as
the insertion of power switch cells.
The Synopsys Galaxy Implementation Platform offers a method of maintaining the UPF
multi-voltage power intent of the design using the original “golden” UPF file throughout the
synthesis, physical implementation, and verification steps, along with supplemental UPF
files generated by the Design Compiler and IC Compiler tools. This method is called the
golden UPF flow.
% vcs <design_files> -sverilog -gupf_config power.config
% ./simv
The -gupf_config option allows you to specify the power configuration file
(power.config). Following are the contents of the power.config file:
db_search_path = "<dir1>,<dir2>,…"
db_link_library = "<file1.db>,<file2.db>,…"
set upf_name_map { {mod1 mod1.nmf} {mod2 mod2.nmf} {mod3 mod3.nmf} … }
read_upf <UPF_FILE_NAME> \
-strict_check false \
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file> \
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist> \
-scope <TARGET MODULE>

text:
Support for Golden UPF
db_search_path
Global variable. Used to search for .db (liberty) files.
db_link_library
Global variable. Used to specify the list of .db files to be used in the design.
upf_name_map
Global variable. Used to specify the name of the map file for a design top module.
read_upf
This command is used to parse the Synopsys flow compatible UPF file.
The read_upf command must be specified for the top-level UPF file. The options of this
command have the following semantics:
-strict_check false
When false (as for golden UPF application to a netlist), default matching rules are used
for name lookups, if no rules are defined.
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file>
Specifies a supplemental UPF file to be loaded after the golden UPF file. The
supplemental UPF additionally supports create_power_domain -elements -update .
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist>
Specifies the target design.
icc_netlist — Specifies that the isolation and retention strategies, and power switches
are implemented in the incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected
to their supplies through the connect_supply_net commands in the incoming UPF.
VCS NLP supports ICC PG netlists where supplies are implemented and
explicitly connected in the netlist.
dc_pg_netlist — Specifies that the supplies are implemented and explicitly connected in
the incoming target DC netlist.
dc_netlist — Specifies that the isolation and retention strategies are implemented in the
incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected to their supplies through
the connect_supply_net commands in the incoming UPF.
-scope

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
Instance or module on which the UPF must be applied.
Following is the sample power.config file:
db_search_path ". /remote/DEMO_LIB/pgdb"
db_link_library "\
demo_aob_12v_pg.db \
demo_iso_12v_pg.db \
demo_ret_12v_pg.db \
demo_psw_12v_pg.db \
demo_els_12v_10v_pg.db \
demo_std_12v_pg.db "
set upf_name_map {{top top.v.nmf}}
read_upf top.upf -supplemental supplemental_upf_dc.upf -scope
top -strict_check false -target dc_pg_netlist
The following features are not supported:
• The correlated_supply_group attribute
• VHDL-only and mixed HDL designs
• Design with mix of RTL and netlist
• Black box flow, ETM, and MACROS with their own UPF
• Mixed-signal simulations with XA
• LP_MSG APIs from SNPS_LP_MSG package for message control
• Low power debug features in Verdi
• query_* and bind_checker commands
• Low power coverage
Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
VCS NLP allows you to define a supply set state partially and then incrementally refine it
to a fully-defined states using the -update option of the add_power_state command. To
begin with, you can initially specify the name of the state, and then incrementally add more
intent to the state using the -update option.

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
This feature is supported for all types of objects (supply set, domain, and group) that are
currently supported with the add_power_state command. Following are the general rules
to achieve a successive refinement flow using the -update option:
1. To begin with, the initial definition of the state can have just the name of the state (It
may or may not have additional information).
2. Additional information for the state (-supply_expr, -logic_expr, and so on) can be
added incrementally using the -update option.
3. If a state defined with the supply network expression (-supply_expr) is updated with
another -supply_expr, the new definition is interpreted as the conjunction of the two.
That is, -supply_expr can be updated in the following ways:
◦ The initial definition can have just the net state ( FULL_ON/OFF) for a functional net
without voltage, and the updated definition can specify the voltage for the functional
net.
◦ The initial definition can have one or more functional nets, and the updated
definition can specify more functional nets.
4. If a state defined with the logic expression (-logic_expr) is updated with another
-logic_expr, the new definition is interpreted as the conjunction of the two.
5. If the -simstate option is specified as NOT_NORMAL, it can be updated to any simstate
other than NORMAL.
6. If the -simstate option is specified as NORMAL, CORRUPT, or CORRUPT_ON_ACTIVITY, it
cannot be updated to any other simstate other than the one originally specified.
7. A partially defined state can be used in the -logic_expr of a group or a domain.
The following example shows successive refinement for a supply set state:
The new intent added to the state at each level are marked in bold font.
1. Define a supply set state with a name
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {}
2. Add -supply_expr to the state, but without voltage
add_power_state SS1 -state ON { -supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON}} }
3. Add voltage to -supply_expr
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 1.0}}}
4. Add -logic_expr to the state
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 1.0}} \
-logic_expr {net1} }

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
5. Add -simstate to the state
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 1.0}} \
-logic_expr {net1} \
-simstate {NORMAL} }
Supported Successive Refinement Styles
The following sections describe different successive refinement styles that are supported
as part of this feature:
Updating an Existing Supply Set State
This section describes the following topics:
Updating an Existing Supply Network Expression
The following example shows how the supply network expression (-supply_expr) can
be updated. Here, voltage information and functional nets are incrementally added to
-supply_expr using the -update option.
Example 124 test.upf
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON}}}
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {ground ==
{FULL_ON}}} -update
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
Example 124 test.upf
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON}}}
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {ground ==
{FULL_ON}}} -update
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0}}} -update
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {ground == {FULL_ON
0.0}}} \
-update
The above UPF is interpreted as follows. This is in line with the UPF 2.1.
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0} && \
{ground == {FULL_ON 0.0}}}
It is illegal to update the state voltage or state type.
Case-1:
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
0.0}}} -update
VCS NLP issues the following error message for case-1:
Error-[UPF_EUSSV] Error updating supply expression voltage for
such scenarios

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
Case-2:
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {OFF}}}
-update
VCS NLP issues the following error message for case-2:
Error-[UPF_EUSST] Error updating supply expression state type
Updating an Existing Logic Expression
You can use the -update option to update an existing logic expression (-logic_expr).
The following example shows how a logic expression can be updated using the -update
option:
Example 125 test1.upf
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net1}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net2}} -update
The above UPF is interpreted as follows. This is in line with the UPF 2.1.
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net1 && net2}}
Updating an Existing Simstate
You can use the -update option to update an existing simstate (-simstate).
The following example shows how a simstate can be updated using the -update option:
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-simstate {NOT_NORMAL}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-simstate {CORRUPT}} -update
Updating an Existing Group/Domain State
This section describes the following topics:
Updating an Existing Logic Expression
You can use the -update option with the -group option to add an additional group state to
a group.
You can use the -update option to update an existing group state. Following is the

Permitting Supply Set States that do not Have a Supply Network Expression in
Group/Domain State
VCS NLP allows you to refer to a supply set state in a group irrespective of whether the
supply set state has a -supply_expr defined or not. The -supply_expr definition for
the supply set state can come later in the flow, after the group is defined. Consider the
following example:
Example 128 test4.upf
add_power_state SS1 -state ON1 {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 0.8}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON2 {-simstate NORMAL}

create_power_state_group GROUP
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS1 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON1}}
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS2 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON2}}
-update
For the above UPF, group states GS1 and GS2 are created successfully.
Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
As per the UPF 3.0, a port is removed from the candidate set if the port name appears in
the -exclude_ports list.

Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
VCS NLP supports the -exclude_ports option of the set_port_attributes command.
This option provides flexibility for specifying ports for the set_port_attributes
The ports in the list of -exclude_ports are excluded from the current
set_port_attributes command.
• If a port is listed in -exclude_ports of the current set_port_attributes, its previous
set_port_attributes setting continues to apply.
• If all the objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the entire command is
an error and has no effect.
• If only some, but not all, objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the
command is applied to the existing objects, and a warning is issued for the non-existing
object.
• If both -exclude_ports and -model are specified, the specified ports of the model are
excluded during candidate set creation. When specified with -model, arguments to the
-exclude_ports option should be simple names. VCS NLP issues an error message if
rooted names are specified in this usage.
Consider the following figure:
Case-1: -exclude_ports with -ports. In the following example, top_in1 is excluded:
set_port_attributes -ports {top_in*} -exclude_ports {top_in1} -attribute
-clamp_value z

The following features are not supported:
• -elements with -exclude_elements
• -elements with -exclude_ports
• Interface/modport support
• VHDL Support
• Bit-level support for -model -exclude_ports
The following attributes are not supported:
• iso_source
• iso_sink
• repeater_power_net
• repeater_ground_net
The
set_retention
set_retention command is enhanced to support the -exclude_elements option in
the UPF. You must use the
-power=ret_exclude
-power=ret_exclude compile option to enable this feature.
This feature allows you to exclude some instances, blocks, or registers from a retention
strategy.
You can use the -exclude_elements option at the time of creating a retention strategy.
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name
[-elements element_list]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[-no_retention]
set_retention RET2 -domain PD1 -elements {u2} -exclude_elements {u2/reg2}
The element u2/reg2 is excluded.
This feature is also supported with the -update option.

set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -elements {u1}
set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -exclude_elements {u1/reg2} -update
The element u1/reg2 is excluded.
Consider a design with the following hierarchy:
I1 I2 I3
I1/J1 I1/J2
I1/J1/K1 I1/J1/K2
I1/J1/K1/L1 I1/J1/K1/L2
Following are the various use case examples of retention application with the
-exclude_elements option:
Example-1
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 } -exclude_elements { I1/flop1 }
Except I1/flop1, every other element in instance I1 and transitively all elements below
I1 belong to retention R1.
Example-2
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 } -exclude_elements { I1/flop1 I1/J1/
flop1 }
Except I1/flop1 and I1/J1/flop1, every other element in instance I1 and transitively all
elements below I1 belong to retention R1.
Example-3
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 } -exclude_elements { I1/J1 }
Element I1/J1 is transitively omitted from retention R1.
In the following figure, the instances with blue color belong to retention R1:
