Setting Attributes on UPF Objects
The set_design_attributes command is enhanced to allow setting attributes on
UPF objects. The UPF objects can be specified using the -elements option of the
set_design_attributes command. The attributes are specified using the -attribute
UPF Objects
The following UPF objects are supported in the -elements option of the
set_design_attributes command:
• Supply net
• Logic net

The set_design_attributes command also allows you to set the attribute on the logic/
supply nets that have HDL implementation.
Wildcards are supported for UPF objects.
Attributes
The set_design_attributes command allows you to set user-defined attributes and
Synopsys predefined attributes. When user-defined attributes are set, VCS NLP issues a
warning and ignores it.
set_design_attributes -elements {Supply_nets/Logic_nets} -attribute
<attribute> <attribute value>
set_design_attributes -elements {VDD mid/VDD} -attribute
logical_supply_net TRUE
set_design_attributes -elements {LogicNet} -attribute
user_defined_attribute TRUE
set_design_attributes -elements {inst1/VDD*} -attribute logic_supply_net
TRUE
Attributes logical_supply_net, user_defined_attribute,
logic_supply_net are user-defined attributes.
The UPF information model captures the power management information which is the
result of application of UPF commands on the user design. It consists of a set of objects
containing information and various relationships between them.

Figure 95 UPF Information Model Flow
The UPF information model consists of a collection of objects. The information is present
on these objects in the form of properties, which can be accessed through APIs. Each
object is denoted by a unique identifier (ID) called UPF handle which is used by the APIs
to access information present on it.
The objects and properties in the information model can be accessed by a HDL object of
upfHandleT type.
The class IDs are unique strings that represent class names in the information model. The
class names are represented in capitalized words with a upf prefix and T suffix.
Example: upfPowerDomainT, upfHdlScopeT
The property IDs are unique strings that represent the properties present on the object.
The property names are denoted by lowercase words separated by a “_” (underscore
character) and a upf prefix.
Examples: upf_name, upf_parent
The classes in the information model are identified in HDL by the enumerated values
defined in upfClassIdE enumerated type. Refer to section 11.2.2.5 of the IEEE Std
1801-2015 LRM for information on mapping between information model classes and
corresponding class id in HDL type.
The HDL interface to the information model allows you to create abstract testbenches to
manipulate UPF objects directly in simulation.
For more information on the UPF information model, see the IEEE Std 1801-2015 LRM.
VCS NLP supports HDL access functions (UPF Package 3.0 APIs) as defined in the
IEEE Std 1801-2015 LRM. For more information, see Supported APIs. You must use the
-power=svapi compile time option to enable this feature.

This feature provides a standard interface that can be used to access power management
information.

IEEE Std 1801-2015 LRM. For more information, see Supported APIs. You must use the

This feature provides a standard interface that can be used to access power management

Supported APIs

• upf_get_handle_by_name

• upf_get_value_str
• upf_get_value_int
• upf_get_value_real
• upf_object_in_class
• upf_convert_int_uvolts_to_real_volts
• get_supply_voltage

• supply_off

upf_get_handle_by_name
VCS NLP supports the following types of handles:
• Object Handles
References to the objects in the UPF information model. These handles can be
compared using a == operator.
• Iterator Handles
Iterators to containers in the UPF information model. These handles can be reused as
iterators are scoped objects and get deleted after the iteration is complete. You must
not use the iterator handles with the == operator for comparison.
• Property Handles
References to property value wrapper. These handles are same for all integer/Boolean
properties, real, string, and supply type properties. You must not use the iterator
handles with the == operator for comparison.
Table 16 Get Handle By Name
Description Returns the handle to the object in the information model from the given path
name.
upf_get_handle_by_name
upfHandleT upf_get_handle_by_name(upfStringT pathname,
upfHandleT relative_to = null);
Example Example: Get handle to a strategy
upfHandleT scope = upf_get_handle_by_name("/top/ dut_i");
upfHandleT iso = upf_get_handle_by_name("pd", scope);
end
Arguments pathname - A string representing handle ID for an object.
relative_to - An optional handle to the object from which the relative path
name is given.
Return Value Returns the handle to the specified property or null if not found.
The path name starts with ‘/’ followed by the object or scope below power top. This API
returns following types of handles:
• Objects
• Iterators

VCS NLP issues the UPF_HANDLE_NOT_FOUND error message for an invalid handle ID. The
following is the error message example:
Error-[UPF_HANDLE_NOT_FOUND] Handle not found in the UPF design.
testbench.v, 146
tb Handle 'top_inst/SW_TOP' specified in 'upf_get_handle_by_name' UPF
package API is not found.
Please specify a valid name of a UPF object.
upf_query_object_properties
This UPF Package 3.0 API allows you to query properties on a given object. The
properties are both static and dynamic as follows:
Static properties – These are populated at the time of UPF compilation.
Dynamic properties – These are populated during the simulation and always have the
current value of the property.
Table 17 Query Object Properties
Description Allows you to query properties on a given object.
upf_query_object_properties
upfHandleT upf_query_object_properties(upfHandleT object_handle,
upfPropertyIdE attr);
Example Example: Get simple name of a power domain
upfHandleT pd = upf_get_handle_by_name("/top/dut_i/ pd");
upfHandleT name = upf_query_object_properties(pd, UPF_NAME);
$display( "PD Name: %s", upf_get_value_str(name));
end
PD Name: pd
Arguments object_handle - UPF handle of the given object.
attr - The enumerated value corresponding to the given property on the

Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
The find_objects command searches for instances, nets, ports, supply ports, or
processes within a scope.
A leaf cell is any cell having no descendants. Standard cells and macros are always
considered to be leaf cells. Any hierarchy with the terminal_boundary attribute is also
considered as a leaf cell. For macros, a UPF_is_hard_macro attribute value of TRUE on
a model or a UPF_is_soft_macro attribute value of TRUE on an instance indicates that it
shall be treated as a leaf cell.
VCS NLP allows you to search the specified scope and its entire descendant hierarchy
without considering the terminal_boundary/UPF_is_soft_macro marking using the
-traverse_macros option. Following is the syntax:
find_objects scope
-pattern search_ pattern
[-object_type <model | inst | port | supply_port | net | process>]
[-direction <in | out | inout>]
[-transitive [<TRUE | FALSE>]]
[-regexp | -exact]
[-ignore_case]
[-non_leaf | -leaf_only]
[ -traverse_macros]
• When you specify the -traverse_macros option, the traversal stops at a standard cell
and hard macro boundaries.
• If the -traverse_macros option is specified, then -transitive TRUE is implicitly
specified.
• The -traverse_macros option is supported only for -object_type model | inst
• VCS NLP issues a warning message when you specify object type ( -object_type)
other than model | inst . For example:
find_objects . -pattern in1 -object_type port -traverse_macros

Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy

Invalid object type for -traverse_macros option
File - ./soft_macro.upf: Line No - 41
Option -traverse_macros can be specified only with '-object_type
model/inst' in command 'find_objects'. The option will be ignored.
'-traverse_macros' can be specified only with '-object_type
model/inst'.
• VCS NLP issues a warning message when object type ( -object_type) is not
specified. For example:
find_objects . -pattern ret_i* -traverse_macros
Following is the sample warning message:
Warning - [UPF_FIND_OBJECTS_TRAVERSE_MACROS_DEFAULT] Only return some
objects when -object_type isn't specified
File - ./soft_macro.upf: Line No - 45
By default, instances, named processes, logic ports, and nets are
returned when -object_type is not specified. When -traverse_macros is
specified, tool continues to return the default types outside macros,
but returns only objects of type 'instance' inside macros.

Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
VCS NLP supports specifying expressions in the pg_function attribute of a liberty cell.
The expression is a 2:1 MUX where the select is a signal pin and the two data inputs are

Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
PG pins. The MUX pg_function support is only implemented for two input supply MUX
power switch with a select pin.
For example, the following figure shows a single liberty cell with two input supplies at the
top, and signal pins at the left and right. The two green power switches are internal to the
liberty definition.
Following are the examples of the pg_function expression specification in the liberty file:
pg_pin (vdda) { … } pg_pin (vddb) { … }
pin (s1) { … }
pg_pin (vddc) {
direction : internal;
pg_function : "(s1 vdda)+(!s1 vddb)";
switch_function : "1"
}

pg_pin (vdda) { … } pg_pin (vddb) { … }
pin (s2) { … } pin (s2) { … }
pg_pin (vddc) {
direction : internal;
pg_function : "(s1 vdda)+(!s1 vddb)";
switch_function : "s2"
}
The following are the invalid scenarios:
Scenario-1: AND function is not allowed in the pg_function expression.
pg_pin (va) { … } pg_pin (vb) { … }
pin (s1) { … }

Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
pg_pin (vc) {
direction : internal;
pg_function : "s1 & va"; /* AND function not allowed */
}
Scenario-2: Switch function name cannot be same as the pin name in the pg_function
expression.
pg_pin (va) { … } pg_pin (vb) { … }
pin (s2) { … }
pg_pin (vc) {
direction : internal ;
pg_function : "(s1 va)+(!s1 vb)";
switch_function : "s1" /* same as pg_function not allowed */
}
• You can specify the pg_function attribute without switch_function on a PG pin.
• You can specify both signal pin and PG pin in the pg_function boolean expression.
• The signal pin and PG pin number specified in the pg_function has no limitation.
However, at least 1 PG pin is required.
• The PG pin specified in the pg_function is not limited to primary or backup power/
ground; It can be internal power/ground.
• This feature is supported only for Verilog DB cells.
• The MUX pg_function when successfully processed is logged in the
library_mapping.rpt file.
Following is the sample report:
PG Function : ((VDD && LS) || (VDDA && ~(LS))) : MUX Function : Select

Instrumentation for pg_function Attribute
The instrumentation for pg_function attribute takes the following scenarios into
consideration:
• Scenario-1: PG pin is power aware and wire type with HDL drivers
In this case, the wire value is used to drive the stage, and voltage is driven by MUX as
inferred from the liberty file.
• Scenario-2: PG pin is power aware and wire type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the PG pin gets the supply_net_type value from the inferred MUX, and
the wire value is a VCT version of the supply_net_type value.

Simulation Control Commands Support
• Scenario-3: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with HDL drivers
In this case, the inferred MUX is not instrumented and the supply_net_type value is
used as is.
• Scenario-4: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the supply_net_type value is driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.
• Scenario-5: PG pin is not power aware
In this case, the supply_net_type node is added and the supply_net_type value is
driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.
Simulation Control Commands Support
This section describes the sim_corruption_control, sim_assertion_control, and
sim_replay_control simulation control commands in the following sections:
• Using the sim_corruption_control Command
• Using the sim_assertion_control Command
• Using the sim_replay_control Command
Using the sim_corruption_control Command
The sim_corruption_control command allows you to turn off corruption semantics for
specific set of design elements. This command allows behavioral modules (for example,
real number modules) to operate correctly in a low power environment. This command is
only applicable for functional verification.
The following is the syntax of the sim_corruption_control command:
sim_corruption_control
[-elements element_list]
[-model model_name]
When -elements is specified, the elements shall be a list of variables, registers, signals
of the specified hierarchical instances. If the element is an instance, then by default the
command applies to all objects defined in that instance and all dependent subtrees.
Wildcards are supported with this option.
When -model is specified, only names that are declared in the model can be referenced
in the -elements option, and all names are interpreted relative to the topmost scope of
the model. You must use this option along with the -elements option, otherwise VCS NLP
issues an error message.

Simulation Control Commands Support
When -elements is specified along with -model, then the specified elements should be
local to the model.
set_port_attributes -ports {in_bus} -driver_supply
PD3_primary sim_corruption_control -elements {in_bus} -model {top}
Following are the limitations of this command:
• This command does not apply to modules instantiated by the bind_checker
• Bit select with -elements is not supported.
• The following options are not supported:
-type, -exclude_elements, -domain, and -transitive
Using the sim_assertion_control Command
The sim_assertion_control command provides a mechanism to disable assertions
during low power verification. This enables the use of non-power-aware assertions in a
power-aware environment. This command is only applicable for simulation.
The sim_assertion_control for each assertion is active when the primary supply of the
domain in which that assertion is instantiated is not NORMAL and becomes inactive when
the primary supply returns to NORMAL simstate.
The following is the syntax of the sim_assertion_control command:
sim_assertion_control
[-domain domain_name]
[-type <reset>]
If -domain is specified, then assertions and instances that are part of the specified domain
are included.
The -type option determines the type of assertion control. The following type is
supported:
reset - Assertions are suspended and reset when the sim_assertion_control is active
and re-enabled when the it becomes inactive. The reset clears the assertions of any
internal state and sequences.
The following command selects all assertions inside the instances that belong to domain
PD1.

Simulation Control Commands Support
sim_assertion_control -domain PD1 -type reset
Following are the limitations of this command:
• The sim_assertion_control command does not apply to assertions within instances
instantiated by the bind_checker command.
• The following options are not supported:
-type kill , -elements, -transitive, -model, -control_expr,
-controlling_domain
Using the sim_replay_control Command
The sim_replay_control command specifies the list of initial blocks which needs to be
replayed when the power is restored after it has been switched off. This command is only
applicable for simulation.
Each initial block targeted by this command is replayed when the primary supply set of the
domain that contains the initial block transitions into the NORMAL state.
The sim_replay_control command provides the ability to reinitialize logic in behavioral
modules of ROM’s or PLL’s during power state transitions in low power simulation.
The following is the syntax of the sim_replay_control command:
sim_replay_control
[-elements element_list ]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[-model model_name]
[-domain domain_name]
The -elements option specifies a specific list of initial blocks and/or instances. If the
element is a named initial block, the command applies to the specified block. The element
is referenced by the hierarchical path and label of the statement. If the element is an
instance, then by default the command applies to all initial blocks defined in that instance
and all dependent subtrees.

If the element is an instance, then by default all initial blocks defined within that instance
and its dependent subtree are excluded.
If the -domain option is specified, then only initial blocks and instances in the element
list that are also a part of the specified domain are included. When -domain is specified
and -elements is not specified, this command applies to all initial blocks found within any
instance in the extent of the specified domain.

Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
When -model is specified, only names that are declared in the model can be referenced
in the arguments to this command, and all names are interpreted relative to the topmost
scope of the model.
VCS NLP issues error message for the following cases:
• Instance specified in the -elements list is already covered by a sim_replay_control
command with -model.
• If neither -elements, -model, nor -domain is specified.
The following command selects all initial blocks whose label starts with L, but excludes
those blocks whose label starts with L1:
sim_replay_control
-elements [find_objects . -pattern "L*" -object_type process]
-exclude_elements [find_objects . -pattern "L1*" -object_type process]
The following command selects all initial blocks inside the modules that belong to domain
PD1:
sim_replay_control -domain PD1
The following command selects all initial blocks labeled InstX/block1 in the module
modA:
sim_replay_control -model modA -elements InstX/block1
Following are the limitations of this command:
• This command does not apply to modules instantiated by the bind_checker
• The following options are not supported:
-transitive, -controlling_domain
Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
VCS NLP supports the -exclude_elements option with the create_power_domain
command. Following is the syntax:
create_power_domain domain_name
[-elements element_list]
[ -exclude_elements exclude_list ]
[-update]

Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
Where, -exclude_elements specifies the list of the design elements to exclude from
the effective element list (set of elements to which the command applies). The effective
element list is constructed from the arguments provided to the command.
When create_power_domain -exclude_elements option is specified, elements listed in
-exclude_elements are not considered as part of the power domain. For example, for the
following command, the effective element list is { A B/b2 B/b3 … } :
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B/*} -exclude_elements {B/b1}
• VCS NLP issues the following error message when the excluded elements does not
belong to any other power domain:
Error-[UPF_EXCLUDED_ELEMENT_NOT_IN_ANY_POWERDOMAIN] Excluded element
not in any power domain
• VCS NLP allows you to specify duplicated elements in the -exclude_elements
list. For example, the following command contains duplicated element B in the
-exclude_elements list:
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B} -exclude_elements {B B}
• Wildcards are supported in the -exclude_elements list. For example,
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B/*} -exclude_elements {B/*}
• You can specify empty elements list for the -exclude_elements option. For example,
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B} -exclude_elements {}
• VCS NLP issues an error message when the elements specified in the
-exclude_elements option are not part of the current design. For example, VCS NLP
issues an error message for the following command as the element C is not found in
the design.
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B} -exclude_elements {C}
• All elements specified with the -exclude_elements option must be part of any other
power domain, else VCS NLP issues an error message. For example, VCS NLP issues
an error message for the following command because element A is not part of any
other power domain:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {. A} -exclude_elements {A}
The following command is legal because element A belongs to the power domain PD_A:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {. A} -exclude_elements {A}
create_power_domain PD_A -elements {A}

Support for Overriding Design Connection With UPF Connection on a Power Switch
Acknowledgment Signal
VCS NLP issues an error message for the following command because power domain
of A/a1 is not specified:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {.}
create_power_domain PD_A -elements {A A/a*} -exclude_elements {A/a1}
• When the -exclude_elements option is specified with the -update option, the power
domain is updated to exclude elements listed in the -exclude_elements option. The
effective element list is computed when all UPF commands are read. For example, for
the following commands, effective element list is {A}.
create_power_domain PD -elements {A}
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {B} -update
create_power_domain PD -elements {B} -update
• VCS NLP allows you to specify multiple -exclude_elements and -update options. For
example, for the following commands, effective element list is {A}.
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B C}
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {B} -update
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {C} -update
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {C} -update
• The -exclude_elements option works with empty power domain. For example, for the
following commands, effective element list is {A}.
create_power_domain PD -elements {} // empty power domain
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {B} -update
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {C} -update
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B C} -update
Support for Overriding Design Connection With UPF Connection
on a Power Switch Acknowledgment Signal

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
In the above example, there are four instances of module bloc in the design and three
power switches in the UPF whose acknowledgment ports are driven from the design (with
a continuous assignment).
When you use the -power=disable_ack_design_driver option at compile time, VCS
NLP disables the HDL driver for acknowledgment ports.
Following are the limitations of this feature:
• XMR driver is not supported
• Partition Compile is not supported
• The following scenarios are not supported when acknowledgment port is an input port:
◦ Interface modport in highconn of the input port
◦ XMR in highconn of the input port
◦ Struct member in highconn of the input port
Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
The following sections describe the support for UPF power-aware converters:
• Introduction
Converter modules convert signal values from one type to another. There will be no
specification of liberty for converter modules. A converter module has two scalar ports of
two different types (input and output). A converter is instantiated between a port and the
signal that is connected at the high-conn of the port connection.
One of the major challenges during simulation in presence of UPF is to correctly simulate
the converter modules that are inserted by the tool at real-logic boundaries. For a logic-to-
real converter, when a logic signal information is sent to a block, the corresponding supply
(that is, power, ground) associated with that logic signal should play a role to determine
the real number value.

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
On the other hand, for a real-to-logic converter, when the real output pin changes its value,
the corresponding supply associated with this pin should be considered to convert the real
number value to corresponding logic value.
VCS supports UPF power-aware converters. The following sections describe how the
converter modules behave in presence of the power sources defined in UPF.
This feature is enabled by default. However, you must specify all the relevant options
that are required for inserting converter modules. For more information, refer to the VCS
Converters section in the VCS User Guide.
If you want to disable the feature, use the following compile-time option:
%vcs -power=disable_supply_aware_converter
Supply-Aware Converter Module
You must provide a converter module whose conversion functionality depends on two
SystemVerilog variables declared locally inside the module. The attributes of the two
variables are snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground respectively. These two local
variables should be of type UPF::supply_net_type.
Conversion functionality depends on two SystemVerilog variables declared locally inside
the module. Following is the converter module example:
In the above example, the local variables are of type UPF::supply_net_type. One
variable has an attribute snps_cm_power and the other variable has snps_cm_ground.
If the above converter module is instantiated in the UPF power-managed region (under
UPF power-top), the local initializations are removed, and the two variables are driven

the following example:
You must make sure that the variables vdd (power) and vss (ground) have the attributes
snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground respectively. The type of these variables should be
of type UPF::supply_net_type.

Following are the limitations of this feature:
• SPA/SRSN as supply is not supported.
• Merged-mode insertion is not supported.
• Super-bidir adapters and local converters are not supported.
• Inout converters+FGP is not supported.
• To have more correct simulation behavior, the -coerce option should be used.

Heterogeneous fanout is a cross-domain net that drives multiple fanouts with different
sink supplies. This feature enables VCS NLP to insert isolation cells in the extent of the
location domain rather than the exact logical hierarchy of the domain boundary.
With this support, the isolation strategy with the -sink or -diff_supply_only option
inserts isolation cells when the fanouts have different supplies and the location is self/
parent.
For example, the following case is supported for isolation heterogeneous fanout support:
set_isolation iso1 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss1
set_isolation iso2 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss2
To enable this feature, you must set the design attribute hetero_fanout_isolation to
TRUE as follows:
set_design_attributes -elements {.} -attribute {hetero_fanout_isolation
TRUE}

ss2
To enable this feature, you must set the design attribute hetero_fanout_isolation to
TRUE as follows:
set_design_attributes -elements {.} -attribute {hetero_fanout_isolation
TRUE}
The attribute must be specified for the top design instance. If the attribute is specified
anywhere in the UPF (for any scope), then it must be defined also for the top scope with
the same value. VCS NLP issues an error message if the attribute value from a block is
different from the value specified for the top.

Isolation Insertion on Heterogeneous Fanout Paths
The following points describe the support for isolation insertion on heterogeneous fanout
paths:
• This feature improves the granularity of the set_isolation -sink/-
diff_supply_only option. Also, this support changes the isolation conflict resolution
by allowing two isolation strategies to have the same options other than -sink/-
diff_supply_only.
• VCS NLP can insert isolation cells wherever they deem fit as long as they do not
violate the isolation constraints. Also, heterogeneous fanout support does not insert
isolation cells as less as possible.
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells can be inserted at any hierarchy boundary
provided that they reside at the power domain specified by the strategy (and do not
cross the power domain).
• Each path is isolated by its highest precedence strategy (assuming all filters are
satisfied) only, otherwise it is not isolated.
• If isolation insertion is not possible due to the location violating the filters, a lower-
precedence strategy is not applied (-diff_supply_only/self, no filters/parent/self).
• The following warning message is issued when the highest precedence strategy is not
applied due to the location violating the -diff_supply_only/-source/-sink filters.
Warning-[UPF_ISO_HETEROGENEOUS_FANOUTS] Isolation skipped due to
hetero fanout
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells from the -applies_to input strategy can be
closer to the output of the power domain boundary than the input.
• An error message is issued if both conservative_diff_supply_isolation and
hetero_fanout_isolation are enabled. Following is the sample error message:
Error-[UPF_ATTRS_CONFLICT] Conflicting design attributes specified
./test.upf, 4
Attribute 'conservative_diff_supply_only_isolation' conflicts with
attribute 'hetero_fanout_isolation' specified at ./test.upf, 2.
Please remove one of the conflicting attributes.
• The -diff_supply_only option adds a criteria to filter isolation at sinks. Therefore, the
heterogeneous fanout isolation cell insertion results can be changed with this option.

Heterogeneous fanout support works with location self:
set_isolation iso1 -domain TOP -location self -applies_to input -sink ss1
set_isolation iso2 -domain TOP -location self -applies_to input -sink ss2

ss1

ss2

Heterogeneous fanout support does not insert isolation cells as less as possible. In the
following example, VCS NLP does not insert ISO2 cell before the fork instead of two cells
because it is located far away from the domain boundary (1 or 2 ISOs).

-applies_boundary lower

Example-5
set_isolation iso1 -pd PDB1 -sink ss3 -no_isolation
set_isolation iso2 -pd PDB1 -diff_only -location parent
• The strategy iso1 has no isolation for -sink ss3 .
• Strategy iso2 is applicable on both paths.
• Strategy iso1 is the highest precedence strategy for path A->B.
• Only the path A->C is isolated with iso2.
Example-6

set_isolation iso1 -domain PDB1 -diff_supply_only true -parent
set_isolation iso2 -domain PDB1 -sink ss2 -no_isolation
• The isolation iso1 is applied on A->E since it is the highest precedence strategy.
• The strategy iso2 (no_iso) is applicable on paths A->C and A->D.
• Strategy iso1 is the highest precedence strategy for the path A->B. However, it cannot
be applied since it would violate the -no_isolation requirement on paths A->C and A-
>D.
• A warning message is issued for the path A->B since it remains unisolated.
VCS NLP compile-time reports are dumped by default inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory. For large designs, a lot of information is dumped in each of these reports
resulting in large file sizes. However, you may not need all the reports for diagnostic
purposes. Therefore, this leads to performance degradation and resource utilization.
You can use the -power_report=<switch> compile option to control the dumping of
reports. You can use this option to enable or disable the reports that are dumped in the low
power analysis stage based on your requirement.
This feature improves compile performance for large designs by dumping only the required
reports. Also, you can the disable dumping of all reports by default in the regression mode.

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
The following topics describe this feature in detail:
• Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
• Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
• Precedence Details
• Supported Reports
• Examples
The following is the use model:
% vcs design.v -upf design.upf -sverilog -power_report=<switch>
All reports will have a separate switch name that can be passed to -power_report=
prefixed with either the - sign to disable the report or the + sign to enable the report.
If an invalid switch name is provided, VCS NLP issues a warning message with
the NLP-UNKNOWN-PWR-RPT-OPT tag. If multiple switch names are provided and
one of them is an invalid option, then the warning message is printed only for
the invalid option. The remaining switches are processed without any issues.
Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
This section describes how to enable and disable the dumping of individual reports
using switch. Following is the use model to enable/disable the dumping of the individual
reports:
% vcs -power_report=+/-<report_name>
Examples:
-power_report=+db_inside_db
Enables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.
-power_report=-db_inside_db
Disables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.

Multiple reports can be enabled/disabled to control individual report dumping. For
example,
-power_report=-srsn_spa_association-upf_supply_net-upf_supply_port
Disables the dumping of the srsn_spa_association.rpt, upf_supply_net.rpt,
and upf_supply_port.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports directory during
compilation.
-power_report=new_isolation_association-upf_supply_source
Dumps the new_isolation_association.rpt report that is disabled by default and
disables the upf_supply_source.rpt report that is dumped by default.
Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
The -power_report=<switch> option also provides the feature to enable/disable a group
of reports by passing a single switch. The reports are classified under the following groups
to enable/disable a group of reports:
Group Name Description Group Name
Customer Consumable (CC) Reports used by the users all
NONE Allows you to disable all reports none
DIAG All diagnostic Reports all_diag
STATS Includes profiling reports and reports
containing statistics
stats
SNAPSHOT Includes the snapshot reports snapshot
Using the group feature, you do not have to pass individual reports to the switch. Instead,
the group name can be passed. Following is the use model:
% vcs -power_report=+/-<group_name>
Examples:
-power_report=-all_diag
Disables the dumping of all the diagnostic reports which are dumped by default.
-power_report=stats or -power_report=+stats
Enables the dumping of all the profiling reports and reports containing statistics details.

Precedence Details
The -power_report=<switch> option follows a predefined order in which the switches
are processed. Groups take the lowest precedence, and individual reports have the
highest precedence.
Consider the following case:
% vcs design.v -upf design.upf -power_report=-all_diag+latch_inference
+flop_inference -sverilog
This compile command shows the design being compiled by disabling the all_diag
group and enabling the flop_inference.rpt and latch_inference.rpt reports. These
reports belong to the diagnostic group. The -power_report= feature follows precedence
order and dumps flop_inference.rpt and latch_inference.rpt reports during
compilation.
The following table shows the precedence order for groups:
Group Name Group Name Precedence
Customer Consumable (CC) all 0
NONE none 1
DIAG all_diag 2
STATS stats 2
SNAPSHOT snapshot 2
The following are the key points considered for precedence:
• The CC group has the least precedence regardless of it being prefixed with + (to
enable the group) or - (to disable the group). That is + and - are processed in the
same way. For example,
-power_report=all, -power_report=+all, or -power_report=-all
Enables the dumping of all the CC reports. The all group will not honor the disable (-
sign) option.
• Next in the precedence order is the NONE group. This group too does not honor + and
-. That is, regardless of it being prefixed with + or - it will have the same precedence.
• Next in the precedence order is the remaining groups having precedence number 2.
Here, prefixing the switch name of the group with - will have higher precedence than

prefixing the switch name of the group with +. Groups having the same number have
equal precedence.
• Finally, the individual reports will have the highest precedence. Here too, prefixing the
switch name of the report with - will have higher precedence than prefixing the switch
name of the report with +.

-power_report=stats
All reports in the STATS group are dumped.
-power_report=stats-lp_sig_tree_stats
All reports in the STATS group except lp_sig_tree_stats.rpt are dumped. The reason
is that the individual reports have higher precedence than groups.
-power_report=lp_sig_tree_stats-stats
All STATS reports are disabled except lp_sig_tree_stats.rpt. This is because the
individual reports have higher precedence than groups. Note that even though disable has
higher precedence, the precedence of individual reports will have higher priority in this
case.
-power_report=all-stats
All reports that belong to the CC group are dumped and reports of the STATS group are
disabled. If there is any report that belongs to both groups, it is disabled because the
STATS group has higher precedence than the CC group.

-power_report=-all+stats
All the CC and STATS group reports are dumped. The CC group does not honor - sign.
-power_report=+all_diag-snapshot
In this case, all diagnostic reports are dumped, and the snapshot reports are disabled.
Both these groups have equal precedence. Hence, if there is a report that belongs to both
groups, then it is disabled since disable has higher precedence.
-power_report=stats-stats
All STATS reports are disabled due to the higher precedence of - sign. This case is not
valid for CC and NONE groups.
-power_report=upf_supply_source-+-lp_sig_tree_stats--+stats
If multiple signs are passed, the immediate sign before the report name or
group name is taken into consideration. That is, the above option is equal to
-power_report=upf_supply_source-lp_sig_tree_stats+stats.
You can use the -power=logic_port_net compile option to achieve Synopsys UPF Flow
compatibility for the following UPF commands:
• create_logic_net
• create_logic_port
• connect_logic_net
The following sections describe the semantics of these commands:
• Semantics of the create_logic_net Command
• Semantics of the create_logic_port Command
• Semantics of the connect_logic_net Command
Semantics of the create_logic_net Command
The create_logic_net command creates a wire type net in the scope of the command.
This command accepts a simple name for a net. If the same name net already exists,
then VCS checks its type. If the type of existing net is one of logic, reg, or wire, then it is
the implementation of the UPF net specified in the command. The existing net must be a
scalar of a compatible type (logic, reg, or wire).

Table 45 create_logic_net Command
Purpose Define a logic net

Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
The sim_assertion_control command is a UPF 3.1 command that allows you to control
the behavior of user-defined assertions during low-power verification in a domain or
instance.
VCS NLP now supports the -control_expr option with the sim_assertion_control
command. You must use the -power=sac_ctrl_expr compile option to enable this
feature. Following is the syntax:
sim_assertion_control
[-domain domain_name]
[-control_expr boolean_expression]
[-type <reset | suspend | kill>]
The following sections describe the semantics of these commands:
Any other option specified with the sim_assertion_control command is parsed and
ignored.
• The -type option determines the type of assertion control when the command is
active/inactive:
suspend — Assertions are suspended when sim_assertion_control is active, and
re-enabled when sim_assertion_control becomes inactive.
reset — Assertions are suspended and reset when sim_assertion_control is active
and re-enabled when sim_assertion_control becomes inactive. The reset clears the
assertions of any internal state and sequences.
kill — Assertions are killed when sim_assertion_control is active and the
assertions are not re-enabled or reset.
• The -control_expr option allows you to control all assertions in the design. Consider
the following command:
sim_assertion_control -domain Island_pd_gated -type reset

Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
This command disables all the assertions that are started in this power domain as soon
as the power goes down. Once the power comes back, the assertions are restarted.
However, it might take a few cycles for signals to be stabilized and could still be X.
Therefore, if the assertions start immediately on wake-up, it can still cause failures.
The -control_expr option provides another way, where you can delay enabling the

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
er, it might take a few cycles for signals to be stabilized and could still be X.
Therefore, if the assertions start immediately on wake-up, it can still cause failures.
The -control_expr option provides another way, where you can delay enabling the
assertions until signals are stabilized after power-up.
When this option is specified, the sim_assertion_control command is controlled
by the Boolean value of the expression. If the expression evaluates to TRUE, the
command is active and when it evaluates to FALSE, the command goes inactive. When
the command is active, the assertions controlled by sim_assertion_control are
disabled.
sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr a&&b
For the above command, assertion control is active with type KILL for all power
domains when the control expression a&&b becomes TRUE. When activated, all
assertions in those domains get suspended and are resumed when the control
expression a&&b becomes FALSE.
The sim_assertion_control command can be specified globally or on a particular
domain. The global specification can be overridden by a domain-level specification.
Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2}
The first and third commands enable the assertion control on PD1 and PD2. The second
command specifies the assertion control type as suspend globally on all domains, but
this does not override the domain-level specification in the other two commands as the
domain-level specification takes priority over the global specification.
The same override semantics are applied even in the presence of -control_expr.
Some commands can use domain state, and some can use -control_expr for
controlling assertions. Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr {a == 1'b1}
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2} -control_expr {b ==
1'b1}
In the above example, assertions in PD1 are controlled by domain state (command
1) and assertions in PD2 are controlled by expression b == 1'b1 (command 3).
Assertions in all other domains are controlled with the expression a == 1'b1
(command 2).

Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
Following are the limitations of the sim_assertion_control -control_expr command
support:
• Using UPF logic nets or logic ports in -control_expr is not supported.
• Using power state expressions in -control_expr is not supported.

Overriding Default Bindings
This chapter describes how to override VHDL default bindings using an externally-supplied
file.
This chapter consists of following sections:
• Introduction
VCS allows you set bindings for every instance of a component, or for just one instance,
using a single line.
Suppose your design uses mainly VHDL, and you need to substitute certain instances
with modules from a different library. This other library can be a SPICE library, or a Verilog,
SystemVerilog, or another VHDL library. The standard method is to create a VHDL
configuration. This configuration must include explicit bindings for each component and
instance that you want to change from the default. If these components are located in
many places in your design, the configuration must go through much of the design. This
can make the process complex and hard to manage.
Similarly, specifying architecture other than the most recently analyzed architecture for a
default binding of a given component, the current method is complex.
To avoid errors from nested VHDL configuration syntax, use the -vhdl_bind_override
filename compile-time option to override the default VHDL binding.
This option is described in the following use model.

Chapter 22: Overriding Default Bindings
The option to override default bindings is as follows:
You can use the -vhdl_bind_override filename compile-time option to override default
binding in VHDL. You can apply it to all instances of a component, or to a single unit
(either a VHDL entity or a Verilog module) within a chosen logical library.
Specify non-default bindings using a subset of the Verilog 2K syntax, excluding everything,
except cell and a subset of the use clause.
This option reads the commands from filename, as follows:
cell [orig_library_name.] name liblist library_name [library_name ]
This command uses the library names followed by liblist when creating a default
binding for instances of component name. If present, restrict this to bindings in
orig_library_name.
cell [orig_library_name.] name use [library_name.] entity_name
[(arch_name)]
Same as the command mentioned above, except bind to entity_name. If arch_name is
present, then use it as the architecture, instead of the most recently analyzed architecture.
Examples:
• cell adder use lib1.adder
• cell lib2.adder liblist lib1 lib2
• Only one -vhdl_bind_override command is supported.
For example, vcs <other options> -vhdl_bind_override filename
• If the override file contains two commands for the same component, the first command
takes priority.
• Extended identifiers in the file are supported.
For example, cell adder use lib1.\adder__leaf\
• Comments can be added in the file ( -- or /* - */ ).

Chapter 22: Overriding Default Bindings
The following are the limitations of overriding default bindings:
• Overriding library or entity bindings is not supported for VHDL entities instantiated from
Verilog.
• Currently, only cell-based command is supported. Instance-based command override is
not supported.

Events Per Cycle (EPC) impacts simulation performance, particularly with FGP when
run with higher number of threads. Event activity is one of the primary limiting factor for
FGP performance. The low event activity can be test or design specific. You can use the

The use model is as follows:

-lowepcprof

lowEPCthN

than the threshold number N, where N is an integer value. The default value of N is
1000.
•
maxLowEPCevtsN
maxLowEPCevts: Here, N is an integer value and the default value of N is 100.This sub-
option reports only the top N events.
•-lowepcprof

text:
VCS Performance Tuning Using Dynamic
Performance Optimizer (DPO)
VCS performance is an important aspect that impacts the verification and project time
lines. Traditionally, simulation performance has been a function of CPU performance,
memory efficiency, and serial algorithm. VCS has multiple options to improve the simulator
performance depending on certain characteristics of the design environment that is being
compiled and simulated. These options allow you to identify performance bottlenecks
and tune the command-line arguments and/or coding styles to extract best possible
performance.
Dynamic Performance Optimizer (DPO) is an intelligent automated approach that
enables necessary diagnostics during VCS compile and simulation and leverages AI to
recommend the appropriate set of options for enabling maximum performance without
manual intervention.
DPO supports performance analysis of the full regression or multiple tests per simv.
Enabling DPO With VCS
DPO is enabled by adding the -dpo option to the vcs compile command line. DPO specific
options are enabled using the -dpo_opts <option=value> option. For the complete list
of DPO options, see DPO Options.
-dpo is ignored when specified inside arguments passed to -f/-F/-file. This
option should explicitly be passed on the vcs command line.
DPO Flow
Typical DPO flow involves the following two steps:
Step-1: Learn and Merge
Learn — This step performs analysis and stores learnings/recommendations in the
database. The -dpo_opts mode=learn option at the compile time enables Learn mode.

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
DPO Options
Merge — This step merges the learnings across the designs/tests. This step is mandatory
for applying the learnings. For more information, refer to Merging Learn Databases.
Step-2: Apply
Apply — Learnings/Recommendations are fetched from the merged database and applied
automatically. This step is enabled by default when the -dpo_opts mode option is not
specified or when the -dpo_opts mode=apply option is explicitly specified.
The Apply mode is valid only when a merged learn database is available.
The recommended usage is to run all designs/tests in Learn mode once and then merge
the learnings. You can switch to Apply mode for all subsequent runs.

Supported Apps
You can specify multiple DPO options in the following two ways:
Separate -dpo_opts for each option
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts <option1>=<value> -dpo_opts <option2>=<value> …
Using ‘+’ as the option separator
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts <option1=value> +<option2=value> …
By default, the DPO options specified at vcs stage are used by simv.
If any DPO option is specified at simulation, the option values specified at compile are
overridden.
Supported Apps
The following Apps are supported in the current release of DPO:
• plilearn
Analyzes and optimizes the debug/PLI capabilities to set at compile to improve the
simulation performance.
• gates_sk
Explores the scope to improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations.
• tbopt
Explores potential for simulation performance improvement for the UVM-based
environments.
• ctopt
Analyzes and suggests the options to improve the compile-time.
• fgp
Explores the applicability of the FGP technology for the given design environment
and suggests necessary capabilities to set at compile time to improve simulation
performance.
• lint

Supported Apps
The DPO Lint or Option Recommender (lint) App tries to optimize the simulator
performance by recommending the following:
◦ Removal of command-line options that are not performance friendly.
◦ Addition of certain options that optimize/constrain the default behavior/functionality
of VCS for better performance.
◦ Turning OFF certain default behavior/functionality either coming from language or
simulator.
You can use the -dpo_opts apps=lint compile option to enable this App.
• upfopt
The Low Power or UPF (upfopt)App suggests the options to improve the performance
of the UPF enabled simulation environment. You can use the -dpo_opts apps=upfopt
compile option to enable this App.
• pgates
The Partition Gates (pgates)app suggests the gate-level partitioning options to
improve the compile time. You can use the -dpo_opts apps=pgates compile option to
enable this feature.
• gates_ml
The Gates ML (gates_ml) app utilizes Machine Learning (ML) to explore the scope
and to improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations. Multiple ML
models predict the potential based on the data generated during the learn simulation.
Usage of multiple models increases the reliability of prediction. You can use the
-dpo_opts apps=gates_ml compile option to enable this app. For more information,
refer to Gates ML App.
• gate_keeper
The Gate Keeper (gate_keeper) app parses all options passed to vcs/simv through
command line/-f/-F/-file or nested files and dumps them in vcs_args.json/
simv_args.json inside dpo_workdir. It provides flexibility to monitor a vcs/simv
option with a user script and exit or warn at compile/simulation in its presence.
You can enable the gate keeper app using -dpo_opts in command line. For more
information, refer to Gate Keeper App.
• mg_help
Identifies the necessary Backward Compatibility IDs (BCIDs) during the release
migration. For more information, refer to Migration Helper App.

Design Tag and Test Name
• Automg
The VCS Release Migration Helper (automg) app automates the process of iterative

• Automg
The VCS Release Migration Helper (automg) app automates the process of iterative
refinement of BCID/MHIDs during VCS release migration to ease the migration effort.
You can use -dpo_opts apps=automg on the vcs command line to enable the automg

◦ The lint, upfopt, and pgates Apps must be explicitly enabled using the
-dpo_opts apps=<apps> compile option in both learn and apply modes.
◦ The fgp App is ON by default in the learn mode, and must be explicitly enabled in
the apply mode.
Design Tag and Test Name
The DPO design_tag and test_name options allow you to distinguish the compile and
simulation respectively.
You must make sure that every design is compiled or every unique simulation executable
(simv) built has a unique design tag.
Following is the syntax to set the design tag:
-dpo_opts design_tag=<design name>
If design tag is not set, the default design tag dpo_design is used.
Test name can be set using any of the following runtime options:
Table 52 Runtime Options to Set Test Name
Option Priority
-dpo_opts test_name=<test name>
+DPO_TESTNAME=<test name>
+UVM_TESTNAME=<test name>
+OVM_TESTNAME=<test name>
-cm_test <test name>
-cm_name <test name>
Highest
Default (dpo_default_test) Lowest

Design Tag and Test Name
Test name must contain only alphanumeric and/or special characters except '\',
'?', '*', '$', '(', ')', '/', '&' with maximum length of 255. DPO internally replaces the
forbidden special characters specified in the name, if any, with an underscore
'_'.
Getting the Desired Test Name
You can use the test_type dpo option to override the default priority order of picking
test_name. Following is the use model:
-dpo_opts test_type=<dpo|uvm|ovm|cm_test|cm_name>
dpo – Selects the test name from +DPO_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
uvm – Selects the test name from +UVM_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
ovm – Selects the test name from +OVM_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
cm_test – Selects the test name from -cm_test if it is specified, otherwise default order of
priority is used.
cm_name – Selects the test name from -cm_name if it is specified, otherwise default order of
priority is used.
• If test_type is specified and if the relevant argument is missing, the default order is
considered.
• If test_type is not specified, the default order is considered.
• Specifying -dpo_opts test_name in simulation command line overrides all above,
omitting test_type.

The dporg utility allows you to merge the learn database, dump recommendations into a
csv file, and generate HTML report using the following options:
• merge: Merges learn databases. For more information, see Merging Learn Databases.
• dump: Dumps recommendations for lint and upfopt apps. For more information, see
Dumping Recommendations to the csv File.
• report: Generates HTML report. For more information, see Generating HTML Report.
◦ Each driver should be invoked separately.
You can use the dporg utility as follows:
% $VCS_HOME/bin/dporg <merge/dump/report> <sub-options>
Merging Learn Databases
The dporg merge utility allows you to merge multiple databases available under
design_tag to a merged database. After all the runs are completed, you must run the
utility to consolidate all the recommendations to a merged database. In absence of
merged db with learnings, the Apply phase issues a warning message and continues like a
normal reference run.

_AT_LEAST_ONE_ entry in the testname or test_variant column of the dpo_reco.csv

captures the recommendations per test and decide if a particular recommendation should
be enabled. Sample content of the dpo_reco_detail.csv file is as follows:

Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations
lint,REMOVE,"[['-assert','enable_diag']]",dpo_design,
test1,1,Yes,vcs,"['RT', 'CT']",None,Assertion,Remove heavy assertion
debug flag for regressions

to improve sim performance
Enable/Disable Recommendations in Apply Mode
You must review the dumped CSV file after the learn phase and modify the value
of column enable (Y/N) to have either Y or N. If you want to enable a particular
recommendation, then the value of the field enable (Y/N) must be set to Y. If it is set to N,
then the App considers it as a disabled recommendation.
These feedbacks can be passed to App using either of the following:
• Through the DPO configuration file using the -dpo_opts cfg option. Specify the
recommendations CSV file pointer with App configuration parameter reco_file.
• Through the following DPO option reco_file:
-dpo_opts reco_file=<path_to_reco_csv_file>
◦ Priority is given to the -dpo_opts reco_file option.
◦ If no -dpo_opts reco_file or config options are passed in the Apply phase,
recommendations that are ON by default are applied.
Following is the sample content of DPO configuration file. You can specify reco_file
either at app_configs (applies reco_file globally) or at app as follows:
app_configs:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
lint:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
upfopt:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
The reco_file entry under the app section gets higher priority over the entry under the
app_configs section. For an entry under the app section, only the recommendations
specific to the App are picked from the CSV file.
Dumping recommendations for user review and update is currently enabled for
the lint and upfopt Apps only.

Configuration File
Configuration File
Optional configuration file can be specified by using the -dpo_opts cfg=<config file
path> option to set the necessary DPO specific logging modes, and App parameters to
override any default values for Apps.
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Configuration File Syntax
• Supported Message Logging Modes
• Supported App Configuration Variables
Configuration File Syntax
Following is the configuration file syntax (YAML format ^^):
app_configs:
<Message Logger variables>
< app1_name>:
<app specific config variables>
<config>: <path to app specific config file with
config variables> **
<app2_name>:
<app specific config variables>
<config>: <path to app specific config file with
config variables> **
All variables are specified in the key: value format.
^^ YAML mandates four white spaces for every indentation. Do not use <tab>.
** You can also choose to specify the variable values in an App-specific configuration file
(YAML format).
Sample Configuration File
Following is the sample configuration file:
Example 133 Sample Configuration File
log_output: file
log_level: error
plilearn:
ELAPSED_TIME_THRESHOLD: 600
fgp:
config: /home/cfg_files/fgp_config.yaml

Configuration File
Following is the sample fgp_config.yaml file:
MAX_NUM_THREADS: 6
Supported Message Logging Modes
Messaging is primarily configurable using log_level to choose the severity and
log_output to choose the target for logging. Specify logging related variables in the
app_configs: section of the configuration file. Following is the syntax:
log_level: <info/warning/error> (info is default)
• info: Report messages with info, warning, error severity
• warning: Report messages with warning and error severity
• error: Report messages with error severity
log_output: <stdout/file/quiet> (file is default)
Table 56 Supported Message Logging Modes
Mode Target
file (default) info/warning/error to stdout and dpo_workdir log files
stdout info/warning/error to stdout only
quiet info/warning/error to dpo_workdir log files only
Messages logged to stdout are also captured in the user-specified vcs/simv
log files.

DPO Messages
Recommendations from Learn Mode and action taken during Apply mode are logged to
compile and simulation logs by default.
Learn Mode:
[DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO] DPO mode is set to 'learn'.
[DPO][PLILEARN] [INFO] RECOMMENDATION: NO ACCESS PERFORMED during
simulation. User pli tab files have access capabilities specified.
Please use the updated plilearn tab file with '+applylearn+'.
[DPO][GATES_SK] [INFO] RECOMMENDATION: Potential for improving simulation
time with GATES_SK. Add '-hsopt=gates' as compile command option.

DPO Messages
Apply Mode:
[DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO] DPO mode is set to 'apply'.
[DPO][PLILEARN] [INFO] [PLI MERGE] 'PLI_MERGE_MODE' is set to
'MERGE_ALL'. Considering pli tab files from all learn records in DB.
[DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO] Compile Options: Added:
['+applylearn+<path>/dpo_demo__dpo_pli_merged.tab', '-hsopt=gates'
The following points explain the format of the DPO messages:
• [DPO]: Indicates that the message comes from DPO.
• [APP_MGR]/[<DPO App>]/[<DPO utility>] : Indicates which phase or utility of DPO
is currently running, whether it is app manager, DPO apps, or DPO utilities.
• [INFO]: Indicates severity of the message (info, error, or warning).
• "String": Displays message content.
Following are the DPO message examples:
• [DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO]: DPO mode is set to 'learn'.
The message indicates the DPO mode, whether it is set to Learn or Apply.
• [DPO][CTOPT] [INFO] NO RECOMMENDATION: Elapsed time 5.41 sec for
compile is under the threshold of 100 sec.
The message indicates no recommendation and provides details about the elapsed
time for compile.
• [DPO][DBMERGE] [INFO] DB Merge Summary: Total Input Records = 6,
Records Merged = 6. All records merged successfully.
The message provides the database merge summary.
• [DPO][DBMIGRATE] [INFO] DB Migration Summary: Total Input Records =
1, Records Migrated = 0 and Records NOT migrated = 1. Refer to the
warning/error(s) in /slowfs/vgcs19/snps/IVP_DPO/REGR/probe/6/update/
td/1/db_migrate.log.
The message displays the database migration summary.
• [DPO][DPORG] [INFO] Dpo Dashboard created as …
The message displays details related to the DPO report generation.

Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference mode is an optional step to compile/simulate the design with the DPO enabled
and to capture the performance data into the database. Performance data can then be
compared between the Reference and Apply modes using dporg.
• Reference mode is turned ON using the -dpo_opts apps=vcsgd compile option. No
performance overhead is incurred in reference mode.
• You can choose to have a separate database directory for reference using the
-dpo_opts dbdir=<ref_db_name> compile option.
• Value of DPO options design_tag/test_name must be same as in the Learn/Apply
modes for the corresponding design.
• You can also optionally tag the run using the DPO option user_tag to uniquely identify
the record in the database as reference.
Gates ML App
The Gates ML (gates_ml) app utilizes Machine Learning (ML) to explore the scope and to
improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations. Multiple ML models predict
the potential based on the data generated during the learn simulation.
Usage of multiple models increases the reliability of prediction. You can use the
-dpo_opts apps=gates_ml compile option to enable this app.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts apps=gates_ml <other vcs options>
When gates_ml app is enabled, DPO starts analyzing/optimizing for possible designs.
After the Learn run, you must dump the dpo_reco.csv file using the dporg utility to review
the recommendation, as follows:
In the Apply run, the -dpo_opts reco_file=dpo_reco.csv command is passed to the
command line.
For more information, see Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations.
Gate Keeper App
The Gate Keeper (gate_keeper) app parses all options passed to vcs/simv through the
command line/-f/-F/-file or nested files and makes them available to be processed by

Gate Keeper App
the user script on the fly. It provides flexibility to monitor for one or more vcs/simv options
with a user script and exit or warn at compile/simulation in their presence.
The generated vcs/simv options file in JSON format is passed as input to the user script
with --args_in option. User script is invoked by gate_keeper app as <user_script> --
args_in <args JSON file> .
• User script can be written in any language (python, csh, and so on).
• Ensure that the user script has executable permission before launching vcs/simv with
gate_keeper app enabled.
• User script can read in the args file and do the necessary processing.
• To exit the vcs/simv process from the user script, call exit(1).
Following is the use model:
1. Mention the local script paths for vcs and simv under app_configs, as follows:
% cat cfg
app_configs:
gate_keeper:
vcs_user_script: <User script to monitor/process compile
time options>
simv_user_script: <User script to monitor/process runtime
options>
2. Enable the gate_keeper app using -dpo_opts in command line, as follows:
% vcs <other vcs options> -dpo -dpo_opts apps=gate_keeper+cfg =<path to
config file>
Example: Monitor the VCS options for existence of -debug_access+all and quit compile
if found.
% cat vcs_opts.csh

#!/bin/csh

set args = $argv[2]
echo "ARGS file: $args"
grep "\-debug_access+all" $args
if ($status == 0) then
echo "\nERROR: Option -debug_access+all found. Exit VCS compile.\n"
exit(1)
endif

% cat cfg

DB Migration Utility
The DB migration utility (dpo_db_migrate) allows you to update the existing learn db
(from older version) to the current version without the need to re-learn.
Following is the use model:
dpo_db_migrate [-h] [-d DB_DIR] [-f filelist] [-l logfile]
-d - Specifies the comma separated list of DB directories
-f - Specifies the list of DB directories in a file
-l - Specifies the log file

Plilearn App
• By default, the migrated databases are available in the original directory. DPO saves
the old databases at the database directory level in a new directory <basename>.old/.
All the old .db files are renamed with an extension .db.old.
• If DB migration tool ran on a DB, which has already migrated to the supported version,
DPO issues an info message and will not run any migration.
• When the existing DB version is older than the currently supported tool version, the tool
automatically migrates up.
Plilearn App
The plilearn app supports the following four modes or types of PLI Learn supported by
VCS:
+vcs+learn+pli Enables the module level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli Enables the instance level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli Enables signal PLI learn at the module level.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli
Enables signal PLI learn at the instance level.
You can configure the required PLI Learn mode for a design run using the following dpo
option:
-dpo_opts cfg=dpo_plilearn.cfg
PLI_LEARN_MODE is the configuration variable that decides the type of PLI Learn mode for
a design run. It accepts the following valid values:
MODULE_PLI [Default mode] Generates module PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_PLI Generates instance PLI tab file.
MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates module signal PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates instance signal PLI tab file.
The dpo_plilearn.cfg file contains the following content:
app_configs:
log_level: info

Automg App
log_output: stdout
plilearn:
PLI_LEARN_MODE: MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI
The default PLI_LEARN_MODE is MODULE_PLI. When the PLI Learn mode is not specified in
the cfg file, then the DPO plilearn app generates the module pli tab file.
Incremental Learn Support
The plilearn app is enhanced to run on a set of new or updated tests to incrementally
learn the pli access capability requirement and update the existing learn database. The
incremental learn feature is enabled using the incr_learn dpo option. This option can be
enabled only when the dpo mode is set to learn (mode=learn). If this option is enabled, the
run is considered as incremental learn.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -sverilog test.v -dpo -dpo_opts mode=learn -dpo_opts apps=plilearn
-dpo_opts incr_learn
This feature supports the following flow:
1. Run full regressions in LEARN mode.
2. Continue to run in APPLY mode until RTL/TB changes requiring additional pli access
capabilities come in. When RTL/TB changes, new tests get added and/or existing tests
are updated resulting in the need for additional PLI access capabilities.
3. Run new or set of updated tests with incremental learn for the plilearn app and
generate new learn data.
4. Merge the incremental learnings using dporg merge to update the learn database.
5. Once the learn data is merged, DPO considers the pli learn tab files from step 3 and
step 1 for next apply run.
6. Back to step 2.
This allows you to run a subset of tests to quickly update the learn database ensuring that
the new or updated tests do not fail in the apply regression due to insufficient pli access
capabilities in the learn db.
Automg App
Automg app helps automate the process of iterative refinement of BCID/MHIDs during
VCS release migration to ease the migration effort.

Automg App
BCID provides functionality-related backward compatibility and MHID provides
performance-related backward compatibility. The automg app identifies the appropriate
feature-specific BCIDs and MHIDs automatically for the VCS release migration which
reduces manual effort.
The following is the usage of dpo_automg:
dpo_automg [-h] [-w WORKDIR] [-i] [-b REFERENCE_VERSION] [-u REGID] [-s
{PASS,FAIL}] [-r] -c/--run_script <run script>[--bc_file <bc_file_path>]
[--mh_file <mh_file_path>]
-h/--help displays the help message and text.
-w/--workdir WORKDIR creates automg setup at the specified <dir> instead of the
default directory (default: <current directory>/automg_workdir ).
-i/--init initializes the automg process.
-b/--reference_version REFERENCE_VERSION points to the reference VCS version
where the status of the run_script results in a PASS. For example, 2020.03, 2019.06.
-u/--update REGID provides pointer to the iteration ID. For example, REGID1.
-s/--status {PASS,FAIL} captures status of the run.
-r/--recommendation provides suggestions and the status of the automg process.
--run_script points to the user run script that executes the vcs/simv commands and
updates the status using dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $run_status
--workdir $AUTOMG_WORKDIR .
--bc_file <bc_file_path> is a pointer to the BCID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.
--mh_file <mh_file_path> is a pointer to the MHID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.
The following is the use model:
1. User run script capturing PASS/FAIL status
-dpo_optsapps=automgvcs <other vcs options> -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg
-lca
simv <other simv options>
MY_STATUS=<user defined pass criteria to return PASS/FAIL>
$VCS_HOME/bin/dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $MY_STATUS
--workdir <automg workdir path>

Automg App
Sample run_script:
#!/bin/csh
rm -rf csrc simv simv.daidir ucli.key vcs.cfg

vcs test.sv -sverilog -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg -lca

• [INFO]: Indicates severity of the message (info, error, or warning).
• "String": Displays message content.

Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference mode is an optional step to compile/simulate the design with the DPO enabled
and to capture the performance data into the database. Performance data can then be
compared between the Reference and Apply modes using dporg.
• Reference mode is turned ON using the -dpo_opts apps=vcsgd compile option. No
performance overhead is incurred in reference mode.
• You can choose to have a separate database directory for reference using the
-dpo_opts dbdir=<ref_db_name> compile option.
• Value of DPO options design_tag/test_name must be same as in the Learn/Apply
modes for the corresponding design.
• You can also optionally tag the run using the DPO option user_tag to uniquely identify
the record in the database as reference.
Gates ML App
The Gates ML (gates_ml) app utilizes Machine Learning (ML) to explore the scope and to
improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations. Multiple ML models predict
the potential based on the data generated during the learn simulation.
Usage of multiple models increases the reliability of prediction. You can use the
-dpo_opts apps=gates_ml compile option to enable this app.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts apps=gates_ml <other vcs options>
When gates_ml app is enabled, DPO starts analyzing/optimizing for possible designs.
After the Learn run, you must dump the dpo_reco.csv file using the dporg utility to review
the recommendation, as follows:
In the Apply run, the -dpo_opts reco_file=dpo_reco.csv command is passed to the
command line.
For more information, see Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations.
Gate Keeper App
The Gate Keeper (gate_keeper) app parses all options passed to vcs/simv through the
command line/-f/-F/-file or nested files and makes them available to be processed by

Gate Keeper App
the user script on the fly. It provides flexibility to monitor for one or more vcs/simv options
with a user script and exit or warn at compile/simulation in their presence.
The generated vcs/simv options file in JSON format is passed as input to the user script
with --args_in option. User script is invoked by gate_keeper app as <user_script> --
args_in <args JSON file> .
• User script can be written in any language (python, csh, and so on).
• Ensure that the user script has executable permission before launching vcs/simv with
gate_keeper app enabled.
• User script can read in the args file and do the necessary processing.
• To exit the vcs/simv process from the user script, call exit(1).

time options>
simv_user_script: <User script to monitor/process runtime
options>

DB Migration Utility
The DB migration utility (dpo_db_migrate) allows you to update the existing learn db
(from older version) to the current version without the need to re-learn.
Following is the use model:
dpo_db_migrate [-h] [-d DB_DIR] [-f filelist] [-l logfile]
-d - Specifies the comma separated list of DB directories
-f - Specifies the list of DB directories in a file
-l - Specifies the log file

Plilearn App
• By default, the migrated databases are available in the original directory. DPO saves
the old databases at the database directory level in a new directory <basename>.old/.
All the old .db files are renamed with an extension .db.old.
• If DB migration tool ran on a DB, which has already migrated to the supported version,
DPO issues an info message and will not run any migration.
• When the existing DB version is older than the currently supported tool version, the tool
automatically migrates up.
Plilearn App
The plilearn app supports the following four modes or types of PLI Learn supported by
VCS:
+vcs+learn+pli Enables the module level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli Enables the instance level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli Enables signal PLI learn at the module level.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli
Enables signal PLI learn at the instance level.
You can configure the required PLI Learn mode for a design run using the following dpo
option:
-dpo_opts cfg=dpo_plilearn.cfg
PLI_LEARN_MODE is the configuration variable that decides the type of PLI Learn mode for
a design run. It accepts the following valid values:
MODULE_PLI [Default mode] Generates module PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_PLI Generates instance PLI tab file.
MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates module signal PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates instance signal PLI tab file.
The dpo_plilearn.cfg file contains the following content:
app_configs:
log_level: info

Automg App
log_output: stdout
plilearn:
PLI_LEARN_MODE: MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI
The default PLI_LEARN_MODE is MODULE_PLI. When the PLI Learn mode is not specified in
the cfg file, then the DPO plilearn app generates the module pli tab file.
Incremental Learn Support
The plilearn app is enhanced to run on a set of new or updated tests to incrementally
learn the pli access capability requirement and update the existing learn database. The
incremental learn feature is enabled using the incr_learn dpo option. This option can be
enabled only when the dpo mode is set to learn (mode=learn). If this option is enabled, the
run is considered as incremental learn.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -sverilog test.v -dpo -dpo_opts mode=learn -dpo_opts apps=plilearn
-dpo_opts incr_learn
This feature supports the following flow:
1. Run full regressions in LEARN mode.
2. Continue to run in APPLY mode until RTL/TB changes requiring additional pli access
capabilities come in. When RTL/TB changes, new tests get added and/or existing tests
are updated resulting in the need for additional PLI access capabilities.
3. Run new or set of updated tests with incremental learn for the plilearn app and
generate new learn data.
4. Merge the incremental learnings using dporg merge to update the learn database.
5. Once the learn data is merged, DPO considers the pli learn tab files from step 3 and
step 1 for next apply run.
6. Back to step 2.
This allows you to run a subset of tests to quickly update the learn database ensuring that
the new or updated tests do not fail in the apply regression due to insufficient pli access
capabilities in the learn db.
Automg App
Automg app helps automate the process of iterative refinement of BCID/MHIDs during
VCS release migration to ease the migration effort.

Automg App
BCID provides functionality-related backward compatibility and MHID provides
performance-related backward compatibility. The automg app identifies the appropriate
feature-specific BCIDs and MHIDs automatically for the VCS release migration which
reduces manual effort.
The following is the usage of dpo_automg:
dpo_automg [-h] [-w WORKDIR] [-i] [-b REFERENCE_VERSION] [-u REGID] [-s
{PASS,FAIL}] [-r] -c/--run_script <run script>[--bc_file <bc_file_path>]
[--mh_file <mh_file_path>]
-h/--help displays the help message and text.
-w/--workdir WORKDIR creates automg setup at the specified <dir> instead of the
default directory (default: <current directory>/automg_workdir ).
-i/--init initializes the automg process.
-b/--reference_version REFERENCE_VERSION points to the reference VCS version
where the status of the run_script results in a PASS. For example, 2020.03, 2019.06.
-u/--update REGID provides pointer to the iteration ID. For example, REGID1.
-s/--status {PASS,FAIL} captures status of the run.
-r/--recommendation provides suggestions and the status of the automg process.
--run_script points to the user run script that executes the vcs/simv commands and
updates the status using dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $run_status
--workdir $AUTOMG_WORKDIR .
--bc_file <bc_file_path> is a pointer to the BCID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.

#!/bin/csh
rm -rf csrc simv simv.daidir ucli.key vcs.cfg

vcs test.sv -sverilog -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg -lca
-l vcs.log

if ($status == 0) then
set MY_STATUS="PASS"
set MY_STATUS="FAIL"
endif
echo $MY_STATUS
$VCS_HOME/bin/dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $MY_STATUS
--workdir <automg workdir path>

% dpo_automg --reference_version <passing stream> --run_script <path
to script that launches the run and passes the status of the run back

% dpo_automg --reference_version 2020.12 --run_script ./bm_run.csh --
init
