SDC Verification With Simulation
VCS allows you to validate SDC constraints specified in SDC, during RTL and zero-delay
GLS simulation. The advantages of SDC verification path are as follows:
• Faster turn-around time
• Improved simulation coverage
The following figure shows the steps involved in SDC verification solution with simulation:
Figure 1 SDC Verification Solution With Simulation
The following example illustrates the difference seen in simulation with and without SDC
validation.
Consider the following code snippet:
//MCP source register
always@ (posedge clk or negedge rst) if( !rst ) ff1 <= 0;
else ff1 <= in;
assign mout = ff1 * 2; // multiply takes 2 cycles

// MCP destination register
always @ (posedge clk or negedge rst) if( !rst ) ff2 <= 0;
else ff2 <= mout;

Since multiply operation is expected to take two cycles, the following constraint is defined
in SDC to ensure that any update on signal ff2 due to any changes at ff1 happens only
after two clock cycles.
set_multicycle_path 2 -setup -from ff1* -to ff2*
The default simulation waveform for this code is as follows:
Figure 2 Default Simulation Waveform Without MCP Validation
As shown in Figure 2, a value change in source flop ff1 at timestamp 110 causes a change
in destination flop ff2 within one clock cycle. This is against the intended design delay
specified in SDC.
With the current solution of MCP validation with simulation, the simulation waveform
observed is as follows:
Figure 3 Simulation Waveform With MCP Validation
In Figure 3, when value changed in source flop ff1, ‘X’ gets inserted between source ff1
to destination ff2 and destination ff2 gets the x value because there is an early capture at
destination ff2 time 130.

• Forced signals maintain their value regardless of violations. Violation
messages are for diagnostic purpose, and they do not change simulation
behavior for forced signals.
The following section describes the various options supported for SDC validation. All these
options need to be passed to -sdc=option. The use model is as follows:
% vcs <other_compile_options> -sdc=<sdc_file_path>
This section consists of the following topics
• Compile Time Options
• Using synopsys_program_name variable
• Log Files Generated in mcpLogs Directory
• Enabling Liberty DB Support for VCS SDC Verification
• Runtime Options
• Config File Support
Compile Time Options
Following are the compile time options that you can use along with the -sdc= option:
• -sdc=current_design:<module_name>
This option sets the working design scope for the remaining SDC commands.
If the module scope to be specified is multiply instantiated in a design, specify
current_design in VCS compile command instead of the SDC file.
MCP related statistics after compilation is available in the mcpLogs directory. For more
information, see Log Files Generated in mcpLogs Directory section.
• -sdc=sanity:clock_off
This compile time option is used to disable clock sanity instrumentation.
• -sdc=sanity:constant

This option checks the constant value specified in sdc file using the
set_case_analysis command against the value assigned during simulation. If there
is any difference, an SDC-ERROR is generated at runtime, highlighting the mismatch
between the SDC specified value and simulation driven value. An example error is as
follows:
SDC-ERROR @ time 190 : set_case_analysis testbench.mult.ff1[0],
expected value 0 got X
if the signal that has set_case_analysis set to 0 or 1 is at X, violation is
not reported at time 0 .
• Note:
Example 1 Description of a Sample MCP Violation Report
Early capture violation messages are prefixed with the violation type.
The violation types are as follows:
Violation Type Prefix
Multi-Cycle Path [MCP]
False Path [FP]
Clock Groups [CG]
Max Delay [MXDEL]
False path with maximum delay:
[FP][MXDEL]-EARLY-CAPTURE-VIOLATION @ Time: 290. TO testbench.mult.ff2[1]
(Clock: testbench.mult.clk (sys_clk:basic_test1.sdc:2))

|--> FROM testbench.mult.ff3[0] ……
|--> FROM testbench.mult.ff4[0] ……
Multi-cycle path:
[MCP]-EARLY-CAPTURE-VIOLATION @ Time: 210. TO testbench.mult.ff5[2]
(Clock: testbench.mult.clk (sys_clk:basic_test1.sdc:2))
|--> FROM testbench.mult.ff3[0] ……
• -sdc=verify_false_path:<N>
With this option, every set_false_path command in SDC file is modeled as an MCP
command.
If no value is specified, a multicycle path delay of 10 destination clock cycles is
computed by default. You can override the default delay by substituting argument 'N'
with the required value. For example, -sdc=verify_false_path:2
Figure 4 Example waveform with false path implementation with delay of 2 destination
clock cycles
SDC command used in this example is set_false_path -from [get_cells q1*]
-to [get_cells q4*]
In this command line, since you used -sdc=verify_false_path:2, you can observe
that changes from q1 to q4 gets reflected after 2 clock cycles. (circled in blue)
• -sdc=verify_max_delay
This option evaluates set_max_delay commands present in SDC similar to
set_multicycle_path command. Random delay mode for MCP applies to
set_max_delay path commands also. For information about random delay mode, see
the -sdc=random_delay section.
Figure 5 set_max_delay computation for an example scenario

For a change in ff1, the tool has flagged a violation for a change before 20 timestamps
and the new value is propagated only after 20 timestamps.(absolute value is being
considered as the argument to set_max_delay is an absolute value)
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:<N>
When you use this option, the paths between clocks grouped as asynchronous in
SDC (using set_clock_groups -asynchronous commands) are modeled similar to
multicycle paths but with boolean value inserted (instead of X). If no value is specified,
a multicycle path delay of two destination clock cycles is computed by default. You can
override the default delay by substituting argument 'N' with the required value.
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle
A multicycle path is specified when the path between sequential elements needs
multiple clock cycles, which would otherwise need a single cycle. Therefore, by default,
the tool expects the setup multiplier to be a number greater than 1. If a setup multiplier
of 1 is specified, by default, MCP analysis is not performed, and instead the following
warning is reported:
Warning-[MCP-SINGLE-CYCLE] MCP of single cycle
MCP command(test.sdc:3) has cycle multiplier of 1 and will be ignored
during analysis. Use -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle to turn
on MCP verification of single cycles.
To avoid this warning, -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle compile time
switch can be used.
• -sdc=verify_reset
This option exposes reset domain crossing bugs via X injection at all resettable flops
under the current_design when reset trigger happens.
The -sdc=verify_reset option adds the following options, as it is not
recommended to run verify_reset together with the FP/MCP/CG
verification:
◦ -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:off
◦ -sdc=verify_false_path:off
◦ -sdc=verify_clock_group:off
The following warning message is reported:
Warning-[SDC-RESET-NYS] SDC verification with verify reset is
not yet supported
'SDC' command is getting ignored in presence of
-sdc=verify_reset

With verify_reset, usage of verify_max_delay and dynamic_multi_clock
compile-time switches, like MCP/FP/CG is not recommended.
Figure 6 verify_reset sample waveform
If the destination does not reset at the same time (due to different reset or non-
resettable register), this causes metastability at destination.
By default, X injection happens for one clock cycle of the source clock and can be
controlled by substituting argument ‘N’ with the required value.
An optional configuration file can also be passed with this option to exclude reset
verification on a particular module or hierarchy. An example of configuration file usage
is as follows:
%cat reset.cfg
module {dest_reg} {noSdcReset}; //to exclude a particular module tree
{ddie} {noSdcReset}; //to exclude a particular hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetInsertX}; //insert X on a
particular module/hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetInsertBool}; //insert boolean on
a particular module/hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetInsertRandomDelay};// inserts a
random delay on a on a particular module/hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetNoRandomDelay};//
delays random delay on a particular module/hierarchy

The use model is as follows:

-sdc=verify_reset +optconfigfile+<config_file_name>
For more information about optional configuration file, see the Config File Support
section.
• -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock
This option verifies latency aspect for all constrained (timed by STA) paths and setup
violation aspect of all unconstrained (untimed by STA) paths.

The use model is as follows:
The compile time option is as follows:
% vcs -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock
When -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock switch is not used, and there are multiple clocks
propagating to a sequential element, the tool always picks the fastest clock among
them for analysis. When this switch is used, the tool dynamically selects the clock that
propagates to the sequential element for analysis.
Example, consider the below multi clock scenario:
Following SDC constraints are applied:
set_multicycle_path 3 -from [get_clocks clkA] -to [get_clocks clkC]
set_multicycle_path 4 -from [get_clocks clkB] -to [get_clocks clkC]
-start
There are 4 possible combinations here:
• Combination 1 (clkA => clkC) This is a Multiple Cycle Path, and the path latency
analysis in this case is carried out as: PathLatency(r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less
than 3*Period(clkC)
• Combination 2 (clkA => clkD) This is a Single Cycle Path, and the path latency analysis
in this case is carried out as: PathLatency (r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less than min
(Period(clkA), Period(clkD))

• Combination 3 (clkB => clkC) This is a Multiple Cycle Path, and the path latency
analysis in this case is carried out as: PathLatency (r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less
than 4*Period(clkB)
• Combination 4 (clkB => clkD) This is a single cycle path, and the path latency analysis
in this case is carried out as: PathLatency(r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less than
min( Period(clkB), Period(clkD) )
Once all the possible combinations are evaluated, the tool chooses the combination with
the smallest possible delay for analysis. Based on the above 4 combinations, the tool
validates:
PathLatency(r1_reg=>r2_reg) = min{ 3*Period(clkC), 4*Period(clkB),
Period(clkA), Period(clkB), Period(clkD) }
Dynamic clock sanity checks happen at different points in the clock tree.
• At compile time, the VCS tool gathers all clock signals that are statically connected to
each sanity check point.
• During simulation, the VCS tool checks if the active clock belongs to the list of
structurally connected clocks.
The following sanity checks are performed during simulation:
• WRONG-MASTER-GENCLK
If the clock associated with the source specified for a generated clock in SDC is
different from the clock mentioned as the master clock, then VCS flags WRONG-
MASTER-GENCLK during runtime.
Consider the following HDL code. It includes two input clocks,clk1 andclk2, and an
internal clock gating circuit. The output of the clock gating circuit is a third clock signal
namedclk.
module mult2x(input[1:0] in, input clk1, input clk2, output[1:0] out,
input rst);
clkgater u_clkgater(clk1, clk2, clk);

module clkgater(input clk1, input clk2, output clk);
assign clk = clk1 | clk2;
The following is the SDC corresponding to this RTL:
create_clock -period 20 -name sys_clk1 [get_ports clk1]
create_clock -period 30 -name sys_clk2 [get_ports clk2]

create_generated_clock -add -name sys_clk3 [get_ports u_clkgater/clk]
-master_clock [get_clocks {sys_clk2}] -source [get_ports
u_clkgater/clk1]
The following message is displayed:
[WRONG-MASTER-GENCLK] @ time 10 at top. mult.u_clkgater. clk
(sys_clk3:dynclk_1. sdc:5) Due to top. mult.clk1
(sys_clk1:dynclk_1. sdc:2)
Expected Master clocks
|--> top. mult.clk2 (sys_clk2:dynclk_1. sdc:3)
Reached max clock violations, disabling further violation check on
this clock.
Use -sdc=sanity:clock:violations:<N> to increase limit.
Generating UNKNOWN clock from this point.
To resolve this, ensure that the -source argument corresponds to the SDC clock
specified in the first create_generated_clock command. Additionally, define the
second possible generated clock at the output of the clock gater , u_clkgater/clk.
create_generated_clock -add -name sys_clk3 [get_ports u_clkgater/clk]
-master_clock [get_clocks {sys_clk1}] -source [get_ports
u_clkgater/clk1]
create_generated_clock -add -name sys_clk4 [get_ports u_clkgater/clk]
-master_clock [get_clocks {sys_clk2}] -source [get_ports
u_clkgater/clk2]
• UNKNOWN-MASTER-GENCLK
If the master clock specified for the generated clock in SDC does not reach the-source
pin, then UNKNOWN-MASTER-GENCLK is reported during simulation:
The following is the RTL file:
module mult2x(input[1:0] in, input sel, input clk1, input clk2,
output[1:0] out, input rst);
bit clk3;
always begin #10; clk3 = ~clk3;end
clkmux u_clkmux (.clk1 (clk1), .clk2 (clk3), .sel(sel), .clk(clk));
assign clk = (sel)? clk1: clk2;
The following is the SDC corresponding to above RTL:
create_clock -period 20 -name sys_clk1 [get_ports clk1]
create_clock -period 20 -name sys_clk2 [get_ports clk2]
create_generated_clock -add -name sys_clk3 [get_ports u_clkmux/clk]
-master_clock [get_clocks {sys_clk1}] -source [get_ports
u_clkmux/clk1]

create_generated_clock -add -name sys_clk4 [get_ports u_clkmux/clk]
-master_clock [get_clocks {sys_clk2}] -source [get_ports
u_clkmux/clk2]
The following message is displayed:
[UNKNOWN-MASTER-GENCLK] @ time 10 at top.mult.u_clkmux.clk
(sys_clk4:dynclk_1.sdc:7)
Expected Master clocks
|--> top.mult.clk2 (sys_clk2:dynclk_1.sdc:3)
|--> top.mult.clk1 (sys_clk1:dynclk_1.sdc:2)
Reached max clock violations, disabling further violation check on
this clock.
Use -sdc=sanity:clock:violations:<N> to increase limit.
Generating UNKNOWN clock from this point.
To resolve this, ensure that the RTL design matches the SDC clock definitions. In the
RTL, connect clk2 to the u_clkmux instance instead of clk3, as the following:
clkmux u_clkmux (.clk1 (clk1), .clk2 (clk2), .sel(sel), .clk(clk));
• DYNAMIC-CLOCK-VIOLATION
Assume that the design has a clock mux between 2 clocks, which is controlled by a
select signal. If the select signal changes state when the clocks reaching that mux are
stable and have inverted values, then the mux output is affected by the select signal
change. In such a scenario, the following message is displayed:
The example gives the following violation:
DYNAMIC-CLOCK-VIOLATION @ time 175 : clock
testbench.u_mult2x_wrap.mult2x_clk changed by Unknown Clock
Expected SDC clocks
|--> testbench.u_mult2x_wrap.clk2 (turbo_clk:test.sdc:3)
|--> testbench.u_mult2x_wrap.clk1 (normal_clk:test.sdc:2)
Reached max dynamic clock violations on clock
testbench.u_mult2x_wrap.mult2x_clk, disabling further violation check
on this clock.

The waveform shows that at the timestamp mentioned above, the clock mux select
signal is changed while both input clocks are active (high and low), affecting the output
due to the select signal change. Due to this, VCS SDC reports a DYNAMIC-CLOCK-
VIOLATION message.
To resolve such violations, ensure that the clock mux output change is not triggered by
changes in the select signal.
%The following is the SDC corresponding to the below RTL:

current_design mult2x_wrap
create_clock -period 20 -name normal_clk [get_ports clk1]
create_clock -period 10 -name turbo_clk [get_ports clk2]
set_false_path -from [ get_clocks { normal_clk }] -to [get_clocks
{ turbo_clk } ]

%The following is the RTL file:

module testbench;

reg tclk1, tclk2, trst;
reg[7:0] tin;
bit clk_sel =1 ;
wire[7:0] tout;

always @(tclk1) tclk1 <= #(10) ~tclk1;
always @(tclk2) tclk2 <= #(5) ~tclk2;

mult2x_wrap u_mult2x_wrap(.in (tin),
.clk1(tclk1),
.clk2(tclk2),
.clk_sel(clk_sel),
.out(tout),
.rst(trst));
initial begin
trst = 0; tin = 0;
#1 trst = 1; end
initial begin
$display("CLOCK MUX starts with identical source and destination
clocks at time %t", $time);
clk_sel =1; // u_mult2x.clk2 == u_mult2x.clk1 == clk1
#100; tclk1 = 0; tclk2 =0;
#5 tin = 2;
#62 ;
$display("CLOCK MUX CHANGE, different source and destination clocks
at time %t", $time);
clk_sel =0; // u_mult2x.clk2 == clk2, != u_mult2x.clk1
#5 tin = 4;
#20 $finish ;
end

module mult2x_wrap (input[7:0] in, input clk1, input clk2, input
clk_sel, output[7:0] out, input rst);
wire mult2x_clk;
assign mult2x_clk = clk_sel ? clk1 : clk2 ;
mult2x u_mult2x(.in(in), .clk1(clk1) , .clk2 (mult2x_clk),
.out(out) , .rst(rst)); // DUT

module mult2x(input[7:0] in, input clk1, input clk2, output[7:0] out,
input rst);
reg[7:0] ff1,ff2,ff3;
wire[7:0] mout;
always @(posedge clk1 or negedge rst)
if (!rst) ff1 <= 0;
else ff1 <= in;
assign mout = ff1*2;
always @(posedge clk2 or negedge rst)
if (!rst) ff2 <= 0;
else ff2 <= mout;
assign out = ff2;
Use the following to compile and simulate:
%vcs -sverilog test.v -sdc=test.sdc -R -full64 -sdc=sanity:constant
-sdc=print_violation -sdc=verify_false_path -sdc=verify_clock_group
-debug_acc -kdb -lca +vcs+fsdbon -sdc=diag:clock
-sdc=dynamic_multi_clock
• -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock:advanced
In Dynamic Multi Clock Advanced mode, the tool does not check minimum path latency
and MCP validation happens for only the clock combinations as mentioned in SDC
constraints:
Example, consider the below multi clock scenario:

Following SDC constraints are applied:
set_multicycle_path 3 -from [get_clocks clkA] -to [get_clocks clkC]
set_multicycle_path 4 -from [get_clocks clkB] -to [get_clocks clkC]
-start
The following are the two possible Combinations:
◦ Combination 1: (clkA => clkC) This is a MCP, PathLatency(r1_reg=>r2_reg) should
be less than 3*Period(clkC).
◦ Combination 3 :(clkB => clkC) This is a MCP, PathLatency (r1_reg=>r2_reg) should
be less than 4*Period(clkB).
Sanity checks are performed with -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock and also with
-sdc=dynamic_multi_clock:advanced.
• -sdc=j:<n> -sdc_parallel
This option enables SDC analysis to happen in parallel. It is suitable for designs where
compile time with SDC is higher and SDC processing consumes higher compile time.
You can specify the number of cores on which to parallelize SDC analysis by specific
value of <n>.
For example, %vcs -sdc=j:4 -sdc_parallel
The option -sdc_parallel -sdc=j:N , where N > 3 significantly increases the memory
consumption during elaboration. if there is insufficient memory, the elaboration
terminates with the following message.
"Child process terminated abruptly. Exiting master process.
Please check compile log for potential crashes or try reducing number
of parallel processes using -sdc=j:<num_proc> to avoid processes
going out of memory".
• -sdc=allerrors
This option enables reporting of all the encountered parsing errors. Without this option
the maximum number of parsing errors reported is limited to 1000.
• -sdc=parser_verbose
This option generates an additional diagnostic file at mcpLogs/
sdc_parser_verbose.log. All the parser related messages and prints are dumped in
this file.
• -sdc=hold
This option enables hold checks.
Refer to the Hold Checks section for more details.

• -sdc=mda_struct
This option enables the support for multidimensional arrays and structures. By default,
any reference, implicit or explicit, to multidimensional arrays or SystemVerilog structure
fields is not supported.
Following are the limitations with the current MDA and structural support:
◦ Bus naming support is not available for MDAs and structure types.
◦ Structures within interface are not supported.
The limitations of single-dimension memories or vectors are also applicable here:
◦ Generating with wildcards is not supported.
◦ Parsing with escaped names.
◦ Parsing of up-indexing and down-indexing of vectors/arrays.
• -sdc=allow_nba
This option enables support for extraction of paths assigned by the non-blocking
assignment in the non-clocked procedural blocks.
For example, the following description results in path extraction only with the
-sdc=allow_nba option. Without this option, the propagation stops at this point.
always@(*) begin
mout <= ff1*2;
end
• -sdc=allow_clk_edge
If the source flop fans out to clock pin of a flop downstream, the tool by default
disregards all paths fanning out from the source flop. No SDC analysis is performed on
them and UNHANDLED EVENT CONTROL IN FANOUT error is reported.
With the compile time switch -sdc=allow_clk_edge, the tool disregards only such
flop output to downstream flop clock pin paths. It still performs SDC analysis on paths
spanning from source flop output to data pins of downstream flops.
Enabling of this switch might cause a runtime performance degradation.
• -sdc=latch
This option enables support for latches to be considered as end points for timing paths.

Following are the limitations with the current latch support:
◦ Resettable latches are not supported.
◦ Latches with complicated latch descriptions (non-trivial enable signals) are not
supported.
For more information on the latch checks, see Latch Checks.

• -sdc=ignoreEndBrace
The -sdc=ignoreEndBrace switch in VCS helps you to handle differences in hierarchy
naming between Verilog designs and SDC files. Some signoff tools generate SDC
paths that do not match the default VCS expectations, especially when dealing
with generate block names that include loop indices in square brackets. The
-sdc=ignoreEndBrace switch allows the parser to ignore the closing square bracket in
generate names, thus preventing parsing errors related to this specific syntax.
The following is the compile time option for the -sdc=ignoreEndBrace option:
% vcs -sdc=ignoreEndBrace

Example
If the Verilog file has the /GEN_XYZ/XYZ[0]/SIZEONLY_sync_flop hierarchy ,and the
SDC generated by signoff tool is /GEN_XYZ_XYZ_0/SIZEONLY_sync_flop.
By default, VCS SDC reports parsing error as it expects GEN_XYZ_XYZ_0_/
SIZEONLY_sync_flop.
With this switch, the closing square bracket is ignored without replacing it with an
underscore.
Limitation
Both types of syntax (with and without closing braces) in the SDC file are not supported
together. When using this switch, ensure that all generate hierarchy object names are
specified without the closing braces.
If the SDC file contains object names like /GEN_XYZ/XYZ_0__SIZEONLY_sync_flop
or /GEN_XYZ/XYZ[0]/SIZEONLY_sync_flop, enabling this switch results in a parsing
error.
• -sdc=rstDest
VCS SDC path analysis skips paths where the source signal is connected to a reset
input of the destination. It enables SDC verification of paths when the source signal
drives a reset input of the destination using the -sdc=rstDest compile-time option.
This option does not change default behavior when it is not specified.
Impact on Analysis results when -sdc=rstDest is enabled:
◦ Additional SDC paths (reset paths) will be reported.
◦ Analysis runtime may increase slightly due to additional path tracing.
To enable the functionality, -sdc=rstDest compile time option can be used.
Example
logic src_ff;
always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
if (!rst_n) src_ff <= 1'b0;
else src_ff <= d_in;
end

logic dst_ff;
always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge src_ff) begin // src_ff is reset!
if (!src_ff) dst_ff <= 1'b0;
else dst_ff <= d_in;
end

SDC:
set_multicycle_path -setup 2 -from src_ff -to dst_ff

- Without -sdc=rstDest: Validated Paths = 0
- With -sdc=rstDest: Validated Paths = 1

Asserting vs De-asserting Reset
Path analysis is direction-independent: with -sdc=rstDest, the async reset pin is a legal
MCP destination, so the path is validated at compile time regardless of which way the
reset moves.
Runtime behavior differs:
• Asserting (transition into the reset's active level): the destination is driven
asynchronously with a reset constant, so there is no cycle count to check. The capture
monitor is suppressed by the reset — the path is still validated, but no violation is
reported.
• De-asserting (transition out of the active level): The destination resumes capturing on
a subsequent clock edge, giving a real cycle separation that is checked against the
constraint, so an MCP violation fires normally.
• Latch is not supported, [MCP-INVALID-FROMTO] warning will be reported.
• Module instance reset ports cannot be specified as SDC source endpoints. [MCP-SRC-
ONBOUNDARY] warning will be reported.
Using synopsys_program_name variable
VCS SDC supports the usage of Tcl variable $synopsys_program_name in SDC file. For
VCS SDC, the value of $synopsys_program_name is set to vcs, by default.

VCS SDC EW Messages
Consider the following piece of code as reference for understanding the EW messages
reported in mcpLogs/sdc_errors.log
%cat test.v
module mult2x(input[1:0] in, input clk1, input clk2, output[1:0] out,
input rst);

reg[1:0] ff1,ff2;

always @(posedge clk1 or negedge rst)
if (!rst) ff1 <= 0;
else ff1 <= in;

wire[1:0] w1;
assign w1 = ff1*1;

always @(posedge clk2 or negedge rst)
if (!rst) ff2 <= 0;
else ff2 <= w1;

assign out = ff1;
The following SDC file for the above RTL describes an MCP from ff1 to ff2.
%cat test.sdc
current_design mult2x
create_clock -period 20 -name sys_clk1 [get_ports clk1]
create_clock -period 30 -name sys_clk2 [get_ports clk2]
set_multicycle_path 2 -from ff1* -to ff2*
The most commonly reported EW messages are:
1. MCP-NO-SOURCE: The message Warning-[MCP-NO-SOURCE] No valid source
found means that there is no starting point for the timing path. It has just the end point.
Without two ends to a timing path, there can’t be timing check.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-NO-SOURCE would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -to sys_clk1\
There is no path ending at ff1 which is driven by sys_clk1.

2. MCP-NO-DESTINATION: The message Warning-[MCP-NO-DESTINATION] No valid
SDC destination found means that there is no end point for the timing path. It has
just the start point. Without two ends to a timing path, there can’t be timing check.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-NO-DESTINATION would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -from sys_clk2
There is no path starting at ff2 which is driven by sys_clk2.
3. MCP-NO-MATCHINGPATH: The message “Warning-[MCP-NO-MATCHINGPATH] No
matching SDC path found ” is reported if the tool is able to trace from the -through
point to the source but is unable to find a destination. The timing path doesn’t match
what is described in the SDC.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-NO-MATCHINGPATH would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -through w1* -to sys_clk1
Here although a path from w1 is traced to the start point (ff1) there is no destination flop
which is driven by sys_clk1.
4. MCP-INVALID-FROMTO: The message “Warning-[MCP-INVALID-FROMTO] MCP Path
endpoint is non-sequential ” is given if one of the endpoints (-to/-from) of timing
exceptions such MCP/FP, is not synchronized to an SDC clock.
For SDC timing analysis, the tool expects the endpoints to be either sequential
elements or ports with set_input_delay/set_output_delay, so that there are
synchronized to an SDC clock.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-INVALID-FROMTO would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -to w1*
There is no path ending at w1 (it is has no SDC clock associated).
Enabling Liberty DB Support for VCS SDC Verification
Introduction
In a System-on-Chip (SoC), there are many sub-systems or IP blocks that have already
been verified. The Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) file for the SoC includes SDC files
for these IP blocks. During SoC-level verification, behavioral IP models are used. These
behavioral IPs may not have all the pins and generated clocks that are referenced in the
SoC-level SDC file. The pins and generated clocks mentioned in the SoC SDC for the IPs
are defined in the liberty files (.lib or .db). Therefore, VCS needs to read the .db files for

all these IPs, along with their behavioral models to process the internal lib reference in the
SDC constraints correctly.
Understanding Liberty DB Support in VCS SDC Verification
Liberty DB support allows VCS to read library(DB) files for IP blocks during SDC parsing.
This ensures that references to internal pins and generated clocks in SOC-level SDC files
are resolved, even if the behavioral IP model does not contain all the required pins.
The Liberty database (.lib) contains descriptions of all RTL-level pins and generated
clocks. The following is an example to describe internal or port pins, generated clocks, and
timing arcs in a .lib file to define clock connectivity:
cell(MY_IP){

generated_clock (GC) {

clock_pin : genclk_a ;

master_pin : clk_100 ;

divided_by : 2 ;

duty_cycle : 50.0;

}

pin(clk_100) {

direction : internal ;

capacitance : 0.012622 ;

max_transition : 3.200000 ;

clock : true ;

}

pin(genclk_a) {

direction : output ;

clock : true ;

min_period : 9.2647 ;

timing ( mstr1_genclk_a ) {

related_pin : " clk_100 " ;

timing_type : rising_edge;

………

}

}

If the IP-level .db file is available during VCS SDC processing, SoC-level references to
internal IP pins and generated clocks can be resolved.
After the IP-level SDC clock references are resolved and all generated clocks are read
from the IP-level Liberty file, clock connectivity is properly established in elaborated
design. Now SDC clocks from IP level liberty file are also propagated through the clock
tree.
If you want to update or redefine the generated clock of a library cell, you can do so using
SDC commands. The SDC command should override the generated clocks of the library
cell.
VCS-SDC reads only Liberty files in the .db format. You must convert all
required .lib files to .db using Library Compiler (LC).
Integrating Liberty Libraries with VCS SDC: Configuration, Reporting, and Timing
Arc Analysis
-sdc=liberty_config:<filename>
Where,
<filename> should contain absolute paths to all DBs, one per line.
-sdc=liberty_config:db.txt, where db.txt is the file and its content are as follows:
sdc_a.db
sdc_b.db

Timing arcs analysis begins at the output pins of each library cell. VCS adds buffer gates
and continuous assignments to help data move along the clock path. The tool builds

Runtime Options
The runtime options are as follows:
• -sdc=no_x
This option does not inject X or Boolean values in the MCP path. However, it only
prints the violation message of the MCP constraint in the simulation log. The simulation
remains untouched (without any X or delay insertion) and is similar to a plain VCS run.
The verify_reset checking (if turned on) remains active even with
-sdc=no_x, that is, reset related X-injection is still observed.

• -sdc=off
This option turns off all the SDC and verify_reset related runtime checks. Therefore,
neither MCP constraint violations are printed nor X-injection happens.
Following is an example of simulation waveform with X-insertion (upper window) and
with no_x sub-option (lower window). Both simulation reports shows MCP violation.
Figure 11 Above Snippet shows simulation waveform with X-injection whereas below
snippet shows the same simulation waveform without X-injection
•
-sdc=diagpath
-sdc=diag:path
This option gives a more detailed report of the active and violating paths. Details of the
SDC command considered, relevant line number in SDC file, hierarchical path of the
signal is mentioned. Snippet of output from this sub-option is as follows:
set_multicycle_path (book_example.sdc:8) is ACTIVE & VIOLATING PATH
top.d.q1 => top.d.q4 is ACTIVE & VIOLATING
MCP path summary: considered 1, active 1, inactive 0, violating 1
• -sdc=random_delay

In this mode, delay between source and destination is randomly selected between 0 to
N(N= MCP delay specified in set_multicycle_path command) cycles. Correct value
is always available after N cycles. In case of an early capture, destination will sample
random value if this runtime switch is specified.
Figure 12 An example of a random delay inserted simulation output
Example command : set_multicycle_path 2 -from ff1* -to ff2*
The portion encircled in red at timestamp 130 shows an early capture for the random
delay that was considered. These details can be seen in simulation log where an early
capture violation message gets printed. Because there is a violation, previous value
of 0 is being held till N cycles (N= MCP delays specified in SDC = 2 in this case ) after
which the current value 4 is propagated.
The portion circled in blue shows a random delay of 1 being chosen (delay can be
between 0 to 2 since 2 is the MCP delay value mentioned in SDC)
• -sdc=random_delay:uniform
This option enables random delay injection support for all the destination flop during
SDC validation. This ensures that random delays are inserted based on the path
multiplier limit, preventing masking of timing issues.
With uniform random delays, VCS-SDC can check a violation when the source
changes within the specified violation window and capture occurs on the destination
side. It adjusts the number of cycles for inserting x or bool values based on the
maximum multiplier value associated with the destination flop and remaining violation
window.
Use the following compile time option:
% vcs -sdc=verify_false_path:N
Here, by default the value of N is 10.
In the following example, the FP constraint has "10" cycles of path multiplier limit and
the tool provides an equal weightage for 1,2,39 cycles (1->10-1) on the destination
flop.

Consider the following RTL:
//FP source flop
dff S2 (in, clk2, rst, ff3);
//FP destination flop
dff D2 (ff3, clk2, rst, ff4);

module dff (input [7:0] d, input clk, input rst, output reg [7:0] q);
always @(posedge clk or negedge rst)
if(!rst) q <= 0;
else q <= d;
Figure 13 False Path from S2 to D2
In the false path from S2 to D2, X- insertion occurs between 0 to 9 cycles randomly. At
runtime, during early capture event for a destination, the tool injects X for a specified
number of clock cycles (N). Let the remaining violation window for destination be W.
This number N is decided randomly between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W). Here, M
is the maximum multiplier value associated with the destination. The probability of
selection of a number between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W) is equal.
• -sdc=sanity:sanitystarttime:<time>
This option defines the time after which the detection of clock sanity violations checks
kicks in, at runtime. For example,
./simv -sdc=sanity:sanitystarttime:105ns
Here, the clock sanity checks start after 105 ns, and takes into consideration of
stabilization from 105 ns onwards. Any violations before this time are not considered,
also no clock stabilization logic kicks in before this time. All analysis takes place post
105ns.
• -sdc=starttime:<time>
This option defines the time after which both EARLY CAPTURE violations and clock
sanity checks are tracked and reported.

./simv -sdc=starttime:274us
A violation initiated before this time is not detected.
If both options are specified, then clock sanity checks starts at
sanity:sanitystarttime.
Alternatively, early Capture Violation checks can also be turned off and on via Verilog
toggles or UCLI command.
Checks are turned on by default.
1. Verilog toggles:
The following system call tasks can be added in the RTL code:
$mcpSdcCheck(0); // To disable sdc checks
$mcpSdcCheck(1); // To enable sdc checks
2. UCLI toggles:
sdc_check -off // To disable sdc checks
sdc_check -on // To enable sdc checks
Example messages reported during simulation with switch toggles are shown in the
following:
SDC-LOG: @time: 100 SDC check mode: on
SDC-LOG: @time: 435 SDC check mode: off
◦ -sdc=dynamicfrequency
Without this option, all delay calculations are computed in the compile time and
are supposed to be the same even if the clocks related to these calculations are
running with a different clock period than what is specified in the SDC files. Any
change in clock period beyond the specified clock-margin would terminate the
analysis for that clock.
When this option is used, the clock period is learnt dynamically (from the testbench)
and that is used to recalculate the relevant delay values based on the clock.
Also, any change in clock period also awaits for stabilization before initiating SDC
analysis based on the updated values.
For additional messages, this switch can be augmented with "diag" and
"hi" options and can be used as either -sdc=dynamicfrequency:diag or
-sdc=dynamicfrequency:diag:hi.

Since clock periods are learnt dynamically, when this feature is enabled
the clock-margin grace argument (-sdc=sanity:clock:margin:n) is
ignored.
Example messages relating to observed clock period change when
dynamicfrequency option is used during runtime:
SDC-WARN @ time 133 s : Clock period violation (due to change in
clock period) has been identified. All further SDC analysis related
to this clock: sys_clk except sanity:clock will be stopped.
SDC-LOG @ time 133 s : Clock period updated for clock:
testbench.mult.clk(sys_clk) (File:dynfreq_fs.sdc, Line:1) from 20 s
to 22 s
SDC-WARN @ time 155 s : Clock period within limits (due to clock
period stabilization). SDC analysis related to clock: sys_clk
started.
◦ -sdc=dynamicfrequency:verbose
Enables the printing of period updates as well as delay value recalculation prints.
◦ -sdc=max_destination_violation:<N>
If you specify <N> in this option and when the given number of violations per
destination is reported, then further violation checks for that destination stops with
the following warning:
SDC-WARN @ Time 130. Max violation per destination count(5) reached
on testbench.mult.ff5 and no further checks will happen on this
destination. Use -sdc=max_destination_violation:<N> to change max
violation per destination
At the end of the simulation the destinations are shown in the simulation report as
follows:
Following destination(s) had reached the maximum violation per
destination and further sdc checks have been stopped on those.
Use -sdc=max_destination_violation:<N> to change the maximum
destination violation count.
1. testbench.mult.ff2
2. testbench.mult.ff5
◦ -sdc=finish_max_violation:<N>
When you specify <N> in this option, simulation terminates once the specified
number of violations (global count) is reached. The default value of N is 1000.

For example, if you specify <N> as 7 and the maximum violation is reached, the
following message is displayed:
Global max violation count(7) reached and exiting.
Use -sdc=finish_max_violation:<N> to change the global max violation
count
◦ -sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:<N>
This option enables the reporting of Early Capture violations on the destination
for the same transition in input on successive N or S -1 clock cycles, whichever is
smaller.
Here N is any number higher than 1, and S is the setup multiplier specified in the
set_multicycle_path command.
By default, the reporting count is limited to 1 for a given input transition
that causes a change in the destination within the violation window.
This reporting count can be increased using by setting N to any number
higher than 1 in -sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:<N>.
Example Command: set_multicycle_path -setup 5 -from ff1*
-to ff2*
By default, only single violation is reported for a given change
in ff1 that causes ff2 to change within 5 cycles. However, if
-sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:10 is used, then Early Capture
violations would be reported on consecutive cycles for 4 cycles for a
given change in ff1.
◦ -sdc=violation_prefix:<prefix>
This option adds <prefix> at the start of violation.
◦ -sdc=verify_reset:off
This option stops all the reset verification checks. All other runtime SDC checks
proceed as normal.
◦ -sdc=noprint_violation
This option stops violation message printing.
◦ -sdc=clockglitch:<N>
This option denotes percentage of clock period which is used for clock shifting
delay. By default, 10% delay is applied.
For example, for -sdc=clockglitch:10, delay of 10% of the period is applied.

◦ -sdc=noprint_violation:<tag>
During simulation time, this option suppresses EARLY CAPTURE violation
messages for particular SDC kinds. Specify the SDC command type as an
argument to this option.
-sdc=noprint_violation:mcp: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_multicycle_path commands.
-sdc=noprint_violation:fp: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_false_path commands.
-sdc=noprint_violation:cg: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_clock_group commands
-sdc=noprint_violation:max_del: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for
set_max_delay commands
-sdc=noprint_violation: This stops all EARLY CAPTURE violation printing.
Options to override clock period violation
At the point of encountering a clock period violation, all SDC checks are disabled. Adding
the following options overrides this behaviour and continues the SDC checks. Following is
an example of the warning message,
SDC-ERROR @ time 225 : Clock period violation has been identified. SDC
analysis will terminate. Please use -sdc=sanity:clock:noexit to continue
checks for other clocks.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:noexit
Although the SDC analysis terminates for paths with identified Clock period violation, with
-sdc=sanity:clock:noexit option SDC checks continues for other clocks. Without
-sdc=sanity:clock:noexit option SDC checks is terminated for all the paths, even for
the clocks with no Clock period violation.
Config File Support
You can use the configuration file to enable or disable the specific SDC instrumentation for
a given:
• Module
• Tree

• Instance
• Signal
Descriptions are provided in the following table:
Optconfig Option Description
Module Disable/Enable SDC checks on the module
Tree Disable/Enable SDC checks on the module and hierarchy below the
module.
Instance Disable/Enable SDC instrumentation on the instance
Signal Disable/Enable SDC instrumentation on the signal
• module <module_name> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: module {dut} {noInsertX};
• tree <module_name> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: tree {dut} {noInsertX};
• instance <hierarchy of instance> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: instance {top.dut1.leaf} {noInsertX};
• signal <hierarchy of signal> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: signal {top.dut1.leaf.data} {noInsertX};
• Comments are supported in config file. Lines starting with ‘ //’ are considered as
comments. Example, //This is a comment
• Wildcarding is supported in config file only for modules and trees. It is currently not
supported with instance and signal options.
module {dut*} {noVerifySdc}; //works
signal {top.dut1.leaf.data*} {noVerifySdc}; //does not work
Disable Verification Options:
The following options are applicable for all the SDC options

• noInsertX
• noInsertBool
• noInsertRandomDelay
• noPrintViolations
• SdcResetNoBool
• SdcResetNoX
The following options can disable all SDC verification for a module/tree/instance/signal:
• noVerifySdc
• noSdcReset
• noClockGlitch
• SdcResetNoRandomDelay
Enable Verification Options:
The following options enable all SDC verification for a module/tree/instance/signal:
• insertX
• insertBool
• insertRandomDelay
• printViolations
• verifySdc
• sdcReset
• clockGlitch
• SdcResetInsertX
• SdcResetInsertBool
• SdcResetInsertRandomDelay
The above mentioned commands are used to enable verification on a leaf module when
you have disabled verification on a tree.
tree {subblock1} {noVerifySdc}
module {leaf} {verifySdc}

Note: Options to control X/bool/random delay injection with verify_reset :
SdcResetInsertX, SdcResetInsertBool, SdcResetInsertRandomDelay,
SdcResetNoRandomDelay.
Options such as insertX/noInsertX, insertBool/noInsertBool,
insertRandomDelay/noInsertRandomDelay are for general SDC verification and have
no impact on X/bool/random delay injection with verify_reset.
Limitations:
In Config File Support, the signal option does not work with following enable and disable
verification options:
• SdcResetInsertBool
• SdcResetInsertX
• SdcResetInsertRandomDelay
• SdcResetNoBool
• SdcResetNoX
• SdcResetNoRandomDelay
Multiple Configurations Options for the Same
Module/Tree/Instance/Signal
The following precedence (from highest to lowest in order) takes place when two or more
configurations are applied for the same module/tree/instance/signal:
1. noVerifySdc/verifySdc
2. noPrintViolations/printViolations
3. noClockGlitch/verifyClockGlitch
4. noSdcReset/verifySdcReset
5. noInsertRandomDelay/insertRandomDelay
6. noInsertBool/insertBool
7. noInsertX/insertX
If any counterpart option are present, the last option is accepted.

Options to Control X-injection at Runtime
Options to Control X-injection at Runtime
The use model is as follows:
% simv -sdc=[sub_option][:X injection_control_option]
Where,
sub_option can be any of the following :
• verify_multicycle_path
• verify_max_delay
• verify_clock_group
• verify_false_path
X-injection_control_option can be as follows:
• x: To inject X at runtime
• bool: To hold the previous value by inserting a delay
By using these sub-options at runtime, you can choose between X-injection and delay
insertion.
If this option is not specified at runtime, default behavior would be X-injection on
respective paths identified. -sdc=verify_clock_group is an exception. This option
has a default behavior of delay insertion in the paths identified which can be overridden
using the-sdc=verify_clock_group:x option.
For example,
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:x (default)
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:bool
• -sdc=verify_max_delay:x (default)
• -sdc=verify_max_delay:bool
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:x
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:bool (default)
• -sdc=verify_false_path:x (default)
• -sdc=verify_false_path:bool
• -sdc=verify_reset:x (default)

Sub-options to Control Reset Domain Crossing Verification at Runtime
Sub-options to Control Reset Domain Crossing Verification at
Runtime
The use model is as follows:
%simv -sdc=verify_reset[:sub_option]
where,
sub_option can be any of the following:
• on: Turns on reset validation at runtime.
• bool: Insert Boolean value instead of X.
• N: Insert X/Boolean value on reset assertion for N cycles. If ‘N’ is not specified, tool will
insert X/Boolean value for 1 clock cycle.
• slowclock: Use slow clock instead of fast clock
• random: Insert X for random number of clock cycles (between 0-N) instead of N
For example,
• -sdc=verify_reset:on
• -sdc=verify_reset:bool
• -sdc=verify_reset:N
• -sdc=verify_reset:slowclock
• -sdc=verify_reset:random
Clock Validation
Clock Sanity Checks
During simulation, VCS compares the runtime waveform of a clock with the constraints
defined in the SDC file. These checks help ensure the clock behaves as expected and
matches timing definitions such as period, duty cycle, and generated-clock alignment.
The following are the clock sanity options:
• -sdc=sanity:clock:[sub_option]
This option enables checks at runtime to verify discrepancies between clocks defined
in SDC file using create_clock/create_generated_clock and the values seen on
these signals during simulation.

Clock Validation
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:[sub_option]
Where, sub_option can be any of the following:
◦ dutycycle: Check for duty cycle validation
◦ aligninvert: Check for alignment and inversion of generated clock with respect to
master clock
◦ advanced: Enable all the above checks (period, dutycycle, aligninvert)
◦ noperiod: Disable check for clock period validation
Examples of use model and corresponding diagnostic message printed:
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:dutycycle
SDC-ERROR:WAVEFORM DUTY-CYCLE @ time 190 s : clock
testbench.mult.genclk(genclk): Duty Cycle Observed: 50.00 %
Expected: 80.00 % (File:test.sdc, Line:3)
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:aligninvert
SDC-ERROR:TIMING-ALIGNMENT: @ time 171 s : clock
testbench.mult.genclk(genclk) [master
clock:testbench.mult.clk(clk)],Edge Timing offset Observed @
time:171 s Expected @ time:170 s (File:test.sdc, Line:3)
SDC-ERROR:GenClk EDGE-INVERSION: @ time 170 s :
clock testbench.mult.genclk(genclk) [master
clock:testbench.mult.clk(clk)]: Observed:posedge(master:posedge)
Expected:posedge(master:negedge) (File:test.sdc, Line:3)
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:advanced
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:noperiod
The following are the additional clock sanity configuration options:
• -sdc=sanity:clock:noflop
Ensures that a sanity clock check is not performed by default, if this clock is not
associated with any flip-flops . You must mark this argument as true to conduct sanity
clock checks on clocks that have not experienced any flops. The default value of this
clock is FALSE .
• -sdc=sanity:clock:higherfreq
Reports clock sanity errors only when the run-time detected clock frequency is higher
than the compile time SDC defined clock frequency. If the frequency is higher, the
margin calculations are done after this check. The default value of this clock is OFF .

Clock Validation
• -sdc=sanity:clock:period:nosdcoff
This switch should be used along with -sdc=sanity:clock:noexit. When both of
these switches are used then SDC checks continues for all the paths, even for the
clocks with identified clock period violation. By default, after a few errors, the SDC
checks are disabled. This switch ensures that SDC checks do not stop just because
period errors occur.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:off
Ensures that sanity clock check is not required. Dynamic and regular clock sanity is
disabled in RT.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:stabilizecount
whenever a clocks period changes in simulation the number of cycles of the clock
period is used to stabilize the new clock, during this time no SDC analysis is
performed. The new period is accepted only after this duration if the period is stable
• -sdc=sanity:clock:margin:<percent>
This option defines the percentage margin beyond which violations for period and duty-
cycle is reported. It is essentially a margin of error, expressed in percentage, for clock
period mismatches between SDC period and the runtime period. This is valid for SDC
period versus runtime period mismatches.
./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:margin:10
If clock period is 100 in sdc and 115 in observed with a margin of 20,that is,
-sdc=sanity:clock:margin:20, then there is no period violation.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:delaymargin:<time>
If there is master versus generated clock misalignment of <<time>> then it ignores and
does not report an error.
./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:delaymargin:1000fs
If the misalignment is >= 1000fs then only the clock timing alignment violation is
reported.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:violations:<N>
The number of reported Dynamic Clock Violations can be controlled using this option
by substituting argument ‘N’ with the required value. Dynamic Clock Violation is
reported whenever the clock reaching a flop changes, example, whenever the clock
mux select toggles and output clock changes.

Reading Multiple SDCs
• -sdc=sanity:clock:uncertainty:<percentage>
This uncertainty option is used when there is a clock jitter. For example, if the period is
approximately 10 ns, it might vary by a range between 10.01 and 9.98 ns. To allow this
flexibility in the clock jitter, stabilization time is used. Without this option, the clock does
not stabilize in a particular period if there is jitter.
Reading Multiple SDCs
This section describes how to read multiple SDC files written for different scopes. You
need to use read_sdc option to read from other SDCs inside a top level SDC file. You can
use the following options:
• Module based multiple SDC
◦ read_sdc -module <module_name> <sdc_file_name>
• Instance Based multiple SDC
◦ read_sdc -instance <instance_name> <sdc_file_name>
When an SDC file encounters this command, the design scope changes from current
design to the module name specified in the above mentioned commands. Once the SDC
file commands are executed, the control is returned to top level SDC file and current
design scope.
Example of a top level SDC file calling multiple SDC files:
Module Based Read Multiple SDC Instance Based Read Multiple SDC
create_clock -name top_clk_1 -period

• Forced signals maintain their value regardless of violations. Violation
messages are for diagnostic purpose, and they do not change simulation

The following section describes the various options supported for SDC validation. All these
options need to be passed to -sdc=option. The use model is as follows:
% vcs <other_compile_options> -sdc=<sdc_file_path>
This section consists of the following topics
• Compile Time Options
• Using synopsys_program_name variable
• Log Files Generated in mcpLogs Directory
• Enabling Liberty DB Support for VCS SDC Verification
• Runtime Options
• Config File Support
Compile Time Options
Following are the compile time options that you can use along with the -sdc= option:
• -sdc=current_design:<module_name>
This option sets the working design scope for the remaining SDC commands.
If the module scope to be specified is multiply instantiated in a design, specify
current_design in VCS compile command instead of the SDC file.
MCP related statistics after compilation is available in the mcpLogs directory. For more
information, see Log Files Generated in mcpLogs Directory section.
• -sdc=sanity:clock_off
This compile time option is used to disable clock sanity instrumentation.
• -sdc=sanity:constant

This option checks the constant value specified in sdc file using the
set_case_analysis command against the value assigned during simulation. If there
is any difference, an SDC-ERROR is generated at runtime, highlighting the mismatch
between the SDC specified value and simulation driven value. An example error is as
follows:
SDC-ERROR @ time 190 : set_case_analysis testbench.mult.ff1[0],
expected value 0 got X
if the signal that has set_case_analysis set to 0 or 1 is at X, violation is
not reported at time 0 .
• Note:

The violation types are as follows:

With this option, every set_false_path command in SDC file is modeled as an MCP
command.
If no value is specified, a multicycle path delay of 10 destination clock cycles is
computed by default. You can override the default delay by substituting argument 'N'

For a change in ff1, the tool has flagged a violation for a change before 20 timestamps
and the new value is propagated only after 20 timestamps.(absolute value is being
considered as the argument to set_max_delay is an absolute value)
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:<N>
When you use this option, the paths between clocks grouped as asynchronous in
SDC (using set_clock_groups -asynchronous commands) are modeled similar to
multicycle paths but with boolean value inserted (instead of X). If no value is specified,
a multicycle path delay of two destination clock cycles is computed by default. You can
override the default delay by substituting argument 'N' with the required value.
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle
A multicycle path is specified when the path between sequential elements needs
multiple clock cycles, which would otherwise need a single cycle. Therefore, by default,
the tool expects the setup multiplier to be a number greater than 1. If a setup multiplier
of 1 is specified, by default, MCP analysis is not performed, and instead the following
warning is reported:
Warning-[MCP-SINGLE-CYCLE] MCP of single cycle
MCP command(test.sdc:3) has cycle multiplier of 1 and will be ignored
during analysis. Use -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle to turn
on MCP verification of single cycles.
To avoid this warning, -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:single_cycle compile time
switch can be used.
• -sdc=verify_reset
This option exposes reset domain crossing bugs via X injection at all resettable flops
under the current_design when reset trigger happens.
The -sdc=verify_reset option adds the following options, as it is not
recommended to run verify_reset together with the FP/MCP/CG
verification:
◦ -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:off
◦ -sdc=verify_false_path:off
◦ -sdc=verify_clock_group:off
The following warning message is reported:
Warning-[SDC-RESET-NYS] SDC verification with verify reset is
not yet supported
'SDC' command is getting ignored in presence of
-sdc=verify_reset

With verify_reset, usage of verify_max_delay and dynamic_multi_clock
compile-time switches, like MCP/FP/CG is not recommended.
Figure 6 verify_reset sample waveform
If the destination does not reset at the same time (due to different reset or non-
resettable register), this causes metastability at destination.
By default, X injection happens for one clock cycle of the source clock and can be
controlled by substituting argument ‘N’ with the required value.
An optional configuration file can also be passed with this option to exclude reset
verification on a particular module or hierarchy. An example of configuration file usage
is as follows:
%cat reset.cfg
module {dest_reg} {noSdcReset}; //to exclude a particular module tree
{ddie} {noSdcReset}; //to exclude a particular hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetInsertX}; //insert X on a
particular module/hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetInsertBool}; //insert boolean on
a particular module/hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetInsertRandomDelay};// inserts a
random delay on a on a particular module/hierarchy
module/tree {<module_name>} {SdcResetNoRandomDelay};//
delays random delay on a particular module/hierarchy

The use model is as follows:

-sdc=verify_reset +optconfigfile+<config_file_name>
For more information about optional configuration file, see the Config File Support
section.
• -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock
This option verifies latency aspect for all constrained (timed by STA) paths and setup
violation aspect of all unconstrained (untimed by STA) paths.

The use model is as follows:
The compile time option is as follows:
% vcs -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock
When -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock switch is not used, and there are multiple clocks
propagating to a sequential element, the tool always picks the fastest clock among
them for analysis. When this switch is used, the tool dynamically selects the clock that
propagates to the sequential element for analysis.
Example, consider the below multi clock scenario:
Following SDC constraints are applied:
set_multicycle_path 3 -from [get_clocks clkA] -to [get_clocks clkC]
set_multicycle_path 4 -from [get_clocks clkB] -to [get_clocks clkC]
-start
There are 4 possible combinations here:
• Combination 1 (clkA => clkC) This is a Multiple Cycle Path, and the path latency
analysis in this case is carried out as: PathLatency(r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less
than 3*Period(clkC)
• Combination 2 (clkA => clkD) This is a Single Cycle Path, and the path latency analysis
in this case is carried out as: PathLatency (r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less than min
(Period(clkA), Period(clkD))

• Combination 3 (clkB => clkC) This is a Multiple Cycle Path, and the path latency
analysis in this case is carried out as: PathLatency (r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less
than 4*Period(clkB)
• Combination 4 (clkB => clkD) This is a single cycle path, and the path latency analysis
in this case is carried out as: PathLatency(r1_reg=>r2_reg) should be less than
min( Period(clkB), Period(clkD) )
Once all the possible combinations are evaluated, the tool chooses the combination with
the smallest possible delay for analysis. Based on the above 4 combinations, the tool
validates:
PathLatency(r1_reg=>r2_reg) = min{ 3*Period(clkC), 4*Period(clkB),
Period(clkA), Period(clkB), Period(clkD) }
Dynamic clock sanity checks happen at different points in the clock tree.
• At compile time, the VCS tool gathers all clock signals that are statically connected to
each sanity check point.
• During simulation, the VCS tool checks if the active clock belongs to the list of
structurally connected clocks.
The following sanity checks are performed during simulation:
• WRONG-MASTER-GENCLK
If the clock associated with the source specified for a generated clock in SDC is
different from the clock mentioned as the master clock, then VCS flags WRONG-
MASTER-GENCLK during runtime.
Consider the following HDL code. It includes two input clocks,clk1 andclk2, and an
internal clock gating circuit. The output of the clock gating circuit is a third clock signal
namedclk.
module mult2x(input[1:0] in, input clk1, input clk2, output[1:0] out,
input rst);
clkgater u_clkgater(clk1, clk2, clk);

• -sdc=j:<n> -sdc_parallel
This option enables SDC analysis to happen in parallel. It is suitable for designs where
compile time with SDC is higher and SDC processing consumes higher compile time.
You can specify the number of cores on which to parallelize SDC analysis by specific
value of <n>.
For example, %vcs -sdc=j:4 -sdc_parallel
The option -sdc_parallel -sdc=j:N , where N > 3 significantly increases the memory
consumption during elaboration. if there is insufficient memory, the elaboration
terminates with the following message.
"Child process terminated abruptly. Exiting master process.
Please check compile log for potential crashes or try reducing number
of parallel processes using -sdc=j:<num_proc> to avoid processes
going out of memory".
• -sdc=allerrors
This option enables reporting of all the encountered parsing errors. Without this option
the maximum number of parsing errors reported is limited to 1000.
• -sdc=parser_verbose
This option generates an additional diagnostic file at mcpLogs/
sdc_parser_verbose.log. All the parser related messages and prints are dumped in
this file.
• -sdc=hold
This option enables hold checks.
Refer to the Hold Checks section for more details.

• -sdc=mda_struct
This option enables the support for multidimensional arrays and structures. By default,
any reference, implicit or explicit, to multidimensional arrays or SystemVerilog structure
fields is not supported.
Following are the limitations with the current MDA and structural support:
◦ Bus naming support is not available for MDAs and structure types.
◦ Structures within interface are not supported.
The limitations of single-dimension memories or vectors are also applicable here:
◦ Generating with wildcards is not supported.
◦ Parsing with escaped names.
◦ Parsing of up-indexing and down-indexing of vectors/arrays.
• -sdc=allow_nba
This option enables support for extraction of paths assigned by the non-blocking
assignment in the non-clocked procedural blocks.
For example, the following description results in path extraction only with the
-sdc=allow_nba option. Without this option, the propagation stops at this point.
always@(*) begin
mout <= ff1*2;
end
• -sdc=allow_clk_edge
If the source flop fans out to clock pin of a flop downstream, the tool by default
disregards all paths fanning out from the source flop. No SDC analysis is performed on
them and UNHANDLED EVENT CONTROL IN FANOUT error is reported.
With the compile time switch -sdc=allow_clk_edge, the tool disregards only such
flop output to downstream flop clock pin paths. It still performs SDC analysis on paths
spanning from source flop output to data pins of downstream flops.
Enabling of this switch might cause a runtime performance degradation.
• -sdc=latch
This option enables support for latches to be considered as end points for timing paths.

Following are the limitations with the current latch support:
◦ Resettable latches are not supported.
◦ Latches with complicated latch descriptions (non-trivial enable signals) are not
supported.
For more information on the latch checks, see Latch Checks.
• -sdc=abort_no_sdc_path
This option is used to terminate a compilation with an error message if no valid path is
found during the SDC analysis.
The following is the use model for the -sdc=abort_no_sdc_path option:
vcs -sdc=abort_no_sdc_path <other_compile_option>
Usage:
Refer to the following example:
vcs <test_file>.v -sdc=<test_file>.sdc,diag:hi -sverilog
-sdc=abort_no_sdc_path
Output
The compilation aborts with the following error message because no SDC path is found
in the design:
[VCS-DIV] -- Error : No SDC paths found for validation, aborting
elaboration as -sdc=abort_no_sdc_path is given. Please look into
mcpLogs directory for detailed diagnostics
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:off
This option is used at the compile time to disable the creation and verification of the
multicycle path.
The following is the compile time option for the -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:off
option:
% vcs -sdc= verify_multicycle_path:off
• -sdc=verify_false_path:off
This option is used at the compile time to disable the creation and verification of the
false path.

The following is the compile time option for the -sdc=verify_false_path:off option:
% vcs -sdc= verify_false_path:off
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:off
This option is used at the compile time to disable the creation and verification of the
clock group commands.
The following is the compile time option for the -sdc=verify_false_path:off option:
% vcs -sdc=verify_clock_group:off
• -sdc=intflogic:enable
By default, the tracing through the interface with wire members is supported. With this
switch the support to logic members of the interface is extended.
The following is the compile time option for the -sdc=intflogic:enable option:
% vcs -sdc=intflogic:enable
Usage:
Refer to the following example:
interface ffbus(input clk, input rst);
logic [1:0] outData;
logic [1:0] inData;
endinterface

set_multicycle_path 2 -through [get_nets I2/inData]
Limitation:
◦ Verdi marking is supported only for the scalar logic members.
◦ set_Input_delay and set_output_delay are not supported for interface logic
members. The following UNSUPP-OBJ errors are reported on such interface logic
members:
▪ set_input_delay 2 -clock clk {I.logic_member} – UNSUPP-OBJ will be
flagged.
▪ set_output_delay 2 -clock clk {I.logic_member} – UNSUPP-OBJ will be
flagged.

• -sdc=coverage:cmt
This option enables the comments from Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC)
commands to be included in the exclusion file together with the coverage report for
all SDC levels. This allows you to quickly and effectively locate commands in the
exclusion file.

This compile time option enables the dumping of the detailed path report
mcp.<current_design>.DetailedPathReport.log.gz in the mcpLogs directory.
The following report contains source or destination information for all paths
corresponding to each SDC command.
Figure 10 Report
• -sdc=ignoreEndBrace
The -sdc=ignoreEndBrace switch in VCS helps you to handle differences in hierarchy
naming between Verilog designs and SDC files. Some signoff tools generate SDC
paths that do not match the default VCS expectations, especially when dealing
with generate block names that include loop indices in square brackets. The
-sdc=ignoreEndBrace switch allows the parser to ignore the closing square bracket in
generate names, thus preventing parsing errors related to this specific syntax.
The following is the compile time option for the -sdc=ignoreEndBrace option:
% vcs -sdc=ignoreEndBrace

text:
Example
If the Verilog file has the /GEN_XYZ/XYZ[0]/SIZEONLY_sync_flop hierarchy ,and the
SDC generated by signoff tool is /GEN_XYZ_XYZ_0/SIZEONLY_sync_flop.
By default, VCS SDC reports parsing error as it expects GEN_XYZ_XYZ_0_/
SIZEONLY_sync_flop.
With this switch, the closing square bracket is ignored without replacing it with an
underscore.
Limitation
Both types of syntax (with and without closing braces) in the SDC file are not supported
together. When using this switch, ensure that all generate hierarchy object names are
specified without the closing braces.
If the SDC file contains object names like /GEN_XYZ/XYZ_0__SIZEONLY_sync_flop
or /GEN_XYZ/XYZ[0]/SIZEONLY_sync_flop, enabling this switch results in a parsing
error.
• -sdc=rstDest
VCS SDC path analysis skips paths where the source signal is connected to a reset
input of the destination. It enables SDC verification of paths when the source signal
drives a reset input of the destination using the -sdc=rstDest compile-time option.
This option does not change default behavior when it is not specified.
Impact on Analysis results when -sdc=rstDest is enabled:
◦ Additional SDC paths (reset paths) will be reported.
◦ Analysis runtime may increase slightly due to additional path tracing.
To enable the functionality, -sdc=rstDest compile time option can be used.
Example
logic src_ff;
always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
if (!rst_n) src_ff <= 1'b0;
else src_ff <= d_in;
end

title: 1 signals toggle at the same time the simulation output does not show ‘X’ at
text:
logic dst_ff;
always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge src_ff) begin // src_ff is reset!
if (!src_ff) dst_ff <= 1'b0;
else dst_ff <= d_in;
end

SDC:
set_multicycle_path -setup 2 -from src_ff -to dst_ff

- Without -sdc=rstDest: Validated Paths = 0
- With -sdc=rstDest: Validated Paths = 1

Asserting vs De-asserting Reset
Path analysis is direction-independent: with -sdc=rstDest, the async reset pin is a legal
MCP destination, so the path is validated at compile time regardless of which way the
reset moves.
Runtime behavior differs:
• Asserting (transition into the reset's active level): the destination is driven
asynchronously with a reset constant, so there is no cycle count to check. The capture
monitor is suppressed by the reset — the path is still validated, but no violation is
reported.
• De-asserting (transition out of the active level): The destination resumes capturing on
a subsequent clock edge, giving a real cycle separation that is checked against the
constraint, so an MCP violation fires normally.
• Latch is not supported, [MCP-INVALID-FROMTO] warning will be reported.
• Module instance reset ports cannot be specified as SDC source endpoints. [MCP-SRC-
ONBOUNDARY] warning will be reported.
Using synopsys_program_name variable
VCS SDC supports the usage of Tcl variable $synopsys_program_name in SDC file. For
VCS SDC, the value of $synopsys_program_name is set to vcs, by default.

assign out = ff1;
The following SDC file for the above RTL describes an MCP from ff1 to ff2.
%cat test.sdc
current_design mult2x
create_clock -period 20 -name sys_clk1 [get_ports clk1]
create_clock -period 30 -name sys_clk2 [get_ports clk2]
set_multicycle_path 2 -from ff1* -to ff2*
The most commonly reported EW messages are:
1. MCP-NO-SOURCE: The message Warning-[MCP-NO-SOURCE] No valid source
found means that there is no starting point for the timing path. It has just the end point.
Without two ends to a timing path, there can’t be timing check.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-NO-SOURCE would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -to sys_clk1\
There is no path ending at ff1 which is driven by sys_clk1.

2. MCP-NO-DESTINATION: The message Warning-[MCP-NO-DESTINATION] No valid
SDC destination found means that there is no end point for the timing path. It has
just the start point. Without two ends to a timing path, there can’t be timing check.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-NO-DESTINATION would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -from sys_clk2
There is no path starting at ff2 which is driven by sys_clk2.
3. MCP-NO-MATCHINGPATH: The message “Warning-[MCP-NO-MATCHINGPATH] No
matching SDC path found ” is reported if the tool is able to trace from the -through
point to the source but is unable to find a destination. The timing path doesn’t match
what is described in the SDC.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-NO-MATCHINGPATH would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -through w1* -to sys_clk1
Here although a path from w1 is traced to the start point (ff1) there is no destination flop
which is driven by sys_clk1.
4. MCP-INVALID-FROMTO: The message “Warning-[MCP-INVALID-FROMTO] MCP Path
endpoint is non-sequential ” is given if one of the endpoints (-to/-from) of timing
exceptions such MCP/FP, is not synchronized to an SDC clock.
For SDC timing analysis, the tool expects the endpoints to be either sequential
elements or ports with set_input_delay/set_output_delay, so that there are
synchronized to an SDC clock.
For example, if the above original MCP command was replaced by the below
command MCP-INVALID-FROMTO would be reported.
set_multicycle_path 2 -to w1*
There is no path ending at w1 (it is has no SDC clock associated).
Enabling Liberty DB Support for VCS SDC Verification
Introduction
In a System-on-Chip (SoC), there are many sub-systems or IP blocks that have already
been verified. The Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) file for the SoC includes SDC files
for these IP blocks. During SoC-level verification, behavioral IP models are used. These
behavioral IPs may not have all the pins and generated clocks that are referenced in the
SoC-level SDC file. The pins and generated clocks mentioned in the SoC SDC for the IPs
are defined in the liberty files (.lib or .db). Therefore, VCS needs to read the .db files for

all these IPs, along with their behavioral models to process the internal lib reference in the
SDC constraints correctly.
Understanding Liberty DB Support in VCS SDC Verification
Liberty DB support allows VCS to read library(DB) files for IP blocks during SDC parsing.
This ensures that references to internal pins and generated clocks in SOC-level SDC files
are resolved, even if the behavioral IP model does not contain all the required pins.
The Liberty database (.lib) contains descriptions of all RTL-level pins and generated
clocks. The following is an example to describe internal or port pins, generated clocks, and
timing arcs in a .lib file to define clock connectivity:
cell(MY_IP){

generated_clock (GC) {

clock_pin : genclk_a ;

master_pin : clk_100 ;

divided_by : 2 ;

duty_cycle : 50.0;

}

pin(clk_100) {

direction : internal ;

capacitance : 0.012622 ;

max_transition : 3.200000 ;

clock : true ;

}

pin(genclk_a) {

direction : output ;

clock : true ;

min_period : 9.2647 ;

timing ( mstr1_genclk_a ) {

related_pin : " clk_100 " ;

timing_type : rising_edge;

………

}

}

If the IP-level .db file is available during VCS SDC processing, SoC-level references to
internal IP pins and generated clocks can be resolved.
After the IP-level SDC clock references are resolved and all generated clocks are read
from the IP-level Liberty file, clock connectivity is properly established in elaborated
design. Now SDC clocks from IP level liberty file are also propagated through the clock
tree.
If you want to update or redefine the generated clock of a library cell, you can do so using
SDC commands. The SDC command should override the generated clocks of the library
cell.
VCS-SDC reads only Liberty files in the .db format. You must convert all
required .lib files to .db using Library Compiler (LC).
Integrating Liberty Libraries with VCS SDC: Configuration, Reporting, and Timing
Arc Analysis
-sdc=liberty_config:<filename>
Where,
<filename> should contain absolute paths to all DBs, one per line.
-sdc=liberty_config:db.txt, where db.txt is the file and its content are as follows:
sdc_a.db
sdc_b.db

Timing Arcs Analysis
Timing arcs analysis begins at the output pins of each library cell. VCS adds buffer gates
and continuous assignments to help data move along the clock path. The tool builds
paths using the related pins for each pin. After parsing, the library_mapping.rpt report
includes timing arc information for each cell.

Runtime Options
The runtime options are as follows:
• -sdc=no_x
This option does not inject X or Boolean values in the MCP path. However, it only
prints the violation message of the MCP constraint in the simulation log. The simulation
remains untouched (without any X or delay insertion) and is similar to a plain VCS run.
The verify_reset checking (if turned on) remains active even with
-sdc=no_x, that is, reset related X-injection is still observed.

chapter: 1 signals toggle at the same time the simulation output does not show ‘X’ at
title: 1 signals toggle at the same time the simulation output does not show ‘X’ at
