• -sdc=off
This option turns off all the SDC and verify_reset related runtime checks. Therefore,
neither MCP constraint violations are printed nor X-injection happens.
Following is an example of simulation waveform with X-insertion (upper window) and
with no_x sub-option (lower window). Both simulation reports shows MCP violation.
Figure 11 Above Snippet shows simulation waveform with X-injection whereas below
snippet shows the same simulation waveform without X-injection
•
-sdc=diagpath
-sdc=diag:path
This option gives a more detailed report of the active and violating paths. Details of the
SDC command considered, relevant line number in SDC file, hierarchical path of the
signal is mentioned. Snippet of output from this sub-option is as follows:
set_multicycle_path (book_example.sdc:8) is ACTIVE & VIOLATING PATH
top.d.q1 => top.d.q4 is ACTIVE & VIOLATING
MCP path summary: considered 1, active 1, inactive 0, violating 1
• -sdc=random_delay

In this mode, delay between source and destination is randomly selected between 0 to
N(N= MCP delay specified in set_multicycle_path command) cycles. Correct value
is always available after N cycles. In case of an early capture, destination will sample
random value if this runtime switch is specified.
Figure 12 An example of a random delay inserted simulation output
Example command : set_multicycle_path 2 -from ff1* -to ff2*
The portion encircled in red at timestamp 130 shows an early capture for the random
delay that was considered. These details can be seen in simulation log where an early
capture violation message gets printed. Because there is a violation, previous value
of 0 is being held till N cycles (N= MCP delays specified in SDC = 2 in this case ) after
which the current value 4 is propagated.
The portion circled in blue shows a random delay of 1 being chosen (delay can be
between 0 to 2 since 2 is the MCP delay value mentioned in SDC)
• -sdc=random_delay:uniform
This option enables random delay injection support for all the destination flop during
SDC validation. This ensures that random delays are inserted based on the path
multiplier limit, preventing masking of timing issues.
With uniform random delays, VCS-SDC can check a violation when the source
changes within the specified violation window and capture occurs on the destination
side. It adjusts the number of cycles for inserting x or bool values based on the
maximum multiplier value associated with the destination flop and remaining violation
window.
Use the following compile time option:
% vcs -sdc=verify_false_path:N
Here, by default the value of N is 10.
In the following example, the FP constraint has "10" cycles of path multiplier limit and
the tool provides an equal weightage for 1,2,39 cycles (1->10-1) on the destination
flop.

Consider the following RTL:
//FP source flop
dff S2 (in, clk2, rst, ff3);
//FP destination flop
dff D2 (ff3, clk2, rst, ff4);

module dff (input [7:0] d, input clk, input rst, output reg [7:0] q);
always @(posedge clk or negedge rst)
if(!rst) q <= 0;
else q <= d;
Figure 13 False Path from S2 to D2
In the false path from S2 to D2, X- insertion occurs between 0 to 9 cycles randomly. At
runtime, during early capture event for a destination, the tool injects X for a specified
number of clock cycles (N). Let the remaining violation window for destination be W.
This number N is decided randomly between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W). Here, M
is the maximum multiplier value associated with the destination. The probability of
selection of a number between 0 to minimum of (M-1 and W) is equal.
• -sdc=sanity:sanitystarttime:<time>
This option defines the time after which the detection of clock sanity violations checks
kicks in, at runtime. For example,
./simv -sdc=sanity:sanitystarttime:105ns
Here, the clock sanity checks start after 105 ns, and takes into consideration of
stabilization from 105 ns onwards. Any violations before this time are not considered,
also no clock stabilization logic kicks in before this time. All analysis takes place post
105ns.
• -sdc=starttime:<time>
This option defines the time after which both EARLY CAPTURE violations and clock
sanity checks are tracked and reported.

./simv -sdc=starttime:274us
A violation initiated before this time is not detected.
If both options are specified, then clock sanity checks starts at
sanity:sanitystarttime.
Alternatively, early Capture Violation checks can also be turned off and on via Verilog
toggles or UCLI command.
Checks are turned on by default.
1. Verilog toggles:
The following system call tasks can be added in the RTL code:
$mcpSdcCheck(0); // To disable sdc checks
$mcpSdcCheck(1); // To enable sdc checks
2. UCLI toggles:
sdc_check -off // To disable sdc checks
sdc_check -on // To enable sdc checks
Example messages reported during simulation with switch toggles are shown in the
following:
SDC-LOG: @time: 100 SDC check mode: on
SDC-LOG: @time: 435 SDC check mode: off
◦ -sdc=dynamicfrequency
Without this option, all delay calculations are computed in the compile time and
are supposed to be the same even if the clocks related to these calculations are
running with a different clock period than what is specified in the SDC files. Any
change in clock period beyond the specified clock-margin would terminate the
analysis for that clock.
When this option is used, the clock period is learnt dynamically (from the testbench)
and that is used to recalculate the relevant delay values based on the clock.
Also, any change in clock period also awaits for stabilization before initiating SDC
analysis based on the updated values.
For additional messages, this switch can be augmented with "diag" and
"hi" options and can be used as either -sdc=dynamicfrequency:diag or
-sdc=dynamicfrequency:diag:hi.

Since clock periods are learnt dynamically, when this feature is enabled
the clock-margin grace argument (-sdc=sanity:clock:margin:n) is
ignored.

◦ -sdc=dynamicfrequency:verbose
Enables the printing of period updates as well as delay value recalculation prints.
◦ -sdc=max_destination_violation:<N>
If you specify <N> in this option and when the given number of violations per
destination is reported, then further violation checks for that destination stops with
the following warning:
SDC-WARN @ Time 130. Max violation per destination count(5) reached
on testbench.mult.ff5 and no further checks will happen on this
destination. Use -sdc=max_destination_violation:<N> to change max
violation per destination
At the end of the simulation the destinations are shown in the simulation report as
follows:
Following destination(s) had reached the maximum violation per
destination and further sdc checks have been stopped on those.
Use -sdc=max_destination_violation:<N> to change the maximum
destination violation count.

For example, if you specify <N> as 7 and the maximum violation is reached, the
following message is displayed:
Global max violation count(7) reached and exiting.
Use -sdc=finish_max_violation:<N> to change the global max violation
count
◦ -sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:<N>
This option enables the reporting of Early Capture violations on the destination
for the same transition in input on successive N or S -1 clock cycles, whichever is
smaller.
Here N is any number higher than 1, and S is the setup multiplier specified in the
set_multicycle_path command.
By default, the reporting count is limited to 1 for a given input transition
that causes a change in the destination within the violation window.
This reporting count can be increased using by setting N to any number
higher than 1 in -sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:<N>.
Example Command: set_multicycle_path -setup 5 -from ff1*
-to ff2*
By default, only single violation is reported for a given change
in ff1 that causes ff2 to change within 5 cycles. However, if
-sdc=maxSuccessiveViolations:10 is used, then Early Capture
violations would be reported on consecutive cycles for 4 cycles for a
given change in ff1.
◦ -sdc=violation_prefix:<prefix>
This option adds <prefix> at the start of violation.
◦ -sdc=verify_reset:off
This option stops all the reset verification checks. All other runtime SDC checks
proceed as normal.
◦ -sdc=noprint_violation
This option stops violation message printing.
◦ -sdc=clockglitch:<N>
This option denotes percentage of clock period which is used for clock shifting
delay. By default, 10% delay is applied.
For example, for -sdc=clockglitch:10, delay of 10% of the period is applied.

◦ -sdc=noprint_violation:<tag>
During simulation time, this option suppresses EARLY CAPTURE violation
messages for particular SDC kinds. Specify the SDC command type as an
argument to this option.
-sdc=noprint_violation:mcp: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_multicycle_path commands.
-sdc=noprint_violation:fp: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_false_path commands.
-sdc=noprint_violation:cg: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for the
set_clock_group commands
-sdc=noprint_violation:max_del: Stops EARLY CAPTURE violation for
set_max_delay commands
-sdc=noprint_violation: This stops all EARLY CAPTURE violation printing.
Options to override clock period violation
At the point of encountering a clock period violation, all SDC checks are disabled. Adding
the following options overrides this behaviour and continues the SDC checks. Following is
an example of the warning message,
SDC-ERROR @ time 225 : Clock period violation has been identified. SDC
analysis will terminate. Please use -sdc=sanity:clock:noexit to continue
checks for other clocks.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:noexit
Although the SDC analysis terminates for paths with identified Clock period violation, with
-sdc=sanity:clock:noexit option SDC checks continues for other clocks. Without
-sdc=sanity:clock:noexit option SDC checks is terminated for all the paths, even for
the clocks with no Clock period violation.
Config File Support
You can use the configuration file to enable or disable the specific SDC instrumentation for
a given:
• Module
• Tree

• Instance
• Signal
Descriptions are provided in the following table:
Optconfig Option Description
Module Disable/Enable SDC checks on the module
Tree Disable/Enable SDC checks on the module and hierarchy below the
module.
Instance Disable/Enable SDC instrumentation on the instance
Signal Disable/Enable SDC instrumentation on the signal
• module <module_name> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: module {dut} {noInsertX};
• tree <module_name> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: tree {dut} {noInsertX};
• instance <hierarchy of instance> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: instance {top.dut1.leaf} {noInsertX};
• signal <hierarchy of signal> <sdc enable/disable option>
◦ Example: signal {top.dut1.leaf.data} {noInsertX};
• Comments are supported in config file. Lines starting with ‘ //’ are considered as
comments. Example, //This is a comment
• Wildcarding is supported in config file only for modules and trees. It is currently not
supported with instance and signal options.
module {dut*} {noVerifySdc}; //works
signal {top.dut1.leaf.data*} {noVerifySdc}; //does not work
Disable Verification Options:
The following options are applicable for all the SDC options

• noInsertX
• noInsertBool
• noInsertRandomDelay
• noPrintViolations
• SdcResetNoBool
• SdcResetNoX
The following options can disable all SDC verification for a module/tree/instance/signal:
• noVerifySdc
• noSdcReset
• noClockGlitch
• SdcResetNoRandomDelay
Enable Verification Options:
The following options enable all SDC verification for a module/tree/instance/signal:
• insertX
• insertBool
• insertRandomDelay
• printViolations
• verifySdc
• sdcReset
• clockGlitch
• SdcResetInsertX
• SdcResetInsertBool
• SdcResetInsertRandomDelay
The above mentioned commands are used to enable verification on a leaf module when
you have disabled verification on a tree.
tree {subblock1} {noVerifySdc}
module {leaf} {verifySdc}

Note: Options to control X/bool/random delay injection with verify_reset :
SdcResetInsertX, SdcResetInsertBool, SdcResetInsertRandomDelay,
SdcResetNoRandomDelay.
Options such as insertX/noInsertX, insertBool/noInsertBool,
insertRandomDelay/noInsertRandomDelay are for general SDC verification and have
no impact on X/bool/random delay injection with verify_reset.
Limitations:
In Config File Support, the signal option does not work with following enable and disable
verification options:
• SdcResetInsertBool
• SdcResetInsertX
• SdcResetInsertRandomDelay
• SdcResetNoBool
• SdcResetNoX
• SdcResetNoRandomDelay
Multiple Configurations Options for the Same
Module/Tree/Instance/Signal
The following precedence (from highest to lowest in order) takes place when two or more
configurations are applied for the same module/tree/instance/signal:
1. noVerifySdc/verifySdc
2. noPrintViolations/printViolations
3. noClockGlitch/verifyClockGlitch
4. noSdcReset/verifySdcReset
5. noInsertRandomDelay/insertRandomDelay
6. noInsertBool/insertBool
7. noInsertX/insertX
If any counterpart option are present, the last option is accepted.

Options to Control X-injection at Runtime
Options to Control X-injection at Runtime
The use model is as follows:
% simv -sdc=[sub_option][:X injection_control_option]
Where,
sub_option can be any of the following :
• verify_multicycle_path
• verify_max_delay
• verify_clock_group
• verify_false_path
X-injection_control_option can be as follows:
• x: To inject X at runtime
• bool: To hold the previous value by inserting a delay
By using these sub-options at runtime, you can choose between X-injection and delay
insertion.
If this option is not specified at runtime, default behavior would be X-injection on
respective paths identified. -sdc=verify_clock_group is an exception. This option
has a default behavior of delay insertion in the paths identified which can be overridden
using the-sdc=verify_clock_group:x option.
For example,
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:x (default)
• -sdc=verify_multicycle_path:bool
• -sdc=verify_max_delay:x (default)
• -sdc=verify_max_delay:bool
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:x
• -sdc=verify_clock_group:bool (default)
• -sdc=verify_false_path:x (default)
• -sdc=verify_false_path:bool
• -sdc=verify_reset:x (default)

Sub-options to Control Reset Domain Crossing Verification at Runtime
Sub-options to Control Reset Domain Crossing Verification at
Runtime
The use model is as follows:
%simv -sdc=verify_reset[:sub_option]
where,
sub_option can be any of the following:
• on: Turns on reset validation at runtime.

text:
Verification at Runtime
Sub-options to Control Reset Domain Crossing Verification at
Runtime
The use model is as follows:
%simv -sdc=verify_reset[:sub_option]
where,
sub_option can be any of the following:
• on: Turns on reset validation at runtime.
• bool: Insert Boolean value instead of X.
• N: Insert X/Boolean value on reset assertion for N cycles. If ‘N’ is not specified, tool will
insert X/Boolean value for 1 clock cycle.
• slowclock: Use slow clock instead of fast clock
• random: Insert X for random number of clock cycles (between 0-N) instead of N
For example,
• -sdc=verify_reset:on
• -sdc=verify_reset:bool
• -sdc=verify_reset:N
• -sdc=verify_reset:slowclock
• -sdc=verify_reset:random
Clock Validation
Clock Sanity Checks
During simulation, VCS compares the runtime waveform of a clock with the constraints
defined in the SDC file. These checks help ensure the clock behaves as expected and
matches timing definitions such as period, duty cycle, and generated-clock alignment.
The following are the clock sanity options:
• -sdc=sanity:clock:[sub_option]
This option enables checks at runtime to verify discrepancies between clocks defined
in SDC file using create_clock/create_generated_clock and the values seen on
these signals during simulation.

Clock Validation
%simv -sdc=sanity:clock:[sub_option]
Where, sub_option can be any of the following:
◦ dutycycle: Check for duty cycle validation
◦ aligninvert: Check for alignment and inversion of generated clock with respect to
master clock
◦ advanced: Enable all the above checks (period, dutycycle, aligninvert)
◦ noperiod: Disable check for clock period validation
Examples of use model and corresponding diagnostic message printed:
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:dutycycle
SDC-ERROR:WAVEFORM DUTY-CYCLE @ time 190 s : clock
testbench.mult.genclk(genclk): Duty Cycle Observed: 50.00 %
Expected: 80.00 % (File:test.sdc, Line:3)
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:aligninvert
SDC-ERROR:TIMING-ALIGNMENT: @ time 171 s : clock
testbench.mult.genclk(genclk) [master
clock:testbench.mult.clk(clk)],Edge Timing offset Observed @
time:171 s Expected @ time:170 s (File:test.sdc, Line:3)
SDC-ERROR:GenClk EDGE-INVERSION: @ time 170 s :
clock testbench.mult.genclk(genclk) [master
clock:testbench.mult.clk(clk)]: Observed:posedge(master:posedge)
Expected:posedge(master:negedge) (File:test.sdc, Line:3)
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:advanced
◦ ./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:noperiod
The following are the additional clock sanity configuration options:
• -sdc=sanity:clock:noflop
Ensures that a sanity clock check is not performed by default, if this clock is not
associated with any flip-flops . You must mark this argument as true to conduct sanity
clock checks on clocks that have not experienced any flops. The default value of this
clock is FALSE .
• -sdc=sanity:clock:higherfreq
Reports clock sanity errors only when the run-time detected clock frequency is higher
than the compile time SDC defined clock frequency. If the frequency is higher, the
margin calculations are done after this check. The default value of this clock is OFF .

Clock Validation
• -sdc=sanity:clock:period:nosdcoff
This switch should be used along with -sdc=sanity:clock:noexit. When both of
these switches are used then SDC checks continues for all the paths, even for the
clocks with identified clock period violation. By default, after a few errors, the SDC
checks are disabled. This switch ensures that SDC checks do not stop just because
period errors occur.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:off
Ensures that sanity clock check is not required. Dynamic and regular clock sanity is
disabled in RT.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:stabilizecount
whenever a clocks period changes in simulation the number of cycles of the clock
period is used to stabilize the new clock, during this time no SDC analysis is
performed. The new period is accepted only after this duration if the period is stable
• -sdc=sanity:clock:margin:<percent>
This option defines the percentage margin beyond which violations for period and duty-
cycle is reported. It is essentially a margin of error, expressed in percentage, for clock
period mismatches between SDC period and the runtime period. This is valid for SDC
period versus runtime period mismatches.
./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:margin:10
If clock period is 100 in sdc and 115 in observed with a margin of 20,that is,
-sdc=sanity:clock:margin:20, then there is no period violation.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:delaymargin:<time>
If there is master versus generated clock misalignment of <<time>> then it ignores and
does not report an error.
./simv -sdc=sanity:clock:delaymargin:1000fs
If the misalignment is >= 1000fs then only the clock timing alignment violation is
reported.
• -sdc=sanity:clock:violations:<N>
The number of reported Dynamic Clock Violations can be controlled using this option
by substituting argument ‘N’ with the required value. Dynamic Clock Violation is
reported whenever the clock reaching a flop changes, example, whenever the clock
mux select toggles and output clock changes.

Reading Multiple SDCs
• -sdc=sanity:clock:uncertainty:<percentage>
This uncertainty option is used when there is a clock jitter. For example, if the period is
approximately 10 ns, it might vary by a range between 10.01 and 9.98 ns. To allow this
flexibility in the clock jitter, stabilization time is used. Without this option, the clock does
not stabilize in a particular period if there is jitter.
Reading Multiple SDCs
This section describes how to read multiple SDC files written for different scopes. You
need to use read_sdc option to read from other SDCs inside a top level SDC file. You can
use the following options:
• Module based multiple SDC
◦ read_sdc -module <module_name> <sdc_file_name>
• Instance Based multiple SDC
◦ read_sdc -instance <instance_name> <sdc_file_name>
When an SDC file encounters this command, the design scope changes from current
design to the module name specified in the above mentioned commands. Once the SDC

If the read_sdc option is used to apply multiple SDC files on same module or instance,
only the first SDC file is applied. All subsequent SDC files for that module or instance are
ignored and an error message is generated in the sdc_error.log file.

Reading Multiple SDCs
For example, consider the following SDC files:
Module Based Read Multiple SDC Instance Based Read Multiple SDC
% cat top.sdc
read_sdc -module sub1 sub1_1.sdc
read_sdc -module sub1 sub1_2.sdc
% cat top.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub1 sub1_1.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub1 sub1_2.sdc
In this case, only sub1_1.sdc option is applied on module/instance. The sub1_2.sdc
and other SDC commands for the same module or instance are ignored and reports the
following error message in the sdc_error.log file:
[Error] SDC_DUPLICATE_MODULE/INSTANCE: Duplicate read_sdc command on
module/instance found for the value {<module/instance name>} specified
for option readsdc(<name of sdc file applied in duplicate cmd>:<line no.
at which the duplicate cmd is present in the topmost sdc file>). This
command or the option will be ignored
Please provide correct module/instance name
More examples to understand read_sdc option and source command usages are
described below:
• To apply commands from multiple SDC files on the same module/instance, the
following syntax can be used using the source command.
Module Based Read Multiple SDC Instance Based Read Multiple SDC
%cat top.sdc
read_sdc -module sub1 sub1.sdcread_sdc
read_sdc -module sub2 sub2.sdc
%cat top.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub1 sub1.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub2 sub2.sdc
%cat sub1.sdc
source sub1_1.sdc
source sub1_2.sdc
Using source command after read_sdc command applies SDC commands from both the
sourced SDC files additionally on module sub1.
Note: The -sdc=current_design:<> or current_design commands in the SDC file
cannot be used in conjunction with the read_sdc command. It results in an elaboration
error.
• If the instance specified in read_sdc command has “generate” hierarchy, then use DC
conventions, that is the square brackets should be replaced with underscore and then
glued to the instance name with an underscore.

Querying the Current Design in SDC Scripts
Instead of:
read_sdc -instance /test/u_ddie/WRAP_INST[0]/u_wrapper wrapper.sdc
//does not work
Use this:
read_sdc -instance /test/u_ddie/WRAP_INST_0__u_wrapper wrapper.sdc
//works
or
read_sdc -instance /test/u_ddie/WRAP_INST[0].u_wrapper wrapper.sdc
//also works
Querying the Current Design in SDC Scripts
This feature allows you to query the name of the current design directly within SDC
scripts. The value of current_design is internally stored and is accessible within SDC.
This allows dynamic referencing of the current design without hard coding its name and
provides a clean and direct way to reference the active design in scripts. You can retrieve
the current design name directly through SDC scripts by using the following:
get_object_name [current_design]
The following are the four ways to set the current_design:
• Use read_sdc -module <module_name> <sdc_file_name> .
• Define read_sdc -instance <instance_name> <sdc_file_name> .
• Use the VCS -sdc=current_design:<module_name> compile time option.
• Define the current design <module_name> directly in the SDC file
The SDC query must be present inside the applied SDC file.

Supported SDC Commands
Consider the following examples:
Figure 14 Example 1
Output
@sub1.sdc:8
sub1
@test.sdc:8
tb
Figure 15 Example 2

sub1
@test.sdc:8

This enhancement is fully backward compatible and does not affect existing ways of
setting current_design . It only adds querying capability.

Support for Multiple Create Clock on same net (MCC)
The SDC framework allows you to define timing constraints for their designs. By default,
when two create_clock commands are defined on the same net, the slower clock is
dropped during the SDC analysis phase, and the following MCC (Multiple Create Clock)
error is flagged in mcpLogs/sdc_errors.log file.
Warning-[MCP-MCC] Multiple create clocks
Multiple create_clock commands are found on Signal:
testbench.u_mult2x_wrap.clk2, dropping sdc clock super_clk (test.sdc:6)
Fastest Sdc clock will be chosen.

Support for Multiple Create Clock on same net (MCC)
This behavior can lead to unintended consequences, such as the dropping of all
generated clocks derived from the slower clock. Consequently, flops associated with these
generated clocks become "flops with no clock," resulting in fewer validated paths during
timing analysis.
create_clock -add -period 20 -name C1 [get_pins A]
create_clock -add -period 40 -name C2 [get_pins A]
create_generated_clock -name genclk1 -divide_by 2 -source [get_pins A]
-master_clock C1 [get_pins I1/clk1]
create_generated_clock -name genclk2 -divide_by 2 -source [get_pins A]
-master_clock C2 [get_pins I1/clk2]
In the above example both C2 and genclk2 are dropped.
Use following compile time option to allow multiple clocks to be created on same net :
-sdc=allow_mcc
All the clocks are propagated to the flops and the fast clock semantic prevails.
In this example, there are two flops, Flop A and Flop B. C1 and C2 propagates to Flop A.
genclk1 and genclk2 propagates to Flop B. As per the fast clock semantics at runtime,
Flop A is evaluated with clock C1. Flop B is evaluated with clock genclk1.
If dynamic multi clock is also enabled, all the clocks are propagated to the flops and they
are carried forward to the runtime.
In this case, VCS SDC dynamically verifies the active clock at runtime and performs SDC
analysis based on the verification. However, as both the clocks are defined on the same
net, both are active. In such a case, the stable period of clocks is calculated at the runtime.
At the point of SDC analysis of Flop A, which ever clock’s period is closest to the stable
period is selected.
MCC Clock Selection Using UCLI
Clocks can be dropped during simulation using the following ucli command:
sdc_check -drop_clock_by_name <SDC_clk_name>
Dropped clocks can be re-enabled by following ucli command:
sdc_check - enable_clock_by_name <SDC_clk_name>

Verbose Message of SDC Report
When the specified clock is dropped from all SDC files. Clock dropping can result in
recursive dropping of generated clocks. Following message is given when generated clock
is dropped due to master clock dropping:
[SDC-INFO] Dropping Clock 1 testbench.mult.clk (fast_clk:test.sdc:2)
dropping generate Clock 5 testbench.mult.ckd.oclk
(slow_clk:test.sdc:6)
When all clocks are dropped from certain generated clock point, it becomes transparent
and passes all the previous clocks through that point. Following message is given when
some node becomes transparent:
[SDC-INFO] All SDC clocks are dropped from testbench.mult.ckd.oclk
Clock dropping is applied at any time during simulation and the effect is visible
immediately after the UCLI command is executed. UCLI based selection can work
together with -sdc=dynamicfrequency.
Verbose Message of SDC Report
The following are the verbose messages that you get from SDC report:
• INACTIVE: Either the source or destination did not toggle.
• ACTIVE: Both the destination and source toggles but source change is outside of the
given latency window.
• WITHIN WINDOW: Source changes within the latency window but path has no early
capture violation because source to destination path is not sensitized.
• VIOLATING: Early capture violation in the path.
Simulation SDC Summary:
Detail sdc activity report
set_multicycle_path (test.sdc:3) is ACTIVE
set_multicycle_path (test.sdc:5) is ACTIVE & WITHIN-WINDOW
set_multicycle_path (test.sdc:7) is ACTIVE & VIOLATING
set_multicycle_path (test.sdc:9) is INACTIVE

reason tags.

Verbose Message of SDC Report
Inactive reason tags:
Reason Tag
Source did not toggle. SRC_NOT_TGL
Destination did not toggle. DEST_NOT_TGL
The source toggled in response
to clock A. However,according to
clock-tree analysis it was expected
to toggle on clock B. For the entire
simulation, the source was always
toggled by the wrong clock.

to clock A. However, according to

entire simulation, the destination

clock.

received correct clocks individually

Performance Overhead Note
The -sdc=inactiveDebug:path option has some acceptable overhead. This is expected
because:
• It tracks detailed debug information for why paths are inactive.
• It needs to record toggle information, clock relationships, and other metadata for each
inactive path.
• It generates the inactiveDebug.rpt.gz report file.
This is a debug switch, it is supposed to be enabled for debugging purpose not
for performance measurement. Also, not every design has the same overhead.
It depends on the total number of paths and more specifically on the number
of inactive paths. Designs with less inactive paths has very less or negligible
overhead due to this switch.
Generate SDC path coverage reports using VCS -cm sdc and URG to measure Active,
Violating, and Inactive MCP constraint paths during simulation.
The SDC coverage report presents a summary of all SDC valid paths that are identified
during tracing.
The URG report for SDC coverage covers the following :
• Total paths relevant for an SDC command.
• Categorization of the paths per “Violating”, “Active” and “Inactive”.
• Details of the paths (start and endpoints).

• Total count and categorization of clock definition and set case analysis commands.
• The URG report provides an overall coverage score, which is computed using the
following formula:
SDC score = ( Active elements - excluded elements) / (Total elements -
excluded elements ) * 100
Here, elements are number of commands, destination nodes, and source-destination
pairs for level 1, 2 and 3 respectively.
The following is the procedure for generating SDC coverage report :
1. Enable -cm sdc compile time switch .
The following is an example vcs command:
vcs -sverilog <design_file>.v -full64 -cm sdc
-sdc=<sdc_file_name>.sdc,current_design:<design_name>
2. Enable -cm sdc runtime switch
The following is an example simv command :
simv -cm sdc -l run.log
3. Generate the URG report using the following command :
urg -dir simv.vdb -format text
URG REPORT LEVELS
Introduction
The Unified Report Generator (URG) provides a granular approach to coverage analysis
by offering three distinct report levels.
Consider the following example figure:
In an SDC file, there are four MCP paths covered by the following MCP command:
set_multicycle_path -from ff2* -to ff5*

Figure 16 MCP Paths
where,
The three levels of sign off criteria (from coarse to fine) are :
• Level 1: Count by the SDC command.
• Level 2: Count by destination.
• Level 3: Count by the source-destination pair.
Use the -sdc level <level N> switch to facilitate reports for the various criteria. With
the -show sdcpath switch, granular information can be provided based on the report
level .
The status of the commands is derived from the underlying paths depending on the
level. For the multiple paths/destination-points/source-destination-pairs associated with
a command, the following hierarchy is maintained while determining the status of the
command:
• INACTIVE
• INACTIVE & CLK_SANITY_SUPPRESSED
• ACTIVE
• VIOLATING
The status of the commands is determined based on the status of the associated
elements. Here, elements are paths, destination nodes, and source-destination pairs for
levels 1, 2 and 3 respectively :
• If the status of an associated element is Violating, the status of the corresponding
command becomes Violating.
• If the status of associated elements is a mix of Active and Inactive, the status of the
corresponding command becomes Partial Active .

• If the status of all the associated elements is Active, the status of the corresponding
command becomes Active.
• If the status of all the associated elements is Inactive, the status of the corresponding
command becomes Inactive.
Level 1 : SDC Command- Based Coverage
If all MCP paths under an MCP command toggle then the MCP command becomes active.
The level 1 criterion provides the coverage report by this SDC command. The status of the
command is calculated based on the paths associated with it.
The following formula is used for the calculation of coverage score:
(sdc active commands + sdc violating commands + SDC partial active +
Duplicate commands + SCA passing + CLK passing + virtual clock) / (total
commands – excluded commands)
Use the following URG command :
urg -dir simv.vdb -format text -sdc level 1
The report includes the information and the status of each SDC command. It does not
contain the paths summary.
The -show sdcpath switch has no effect on the level 1 URG report.

Figure 18 Level 1- Detailed Command Summary
Level 2 : Destination Point - Based Coverage
The level 2 coverage reports the status of commands based on an associated destination
point. When all destinations toggle, the coverage for the destination point is 100%, that is,
active.
The following formula is used for the calculation of coverage score:
(active dest node + partial active dest nodes ) / (total dest nodes -
excluded dest nodes)
Use the following URG command :
urg -dir simv.vdb -format text -show sdcpath -sdc level 2
The -show sdcpath switch also enables the reporting of destination wise status.
The following report provides the information about the status of each SDC command
and the coverage status of destination points under each command. The status of each

Level 3 : Source-Destination Pair Based coverage
The level 3 criterion analyzes the coverage based on a source-destination pair. This level
provides the most detailed coverage analysis.
The following formula is used for the calculation of coverage score:
(active src-dest pairs + partial active src-dest pairs ) / (total src-
dest pairs - excluded src-dest pairs)
Use the following URG command:
urg -dir simv.vdb/ -format text -show sdcpath -sdc level 3
The -show sdcpath switch also enables reporting of source-destination pair status.

Exclusion
Exclusion is used to eliminate the commands, destination points, and source-destination
pairs that are inactive or violating and are reported by coverage analysis. You can dump
the exclusion file while creating a URG report. Based on the coverage report, you can
transfer the exclusion file to a later run for improved coverage by uncommenting the
required exclusions . You can dump the exclusion file with the -dump full_exclusion
switch.

• The fullexclude.sdc: dumps the list of SDC commands and the related destination
nodes or the source- destination pairs based on the specified coverage level. At level
1, this file is the same as fullexclude_command.sdc.

Merging
VCS SDC enables you to create a report by merging the paths from multiple simulation
runs. The simulation data can be merged irrespective of if it was produced from the same
compilation or from different compilations.
Here are a few examples of merging commands used in SDC :
• Same Compilation

%simv -cm sdc -cm_name test_2

%urg -dir simv.vdb -format text
• Different Compilation

sdc
%simv -cm sdc -cm_dir simv_1.vdb

%vcs test_2.v -sdc=test_2.sdc -cm_dir simv_2.vdb -full64 -sverilog -cm
sdc

Explicit Pin Names
An explicit pin is a -through point or a target of create_clock/set_case_analysis

module is an inferred flop cell (that is, it has a `celldefine and is modeled using UDPs).
For example,
If there is a module with input pin name CK, SDC file can reference it as
<module_instance_name>.CK.

Flop endpoints that are currently supported are as follows:
-from
ff_reg, ff_reg/CP, [get_cells ff_reg], [get_pins ff_reg/CP]
(all the above have the same meaning)

To hierarchically reference a generate block in SDC
For generate, square brackets '[' , ']' are replaced with underscore ‘_’. Also, for hierarchy
separator ‘.’ is replaced with ‘_’.
• Example for normal instance:
genvar y;
generate
for (y = 0 ; y < 4 ; y=y+1) begin : CLUSTER_INST
mod_x5 x5 ();
end

Inferencing SDC End Points (Syntax)
Possible hierarchical references at SDC:
set_clock_sense -stop_propagation -clocks clk1 [get_pins
CLUSTER_INST_?__x5/A]
set_clock_sense -stop_propagation -clocks clk1 [get_nets
CLUSTER_INST_?__x5/t]
• Example for multiple instance:
genvar y;
generate
for (y = 0 ; y < 1 ; y=y+1) begin : GENBLK
if (y < 1)
begin : IF_COND mod inst ();
end end
endgenerate
The hierarchical name at SDC is as follows:
top/GENBLK_0__IF_COND_inst/
• Use of question mark ? or wildcard “*” instead of instance index is allowed.

The following syntax is supported:
• <interface_instance_name_in_current_design>_<interface_member>
• <interface_ instance_name_in_current_design>.<interface_member>
interface ffbus(input clk, input rst);
wire [1:0] inData;
modport mp (input clk, input rst, inout inData);
endinterface

module mult2x(input[1:0] in, input clk1, input clk2, output[1:0] out,
input rst, ffbus.mp I1, ffbus.mp I2);
wire [1:0]o1;
wire [1:0]o2;

assign I1.inData = in;
assign I2.inData = o1 * 1;
assign out = I2.inData;

flop ff1(I1,o1);
flop ff2(I2,o2);

module flop(ffbus.mp p, output o);
reg[1:0] o;
always@(posedge p.clk or negedge p.rst) begin

else o <= p.inData;

Defining Module as Black Box
The Black Box Module feature allows you to mark a module as black box for SDC
verification. No SDC validation happens inside the module or through the module. This is
particularly useful when you have modules that are not synthesizable.
This feature does not alter the design’s simulation results.
SDC identifies the modules to be guarded in the following two ways:
• Modules that have only input ports and no output or inout ports are considered as true
black box modules. This identification happens when this feature is run in auto mode.
• You can provide a list of modules from the command line to declare as true black box
modules.
The input clock ports are excluded from guarding.

Memory Optimization by limiting Number of Paths per src-destination Pair
• Use the following option to run this feature in auto mode, that is, auto identification of
trueBB modules:
-sdc=trueBB:auto
• Use the following option to pass a list of trueBB modules from the command line:
-sdc=trueBB:bbMods.txt
where,
bbMods.txt is the text file containing a list of trueBB modules.
• Use this following option to run this feature in auto mode as well as to take the input
from the command line:
-sdc=trueBB:auto,trueBB:bbMods.txt
After VCS compilation, mcpLogs/trueBBMods.txt text file is generated under the
mcpLogs directory. This text file consists of a list of the trueBB modules that are identified
during compilation. It also contains a list of the trueBB modules identified in auto mode
and from the command line.
Limitation
The following are the limitations of Black Box Module:
• Interfaces should not be black boxed.
• A warning message gets displayed in the mcpLogs/trueBB.txt file when a module
does not exist in the design.
Memory Optimization by limiting Number of Paths per
src-destination Pair
Sometimes some SDC commands such as those that include a false path, multicycle
path, or a clock group, use a very high number of paths. This blows up the compile time
memory. By limiting maximum number of paths to be analyzed for every unique pair of
source and destination, the memory requirement can be reduced.
This performance optimization is enabled through the following option:
-sdc=maxSrcDestPath:N

where,
• N is the limit on number of paths between the source and destination.
• If the value of N is not given with -sdc=maxSrcDestPath, then, by default, there is no
limit on number of paths per source-destination pair.
• If the total number of paths from the source to destination pair exceeds a specified N,
the paths above the threshold are ignored.
• The value of N should be a positive integer , that is, 1,2,3 and so on.
Let us say there are N number of ways a destination can be reached from a source signal.
Using above option, the tool chooses only N number of ways, that is, N number of unique
points between the source and destination signal.
src ----> n1 ----> dest

If the read_sdc option is used to apply multiple SDC files on same module or instance,
only the first SDC file is applied. All subsequent SDC files for that module or instance are
ignored and an error message is generated in the sdc_error.log file.

Reading Multiple SDCs
For example, consider the following SDC files:
Module Based Read Multiple SDC Instance Based Read Multiple SDC
% cat top.sdc
read_sdc -module sub1 sub1_1.sdc
read_sdc -module sub1 sub1_2.sdc
% cat top.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub1 sub1_1.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub1 sub1_2.sdc
In this case, only sub1_1.sdc option is applied on module/instance. The sub1_2.sdc
and other SDC commands for the same module or instance are ignored and reports the
following error message in the sdc_error.log file:
[Error] SDC_DUPLICATE_MODULE/INSTANCE: Duplicate read_sdc command on
module/instance found for the value {<module/instance name>} specified
for option readsdc(<name of sdc file applied in duplicate cmd>:<line no.
at which the duplicate cmd is present in the topmost sdc file>). This
command or the option will be ignored
Please provide correct module/instance name
More examples to understand read_sdc option and source command usages are
described below:
• To apply commands from multiple SDC files on the same module/instance, the
following syntax can be used using the source command.
Module Based Read Multiple SDC Instance Based Read Multiple SDC
%cat top.sdc
read_sdc -module sub1 sub1.sdcread_sdc
read_sdc -module sub2 sub2.sdc
%cat top.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub1 sub1.sdc
read_sdc -instance /top/sub2 sub2.sdc
%cat sub1.sdc
source sub1_1.sdc
source sub1_2.sdc
Using source command after read_sdc command applies SDC commands from both the
sourced SDC files additionally on module sub1.
Note: The -sdc=current_design:<> or current_design commands in the SDC file
cannot be used in conjunction with the read_sdc command. It results in an elaboration
error.
• If the instance specified in read_sdc command has “generate” hierarchy, then use DC
conventions, that is the square brackets should be replaced with underscore and then
glued to the instance name with an underscore.

Querying the Current Design in SDC Scripts
Instead of:
read_sdc -instance /test/u_ddie/WRAP_INST[0]/u_wrapper wrapper.sdc
//does not work
Use this:
read_sdc -instance /test/u_ddie/WRAP_INST_0__u_wrapper wrapper.sdc
//works
or
read_sdc -instance /test/u_ddie/WRAP_INST[0].u_wrapper wrapper.sdc
//also works
Querying the Current Design in SDC Scripts
This feature allows you to query the name of the current design directly within SDC
scripts. The value of current_design is internally stored and is accessible within SDC.
This allows dynamic referencing of the current design without hard coding its name and
provides a clean and direct way to reference the active design in scripts. You can retrieve
the current design name directly through SDC scripts by using the following:
get_object_name [current_design]
The following are the four ways to set the current_design:
• Use read_sdc -module <module_name> <sdc_file_name> .
• Define read_sdc -instance <instance_name> <sdc_file_name> .
• Use the VCS -sdc=current_design:<module_name> compile time option.
• Define the current design <module_name> directly in the SDC file
The SDC query must be present inside the applied SDC file.

Support for Multiple Create Clock on same net (MCC)
The SDC framework allows you to define timing constraints for their designs. By default,
when two create_clock commands are defined on the same net, the slower clock is
dropped during the SDC analysis phase, and the following MCC (Multiple Create Clock)
error is flagged in mcpLogs/sdc_errors.log file.
Warning-[MCP-MCC] Multiple create clocks
Multiple create_clock commands are found on Signal:
testbench.u_mult2x_wrap.clk2, dropping sdc clock super_clk (test.sdc:6)
Fastest Sdc clock will be chosen.

Support for Multiple Create Clock on same net (MCC)
This behavior can lead to unintended consequences, such as the dropping of all
generated clocks derived from the slower clock. Consequently, flops associated with these
generated clocks become "flops with no clock," resulting in fewer validated paths during
timing analysis.
create_clock -add -period 20 -name C1 [get_pins A]
create_clock -add -period 40 -name C2 [get_pins A]
create_generated_clock -name genclk1 -divide_by 2 -source [get_pins A]
-master_clock C1 [get_pins I1/clk1]
create_generated_clock -name genclk2 -divide_by 2 -source [get_pins A]
-master_clock C2 [get_pins I1/clk2]
In the above example both C2 and genclk2 are dropped.
Use following compile time option to allow multiple clocks to be created on same net :
-sdc=allow_mcc
All the clocks are propagated to the flops and the fast clock semantic prevails.
In this example, there are two flops, Flop A and Flop B. C1 and C2 propagates to Flop A.
genclk1 and genclk2 propagates to Flop B. As per the fast clock semantics at runtime,
Flop A is evaluated with clock C1. Flop B is evaluated with clock genclk1.
If dynamic multi clock is also enabled, all the clocks are propagated to the flops and they
are carried forward to the runtime.
In this case, VCS SDC dynamically verifies the active clock at runtime and performs SDC
analysis based on the verification. However, as both the clocks are defined on the same
net, both are active. In such a case, the stable period of clocks is calculated at the runtime.
At the point of SDC analysis of Flop A, which ever clock’s period is closest to the stable
period is selected.

sdc_check -drop_clock_by_name <SDC_clk_name>

Debug Report Modes
Above categorization is reported in a separate file inactiveDebug.rpt.gz in the run
area. Two modes are supported.
• Path level. Each inactive path prints with its reason tag.
This mode can be enabled using -sdc=inactiveDebug:path runtime option.
◦ -sdc=inactiveDebug:path — Dumps path level information in the
inactiveDebug.rpt.gz file.
Example: Path-level lines
Command-1 test.sdc:21 : INACTIVE
PATH src1 => dest1 (SRC_NOT_TGL)
PATH src2 => dest2 (DEST_NOT_TGL)
PATH src3 => dest3 (SRC_WRONG_CLK)
PATH src4 => dest4 (DEST_WRONG_CLK)
PATH src5 => dest5 (SRC_DEST_WRONG_CLK_PAIR)

title: 10 [get_nets {clk1}] #switch
text:
Verbose Message of SDC Report
• Command level. For commands where every path is inactive, aggregate counts by tag
are shown as percentages of inactive paths.
◦ -sdc=inactiveDebug: Dumps command level information in the
inactiveDebug.rpt.gz file.
• Example: Command-level summary
Command-1 test.sdc:21 : INACTIVE
SRC_NOT_TGL : 40%
DEST_NOT_TGL: 20%
SRC_WRONG_CLK 20%
DEST_WRONG_CLK: 10%
SRC_DEST_WRONG_CLK_PAIR: 10%
The percentage reflects the number of inactive paths (out of total inactive paths) in
each category.
Priority Order for Inactive Reasons
A path can match more than one reason. The tool reports a single reason using this
priority (highest first). The same order appears in inactiveDebug.rpt.gz.
SRC_NOT_TGL > DEST_NOT_TGL > SRC_WRONG_CLK > DEST_WRONG_CLK >
SRC_DEST_WRONG_CLK_PAIR
Toggle Validation Rules
The tool has following validation rules for source and destination flop toggles:
• Destination toggles: Toggles caused by reset are not counted as valid toggles. Reset-
driven edges do not represent functional path activity.
• Source toggles: Source flop toggles count as valid even when caused by reset.
Inactive Paths Under Active Commands
One SDC command can mix active and inactive paths. The command-level status is
determined by the aggregate behaviour of all constituent paths. That is, if at least one path
is active, the command is classified as ACTIVE (or ACTIVE & VIOLATING if violations
occurs).
Inactive Debug Granularity:
Switch Granularity Behavior
-sdc=inactiveDebug Command-level List commands where all paths are INACTIVE.
Commands with mixed active/inactive paths are
excluded from the report.

Debug Report Modes
The inactive path categorization is reported in a separate file inactiveDebug.rpt.gz in
the run area. Two modes are supported.
• Command level. For commands where every path is inactive, aggregate counts by tag
are shown as percentages of inactive paths.
◦ -sdc=inactiveDebug — Dumps command-level information in the
inactiveDebug.rpt.gz file.
Example: Command-level summary

each category.

Priority Order for Inactive Reasons
A path can match more than one reason. The tool reports a single reason using this
priority (highest first). The same order appears in inactiveDebug.rpt.gz.
SRC_CLK_SUPPRESSED >
DEST_CLK_SUPPRESSED >
SRC_NOT_TGL >
DEST_NOT_TGL >
SRC_WRONG_CLK >
DEST_WRONG_CLK >
SRC_DEST_WRONG_CLK_PAIR
When a path is INACTIVE and the clock is suppressed after clock sanity checks, the tool
checks for source or destination clock suppressed reasons directly. Toggle status is not
evaluated in that case. This is why clock suppressed reasons have the highest priority.
Enhanced Reporting for set_clock_groups Command
For set_clock_groups command, the inactive path report contains additional "from clock"
and "to clock" level information to help identify for which clock pair inactive path status is
being reported.

Toggle Validation Rules
The tool has the following validation rules for source and destination flop toggles:
• Destination toggle validation: For destination flops, toggles caused by reset signals
are not counted as valid toggles. Reset-induced transitions do not represent functional
path activity.
• Source toggle validation: Source flop toggles count as valid even when caused by
reset.
Inactive Paths Under Active Commands
One SDC command can include a mix of active and inactive paths. The command-
level status is determined by the aggregate behaviour of all constituent paths: If at least
one path is active, the command is classified as ACTIVE (or ACTIVE & VIOLATING if
violations occur).
Inactive Debug Granularity:
Switch Granularity Behavior
-sdc=inactiveDebug Command-level Reports only commands where all paths are
inactive. Commands with mixed active/inactive
paths are excluded from the report.
-sdc=inactiveDebug:path Path-level Reports individual inactive paths regardless
of the parent command's overall status. This
enables identification of inactive paths even
within commands that are classified as active.
Example: set_multicycle_path command that expands to multiple paths with varying
activity status.
Runtime path status:
set_multicycle_path
(./Source/inactiveDebug/13_complex_edge_cases/test.sdc:35) : ACTIVE &
PATH testbench.dut.wild_src[0] => testbench.dut.wild_dest[0] : INACTIVE
PATH testbench.dut.wild_src[2] => testbench.dut.wild_dest[2] : ACTIVE &
PATH testbench.dut.wild_src[3] => testbench.dut.wild_dest[3] : INACTIVE
The command contains three paths: two inactive and one active. The command-level
status is ACTIVE & VIOLATING due to the active path.

Command-level report (-sdc=inactiveDebug): This command does not appear in the
report because the command-level status is ACTIVE & VIOLATING.
Path-level report (-sdc=inactiveDebug:path): The path-level report captures both
inactive paths with their respective inactive reasons, even though the parent command is
ACTIVE & VIOLATING.
set_multicycle_path
(./Source/inactiveDebug/13_complex_edge_cases/test.sdc:35) : ACTIVE &
PATH testbench.dut.wild_src[0] => testbench.dut.wild_dest[0]
(SRC_NOT_TGL)
PATH testbench.dut.wild_src[3] => testbench.dut.wild_dest[3]
(DEST_WRONG_CLK)
Performance Overhead Note
The -sdc=inactiveDebug:path option has some acceptable overhead. This is expected
because:
• It tracks detailed debug information for why paths are inactive.
• It needs to record toggle information, clock relationships, and other metadata for each
inactive path.
• It generates the inactiveDebug.rpt.gz report file.
This is a debug switch, it is supposed to be enabled for debugging purpose not
for performance measurement. Also, not every design has the same overhead.
It depends on the total number of paths and more specifically on the number
of inactive paths. Designs with less inactive paths has very less or negligible
overhead due to this switch.
Generate SDC path coverage reports using VCS -cm sdc and URG to measure Active,
Violating, and Inactive MCP constraint paths during simulation.
The SDC coverage report presents a summary of all SDC valid paths that are identified
during tracing.
The URG report for SDC coverage covers the following :
• Total paths relevant for an SDC command.
• Categorization of the paths per “Violating”, “Active” and “Inactive”.
• Details of the paths (start and endpoints).

title: 10 [get_nets {clk1}] #switch
text:
• Total count and categorization of clock definition and set case analysis commands.
• The URG report provides an overall coverage score, which is computed using the
following formula:
SDC score = ( Active elements - excluded elements) / (Total elements -
excluded elements ) * 100
Here, elements are number of commands, destination nodes, and source-destination
pairs for level 1, 2 and 3 respectively.
The following is the procedure for generating SDC coverage report :
1. Enable -cm sdc compile time switch .
The following is an example vcs command:
vcs -sverilog <design_file>.v -full64 -cm sdc
-sdc=<sdc_file_name>.sdc,current_design:<design_name>
2. Enable -cm sdc runtime switch
The following is an example simv command :
simv -cm sdc -l run.log
3. Generate the URG report using the following command :
urg -dir simv.vdb -format text
URG REPORT LEVELS
Introduction
The Unified Report Generator (URG) provides a granular approach to coverage analysis
by offering three distinct report levels.
Consider the following example figure:
In an SDC file, there are four MCP paths covered by the following MCP command:
set_multicycle_path -from ff2* -to ff5*

Figure 16 MCP Paths
where,
The three levels of sign off criteria (from coarse to fine) are :
• Level 1: Count by the SDC command.
• Level 2: Count by destination.
• Level 3: Count by the source-destination pair.
Use the -sdc level <level N> switch to facilitate reports for the various criteria. With
the -show sdcpath switch, granular information can be provided based on the report
level .
The status of the commands is derived from the underlying paths depending on the
level. For the multiple paths/destination-points/source-destination-pairs associated with
a command, the following hierarchy is maintained while determining the status of the
command:
• INACTIVE
• INACTIVE & CLK_SANITY_SUPPRESSED
• ACTIVE
• VIOLATING
The status of the commands is determined based on the status of the associated
elements. Here, elements are paths, destination nodes, and source-destination pairs for
levels 1, 2 and 3 respectively :
• If the status of an associated element is Violating, the status of the corresponding
command becomes Violating.
• If the status of associated elements is a mix of Active and Inactive, the status of the
corresponding command becomes Partial Active .

• If the status of all the associated elements is Active, the status of the corresponding
command becomes Active.
• If the status of all the associated elements is Inactive, the status of the corresponding
command becomes Inactive.
Level 1 : SDC Command- Based Coverage
If all MCP paths under an MCP command toggle then the MCP command becomes active.
The level 1 criterion provides the coverage report by this SDC command. The status of the
command is calculated based on the paths associated with it.
The following formula is used for the calculation of coverage score:
(sdc active commands + sdc violating commands + SDC partial active +
Duplicate commands + SCA passing + CLK passing + virtual clock) / (total
commands – excluded commands)
Use the following URG command :
urg -dir simv.vdb -format text -sdc level 1
The report includes the information and the status of each SDC command. It does not
contain the paths summary.
The -show sdcpath switch has no effect on the level 1 URG report.

Figure 18 Level 1- Detailed Command Summary
Level 2 : Destination Point - Based Coverage
The level 2 coverage reports the status of commands based on an associated destination
point. When all destinations toggle, the coverage for the destination point is 100%, that is,
active.
The following formula is used for the calculation of coverage score:
(active dest node + partial active dest nodes ) / (total dest nodes -
excluded dest nodes)

The level 3 criterion analyzes the coverage based on a source-destination pair. This level

dest pairs - excluded src-dest pairs)

Merging
VCS SDC enables you to create a report by merging the paths from multiple simulation
runs. The simulation data can be merged irrespective of if it was produced from the same
compilation or from different compilations.
Here are a few examples of merging commands used in SDC :
• Same Compilation
%vcs test.v -sdc=test.sdc -full64 -sverilog -cm sdc

%simv -cm sdc -cm_name test_1

%simv -cm sdc -cm_name test_2

%urg -dir simv.vdb -format text
• Different Compilation
%vcs test_1.v -sdc=test_1.sdc -cm_dir simv_1.vdb -full64 -sverilog -cm
sdc
%simv -cm sdc -cm_dir simv_1.vdb

%vcs test_2.v -sdc=test_2.sdc -cm_dir simv_2.vdb -full64 -sverilog -cm
sdc
%simv -cm sdc -cm_dir simv_2.vdb

%urg -dir simv_1.vdb simv_2.vdb -format text

merging). For merging multiple vdbs into a single database, the following command can be

Test correlation enables visibility into which specific tests cover each object in the design.

Defining Module as Black Box
The Black Box Module feature allows you to mark a module as black box for SDC
verification. No SDC validation happens inside the module or through the module. This is
particularly useful when you have modules that are not synthesizable.
This feature does not alter the design’s simulation results.
SDC identifies the modules to be guarded in the following two ways:
• Modules that have only input ports and no output or inout ports are considered as true
black box modules. This identification happens when this feature is run in auto mode.
• You can provide a list of modules from the command line to declare as true black box
modules.
The input clock ports are excluded from guarding.

Memory Optimization by limiting Number of Paths per src-destination Pair
• Use the following option to run this feature in auto mode, that is, auto identification of
trueBB modules:
-sdc=trueBB:auto
• Use the following option to pass a list of trueBB modules from the command line:
-sdc=trueBB:bbMods.txt
where,
bbMods.txt is the text file containing a list of trueBB modules.
• Use this following option to run this feature in auto mode as well as to take the input
from the command line:
-sdc=trueBB:auto,trueBB:bbMods.txt
After VCS compilation, mcpLogs/trueBBMods.txt text file is generated under the
mcpLogs directory. This text file consists of a list of the trueBB modules that are identified
during compilation. It also contains a list of the trueBB modules identified in auto mode
and from the command line.
Limitation
The following are the limitations of Black Box Module:
• Interfaces should not be black boxed.
• A warning message gets displayed in the mcpLogs/trueBB.txt file when a module
does not exist in the design.
Memory Optimization by limiting Number of Paths per
src-destination Pair
Sometimes some SDC commands such as those that include a false path, multicycle
path, or a clock group, use a very high number of paths. This blows up the compile time
memory. By limiting maximum number of paths to be analyzed for every unique pair of
source and destination, the memory requirement can be reduced.
This performance optimization is enabled through the following option:
-sdc=maxSrcDestPath:N

where,
• N is the limit on number of paths between the source and destination.
• If the value of N is not given with -sdc=maxSrcDestPath, then, by default, there is no
limit on number of paths per source-destination pair.
• If the total number of paths from the source to destination pair exceeds a specified N,
the paths above the threshold are ignored.
• The value of N should be a positive integer , that is, 1,2,3 and so on.
Let us say there are N number of ways a destination can be reached from a source signal.
Using above option, the tool chooses only N number of ways, that is, N number of unique
points between the source and destination signal.
src ----> n1 ----> dest
src ----> n2 ----> dest
-----------------------
src ----> N ----> dest

Handling CDC Synchronizer
Handling CDC Synchronizer
Consider the following example where CLKA and CLKB are asynchronous clocks defined
in the SDC file by the following command:
set_clock_groups -async -group CLKA -group CLKB
Using the -sdc=verify_clock_group option, the tool determines CDC path between
Source flop and Stage 1 flop of N stage synchronizer. By default, tool identifies early
capture at Stage 1 flop and holds the previous value for 1 cycle of CLKB and prints
violation message for Stage 1 flop. This can create many runtime messages which may
not be of any use.
To avoid this, use the following SDC config file to suppress violation messages in the
synchronizer cells. This configures the tool not to give any violation message inside
synchronizer cell and only hold the previous value.
---------- sdc.cfg ---------
tree {synchronizer_cell} {noPrintViolations,insertBool};
-------------------------------
The compilation option is vcs +optconfigfile+sdc.cfg …
Also, if N stage synchronizer is used for all CDC paths, it is recommended to use the
-sdc=verify_clock_group:N so that the tool holds the previous value at stage 1 flop for
N-1 cycles.
The following config command can also used to randomize the previous value holding at
stage 1 flop between 0 to N-1 cycles.
tree {synchronizer_cell}
{noPrintViolations,insertBool, insertRandomDelay};

Latch Checks
Latch Checks
This section describes latch check support in the following topics:
• Latch as Source
• Latch as Destination
Latch as Source
In the following waveform example, ff1 is the source Latch and ff2 is the destination
Flop, Clock (clk) goes as enable signal to ff1 and as a clock to ff2
Figure 32 Latch as Source
The source time stamping takes place when the source (ff1) value changes and is not
dependent on the clock transitions. The constraint equation is as follows:
t_capture- t_launch>(n-1)ClkPeriod
• t_capture and t_launch are the time stamps of destination and source change
respectively.
• n specifies the clock cycle.
• ClkPeriod is the time period of the destination or source clock based on -end/-start.
If the above equation fails, this results in an SDC violation.
Latch as Destination
In the following waveform as an example, the ff1 is the source Flop with clk as Clock, and
ff2 is the destination Latch with clk2 as enable signal.

Figure 33 Latch as Destination
The destination is time-stamping and precise checks take place when the destination(ff2)
value changes and is not dependent on clock transitions. Therefore, as observed in the
earlier mentioned example that ff2 changes multiple times during the level high of clk2, for
each ff2 change precise checks are done.
The constraint equation is as follows:
t_capture- t_launch>(n-1)ClkPeriod
• If the violation occurs, the duration of destination corruption depends on where the
violation window finishes.
◦ If the violation window finishes at the level high state of the latch, then corruption
occurs until this point.
◦ If the violation window finishes at the level low state of the latch, then corruption
continues until the next high state of the latch.
You need to examine the behaviour of Hold and Setup path-multiplier for the following
three cases:
Case1: Hold and Setup are in pair or used together but the value of Setup is higher:
Example 2 Setup Value is 3 and Hold is 0
set_multicycle_path -setup 3 -from src -to dest
set_multicycle_path -hold 0 -end -from src -to dest
This is equivalent to specifying set_multicycle_path setup command alone, without
hold.

Setup: Maximum delay between source and destination can be 3 cycles.
Hold: Minimum delay between source and destination must be two cycles
As per the specified constraints since data can't arrive before two cycles, the tool
maintains the previous value at destination for cycles 1-3. Therefore, no violations are
reported and no X-injection in this case.
Example 3 Setup value is 3 and Hold is 1
set_multicycle_path -setup 3 -from src -to dest
set_multicycle_path -hold 1 -end -from src -to dest
Setup: Maximum delay between source and destination can be three cycles.
Hold: Minimum delay between source and destination must be one cycle.
As per the specified constraints since data can't arrive before 1 cycle, the tool maintains
the previous value at destination for cycles 1-2. Therefore, no violations are reported and
no X-injection in this window.

Violation window is cycle 2-3, during which, if the destination changes (EARLY
CAPTURE), it will be metastable (X or previous value).
Example 4 Setup Value is 3 and Hold is 2
set_multicycle_path -setup 3 -from src -to dest
set_multicycle_path -hold 2 -end -from src -to dest
Setup: Maximum delay between source and destination can be 3 cycles.
Hold: Minimum delay between source and destination is 0 cycles.
Violation window is cycle 1-3, during which if the destination changes (EARLY CAPTURE),
it will be metastable (X or previous value). This is similar to the tool behaviour (default)
when -sdc=hold compile time switch is not used.
Case 2: Hold and Setup are in pair or used together but the value of Hold is higher
Example 5 Setup Value is 2 and Hold is 3
create_clock -period 20 -name sys_clk1 [get_ports clk1]
set_multicycle_path -setup 2 -start -from ff1* -to ff2*
set_multicycle_path -hold 3 -start -from ff1* -to ff2*

(Clock: testbench.dut1.clk1 (sys_clk1:test.sdc:1)) Last Capture-Q change

Hold: Minimum delay between source and destination is 2 cycles.
As per the specified constraints, for the data to remain stable no new data should be
