When using -sdc=hold along with -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock:advanced, if the data
at the destination is captured by an unknown clock, the hold violation associated with that
destination data change is not reported.
Limitations:
• The hold commands does not support if the expression is involved with a concat. The
following error message is printed into sdc_errors.log file for such unsupported
constructs.
set_multicycle_path 2 -from [get_nets epx_ap2_rptr_o] -hold
Warning-[SDC-HOLD-NYS] New hold check will not be supported.

MCP path destination 'bBBug.epx_ap2_rptr_o[1]' is a concat :
Unsupported-construct(bBBug.sdc:7)
• The hold commands are not supported along with -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock
switch. Instead, it is supported with -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock:advanced.

If -sdc=hold is used together with -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock, the following error is
observed:
EW_1: Warning-[SDC-HOLD-NYS] -sdc=hold is not supported with
-sdc=dynamic_multi_clock (without :advanced).
Use -sdc=dynamic_multi_clock:advanced instead.
• If the source is a latch, the following warning message is added into the
sdc_erros.log file.
Figure 36
• If the source is a UDP, the following warning message is added into the
sdc_erros.log file.
Figure 37
Enable DATA_STABILITY_VIOLATION reporting in VCS-SDC with -sdc=hold to detect
source signal changes inside the data stability window.
The VCS-SDC tool reports a violation message, DATA_STABILITY_VIOLATION, in the
simulation log file whenever the source data changes within the data stability window
(DSW).
Normally, the violation window is based on the SETUP limit. If the setup limit is “N” cycles,
the DSW covers 0 to N cycles. The source signal must remain stable during this window,
if the source changes within this window, VCS reports a DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION

message. During the precise data stability check, the tool flags a violation if the destination
changes.
Overview
Enabling Data Stability Violation Reporting with -sdc=hold
• Scenario 1: When SETUP is greater than HOLD and hold checks are enabled,that is
-sdc=hold is specified. The DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION window is based on the
SETUP limit.
◦ The violation window always follows the SETUP limit, irrespective of the HOLD
limit .
◦ If the SETUP limit is "N" cycles, the window is from 0 to N cycles.
◦ The source signal must stay stable during this window.
◦ If the source changes within this window, VCS reports a DATA-STABILITY-
VIOLATION message.
• Scenario 2: When SETUP is less than or equal to HOLD and hold checks are enabled,
that is -sdc=hold is specified. The DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION window is always
HOLD + 1 cycles, regardless of the SETUP limit.
Consider the following example: SETUP is 1 cycle, HOLD is 1 cycle, the DSW window
is 2 cycles, that is HOLD + 1.
◦ The source signal must stay stable for 2 cycles.
◦ VCS reports a DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION message, if the source changes within
these 2 cycles.
With the -sdc=hold option, hold check for setup = 1, hold = 1 case is also
enabled.
Example Scenarios:
Example 1: Setup = N Hold = N
In the following figure, Setup = 1 and hold =1 or Setup is not given and hold = 1

Figure 38
Source is stable with 0 – 2 cycles. DSW = 2
Example 2: Setup <= Hold

Figure 39
Source is stable with 0 – 4 cycles. DSW = 4
Example 3: Setup >Hold
In the following figure, Setup =3, Hold = 2 or Setup = 3, Hold = 1 or Setup = 3, Hold = 0/no
hold

Figure 40
Source is stable between 0 - 3 cycles. DSW = 3
Example 4
set_multicycle_path 1 -setup -from ff1 -to ff2

set_multicycle_path 1 -hold -from ff1 -to ff2

Following Data Stability violation is flagged at 130
Figure 41

The following warning message is displayed:
Warning-[SDC_DATA_VIOL] SDC DATA STABILITY VIOLATION

DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION @ Time: 130, Source expected to be stable for

cycles, observed to be stable for 1 cycles

Source : top.mult.ff1 (set_multicycle_path case3.sdc:5)
Example 5
In the following figure, the default limit for the data stability violations per source is 6, after
reaching 6 violations the following message gets printed:
Figure 42
The limit of data stability violations can be changed through the
-sdc=max_data_stability_count:N option.

Example 6:
Figure 43
The source ff1 changes at time 110, which is within the DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION
window based on the setup window. Therefore, a data stability violation is reported at the
first destination capture point at time 130. Additionally, data stability violations are checked
at every positive edge throughout the delay injection window.
• The max_destination_violation and maxSuccessiveViolations SDC
options do not impact the count of data stability violations.
• Under the -sdc=hold option, hold only commands are shown in the SDC
command summary section of the mcp.Summary.log file.

Memory Cell Support
• Data stability checks were not previously performed for paths within the
minimum delay window. This support has now been added.
• Hold support is not available for sources such as "UDP," "latch," or "concat."
The hold option also does not work with the dynamic_multi_clock switch.
For more information about warning messages, see the Limitations section.
Memory Cell Support
Configure memory modules in VCS-SDC using -sdc=memory_config to apply MCP
constraints on SRAM pins without instrumenting internal memory logic.
VCS-SDC allows you to specify and infer memory modules.
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Specifying Memory Modules
• Inferring Memory Modules
• Using Memory Module Pins in SDC Constraints
Specifying Memory Modules
You can specify the memory modules using the compile option
-sdc=memory_config:<mem.cfg>. The file <mem.cfg> should contain module names
separated by new line.
The following is an example for specifying the memory module:
%vcs -sverilog -debug_access -sdc=memory_config:mcp_mem.cfg -kdb -lca
EARLY-CAPTURE_VIOLATION message does not get printed during
simulation. This occurs because the memory model is not instrumented. An "X"
value is injected only on the memory pins during the first cycle, which causes
the "X" to propagate. You can observe the memory boundary port and inject
the delay/X on boundary ports but this does not ensure that the memory is
corrupted.

Memory Cell Support
However, in the summary report at the end of simulation, this path is reported
as violating if there is an early capture on the boundary pin. You can view the
X/Delay injection in Verdi including marker as illustrated in the following :
Figure 44 X-injections observed at memory boundary input pin
Inferring Memory Modules
You can use the -sdc=memory_config:auto compile option to infer memory modules.
Memory module internal logic is not used by the tool for any analysis.
You can use the following option for allowing SDC on memory module which has multiple
output port:
-sdc=memory_config:auto:<N>
Where, <N> is the number of the output ports in memory module.
Memory modules can be inferred in the following cases:
• Memory modules should be present inside celldefine.
• Memory module should contain MDA or Verilog memory or dynamic array or
associative array.
Identified memory modules are reported in mcpLogs/mem_config.txt file. The following is
an example:
vcs -sverilog -debug_access -sdc=memory_config:auto:2 -kdb -lca
Using Memory Module Pins in SDC Constraints
Memory module pins can be referenced in SDC constraints (set_multicycle_path,
set_false_path) as follows:
-from/-through [get_pins sram_inst/clk_pin_name]
-from/-through [get_pins sram_inst/output_pin_name]
-to/-through [get_pins sram_inst/input_pin_name]

Handling Combination Loops During Simulation
Multi-clock memories are not supported; therefore, no paths are created to or from multi
clock memory ports.
Handling Combination Loops During Simulation
The combination loops detection feature enables VCS SDC to detect a combo loop (which
might be broken by a designer by adding delays) connected to a source signal. The
simulation detects loops on top of the events scheduled at each timestamp.
To enable printing detected loop info, use the following compile time option:
debug_access+r
To enable loop detection, use the following runtime option :
-sdc=combo_loop
A loop is reported in the following format:
COMBO-LOOP @ Time: 25. TO top.d1.ff2
|--> FROM top.d1.ff1
|--> Loop
where,
• Time represents when the loop is detected.
• TO and FROM represent the receiver and driver respectively.
The loop prints signals where it is formed.
bit x,y;
wire z;
assign z = y;
assign x=z;
assign #1 y = ~(x^in1);
The above logic has a loop in zero delay simulation.
Handling XMR
When upwards or downwards XMR appears in an SDC path, the source
is dropped and path is not verified. In these situations,the error message
UNHANDLED_COMPLEX_XMR_IN_FANOUT is logged in mcpLogs/sdc_errors.log file.

Handling XMR
These paths can be retained by guarding the upwards and downwards XMR using the
-sdc=allow_xmr_guard:on compile time option.
Here,
b1.sig is used outside as either as a driver or load, that is an XMR.
module top;
bot b1();
always @(b1.sig)
$display(b1.sig); // b1.sig = 1'b1;

module bot(input in);
reg sig;
reg local;
reg ff;
always @(sig)
local = ~sig;
always @(in)
sig = in;
always @(posedge clk)
ff = local;
• SDC Error Log Before Guarding:
------------------- UNSUPPORTED OBJECTS BEGINS ----------

module DFFR
//////////////////////
EW_1:
/*UNHANDLED COMPLEX XMR IN FANOUT*/
dut.v : 27
sig

//////////////////////
Endmodule
------------------- PARSING ERRORS ENDS -------------------
• SDC Error Log After Guarding:
------------------- PARSING BEGINS OF test.sdc FOR INSTANCE
testbench/mult-------------------
------------------- PARSING ERRORS ENDS -------------------
Limitation
Force information originating from UCLI for PLI nodes cannot be determined. As a result, it
is not possible to apply XMR guarding in these cases.

Automatic Inference of Synchronous Ports
Automatic Inference of Synchronous Ports
By default, top module input, output, and inout ports are treated as asynchronous unless
explicitly constrained using set_input_delay or set_output_delay commands. This can
result in errors when using certain SDC commands that require synchronous timing paths.
The -sdc=aisp (Auto Infer Sync Ports) option automatically treats top module input and
output ports as synchronous by associating them with timing constraints, eliminating
common constraint errors.
Default Behavior (Without -sdc=aisp)
Without the -sdc=aisp option, top module ports are only treated as synchronous if you
explicitly specify timing constraints:
set_input_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {in}
set_output_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {out}
If these constraints are not defined, commands such as:
set_false_path -from {in} # top module input port
set_false_path -to {out} # top module output port
This generates the MCP-SRC-ONBOUNDARY or MCP-DEST-ONBOUNDARY errors in
the mcpLogs/sdc_errors.log.
Behavior with -sdc=aisp
When the -sdc=aisp option is enabled, the SDC tool automatically:
• Identifies all input and output ports (excluding inout ports) of the top module.
• Checks if set_input_delay or set_output_delay constraints are already defined for
these ports.
• For ports without explicit delay constraints, automatically treats them as synchronous
by associating them with an internal clock reference.
With this option, commands as shown below does not generate errors, and timing paths
will be created even if set_input_delay or set_output_delay are not explicitly defined.
set_false_path -from {in} # top module input port
set_false_path -to {out} # top module output port
To enable automatic inference of synchronous ports, add the -sdc=aisp option to your
VCS command line
vcs -sdc=aisp <other_options>

Automatic Inference of Synchronous Ports
Limitations:
• Inout ports are excluded: Only input and output ports are automatically treated as
synchronous. Inout ports are not included in this behavior.
• Applies to all top-level ports: When -sdc=aisp is used, all top-level input/output ports
are processed for synchronization, regardless of whether they are explicitly mentioned
in SDC commands.
• Vector ports: If a port is a vector, the option applies to all bits of the vector. However,
delay paths are only formed for the specific bits referenced in the SDC command.
• Clock selection for delay calculation:
◦ For input ports: The clock connected to the destination flop is used for delay
calculation, not the clock associated with the input port.
# Uses clock connected to ff1
set_multicycle_path -setup 3 -from {in} -to {ff1}
set_multicycle_path -setup -end 3 -from {in} -to {ff1}

# Throws MCP-SRC-ONBOUNDARY error (requires source clock)
set_multicycle_path -setup -start 3 -from {in} -to {ff1}
The -start option throws an error because it requires the source (input port) clock,
which is an internal reference and cannot be explicitly used.
◦ For output ports: The clock connected to the source flop is always used for delay
calculation.
# Uses clock connected to ff1 (source clock)
set_multicycle_path -setup -start 3 -from {ff1} -to {out}
set_multicycle_path -setup -end 3 -from {ff1} -to {out}
# Without -sdc=aisp: Requires explicit constraints
set_input_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {in}
set_output_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {out}
# Throws MCP-DEST-ONBOUNDARY error if set_output_delay is not
specified (requires source clock)
set_multicycle_path -setup -end 3 -from {ff1} -to {out}

# With -sdc=aisp: Automatic synchronous treatment
# No set_input_delay/set_output_delay needed
set_false_path -from {in}
set_false_path -to {out}
# These commands work without errors

• For the below multicycle path, MCP-SRC-DEST-ONBOUNDARY error is thrown if input and
output delays are not defined and -sdc=aisp switch is provided:
set_multicycle_path 2 -setup -from {in} -to {out}
The Warning-[MCP-SRC-DEST-ONBOUNDARY] SDC path endpoint is non-sequential. You
need to specify the set_input_delay, set_output_delay in the SDC file.
The following are the limitation of MCP instrumentation:
The following scenarios, data types, and technologies are not supported:
• VHDL/MX hierarchy (MCPs across VHDL portions are not supported. Can handle if
MCPs are limited to Verilog portions).
• NLP
• Partition Compile/PIP
• FGP
• If multi-cycle path traverses through SystemC hierarchy, MCP validation is not
supported
• MCP validation is not supported on paths through non-synthesizable constructs.
• Unsupported flop path end points:
◦ ff_reg_1_/Q, // the underscore after index "1" causes parsing error.
◦ SDC paths through latches with time-borrowing (MCP Validation is supported on
latches without time-borrowing)
◦ SDC paths through resettable latches
• If one of the MCP endpoints is coming through a mux and the mux select is tied to a
specific value in the testbench in such a way that only one data path is sensitized, the
other data paths would also be reported as ACTIVE.
For example, in the following design mux sel is set to “0”. Therefore, both the paths
ff1[0] to ff2 and ff1[1] to ff2 are reported as ACTIVE (although ff1[1] to ff2
path is expected to be inactive).

•Figure 45
• Integer (Flop created with the integer data type signal is not supported while creating
or mapping paths).
• Enum data type support is not available. The end points of the Enum data type are
ignored.
• Forced signals maintain their value regardless of violations. Violation messages are for
diagnostic purpose, and they do not change simulation behavior for forced signals.

text:
Handling CDC Synchronizer
Handling CDC Synchronizer
Consider the following example where CLKA and CLKB are asynchronous clocks defined
in the SDC file by the following command:
set_clock_groups -async -group CLKA -group CLKB
Using the -sdc=verify_clock_group option, the tool determines CDC path between
Source flop and Stage 1 flop of N stage synchronizer. By default, tool identifies early
capture at Stage 1 flop and holds the previous value for 1 cycle of CLKB and prints
violation message for Stage 1 flop. This can create many runtime messages which may
not be of any use.
To avoid this, use the following SDC config file to suppress violation messages in the
synchronizer cells. This configures the tool not to give any violation message inside
synchronizer cell and only hold the previous value.
---------- sdc.cfg ---------
tree {synchronizer_cell} {noPrintViolations,insertBool};
-------------------------------
The compilation option is vcs +optconfigfile+sdc.cfg …
Also, if N stage synchronizer is used for all CDC paths, it is recommended to use the
-sdc=verify_clock_group:N so that the tool holds the previous value at stage 1 flop for
N-1 cycles.
The following config command can also used to randomize the previous value holding at
stage 1 flop between 0 to N-1 cycles.
tree {synchronizer_cell}
{noPrintViolations,insertBool, insertRandomDelay};

title: 2 cycle delay (set_false_path base_false_path.sdc:23)
text:
Latch Checks
Latch Checks
This section describes latch check support in the following topics:
• Latch as Source
• Latch as Destination
Latch as Source
In the following waveform example, ff1 is the source Latch and ff2 is the destination
Flop, Clock (clk) goes as enable signal to ff1 and as a clock to ff2
Figure 32 Latch as Source
The source time stamping takes place when the source (ff1) value changes and is not
dependent on the clock transitions. The constraint equation is as follows:
t_capture- t_launch>(n-1)ClkPeriod
• t_capture and t_launch are the time stamps of destination and source change
respectively.
• n specifies the clock cycle.
• ClkPeriod is the time period of the destination or source clock based on -end/-start.
If the above equation fails, this results in an SDC violation.
Latch as Destination
In the following waveform as an example, the ff1 is the source Flop with clk as Clock, and
ff2 is the destination Latch with clk2 as enable signal.

Figure 33 Latch as Destination
The destination is time-stamping and precise checks take place when the destination(ff2)
value changes and is not dependent on clock transitions. Therefore, as observed in the
earlier mentioned example that ff2 changes multiple times during the level high of clk2, for
each ff2 change precise checks are done.
The constraint equation is as follows:
t_capture- t_launch>(n-1)ClkPeriod
• If the violation occurs, the duration of destination corruption depends on where the
violation window finishes.
◦ If the violation window finishes at the level high state of the latch, then corruption
occurs until this point.
◦ If the violation window finishes at the level low state of the latch, then corruption
continues until the next high state of the latch.
You need to examine the behaviour of Hold and Setup path-multiplier for the following
three cases:
Case1: Hold and Setup are in pair or used together but the value of Setup is higher:
Example 2 Setup Value is 3 and Hold is 0
set_multicycle_path -setup 3 -from src -to dest
set_multicycle_path -hold 0 -end -from src -to dest
This is equivalent to specifying set_multicycle_path setup command alone, without
hold.

Setup: Maximum delay between source and destination can be 3 cycles.
Hold: Minimum delay between source and destination must be two cycles
As per the specified constraints since data can't arrive before two cycles, the tool
maintains the previous value at destination for cycles 1-3. Therefore, no violations are
reported and no X-injection in this case.
Example 3 Setup value is 3 and Hold is 1
set_multicycle_path -setup 3 -from src -to dest
set_multicycle_path -hold 1 -end -from src -to dest
Setup: Maximum delay between source and destination can be three cycles.
Hold: Minimum delay between source and destination must be one cycle.
As per the specified constraints since data can't arrive before 1 cycle, the tool maintains
the previous value at destination for cycles 1-2. Therefore, no violations are reported and
no X-injection in this window.

Violation window is cycle 2-3, during which, if the destination changes (EARLY
CAPTURE), it will be metastable (X or previous value).
Example 4 Setup Value is 3 and Hold is 2

set_multicycle_path -hold 2 -end -from src -to dest
Setup: Maximum delay between source and destination can be 3 cycles.
Hold: Minimum delay between source and destination is 0 cycles.
Violation window is cycle 1-3, during which if the destination changes (EARLY CAPTURE),
it will be metastable (X or previous value). This is similar to the tool behaviour (default)
when -sdc=hold compile time switch is not used.

Enable DATA_STABILITY_VIOLATION reporting in VCS-SDC with -sdc=hold to detect
source signal changes inside the data stability window.
The VCS-SDC tool reports a violation message, DATA_STABILITY_VIOLATION, in the
simulation log file whenever the source data changes within the data stability window
(DSW).
Normally, the violation window is based on the SETUP limit. If the setup limit is “N” cycles,
the DSW covers 0 to N cycles. The source signal must remain stable during this window,
if the source changes within this window, VCS reports a DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION

message. During the precise data stability check, the tool flags a violation if the destination
changes.
Overview
Enabling Data Stability Violation Reporting with -sdc=hold
• Scenario 1: When SETUP is greater than HOLD and hold checks are enabled,that is
-sdc=hold is specified. The DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION window is based on the
SETUP limit.
◦ The violation window always follows the SETUP limit, irrespective of the HOLD
limit .
◦ If the SETUP limit is "N" cycles, the window is from 0 to N cycles.
◦ The source signal must stay stable during this window.
◦ If the source changes within this window, VCS reports a DATA-STABILITY-
VIOLATION message.
• Scenario 2: When SETUP is less than or equal to HOLD and hold checks are enabled,
that is -sdc=hold is specified. The DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION window is always
HOLD + 1 cycles, regardless of the SETUP limit.
Consider the following example: SETUP is 1 cycle, HOLD is 1 cycle, the DSW window
is 2 cycles, that is HOLD + 1.
◦ The source signal must stay stable for 2 cycles.
◦ VCS reports a DATA-STABILITY-VIOLATION message, if the source changes within
these 2 cycles.
With the -sdc=hold option, hold check for setup = 1, hold = 1 case is also
enabled.

title: 2 cycle delay (set_false_path base_false_path.sdc:23)
text:
Memory Cell Support
• Data stability checks were not previously performed for paths within the
minimum delay window. This support has now been added.
• Hold support is not available for sources such as "UDP," "latch," or "concat."
The hold option also does not work with the dynamic_multi_clock switch.
For more information about warning messages, see the Limitations section.
Memory Cell Support
Configure memory modules in VCS-SDC using -sdc=memory_config to apply MCP
constraints on SRAM pins without instrumenting internal memory logic.
VCS-SDC allows you to specify and infer memory modules.
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Specifying Memory Modules
• Inferring Memory Modules
• Using Memory Module Pins in SDC Constraints
Specifying Memory Modules
You can specify the memory modules using the compile option
-sdc=memory_config:<mem.cfg>. The file <mem.cfg> should contain module names
separated by new line.
The following is an example for specifying the memory module:
%vcs -sverilog -debug_access -sdc=memory_config:mcp_mem.cfg -kdb -lca
EARLY-CAPTURE_VIOLATION message does not get printed during
simulation. This occurs because the memory model is not instrumented. An "X"
value is injected only on the memory pins during the first cycle, which causes
the "X" to propagate. You can observe the memory boundary port and inject
the delay/X on boundary ports but this does not ensure that the memory is
corrupted.

Memory Cell Support
However, in the summary report at the end of simulation, this path is reported
as violating if there is an early capture on the boundary pin. You can view the
X/Delay injection in Verdi including marker as illustrated in the following :
Figure 44 X-injections observed at memory boundary input pin
Inferring Memory Modules
You can use the -sdc=memory_config:auto compile option to infer memory modules.
Memory module internal logic is not used by the tool for any analysis.
You can use the following option for allowing SDC on memory module which has multiple
output port:
-sdc=memory_config:auto:<N>
Where, <N> is the number of the output ports in memory module.
Memory modules can be inferred in the following cases:
• Memory modules should be present inside celldefine.
• Memory module should contain MDA or Verilog memory or dynamic array or
associative array.
Identified memory modules are reported in mcpLogs/mem_config.txt file. The following is
an example:
vcs -sverilog -debug_access -sdc=memory_config:auto:2 -kdb -lca
Using Memory Module Pins in SDC Constraints
Memory module pins can be referenced in SDC constraints (set_multicycle_path,
set_false_path) as follows:
-from/-through [get_pins sram_inst/clk_pin_name]
-from/-through [get_pins sram_inst/output_pin_name]
-to/-through [get_pins sram_inst/input_pin_name]

title: 2 cycle delay (set_false_path base_false_path.sdc:23)
text:
Handling Combination Loops During Simulation
Multi-clock memories are not supported; therefore, no paths are created to or from multi
clock memory ports.
Handling Combination Loops During Simulation
The combination loops detection feature enables VCS SDC to detect a combo loop (which
might be broken by a designer by adding delays) connected to a source signal. The
simulation detects loops on top of the events scheduled at each timestamp.
To enable printing detected loop info, use the following compile time option:
debug_access+r
To enable loop detection, use the following runtime option :
-sdc=combo_loop
A loop is reported in the following format:
COMBO-LOOP @ Time: 25. TO top.d1.ff2
|--> FROM top.d1.ff1
|--> Loop
where,
• Time represents when the loop is detected.
• TO and FROM represent the receiver and driver respectively.
The loop prints signals where it is formed.
bit x,y;
wire z;
assign z = y;
assign x=z;
assign #1 y = ~(x^in1);
The above logic has a loop in zero delay simulation.
Handling XMR
When upwards or downwards XMR appears in an SDC path, the source
is dropped and path is not verified. In these situations,the error message
UNHANDLED_COMPLEX_XMR_IN_FANOUT is logged in mcpLogs/sdc_errors.log file.

title: 2 cycle delay (set_false_path base_false_path.sdc:23)
text:
Handling XMR
These paths can be retained by guarding the upwards and downwards XMR using the
-sdc=allow_xmr_guard:on compile time option.
Here,
b1.sig is used outside as either as a driver or load, that is an XMR.
module top;
bot b1();
always @(b1.sig)
$display(b1.sig); // b1.sig = 1'b1;

module bot(input in);
reg sig;
reg local;
reg ff;
always @(sig)
local = ~sig;
always @(in)
sig = in;
always @(posedge clk)
ff = local;
• SDC Error Log Before Guarding:
------------------- UNSUPPORTED OBJECTS BEGINS ----------

module DFFR
//////////////////////
EW_1:
/*UNHANDLED COMPLEX XMR IN FANOUT*/
dut.v : 27
sig

//////////////////////
Endmodule
------------------- PARSING ERRORS ENDS -------------------
• SDC Error Log After Guarding:
------------------- PARSING BEGINS OF test.sdc FOR INSTANCE
testbench/mult-------------------
------------------- PARSING ERRORS ENDS -------------------
Limitation
Force information originating from UCLI for PLI nodes cannot be determined. As a result, it
is not possible to apply XMR guarding in these cases.

Automatic Inference of Synchronous Ports
Automatic Inference of Synchronous Ports
By default, top module input, output, and inout ports are treated as asynchronous unless
explicitly constrained using set_input_delay or set_output_delay commands. This can
result in errors when using certain SDC commands that require synchronous timing paths.
The -sdc=aisp (Auto Infer Sync Ports) option automatically treats top module input and
output ports as synchronous by associating them with timing constraints, eliminating
common constraint errors.
Default Behavior (Without -sdc=aisp)
Without the -sdc=aisp option, top module ports are only treated as synchronous if you
explicitly specify timing constraints:
set_input_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {in}
set_output_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {out}
If these constraints are not defined, commands such as:
set_false_path -from {in} # top module input port
set_false_path -to {out} # top module output port
This generates the MCP-SRC-ONBOUNDARY or MCP-DEST-ONBOUNDARY errors in
the mcpLogs/sdc_errors.log.
Behavior with -sdc=aisp
When the -sdc=aisp option is enabled, the SDC tool automatically:
• Identifies all input and output ports (excluding inout ports) of the top module.
• Checks if set_input_delay or set_output_delay constraints are already defined for
these ports.
• For ports without explicit delay constraints, automatically treats them as synchronous
by associating them with an internal clock reference.
With this option, commands as shown below does not generate errors, and timing paths
will be created even if set_input_delay or set_output_delay are not explicitly defined.
set_false_path -from {in} # top module input port
set_false_path -to {out} # top module output port
To enable automatic inference of synchronous ports, add the -sdc=aisp option to your
VCS command line
vcs -sdc=aisp <other_options>

Automatic Inference of Synchronous Ports
Limitations:
• Inout ports are excluded: Only input and output ports are automatically treated as
synchronous. Inout ports are not included in this behavior.
• Applies to all top-level ports: When -sdc=aisp is used, all top-level input/output ports
are processed for synchronization, regardless of whether they are explicitly mentioned
in SDC commands.
• Vector ports: If a port is a vector, the option applies to all bits of the vector. However,
delay paths are only formed for the specific bits referenced in the SDC command.
• Clock selection for delay calculation:
◦ For input ports: The clock connected to the destination flop is used for delay
calculation, not the clock associated with the input port.
# Uses clock connected to ff1
set_multicycle_path -setup 3 -from {in} -to {ff1}
set_multicycle_path -setup -end 3 -from {in} -to {ff1}

# Throws MCP-SRC-ONBOUNDARY error (requires source clock)
set_multicycle_path -setup -start 3 -from {in} -to {ff1}
The -start option throws an error because it requires the source (input port) clock,
which is an internal reference and cannot be explicitly used.
◦ For output ports: The clock connected to the source flop is always used for delay
calculation.
# Uses clock connected to ff1 (source clock)
set_multicycle_path -setup -start 3 -from {ff1} -to {out}
set_multicycle_path -setup -end 3 -from {ff1} -to {out}
# Without -sdc=aisp: Requires explicit constraints
set_input_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {in}
set_output_delay -clock [get_clocks sys_clk] 0 {out}
# Throws MCP-DEST-ONBOUNDARY error if set_output_delay is not
specified (requires source clock)
set_multicycle_path -setup -end 3 -from {ff1} -to {out}

2 cycle delay (set_false_path base_false_path.sdc:23)
text:
• For the below multicycle path, MCP-SRC-DEST-ONBOUNDARY error is thrown if input and
output delays are not defined and -sdc=aisp switch is provided:
set_multicycle_path 2 -setup -from {in} -to {out}
The Warning-[MCP-SRC-DEST-ONBOUNDARY] SDC path endpoint is non-sequential. You
need to specify the set_input_delay, set_output_delay in the SDC file.
The following are the limitation of MCP instrumentation:
The following scenarios, data types, and technologies are not supported:
• VHDL/MX hierarchy (MCPs across VHDL portions are not supported. Can handle if
MCPs are limited to Verilog portions).
• NLP
• Partition Compile/PIP
• FGP
• If multi-cycle path traverses through SystemC hierarchy, MCP validation is not
supported
• MCP validation is not supported on paths through non-synthesizable constructs.
• Unsupported flop path end points:
◦ ff_reg_1_/Q, // the underscore after index "1" causes parsing error.
◦ SDC paths through latches with time-borrowing (MCP Validation is supported on
latches without time-borrowing)
◦ SDC paths through resettable latches
• If one of the MCP endpoints is coming through a mux and the mux select is tied to a
specific value in the testbench in such a way that only one data path is sensitized, the
other data paths would also be reported as ACTIVE.
For example, in the following design mux sel is set to “0”. Therefore, both the paths
ff1[0] to ff2 and ff1[1] to ff2 are reported as ACTIVE (although ff1[1] to ff2
path is expected to be inactive).

•Figure 45
• Integer (Flop created with the integer data type signal is not supported while creating
or mapping paths).
• Enum data type support is not available. The end points of the Enum data type are
ignored.
• Forced signals maintain their value regardless of violations. Violation messages are for
diagnostic purpose, and they do not change simulation behavior for forced signals.

The SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) Checker
Library
The SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) Checker Library consists of two parts:
• SVL (described in Chapter 2) consists of checkers that have the same behavior and
controls as those in the Open Verification Library (OVL) - see the Accellera Open
Verification Library Reference Manual available at http://www.accellera.org/downloads/
standards/ovl. These checkers have additional features such as coverage in the SVA
Library.
• SVA Advanced Checkers (described in Chapter 3) contains checkers that generally
verify more complex behaviors. These have similar controls to the SVL checkers,
but, in addition, they allow selecting the sampling clock edge(s), posedge or negedge
Coverage is also provided.
Note that the header of each checker file also contains a description of the behavior and
parameters.
The checker library resides in a release in the directory
$VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg/
The
library, locationheader file
library consists of 53 checker files having the name assert_checker_name.v. There is

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
a description of the behavior and
parameters.
The checker library resides in a release in the directory
$VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg/
The
library, locationheader file
library consists of 53 checker files having the name assert_checker_name.v. There is
also a symbolic link to that file with the name assert_checker_name.sv that can be used
in situations where parts of the Verilog design follow Verilog2001 syntax and should be
compiled with that in mind to avoid keyword clashes with SystemVerilog keywords. In that
way, the extension .sv identifies the checkers to be compiler with SystemVerilog, while the
files with the .v extension compiles with Verilog2001 syntax and keywords.
The checkers have dual functions:
1. As a verification object using assert property statements. This form is employed for
verifying the behavior as specified for the checker.
2. As a coverage objects using cover property and cover points implemented using
the equivalent of covergroup statements. This form is employed to obtain information
about the observed presence of certain behavioral patterns in the design - coverage of
such patterns.
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

Global Controls
The two forms can coexist or be enabled independently as described later -the sections
Global Controls and Shared Syntax.
Note also that there is header file sva_std_task.h in the directory. It contains user-
modifiable reporting tasks and is included in each checker using 'include.
This chapter includes the following topics:
• Global Controls

Global Controls
The following symbols are macro’s defined using 'define and apply to all instances of the
checkers.ASSERT_ON, global controlGlobal Controls, ASSERT_ON
ASSERT_ON
When this macro is defined, the assertions and related variables in checkers are included,
that is., the checking functionality is enabled.COVER_ON, global controlGlobal Controls, COVER_ON
COVER_ON
When this macro is defined, the coverage items in the checkers are included.
That is, the coverage functionality is enabled. Note that the additional per-
instance control is provided using the checker parameters coverage_level_1,
coverage_level_2,andcoverage_level_3.
ASSERT_INIT_MSG, global controlGlobal Controls, ASSERT_INIT_MSG
ASSERT_INIT_MSG
When this macro is defined, then all checker instances display a message to stdout to
indicate their hierarchical name.ASSERT_GLOBAL_RESET, global controlGlobal Controls, ASSERT_GLOBAL_RESET
ASSERT_GLOBAL_RESET
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

Global Controls
When this macro is defined its defining expression is taken as the reset signal for all the
checkers. Otherwise, the reset_n port signal is used as reset.
ASSERT_MAX_REPORT_ERROR, global controlGlobal Controls, ASSERT_MAX_REPORT_ERROR
ASSERT_MAX_REPORT_ERROR
When this global macro variable is defined, the assertion instance stops reporting
messages if the number of errors for that instance is greater than the value defined
by the macro. Using this macro as described requires modifying the reporting tasks in
sva_std_task.h.SVA_CHECKER_INTERFACE, global controlGlobal Controls, SVA_CHECKER_INTERFACE
SVA_CHECKER_INTERFACE
If not defined, the
interface, SVA
interface is a SystemVerilog "module". If defined then the checker
interface is "interface". The parameters and ports remain the same in both cases.SVA_CHCKER_NO_MESSAGE, global controlGlobal Controls, SVA_CHCKER_NO_MESSAGE
SVA_CHECKER_NO_MESSAGE
When defined it eliminates reporting the user message when an assertion fails. It does not
control the default failure message from the simulator.
SVA_COV_LEVEL_i, i=1..3,
Globally selects coverage level 1. If user defines a value for coverage_level_i parameter in
a checker instance, it overrides the macro definition. By defining different values to these
macros and mot using the coverage level parameters in the checker instance(s), it allows
to select the same level(s) in all checkers.
SVA_ASSERT 0, SVA_ASSUME 1, SVA_IGNORE 2,
Can be used with the property_type parameter to select the verification statement, either
assert or assume or none. That parameter replaces the original options parameter in the
OVL-like checkers.
SVA_FATAL 0, SVA_ERROR 1,SVA_WARNING 2, SVA_INFO 3:
Predefined macros for severity can be used as actuals with the severity parameter.
SYNTHESIS
When defined, eliminates non-synthesizable code.
There are no //synopsys translate_on/off pragmas used anymore.
SVA_NO_DELAYED_SAMPLING
If defined, it excludes #1 delay in sampling of variables, otherwise include it to emulate
sampling in the preponed region for assignments in always blocks. The macro should only
be defined if the design contains no critical races.

Checker Triggering
Checker Triggering
In the SVL library (Chapter 2) all but one checker, assert_proposition is triggered at the
positive edge of a triggering signal or expression clk.
In the Advanced Checker Library (Chapter 3), all the checkers can select the sampling
edge(s) using a parameter. It can be either the positive or the negative edge of the clock
port expression.
The values of all actual signals or expressions in the ports of the checkers are sampled
just before the sampling edge of clk. Therefore, any pulses happening on the signals /
expressions between consecutive sampling edges of clk are not observed by the
checkers.
Moreover, whenever an edge of a signal / expression on a port of a checker other than
the clock is used in the checker, the value is the sampled form of the edge as detected by
looking at two consecutive samples of the signal.

Checkers With VMM Reporting Service
All checkers are enhanced to incorporate VMM messaging service. This would qualify the
simulation as PASSED or FAILED based on the assertion result.
Inclusion of VMM messaging service also allows you to control the simulation based on
the severity level of the checker instance. A severity level of 0 would continue with the
simulation, and a severity level other than 0 would terminate the simulation.
Inclusion of VMM messaging service is under a global control macro defined using
`define, namely “SVA_VMM_LOG”.
Custom Reporting
As in OVL, if you want to have more elaborate error reporting, counting, and so on., you
must edit the sva_std_task.h file that is distributed with the library and also resides in the
directory
$VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg/
This file is automatically ‘include -ed in each checker. If the location of the header file is
changed, the +incdir+ directive must also be modified accordingly.

Shared Syntax
Shared Syntax
Many checkers share the same syntax elements. These elements are described in this
section to avoid repeating their descriptions throughout this document.
severity_level
Severity of the failure with default value of 0. Currently SystemVerilog does not provide
support of severity levels through a parameter or a variable, therefore, this parameter is
provided only for compatibility with older versions of the checkers. However, by modifying
the error tasks in the sva_std_task.h file appropriately, severity level can be taken into
account. For example, the simulation can be terminated when a failure of an assertion
occurs and the checker severity level is set to some specific value.
options
Currently, the only supported option is options=1, which defines the assertion as an
assumption for formal tools. The default is 0 (no options specified). Note that Magellan
does not use options to determine the role (assume or assert) of the assertions.

msg
Error message that is printed when the assertion fires using the default definition of the
sva_checker_error task that is included in the sva_std_task.h file. Its output can also
be controlled by the macro SVA_CHCKER_NO_MESSAGE.
category
Specifies the category of the assertion (Default = 0). This parameter can be used to group
assertions used for a similar purpose, and provide a selection/filtering mechanism to
enable/ disable individual or groups of assertions.
coverage_level_i
Specifies which
coverage levels, definitionslevels, coverage
coverage levels should be enabled (provided that the symbol COVER_ON
is defined) by specifying parameters. There are three coverage levels controlled by
parameters coverage_level_,coverage_level_2,and coverage_level_3.The bits in each
of the parameters when set to 1 enable some specific coverage point, one per bit. The
number of bits used thus depends on the number of cover points in the checker at each
level and varies from checker to checker. Generally, the following levels are supported
(Default = Coverage Level 1).
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

Using Coverage Levels to Report Checker Results
Level 1:Basic coverage, implemented using cover property statements. Used by
simulation and Magellan.
Level 1 coverages are enabled by setting bits in coverage_level_1 to 1.
Example: The number of Enqueues and Dequeues in a FIFO.
Level 2:Usually includes data coverage on ranges of values. These are coverage items
which show certain interesting activities of the RTL behavior in the form of statistics. Used
in simulation only but might also include cover properties on some particular sequences
that can be of interest as search goals for formal tools.
Level 2 coverages are enabled by setting bits in coverage_level_2 to 1.
Example: Range of latency values classified on at-least-once basis.
Level 3:Cover property coverage of specific corner points as specified. Used primarily by
formal tools as goals. These cover properties can be enabled in simulation too, however,
the same information can be obtained from Level 2 range coverages in the extreme bins.
These coverage items ensure that the corner case condition of the RTL design block are
verified during testing.
Level 3 coverages are enabled by setting bits in coverage_level_3 to 1.
Examples: The number of times FIFO reached HIGH water mark. The number of times
ACK was received at the next clock after REQ was issued. The number of times the
specified Min latency value was reached.
inst_name
Instance name of assertion monitor.
clk
Sampling clock of the assertion.
reset_n
Signal indicating completed initialization when set to 1. reset_n is used as an
asynchronous reset so that glitches on the sequence or expression might cause the
checker to reset. It is a good practice to assert the reset signal at least for one clock cycle
to avoid problems with initialization of internal variables in the checker.

Parameter Checks for SVA CG Checker Library
SVA CG library enables you to parameterize the checkers. To avoid errors due to invalid
parameter values at runtime, the checker library does a compile-time check on the
parameters.
The parameter checks are implemented using the IEEE1800-2009 elaboration system
tasks $info/$warning/$error/$fatal to ensure that the identified parameters have
only the valid values passed during the instantiation. All the invalid values are reported in a
single compilation, so that it can be corrected in a single iteration.
Use Model
To enable the parameter checks on all SVA CG checkers at compilation, add
+define+SVACG_ENABLE_ALL_ELAB_PARAM_CHECKS
To enable the parameter checks on an individual SVA CG checker at compilation, add
+define+SVACG_ENABLE_ELAB_PARAM_CHECKS_<checker name in lowercase>
To disable the parameter checks on an individual SVA CG checker at compilation, add
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

Parameter Checks for SVA CG Checker Library
+define+SVACG_DISABLE_ELAB_PARAM_CHECKS_<checker name in lowercase>
By default, the elaboration warnings are enabled and they occur when a required condition
is not satisfied.
To disable these warnings, add +define+SVACG_DISABLE_WARNINGS
Example 1 Example of Elaboration System Task Error
Error-[EEST] $error elaboration system task
msg: SVA CG CHECKER LIBRARY: Parameter 'category' has an invalid value
of -1
Permissible limits are category >= 0
location: file ../../sva_cg_w_check/assert_zero_one_hot.v line 255
path: tb_assert_zero_one_hot.inst7
Example 2 Example of Elaboration System Task Warning
Warning-[WEST] $warning elaboration system task
msg: SVA CG CHECKER LIBRARY: Bits 0 to 1 are only valid for Parameter
'coverage_level_1'. Received value '111'. Other bits is ignored
location: file
/users/vcs_user/scratch/ELAB_CHECKS/sand/packages/sva_cg/assert_delta.v
line 295
path: tb_assert_delta.inst13
Since the parameter checks are implemented using elaboration system tasks
$info/$warning/$error/$fatal, you should pass the compile-time option
-assert svaext as VCS supports these tasks only under this option.

as follows:
vcs -sverilog +define+ASSERT_ON+COVER_ON \
<design files and other options > \

+incdir+$VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg
Note that +define+ASSERT_ON on the VCS command line is necessary to turn on the
assertions in all checker instances. Alternatively or in addition, by defining COVER_ON the
coverage functionality can be included (it can be further controlled at the instance level by
the checker parameter coverage_level_i, where, i=1, 2, or 3.
To gather coverage information using the coverage functionality of the checkers, do
not include the -cm assert option. This is because coverage on cover property and
covergroup statements is automatically turned on in VCS.
The backward compatible form of the sva_cg library makes the checker
interfaces identical to those in the old sva library. Also, the checker behavior
is restricted to those supported by the old library. If you are migrating from

SVA Basic Checkers
This chapter contains 31checkers. All checkers, except assert_proposition, are
triggered at the positive edge of a triggering signal or expression clk.
The values of all actual signals or expressions in the ports of the checkers are sampled
just before the positive edge of clk. Therefore, any pulses happening on the signals /
expressions between consecutive positive edges of clk are not observed by the checkers.
Moreover, whenever an edge of a signal / expression on a port of a checker other than the
clock is used in the checker, it is the sampled form of the edge as detected by looking at
two consecutive samples of the signal.
The checker assert_proposition monitors an expression at all times and triggers at the
falling edge of the test_expr.

alternative name-based format.

clock, clk. It verifies that test_expr always evaluates true. If test_expr evaluates to false,
the assertion fires (that is, an error condition is detected in the code). The test_expr can
be any valid Verilog expression>>

Parameter Checks for SVA CG Checker Library
SVA CG library enables you to parameterize the checkers. To avoid errors due to invalid
parameter values at runtime, the checker library does a compile-time check on the
parameters.
The parameter checks are implemented using the IEEE1800-2009 elaboration system
tasks $info/$warning/$error/$fatal to ensure that the identified parameters have
only the valid values passed during the instantiation. All the invalid values are reported in a
single compilation, so that it can be corrected in a single iteration.

Migration From Old SVA Library $VCS_HOME/packages/sva to
New SVA Library $VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg
The sva_lib_compatible VHDL package in the components.sva_lib_compatible.vhd
file located in the $VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg directory, contains the VHDL component
definitions for all the checkers. It is intended to aid migration from the old library to the new
library.
For a smooth transition, perform the following steps:
1. Compile the component package intended for migration of the library. For example,
if the default WORK library is used, then the command to compile the package is as
vhdlan $VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg/components.sva_lib_compatible.vhd
2. Compile the selected SVA checkers using vlogan with +define
+SNPS_SVA_LIB_COMPATIBLE, and deposit them in a VHDL library. For example, if the
default WORK library is used, and if you want to compile all the checkers in the library
(it takes a fraction of a second to complete), then the command to compile the selected
SVA checkers is as follows (if coverage is requested, +define+COVER_ON must also be
added):
vlogan -sverilog $VCS_HOME/packages/sva_cg/*.v \ +incdir+$VCS_HOME/
packages/sva_cg \ +define+ASSERT_ON +define+SNPS_SVA_LIB_COMPATIBLE
3. To use the compiled checkers in the VHDL design, you must include commands to use
the following libraries:
library IEEE; use IEEE.STD_LOGIC_1164.all; library WORK; use WORK.
sva_lib_compatible.all;
Instantiate the checker component(s) as any other VHDL entity.
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

SVA Basic Checkers
This chapter contains 31checkers. All checkers, except assert_proposition, are
triggered at the positive edge of a triggering signal or expression clk.
The values of all actual signals or expressions in the ports of the checkers are sampled
just before the positive edge of clk. Therefore, any pulses happening on the signals /
expressions between consecutive positive edges of clk are not observed by the checkers.
Moreover, whenever an edge of a signal / expression on a port of a checker other than the
clock is used in the checker, it is the sampled form of the edge as detected by looking at
two consecutive samples of the signal.
The checker assert_proposition monitors an expression at all times and triggers at the
falling edge of the test_expr.
In this chapter:
• Checker Descriptions
This section provides syntax and descriptions, and examples for all SVA checkers.
Note that each checker example is followed by an example of the checker written in the
alternative name-based format.
assert_always
The assert_always checker continuously monitors test_expr at every positive edge of
clock, clk. It verifies that test_expr always evaluates true. If test_expr evaluates to false,
the assertion fires (that is, an error condition is detected in the code). The test_expr can
be any valid Verilog expression>>

The assert_next checker validates proper cycle timing relationships between two events
in the design. When a start_event evaluates true, then the test_expr must evaluate true
exactly num_cks number of clock cycles later.
This checker supports overlapping sequences. For example, if you assert that test_expr
evaluates true exactly four cycles after start_event, it is not necessary to wait until the
sequence finishes before another sequence can begin.
num_cks
The number of clocks test_expr must evaluate to true after start_event is asserted.
check_overlapping
If 1, permits overlapping sequences (Default is 1). A new start_event can occur (starting
a new sequence in parallel) while the previous sequence continues. If 0, then overlap
checking is performed.
only_if
If true, a test_expr can only evaluate true, if preceded num_cks earlier by a
start_event. If test_expr occurs without a start_event, then an error is flagged. Default is
0.

checking is performed.

SVA Advanced Checkers
The second part of the checker library contains 22 checkers plus an
sva_std_edge_select.v file that contains an interface definition that is instantiated in all
these new checkers and computes the appropriate clock edge.
The new checkers use the same controls as the SVL checkers in the previous chapter, but
in addition they have a clock edge selection parameter, edge_expr.
In this chapter:
• Checker Descriptions
This section provides syntax and descriptions, and examples for all checkers.syntax, shared
Shared Syntax
Many checkers share the same syntax elements. In addition to using severity_level,
reset_n, clk,property_type, msg, and coverage_level_i, where, i= 1, 2, or 3, described
in Chapter 1, the checkers in this chapter can select the active edge of the clock:
edge_expr, shared syntax
edge_expr
Specifies the active edge for the clock signal (clk) in unit syntax. Use the following values
to specify the edge type:
• posedge: 0 (the default)
• negedge: 1
If edge_expr is not specified, it defaults to posedge.
assert_arbiter
Ensures that a resource arbiter provides grants to corresponding requests within min_lat
and max_lat cycles.
The checks are not enabled unless reset_n evaluates true at the time of the request. The
checks are performed on the active clk edge specification.
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

assert_arbiter [# (severity_level, no_chnl, bw_prio,
grant_one_chk, req_priority_chk,
arbitration_rule, min_lat, max_lat,
property_type)]
inst_name ( clk, reset_n, reqs, req_priority, grants );
no_chnl
The number of channels (bits) in requests and grants. Default = 2.
bw_prio
The number of bits that are used to encode req_priority.
Default = 1.
grant_one_chk
If true, then the unit checks to ensure that only one grant is issued per clock cycle. Default
= 1.
req_priority_chk
If true, then this checker ensures that grants are issued according to the priority indicated
in the req_priority vector. req_priority_chk. req_priority_chk functions on top of any other
scheme using arbitration_rule. That is, if priority and FIFO are selected then first priority
arbitration is applied and if multiple requests exist at the highest priority level, the final
selection must satisfy the FIFO rule.
If req_priority_chkis 0 (disabled), then req_priority is not taken into account in any
of the other checks. However, the argument req_priority must still have the correct
dimension even though the actual values do not matter (for example., pass vector of
0’s). The req_priority vector might be a design vector (that is., not a constant array).
However, while a request is being processed the req_priority should not change,
otherwise certain checks might produce incorrect results (success or failure). Default = 0.
arbitration_rule
Selects which arbitration algorithm is verified among fairness, FIFO or least-recently used
(LRU). It must be a compile-time constant.
arbitration_rule = 0 - no rule checked
arbitration_rule = 1 - fairness (round-robin)
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

arbitration_rule = 2 - FIFO
arbitration_rule = 3 - LRU
If fairness is selected, then this checker ensures that no channel is issued more than one
grant while other channels have requests pending except if this is the only request at the
highest req_priority when req_priority_chk is asserted.
If FIFO is selected, then this checker ensures that grants are issued according to the order
that their requests were received unless req_priority_chk is asserted which means that the
FIFO check is performed only on requests of the current highest req_priority.
If LRU is selected, then this checker ensures that grants are issued to the least recently
granted request. If req_priority_chk is also asserted than LRU is applied to (simultaneous)
highest priority requests. Note that initially, all requests are assumed to have happened
equally in the past, so that the selection between them is arbitrary until granted at least
once.
min_lat
The minimum global grant latency. Default = 1.
If min_lat = 0, then grant is expected starting the same cycle as the request. Therefore,
combinational arbiter is possible with both min_lat and max_lat=0.
If priority arbitration check is enabled, then min_lat should be 0 or 1 only.
min_lat should never be less than zero.
max_lat
The maximum global grant latency. Default = 0.
If max_lat=0 and min_lat>0, then grant is expected after min_lat clock cycles. No
maximum latency check is performed.
If max_lat > 0, then a persistent request is granted within max_lat clock cycles. This
check is useful in systems where a request is granted within a certain latency even in the
presence of other requests.
If max_lat < 0, then both maximum and minimum global grant latency check is disabled.
reqs
Requests signals as vectors.
Vector of size [no_chnl-1:0] where the bits correspond to the corresponding channels in
reqs . req is assumed to be 1 when active.
req_priority

A[bw_prio*no_chnl-1 : 0] bitvector of bw_prio*no_chnl bits formed by concatenating non-
negative integer req_priority values corresponding to the request lines. The right-most
bw_prio bits in req_priority corresponds to channel 0, and so on. The req_priority
value 0 is the lowest req_priority.

Assumptions
When req_priority_chk = 0 it is assumed that the req_priority vector is set to all 0
values.
It is preferable that min_lat > 0 when req_priority_chk = 0 , that is., combinational
response is possible only in req_priority - based arbitration.
A grant is expected to be one clock cycle wide, unless the grant is for more than one
consecutive request.
It is assumed that a request holds asserted until granted. It is assumed that a request is
removed on the clock tick the grant is sampled, unless another request is immediately
asserted. Its removal before a grant causes the grant to be canceled, and this does cancel
the check for a grant.
Upon failure assertion assert_arbiter_one_cycle_gnt[i] reports !grants[i] as the
failing expression meaning that in position i the grant signal was not deasserted on the
next cycle.
Assertion assert_arbiter_req_granted[i] reports failure when in position i the grant
signal did not arrive within the specified latency.
Assertion assert_arbiter_granted_only_if_req[i] reports failure when in position i
the grant signal occurred without a request being asserted at the same time.
Assertion assert_arbiter_highest_grant[i] reports failure when line i the granted
request was not that of the highest req_priority.
Assertion assert_arbiter_fifo_chk[i][j] reports failure if on line j the grant was
asserted before the grant on line i while the requests came in the opposite order.
Assertion assert_arbiter_two_active[i][j] , a failure means that although there
were continuous requests on line i and j, the grant on line i arrived twice without a grant
on line j.
Assertion assert_arbiter_single_grant reports failure there were more than one
grant at the same time.

chapter: 0 and 1 for channel 1, encoded over one bit; grant_one_chk=1, req_priority_chk=1,
title: 0 and 1 for channel 1, encoded over one bit; grant_one_chk=1, req_priority_chk=1,
text:
arbitration_rule=0, min_lat=1, max_lat=5 . Signals are sampled at posedge
clk. The (optional) message is "arbiter failed" and it is output in addition to the standard
simulator message. Coverage levels 1 and 2 are enabled.
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

assert_arbiter #(.severity_level(0),. no_chnl(2),
. bw_prio(1),.grant_one_chk(1),.req_priority_chk(1),
. arbitration_rule(0),.min_lat(1),.max_lat(5),
. edge_expr(0),.msg(""arbiter failed "),.category(0),
.coverage_level_1(15),.coverage_level_2(15),
arbiter_inst (.clk(clk),.reset_n(1 ),.reqs( requests),
.req_priority( 2'b1_0),.grants(grants));
assert_bits
Ensures that the value of exp has between min and max number of bits that are asserted
or deasserted as indicated by the asserted flag. To specify a single number and not a
range, usemin == max.
assert_bits [#(severity_level, min, max, asserted, exp_bw,
property_type )]
inst_name ( clk, reset_n, exp);
min
Minimum number of bits asserted or deasserted. Valid values of constant parameters: min,
max must be non-negative integers. Default = 1.
max
Maximum number of bits asserted or deasserted. Valid values of constant parameters:
min, max must be non-negative integers. Default = 1.
asserted
If deasserted evaluates true, then the check is to ensure that the specified number or
range of bits in exp is 1. Otherwise, the check is to ensure the specified number or range
of bits in exp is 0. Default = 1, meaning that the test is for bits set to 1.
exp_bw
The number of bits in exp.
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

Upon failure, if asserted = 1, then failure indicates that the number of bits set to 1 in exp
was not in the interval[min, max], and if deasserted = 1, then failure indicates that the

depth
The maximum number of elements in the queue. Default = 2. The specified depth can be
at most 216.
elem_sz
The size of queue elements in bits. Default = 1.

hi_water_mark
If hi_water_mark is a positive value, then the level of the fill of the queue after enqueue
is checked to see if hi_water_mark is exceeded. Once high water has been exceeded,
this check is disabled until the FIFO size decreases again to or below the mark. If
hi_water_mark = 0 then the high-water mark check is disabled and only overflow is
checked, that is., when the depth of the queue is exceeded (provided that oflow_chk =
1). Default = 0, check disabled.
enq_lat
A compile-time non-negative integer constant that indicates the number of cycles between
enq being asserted 1 and enq_data being valid in the corresponding position. At that point
all enqueue data is dropped and further checking is disabled until dequeue occurs. If an
enqueue and dequeue happen simultaneously then no overflow is reported. Default = 0.
deq_lat

oflow_chk
When an enq bit is asserted 1: If oflow_chk evaluates true, ensures that queue does not
overflow the max size given in depth. depth (maximum size = t 2**16). Default = 1.
uflow_chk
When a deq bit is asserted 1:if uflow_chk evaluates true, ensures that queue was not
empty (underflow); if a dequeue on empty is detected, then the check is disabled until the
next enqueue operation. Default = 1.
If value_chk evaluates true, ensures deq_data as selected by the same position as the
highest priority deq bit is the same as that at the head of the queue. Default = 1.
pass_thru
If an enqueue and dequeue operation happens simultaneously on an empty queue, then
the behavior depends on the pass_thru parameter (it must be a compile-time constant):
If pass_thru= 0 then the dequeue happens before enqueue, therefore, the empty condition
is detected and reported and an underflow (provided that uflow_chk= 1). If value_chk= 1
then the value check fails. Default = 0.
If pass_thru = 1 then it is assumed that enqueue happens first and the data is
immediately dequeued and compared with deq_data if value_chk is enabled. Also, there
is no underflow error reported.

failure.

assert_hold_value
Ensure that exp remains at value for min to max number of cycles. That is, it must stay at
value for min cycles, then it might change and after max cycles it must change to some
other value. bw is the bit-width of exp.
The check is not enabled unless reset_n evaluates true (1). reset_n is checked only
once at the beginning of each sequence.
The check is performed on the active clk edge specification and is triggered by a value
change of exp to value.
min = max = 0 means that exp changes every cycle (that is., keeps the value for one
cycle).
min = max = 1 means that exp keeps value for two cycles.
A value min > 0 and max = 0 is interpreted as the open-ended interval [min:$].

coverage_level_2,coverage_level_3) ]
property_type )]
inst_name ( clk, reset_n, exp, value);
min
Minimum number of clock cycles to hold the value. Default = 0.
max
Maximum number of clock cycles to hold the value. Default = 0.
For an open-ended interval [min ..] , set max equal to zero and min to greater than zero.
bw
The number of bits in the signal being tested (exp). Default = 2.
exp
Expression or signal being tested.
value

Value to hold by exp.
The assertion assert_hold_value reports failure if exp does not hold the value for at least
min+1 clock ticks or if it does not change from value at max+1 clock ticks at the latest.
Cover property, cover_nb_of_exp_changes, indicates that the exp changed value.
Cover point, observed_hold_time, reports the observed number of clock cycles during
which exp was held at value triggered whenever there was a transition on exp to value.

exactly equal to value for the specified min_clks.
Cover property, cover_hold_value_for_max_clks, indicates that the exp was held
exactly equal to value for the specified max_clks.

All Level_1 and Level_2 coverages are enabled.

When addr_chk evaluates true, ensures that start_addr £ raddr £ end_addr when ren
is true, and that start_addr £ waddr £ end_addr when wen is true. All other checks apply
only if the address is valid. Therefore, It is recommended to enable addr_chk.
When init_chk evaluates true, ensures that addresses read have been previously
written.
When value_chk evaluates true, ensures that the value read from an address is the value
that was written to that address.
A read/write conflict occurs when a read operation occurs simultaneous with a write
operation on the same address. When a conflict occurs, a read is assumed to happen
before a write in the same cycle.
When conflict_chk evaluates true, ensures that simultaneous reading and writing of the
same address does not occur. This check should only be enabled when rclk == wclk.
When the two clocks are different the conflict check does not make much sense.
The pass_thru specification defines the behavior of the memory when a read and write
occur simultaneously on the same address. When pass_thru = 0 then the read operation
obtains the old data (before the write takes place). If pass_thru = 1, then the read
operation gets the new value written in memory. Note that this option has effect only when
value_chk or init_chk are enabled. Furthermore, pass_thru should only be enabled
when rclk = wclk and conflict_chk = 0.
When read1_chk evaluates true, ensures that an address has at most one read in
between writes.
When write1_chk evaluates true, ensures that an address is read at least once before it
is overwritten by different data.
Separate read and write port RAMs are naturally supported. For single-port R/W RAMs,
simply associate the same actuals with the appropriate parameters. For single clock
synchronous RAMs, provide the same clock edge parameter for both rclk and wclk.
The parameters data_bits = number of bits in the data, addr_bits = number of bits
in the addresses, start_addr = first address, end_addr = last address, and mem_sz
= number of words, are compile-time constant values which describe the layout of the
memory. Note that end_addr - start_addr + 1 must be less than or equal to mem_sz.

before reading and there was no simultaneous read and write with pass through allowed.

the limits when wen was asserted.
Assertion assert_mem_raddr_chk reports failure when the read address was not within
the limits when ren was asserted.
Assertion assert_mem_conflict_chk reports failure when wen and ren were asserted
simultaneously and the write and read addresses were the same sampled by the write
clock wclk.
Assertion assert_mem_read1_chk reports failure when at the time of failure the sva
variables recording reads and writes indicated the same state. therefore, there was more
than one read between writes.
Assertion assert_mem_write1_chk reports failure when after a memory location
was initialized, neither the location was read before the next write nor there was a
simultaneous read and write (as sampled by the write clock wclk) with pass_thru
disabled.
Assertion assert_mem_val_chk reports failure when pass through is allowed and read
and write happen at the same time (as sampled by the read clock rclk) to the same
address and the data is not equal.

no_ports, hi_water_mark, enq_lat, deq_lat,
oflow_chk, uflow_chk, value_chk, pass_thru,
property_type )]
inst_name ( clk, reset_n, enq, enq_data, deq, deq_data );
depth
The maximum number of elements in the queue. Default = 2. The specified depth can be
at most 216. Default = 2.
elem_sz
The size of queue elements in bits. Default = 1.
no_ports
Number of ports. Default = 2.
hi_water_mark
If hi_water_mark is a positive value, then the level of the fill of the queue after enqueue
is checked to see if hi_water_mark is reached. Once high water has been reached
once, this check is disabled until the FIFO size decreases again to or below the mark.
If hi_water_mark = 0 then the high-water mark check is disabled and only overflow is
checked, that is., when the depth of the queue is exceeded (provided that oflow_chk =
1). Default = 0.
enq_lat
A compile-time non-negative integer constant that indicates the number of cycles between
enq being asserted 1 and enq_data being valid in the corresponding position. At that point
all enqueue data is dropped and further checking is disabled until dequeue occurs. If an
enqueue and dequeue happen simultaneously then no overflow is reported. Default = 0.
deq_lat
The number of deq_clk cycles between deq being asserted 1 and deq_data being valid.
oflow_chk
When an enq bit is asserted 1: If oflow_chk evaluates true, ensures that queue does not
overflow the max size given in depth. depth (maximum size = t 2**16). Default = 1.
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

uflow_chk
When a deq bit is asserted 1:if uflow_chk evaluates true, ensures that queue was not
empty (underflow); if a dequeue on empty is detected, then the check is disabled until the
next enqueue operation. Default = 1.
If value_chk evaluates true, ensures deq_data as selected by the same position as the
highest priority deq bit is the same as that at the head of the queue. Default = 1.
pass_thru
If an enqueue and dequeue operation happens simultaneously on an empty queue, then
the behavior depends on the pass_thruparameter (it must be a compile-time constant):
If pass_thru= 0 then the dequeue happens before enqueue, therefore, the empty condition
is detected and reported and an underflow (provided that uflow_chk= 1). If value_chk= 1
then the value check fails. Default = 0.
If pass_thru = 1 then it is assumed that enqueue happens first and the data is
immediately dequeued and compared with deq_data if value_chk is enabled. Also, there
is no underflow error reported.
If an enqueue and a dequeue operation happen simultaneously on a full queue then no

enqanddeq
Bit vectors of equal size no_ports. Each pair of corresponding bits in these vectors
defines the enqueue and dequeue signals for a port. Their priority is such the bit 0 is
the lowest priority, the highest order bit no_ports-1 is the highest priority. That is, the
enqueue port and the dequeue port of the highest priority are processed at every clk tick.

as [no_ports*elem_size-1:0], with data vectors appearing in the same order as
the enqrequests. Whenever a bit in enq is asserted 1, the corresponding data part in
enq_dat must be valid after enq_lat clock cycles. Only the highest priority data is actually
enqueued.
deq_data
A concatenation of the data from the different ports. It is assumed that it is dimensioned
as [no_ports*elem_size-1:0], with data vectors appearing in the same order as the deq
requests. Whenever a bit in deq is asserted 1, the corresponding data part in deq_dat
must be valid after deq_lat clock cycles. The highest priority data is compared with the
data at the head of the queue if value_chk evaluates true.

Set to 1 when data is being pushed.

• All operations including reset are synchronous to a tick of clk.
• reset_n asserted 0 initializes the stack to empty.
VCS® SystemVerilog Assertions Checker Library with Coverage Level Reporting Reference Manual

• When push is asserted 1: Ensures no stack overflow. push_lat specifies the number
of ticks of clk between the asserting of push and when push_data is valid. It must be
a compile-time non-negative integer constant (not an interval).
• If hi_water_mark is a positive value, then the fill of the stack after the push is checked
to see if hi_water_mark is exceeded (>=). Once high water has been exceeded, this
check is disabled until the stack falls below the mark again (<). hi_water_mark can be
a constant or a design variable.
• If the stack depth is exceeded, a failure is reported and all further checks are disabled
until the stack is reset.
• When pop is enabled: Ensures the stack is not empty when popped. If a pop is
performed on an empty stack, all checking of pop operations is disabled until reset is
applied or a push occurs.
• If value_chk evaluates to 1, it ensures pop_data is what was on the top of the stack.
pop_lat specifies the number of cycles of clk between the asserting of pop and when
pop_datais valid. It must be a compile-time non-negative integer constant (not an
interval).
• If push_pop_chk evaluates 1, ensures that push and pop operations do not occur
simultaneously. If push and pop do occur simultaneously, the effect is the same as if
push were done first followed by a pop (that is, the stack is not changed). If value_chk
= 1, then pop_data is compared with push_data.
Assertion assert_stack_overflow reports a failure when push is issued and the stack
is full. The reported time of failure is on the clock tick following the failed deferred push
operation.
Assertion assert_stack_underflow reports a failure when pop is issued and the stack
is empty (and no simultaneous push). The reported time of failure is on the clock tick
following the failed deferred push operation.
Assertion assert_stack_value_chk reports failure when pop_data value does not match
the expected top-of-stack value, provided the stack is not empty or when the stack is
empty and there is a simultaneous push and the value pushed on the stack does not
match the value popped off the stack.
Assertion assert_stack_hi_water_chk reports a failure if the stack is filled above the
high-water mark.
Assertion assert_stack_push_pop_fail reports a failure if push and pop are enabled
simultaneously (and push_pop_chk is 1).
